title: [Simulator] Add InferCast time predictor adapter
body:
## Summary
- integrate InferCast through the existing `InferTimePredictor` abstraction and direct UMD per-forward APIs
- preserve prepared `EXTEND`, `MIXED`, and `DECODE` metadata with the frozen `mean_attention_flops_v1` reduction
- fail before iteration or time accounting on unsupported modes, missing data, invalid output, or the explicit non-zero-prefix TODO
- record portable provider, FIDB stack, topology, runtime, forward-mode, and call-count evidence

## Scope
This branch is based on merged #33824. SGLang retains ownership of cache hits and chunk boundaries. Reduced `P > 0` reaches `estimate_extend_forward_ms` but remains numerically unsupported until InferCast adds the corresponding operation boundary.

## Commit structure
1. preserve predictor forward and time-accounting semantics
2. add the InferCast predictor and lazy optional-provider loading
3. add focused contract, binding, provenance, and failure tests
4. add concise operator documentation and a silicon configuration template
5. bind FIDB lookup to the configured canonical system identifier
6. expose InferCast in the main simulator user guide

title: [Unified Cache] Abort requests whose external linker load fails instead of crashing the scheduler
body:
## Motivation

With the external cache linker (Mooncake / UMBP direct L3), any storage read error during a layer-wise load raised inside the model forward and brought the whole server down (SIGQUIT). Nodes were also published to the radix tree before their KV landed, so simply catching the error would have let other requests reuse unloaded slots.

## Modifications

- A linker load now lands in device slots private to the loading request. `load_back` no longer inserts the tail; the request inserts it like computed KV once the load is confirmed (`load_back_is_cache_owned()` keeps `cache_protected_len` at the device hit).
- `LayerWiseLoadCounter.wait_until` no longer raises. After the forward, `run_batch` calls `finish_external_linker_loads()`, which waits for the batch's load and agrees on the result across ranks (MIN), since an MLA dedup peer never sees the source's error.
- Requests whose load failed are aborted with 503 and never inserted into the tree; chunked requests go through the existing chunked-abort path. The MLA dedup source still issues its layer broadcasts on failure, so peers do not hang.
- The two backends share one `LayerWiseLoadCounter` (first commit, behavior-neutral). The pending-load locks, the load completion queues, and the COMMIT / adopted-page load phase are removed.

## Tests

- `test_unified_cache_linker.py`: request-private load, dedup on insert, failed-load cleanup (Full and Full+SWA) on both tree cores, cross-rank verdict, counter semantics.
- End to end with Mooncake on DeepSeek-V3.2 (TP1, and TP2 with `--enable-linker-mla-dedup`), injecting a mid-load failure: the request gets a 503, the server keeps serving, and the next identical request hits L3 with output identical to a cold run.

title: HiCache NIXL Tier-3 Bug Fixes
body:
# Motivation

Three bug classes were found in the HiCache NIXL tier-3 (L3) path while
benchmarking the storage tier. The bugs compound in the default configuration:

1. **O_DIRECT tier-3 writes failed but were treated as cache hits.** The XPU
   pinned host allocation is page-aligned, but is not `get_user_pages()`-able,
   so NIXL's O_DIRECT path receives `EFAULT`, while buffered I/O using the same
   buffer succeeds. Since O_DIRECT is the default, affected writes created
   zero-length files, while the subsequent cache lookup treated file existence
   as a cache hit. The existing guard only checked page alignment, which is
   insufficient for this allocation type.

2. **Failed transfers were reported using requested bytes.** `_log_xfer_stats`
   derived the logged byte count and bandwidth from the requested buffer sizes
   regardless of transfer outcome. As a result, a batch that wrote no data
   could still be reported as 2.173 GiB at 3.11 GiB/s, which did not represent
   actual storage traffic and could mask the underlying write failure.

3. **NIXL backend configuration was not normalized or validated
   consistently.** JSON boolean values were stringified as `"True"`/`"False"`
   and therefore did not match NIXL's case-sensitive boolean options.
   SGLang-only options such as `use_direct_io` and `l3_cleaner_*` were also
   only read from the top level, so their documented nested form could
   silently fall back to defaults. In addition, malformed or incomplete
   `plugin` sections could raise during backend selection instead of falling
   back to `SGLANG_HICACHE_NIXL_BACKEND_PLUGIN`.

# Modifications

Four focused commits implement the fixes and regression coverage:

| Commit | Subject |
|---|---|
| `7fe92c1a9f` | Fall back to buffered tier-3 I/O when O_DIRECT rejects the host pool |
| `9cca392c32` | Stop reporting requested bytes as transferred for a failed NIXL transfer |
| `faaac05b07` | Fix NIXL backend configuration normalization and fallback handling |
| `bd6f6f86b9` | Add regression tests for the NIXL tier-3 fixes |

## 1. Fall back to buffered tier-3 I/O when O_DIRECT rejects the host pool

Probe O_DIRECT usability once per pool registration instead of assuming that
page alignment is sufficient.

The probe opens a temporary file under each configured base directory and
performs a real page-aligned `pwrite` using the pool's own source buffer. If
the probe fails, O_DIRECT and its page-alignment requirement are disabled for
that pool, and the reason is logged.

The probe covers all relevant tier-3 source-buffer types:

- v1 zero-copy `kv_buffer`
- copy-mode bounce buffers
- v2 hybrid mamba/SWA pool buffers
- V4 `LogicalHostPool` marker buffers

Each base directory is probed independently because directories can reside on
different filesystems or mounts.

`O_TMPFILE` is used where supported to avoid leaving probe files that could be
picked up by the L3 cleaner. A named temporary file is used as the fallback.

The fallback also covers path mode, where O_DIRECT is passed to NIXL as the
`"direct"` token in the file specification.

## 2. Stop reporting requested bytes as transferred for a failed NIXL transfer

Update `_log_xfer_stats` to derive the logged byte count from successfully
completed transfers rather than requested buffer sizes.

Bandwidth is calculated from the completed byte count so failed or partial
transfers cannot be reported as successful full-size transfers.

## 3. Fix NIXL backend configuration normalization and fallback handling

Normalize JSON boolean values to the lowercase strings expected by NIXL:

```text
True  -> "true"
False -> "false"
```

Literal `"True"`/`"False"` strings are folded with a warning. Other string
values are preserved unchanged.

SGLang-only options such as `use_direct_io` and `l3_cleaner_*` are promoted
from `plugin.<name>` to the top level when required.

Configuration precedence is:

1. Existing top-level value.
2. Nested plugin value when the top-level value is absent.
3. Conflicting values from multiple plugins are not promoted.

The `active` plugin selector is consumed by SGLang and is no longer forwarded
to `create_backend`.

Backend selection now handles malformed plugin configuration by falling back
to `SGLANG_HICACHE_NIXL_BACKEND_PLUGIN` instead of raising:

- non-mapping `plugin` section
- no active plugin
- unusable plugin options

## 4. Add regression tests for the NIXL tier-3 fixes

34 new regression cases were added across two test files.

`test_hicache_nixl_utils.py` adds 19 CPU-gated cases covering:

- NIXL configuration normalization
- nested plugin-option handling
- plugin selector fallback
- malformed configuration
- O_DIRECT probe behavior

`test_hicache_nixl_storage.py` adds 15 GPU-gated cases covering:

- failed-transfer statistics at all four call sites
- v1 registration
- v2 hybrid registration
- logical-anchor registration
- O_DIRECT probe coverage for relevant buffer types

# Accuracy Tests

Bug 1 was reproduced on ext4/NVMe with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct:

| Configuration | Files | Stored data |
|---|---:|---:|
| O_DIRECT | 2350 | 0 bytes |
| Buffered I/O | 2476 | 0.529 GiB |
| O_DIRECT + probe/fallback | — | 0.529 GiB |

The probe detects that O_DIRECT cannot successfully use the affected XPU host
pool and switches the pool to buffered I/O.

Bug 3 was verified using `strace` with:

```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "posix": {
      "use_uring": true
    }
  }
}
```

Before this change, the POSIX backend issued `io_setup` and selected libaio.

After this change, it issued `io_uring_setup`, confirming that the nested
boolean configuration reaches the intended backend option.

# Test Results

```text
55 passed, 1 skipped, 11 subtests passed
```

The skipped test is the MinIO OBJ fixture, which requires a `minio` binary on
the test runner.

Reverting the three functional changes to the merge base causes **27 of the
34 new regression cases to fail**.

The remaining seven cases are intentional negative-branch contracts expected
to pass on both sides of the change, including:

- successful O_DIRECT probe keeps O_DIRECT enabled
- unaligned hybrid pool continues using bounce buffers
- anchor pool can still register
- successful transfer still reports bandwidth
- literal `"TRUE"` is preserved
- malformed plugin section can still reach the plugin unchanged

Targeted mutations were also used for branches that a whole-file revert
cannot distinguish, including both probe call sites, probe exception
handling, and successful transfer outcomes at the affected statistics call
sites.

# Performance Impact

No steady-state fast-path overhead is introduced.

- O_DIRECT probing runs once per pool registration.
- One temporary-file probe is performed per base directory.
- Statistics only change which byte count is used for the existing log line.
- Configuration normalization runs once during backend creation.

For affected pools, falling back from O_DIRECT to buffered I/O is a correctness-over-throughput trade-off. The fallback is selected only when the
probe shows that O_DIRECT cannot successfully write from the pool's source
buffer.

# Files Changed

```text
mem_cache/storage/nixl/hicache_nixl.py  (+92)
mem_cache/storage/nixl/nixl_utils.py    (+202)
mem_cache/memory_pool_host.py           (+2)
tests/...                               (2 test files)
```

# Checklist

- [x] Code formatted
- [x] `pre-commit run --files ...` passes
- [x] New tests registered in CI
- [x] CPU tests registered under `base-a-test-cpu`
- [x] GPU tests registered under `base-b` / `1-gpu-small`
- [x] Each commit builds and imports successfully on its own

title: fix(dsv4): support R3 capture and MXFP4 online updates
body:
Replaces #38282, which GitHub auto-closed when its base branch was deleted and recreated.

## Summary

- Capture logical expert IDs from DeepSeek V4 HashTopK before logical-to-physical remapping for R3 replay. Mask CUDA-graph padding, disable target capture from draft modules, and reject the unsupported HashTopK waterfill/capture combination.
- Synchronize CUDA IPC tensor imports in the weight updater before returning to the producer, including flattened buckets and other tensor load formats.
- Support repeated TRT-LLM MXFP4 online loads: permute expert weights in place, retain checkpoint-layout scale parameters, and maintain separate shuffled scale copies with stable kernel addresses. Pass unsigned byte views at the FlashInfer packed-FP4 call boundary without changing load parameters.
- Register the GEMM1 clamp limit as a non-persistent buffer so memory offload preserves it.
- Keep the padded-row Triton fast path off CPU tensors.

## Rebase (2026-09-23)

Based directly on `sglang-miles` at `67e4cd1885155bf9b08366b348c59d5b79a7fb7b`.

The previous 12 commits were consolidated into one signed commit, preserving their net production changes. The stable patch-id of the production-code diff is identical before and after the rebase. That consolidated baseline changed 9 files (+450/-100); no unrelated commits from the old base were carried over. A subsequent FP8/MXFP8 lifecycle fix is described below.

Test integration adjustments:
- Preserve the upstream CPU suite rename to `stage-a-test-cpu-intel`, with the existing 30-second estimate.
- Move the MXFP4 hot-reload test to `test/registered/kernel/quantization/` and register it on `base-b-kernel-unit` / `4-gpu-b200`. Its SM100+ requirement meant the old H100 registration would skip it. The test itself uses one GPU.

Previous head: `0d4f00c7aad9ebc0c117aa2a6be058d1f3d8ab09`.
Rebased head: `23837cdabfedb1d4691c8f0bf56d05b7e19b48ad`.

## Validation

On the rebased source:
- HashTopK tests: **7 passed** with CUDA hidden in the existing local SGLang container.
- MXFP4 hot-reload test: **1 skipped** because the local container cannot access CUDA. GPU execution was not revalidated for this head.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks: passed with `GITHUB_BASE_REF=sglang-miles`.
- Changed Python files: `py_compile` passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The previous head had passed the hot-reload test on B300. This historical result is not a substitute for testing the new base; no new end-to-end RL run was performed.

## FP8/MXFP8 activation-state follow-up (2026-09-23)

Commit `104716dc91` also fixes the TRT-LLM activation tensors introduced in the new base's FP8/MXFP8 path. These alpha/beta/clamp tensors were ordinary attributes, so the memory-saver static-state backup omitted them. Repeated postprocessing also replaced their storage even though CUDA graphs retained the old addresses. Register them as non-persistent buffers and copy into existing storage on reload.

Evidence: an isolated reproduction using the actual preparation and static-state export/import functions left the old clamp at zero after simulated storage loss; re-preparation created a different pointer holding 10. The same function-level check passes after the fix (restored values, stable storage, no checkpoint entries). The existing runner-ownership test fixture now also covers this lifecycle.

The prior `23837cdabf` source passed 7 HashTopK tests and the GPU MXFP4 hot-reload test on OCI-AGA GB300 (job 835075), but an end-to-end P1 run subsequently exhibited repetitive output and could not collect valid training groups. The activation-state defect is confirmed; attributing the complete rollout failure to it still requires a new RL run. Updated-source integration job **835403** completed successfully on OCI-AGA GB300: 51 Miles integration tests, 6 GPU MXFP4 QAT tests, and 12 SGLang tests (HashTopK, MXFP4 hot reload, and FP8 runner ownership/activation-state lifecycle). Changed-file pre-commit passed with `GITHUB_BASE_REF=sglang-miles`. P1 smoke **835471**, with all other source/config pins unchanged, collected valid normal-mode samples and completed one valid optimizer step (`ppo_kl=0`, rollout/train log-prob absolute difference 0.02877). It then failed with Slurm host-memory OOM during trainer CPU offload; this is not a three-step end-to-end pass. The first `actor_train` timer was 703.9 seconds, not a steady-state performance measurement. P1 retry **835929** subsequently **passed all three optimizer steps** and exited Slurm `COMPLETED / 0:0` (1:03:47), with the same source pins and training settings and additional host-memory diagnostics. `actor_train`: 699.8 / 127.0 / 105.5 seconds; `ppo_kl=0` for all three steps; train/rollout log-prob absolute difference 0.02852 / 0.02860 / 0.02731. No host or CUDA OOM was observed in this run. This does not establish the earlier host-OOM root cause: the physical nodes and Ray-head/PP-stage placement differed. W&B: https://wandb.ai/megatron-core-moe-dev/miles-run_deepseek_v4/runs/qaptznwe . P2 **836374** and P3 **836375** both failed during the initial SGLang autotune forward, before online weight sync or training: `ValueError: Unsupported trtllm-gen input tensor`. The MXFP4 method passed signed checkpoint parameters directly to FlashInfer instead of zero-copy unsigned-byte views; the same issue exists in the pre-rebase PR head. The idle outer launchers were cancelled. SGLang commit `f9cfbec2d2` fixes that boundary with zero-copy uint8 views, preserving signed load parameters and storage. The new real-kernel case fails with the original exception before the fix; after the fix, all 13 local B300 SGLang tests pass (including real MXFP4 x MXFP8 forward and reload). OCI-AGA ARM preflight **836746** completed successfully: **70 tests passed** (51 Miles, 6 GPU QAT, 13 SGLang), exit `0:0`. P2 retry **836780** and P3 retry **836781** now use `f9cfbec2d2` with the same training settings and other repository pins; their end-to-end success is not yet claimed. The completed P1 run above used SGLang `104716dc91`; it predates this MXFP4-only follow-up.

title: [AMD] Critical fix enabling Qwen3.8 FP8: restore dropped fused shared-expert weights
body:
## Motivation

Text-only Qwen3.5-MoE checkpoints (architecture `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, e.g. `Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8`) load into `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`, whose `load_weights` was missing the shared-expert fusion remapping that the multimodal `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` already implements. On ROCm with aiter shared-expert fusion enabled (`SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`), `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock` serves the shared expert as an extra fused MoE slot at index `num_experts`, but `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM.load_weights` kept `num_experts` unchanged and never remapped `mlp.shared_expert.*` onto that slot. Every layer's shared-expert weights were therefore silently dropped ("Parameter ...mlp.shared_expert... not found in params_dict") and the fused slot was left uninitialized, zeroing the shared expert across all layers and collapsing accuracy (gsm8k near random) while the server still loaded and served.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py`, class `Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM`:
  - `__init__`: compute `num_fused_shared_experts` / `enable_shared_expert_fusion` when aiter fusion is active, via a new `_get_num_fused_shared_experts()` that scans local MoE layers (PP-safe: non-local slots are `PPMissingLayer` with no `.mlp`).
  - `load_weights`: grow `make_expert_params_mapping(num_experts=...)` by the fused shared count when fusion is on; extend `fused_expert_params_mapping` with the shared-slot entries; remap `mlp.shared_expert.* -> mlp.experts.{num_experts}.*`; load the fused shared slot into `experts.w13_weight` / `experts.w2_weight`.
- This mirrors the existing, working handling in `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` (added in #20736 for the multimodal path) so the text-only entry class behaves identically.

## Accuracy Tests

Verified on `Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-FP8`, TP8 / PP2, 2x MI300X, `--attention-backend aiter`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`:

| Metric | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|
| `mlp.shared_expert.* not found in params_dict` warnings (per rank set) | 1104 | 0 |
| Shared expert loaded (per layer) | dropped (zeroed) | loaded into fused slot |
| Sample gsm8k generations | incoherent / wrong | coherent and correct |

Full gsm8k sweep (sglang few-shot, 1314 questions):

| Run | gsm8k score |
|---|---|
| Reference (known-good, pre-regression) | 0.9749 (97.49%) |
| After fix | 0.9741 (97.41%) |

The shared expert is loaded and accuracy matches the known-good baseline.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

title: [NPU] Support host_rdma transfer protocol for PD disaggregation on A5
body:
## Motivation

Atlas 950 (A5) machines require the `host_rdma` protocol for KV cache transfer in PD disaggregation. However, `AscendTransferEngine` currently only supports `sdma` and `device_rdma`, and there is no way to pass a NIC endpoint to the underlying MemFabric transfer engine.

## Modifications

**Code** (`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/ascend/transfer_engine.py`):
- Resolve `host_rdma` (from `ASCEND_MF_TRANSFER_PROTOCOL`) to the new `TransDataOpType.HOST_RDMA` op type, alongside the existing `sdma` / `device_rdma` handling.
- Add the `nic` kwarg to `engine.initialize()` and derive each worker's HOST_RDMA listen port in the framework:
worker_port = BASE + role_offset + npu_id * 8 
role_offset: Decode = 0, Prefill = 128
Rationale: MemFabric binds `base_port + group rank (0..7)` within the endpoint it is given, so each worker must own a disjoint stride of ports, and the multi-rank topology is only known to the framework. The role offset lets Prefill and Decode share a host without conflicts.
- Fail fast with a clear error when `host_rdma` is selected but `ASCEND_MF_NIC` is unset (the engine would otherwise bind a loopback endpoint that peers cannot reach), when the value is malformed, or when the derived port is out of range.
- Log the resolved endpoint (role / npu_id / base / endpoint) per worker.
- When the protocol is not `host_rdma`, `nic=None` is passed and existing `sdma` / `device_rdma` behavior is unchanged.

**Docs**:
- `environment_variables.mdx`: document `ASCEND_MF_TRANSFER_PROTOCOL` (`sdma` default / `device_rdma` / `host_rdma`) and `ASCEND_MF_NIC`.
- `glossary.mdx`: note that A5 (Atlas 950) uses `host_rdma` and requires `ASCEND_MF_NIC`.
- `installation.mdx`: add "Atlas 950 A5" example tabs for both prefill and decode servers in the PD disaggregation guide.

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Values | Notes |
|----------|--------|-------|
| `ASCEND_MF_TRANSFER_PROTOCOL` | `sdma` (default) / `device_rdma` / `host_rdma` | Unsupported values fall back to `sdma` with a warning |
| `ASCEND_MF_NIC` | `IP:PORT` (or `tcp://IP:PORT`) | Required with `host_rdma`. Base endpoint; each worker listens on `PORT + role offset (Decode 0 / Prefill 128) + npu_id * 8` |

## Checklist

- [x] Code changes are minimal and localized to the Ascend transfer engine
- [x] Existing `sdma` / `device_rdma` behavior is unchanged
- [x] Docs updated for the new environment variables
- [ ] Verified on A5 hardware (pending)

title: [Fix] Resolve Inkling think-end IDs in ReasonerGrammarBackend and gate the canonical-schema bypass
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #40468, stacked on it (contains its commits until it merges). Two issues from review:

1. `ReasonerGrammarBackend.__init__` still resolved `think_end_ids` by encoding `think_end_token` as ordinary text. For Inkling the native `END_MESSAGE` id (200010) differs from its printed-spelling encoding, so every grammar that keeps the wrapper — strict thinking mode, and non-canonical constraints (json_schema / regex / modified structural_tag) with reasoning enabled — never observes think end and stays in the thinking phase. #40468 fixed the scheduler's `model_config.think_end_ids`, but `create_grammar_backend` only uses that value as a construction gate; the constructor re-encoded the marker on its own.

2. The canonical-schema bypass matched schema content alone, so a byte-identical user-supplied `structural_tag` response format would bypass reasoning deferral regardless of the model's reasoning detector.

## Modifications

- Resolve `think_end_ids` via `reasoning_parser.detector.get_think_end_token_ids(tokenizer)` (the hook #40468 added) in `ReasonerGrammarBackend.__init__`.
- Gate the canonical-schema bypass on the Inkling reasoning detector, and build the canonical schema once as a lazy module constant instead of reconstructing it per dispatch.
- Tests: the backend resolves the native `END_MESSAGE` id and the wrapper transitions on it in both strict and non-strict mode; the canonical schema with a non-Inkling detector still defers until reasoning ends.

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/constrained/test_reasoner_grammar_backend.py`: 36 passed, 24 subtests passed (CPU devbox, torch + xgrammar).

title: Support a reduced draft vocabulary in rejection sampling
body:
## Motivation

`--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` with EAGLE3 and a reduced draft vocabulary (e.g. `draft_vocab_size=32000`, `target_vocab_size=201216`) currently refuses to start:

```
ValueError: --speculative-use-rejection-sampling requires the draft and target to
share one vocab, but the draft vocab (32000) != target vocab (201216).
```

The FIXME at `eagle_worker_v2.py:328` says *"support reduced (hot) draft vocab by scattering draft probs into the target vocab via the d2t map before the sampling kernel"*. This PR implements exactly that.

### Why it matters for correctness

Without this, EAGLE3 with `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` falls through to the official tree verifier (`rejected_probs=zeros`), which never consumes the actual draft distribution `q`. On a 201K-vocab model with a 32K hot-vocab EAGLE3 draft (TP=8, H800):

| Setting | Old path (`rejected_probs=zeros`) | New path (classic + scatter) | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| target T=1, draft T=1, mean accept length over 11 benchmarks | 2.841 | 3.583 | **+26.1%** |
| target greedy, draft T=1, mean accept length over 12 benchmarks | 4.535 | 3.509 | -22.6% (see note) |

Note on the -22.6%: it is expected, and it shows the old number was mislabeled. Under `rejected_probs=zeros` the draft is always argmax regardless of draft temperature, so "draft T=1" was really measuring greedy-greedy. The new path samples from `q` with the real temperature, and acceptance drops because a sampled token now has to match the greedy target. That is the correct behavior for this configuration.

A four-arm distributional test (two-sample G-test on token-frequency histograms, 10K samples per prompt, positions 2-4, 8 prompts, T=1/top_k=-1/top_p=1) confirms unbiasedness:

```
                     G/2N (nats/token)   relative to cross-launch floor
ref_a_vs_ref_b       1.429e-03           (within-arm floor)
ref_vs_ref2          2.059e-03           1.00  (cross-launch floor)
ref_vs_new           2.035e-03           0.99  <- indistinguishable from floor
ref_vs_old           2.494e-03           1.21  <- biased, pooled p = 3.2e-26
```

`ref2` is a second independent non-speculative launch. It is required as the baseline because this model is not batch-invariant (bs=1 vs bs=20 greedy decoding already diverges on 7/20 prompts), so a within-arm floor understates the noise and misattributes cross-process numerics to the verifier.

## Modifications

`spec_utils.py` - add `scatter_draft_probs_to_target_vocab()`:
- `index_copy_` the hot-vocab `q` into a target-vocab-width zero tensor. This is exact, not an approximation: the draft can only ever propose a hot token, so `q(x) = 0` off the hot set is the true proposal mass, and `relu(p - q)` keeps the full `p` there.
- Force fp32 so the eager and CUDA-graph paths hand the kernel the same dtype.
- No buffer reuse: the returned tensor outlives the call under overlap scheduling, so a cached buffer would alias across iterations.

`eagle_worker_v2.py`:
- Replace the FIXME `raise ValueError` with an info log.
- Add `_build_verify_draft_probs()`, which stacks the per-step `q` and scatters once at the kernel boundary rather than in each producer.
- Under `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT`, assert `q > 0` at every proposed token. A misaligned or mis-scattered `q` reads back as `q == 0`, which makes the `coin * q < p` accept test vacuously true: accept length pins to `num_steps` while the text silently degrades. The gather is gated so it never runs in production.
- Initialize `draft_probs_list = None` outside the rejection-sampling branch, since the new call sites would otherwise raise `NameError` when rejection sampling is off.

`arg_groups/speculative_hook.py` - `_should_auto_enable_hip_rejection_sampling` carried the same FIXME in its docstring ("rejection sampling still cannot consume a reduced / hot draft vocab"). Updated to reflect that the scatter now exists. The conservative behavior is kept: ROCm still does not auto-enable rejection sampling for EAGLE3 or for an EAGLE run with a token map, because this path has not been validated on ROCm. Passing the flag explicitly works.

`docs/docs/advanced_features/speculative_decoding.mdx` - `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` had no row in the speculative parameter table, only a passing mention under the UNO limitations. Added one, documenting the default, the `--speculative-eagle-topk 1` requirement, the EAGLE/EAGLE3-only restriction, the incompatibility with the accept thresholds and deterministic inference, and the new reduced-vocabulary support. All of it verified against `arg_groups/speculative_hook.py` rather than assumed.

`test/registered/unit/spec/test_draft_probs_reduced_vocab.py` - 7 unit tests: hot columns land on their target ids, non-hot mass is exactly zero, total mass preserved, output is fp32 for any input dtype, no buffer aliasing across calls, width satisfies the `eagle_utils` guard, and a 400K-sample Monte Carlo showing chain rejection sampling with a truncated `q` reproduces `p` (max deviation within 4 standard errors).

## Accuracy Tests

See the four-arm G-test table above. The classic chain verifier with scattered `q` sits on the cross-launch noise floor; the `rejected_probs=zeros` path is 21% above it with pooled p = 3.2e-26.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Per-benchmark accept-length gain at target T=1 / draft T=1, same model and hardware as above:

| Benchmark | Accept delta |
|---|---|
| mt-bench | +40.2% |
| alpaca | +34.5% |
| arena-hard | +29.8% |
| aime25 | +28.9% |
| livecodebench | +28.0% |
| summarization | +28.0% |
| math500 | +27.3% |
| gsm8k | +27.1% |
| mbpp | +20.5% |
| humaneval | +16.4% |
| translation | +14.6% |

Gains correlate with task entropy: higher-entropy tasks benefit more from the `relu(p - q)` residual resampling that the classic verifier provides and the tree verifier does not.

The added work is a single `index_copy_` per verify step on a `(bs, num_steps, target_vocab)` tensor. This path was previously unreachable for reduced-vocab drafts, so there is no prior behavior to regress.

The accept-length and distributional numbers were measured on a fork of this branch carrying the ERNIE-5 model support, since that is where a 201K-vocab target with a 32K-hot-vocab EAGLE3 draft exists. The scatter code under review is identical.

title: feat(npu): Support returning indexer top-k results
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

`enable_return_indexer_topk` currently supports the CUDA indexer path, but the NPU backend does not create an indexer-topk capturer or expose the top-k results produced by NPU attention indexers.

  Ascend NPU already provides indexer implementations for:

  - DeepSeek DSA models, through `torch_npu.npu_lightning_indexer`
  - DeepSeek-V4 C4 indexers, through `torch.ops.custom.npu_quant_lightning_indexer`

  However, their results were not connected to the existing request-level return pipeline. As a result, NPU inference requests could not return indexer top-k metadata even when `--enable-return-indexer-topk` and `return_indexer_topk=true` were specified.

  This PR connects the NPU producer paths to the existing indexer-topk capturer and response pipeline while preserving the same output format and layer-index semantics as the CUDA implementation.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Enable indexer-topk capturer creation on both CUDA and NPU backends.
    - Model-specific layer counts continue to be resolved through `get_num_indexer_layers()`.
    - DSA models use one capturer slot per transformer layer.
    - DeepSeek-V4 uses one capturer slot per C4 compression layer.

- Add indexer-topk capture to the NPU DSA path.
    - Capture results from `forward_dsa_prepare_npu()`.
    - Cover both freshly computed top-k results and `skip_topk` layers that reuse the previous layer's result.
    - Preserve the transformer layer id in the capturer layout.

- Add indexer-topk capture to the NPU DeepSeek-V4 C4 path.
    - Capture the output of `npu_quant_lightning_indexer`.
    - Use `token_to_kv_pool.layer_mapping[].compress_layer_id` to map raw transformer layers to contiguous C4 capturer slots.
    - Keep the captured indices in the logical compressed-token coordinate system used by the NPU sparse attention path.

- Extend overlap result handling to NPU.
    - Reuse the existing `TopkCaptureOutput` and result-finalization pipeline.
    - Add NPU support to asynchronous device-to-host copies through `torch.get_device_module()`.
    - Preserve the existing synchronous path when overlap scheduling is disabled.

- Add unit tests covering:
    - NPU DSA capturer initialization.
    - DeepSeek-V4 C4 layer-count resolution.
    - Non-indexer models being disabled through a zero indexer-layer count.
    - Invalid `index_topk` configurations.

title: [AMD] Fix AITER DSA prefill with an FP8 KV cache
body:
# [AMD] Fix AITER DSA prefill with an FP8 KV cache

## Motivation

SGLang gathers the KV entries selected by DeepSeek Sparse Attention into a
compact buffer before calling AITER. Each query's range in that buffer is
described by `kv_indptr`.

The existing integration configures AITER as if the input still used a fixed
sparse top-k layout. It also forces 64 work splits, allocates FP8 output for an
operation that returns BF16, and replaces the KV-cache scale with `1.0`. These
assumptions can produce invalid work metadata and incorrect output at long
context.

## Modifications

- Select AITER's v1.2 metadata builder with `fast_mode=True`.
- Disable the legacy v1.0 path with `intra_batch_mode=False`.
- Pass `topk=-1` because the KV entries are already compact. This makes AITER
  use the ranges in `kv_indptr`; it does not disable DSA top-k selection.
- Remove the fixed `max_split_per_batch=64` value so AITER derives the split
  count from the workload.
- Allocate BF16 output when the query input is FP8.
- Pass query scale `1.0` and the layer's KV-cache scale to AITER.
- Add AITER to the existing DSA FP8-prefill test matrix.

Cross-layer metadata reuse is intentionally excluded and will be submitted
separately.

## Accuracy Tests

Hardware: AMD MI355X, TP4, FP8 KV cache.

The existing DSA attention test suite passed the AITER BF16 and FP8 sparse
prefill cases:

```bash
python3 test/registered/attention/unittests/dsa/test_dsa.py
```

For a long-context output test, the same two fixed-seed random prompts were run
once with AITER prefill and once with TileLang prefill. Each prompt used 60,000
input tokens and 64 output tokens, with `temperature=0` and `top_p=1`. The
generated texts matched for both prompts.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is a correctness fix. The metadata builder changes from a fixed split
policy to AITER's workload-adaptive policy, but this PR does not claim a
standalone serving-speed improvement.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and code-style checks pass.
- [x] Existing DSA accuracy tests cover the AITER FP8-prefill path.
- [x] Long-context output matches TileLang for both test prompts.
- [x] No user-facing documentation change is required.

title: [Fix] Request exact label logprobs for Qwen3-VL reranking
body:
## Motivation

The Qwen3-VL reranker needs both label probabilities to compute `P(yes) / (P(yes) + P(no))`. The current implementation searches the first generated token's top-50 logprobs and leaves a missing label's probability at zero. A label being absent from the returned list does not mean its probability is zero: this can clip scores to 0 or 1, create artificial ties, and change document ranking.

The implementation introduced in [#16403](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/16403) uses `top_logprobs_num=50` with the comment "Get enough logprobs to find yes/no tokens". This relies on both labels appearing in a bounded candidate list; neither is guaranteed to rank in the top 50. `top_logprobs_num` controls the returned candidate logprobs and is separate from the sampling parameter `top_k`.

This reproduces with the actual Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B model. For the query "What is the capital of France?" and document "Bananas are yellow fruit.", `/v1/rerank` returns 0 because `yes` is absent from the top-50 list. Explicitly requested logprobs are approximately -7.425894 for `yes` and -5.425894 for `no`, giving a score of **0.119202922**. A small absolute probability can still contribute materially to the ratio between the two labels.

Since the required token IDs are known, requesting their logprobs directly supplies both inputs to the scoring formula. Increasing the arbitrary cutoff would retain the same coverage assumption; returning the entire vocabulary is unnecessary. This change requests only the two required labels.

## Modifications

- Request the cached yes/no token IDs via token_ids_logprob and read output_token_ids_logprobs for the first generated token.
- Use logprob_start_len=-1 because reranking only needs the output-token distribution, avoiding unused prompt logprobs.
- Add registered CPU regressions covering a label outside top-50, correct top_n document selection, and token-ID-based extraction; update the existing VL reranker fixture to the selected-token response field.

Text-only decoder reranking and cross-encoder routing are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Tested base: aa0b65c7c79ca67ba96f0484de814f22b980cc6e.

- The unmodified implementation fails the new score and document-ranking regressions.
- Both related test files: **16 passed, 2 subtests passed**.
- New registered CPU file executed directly with -f: **3 tests passed**.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=99 python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_vl_rerank.py \
  test/registered/prefill_only/test_serving_rerank.py
PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=99 python \
  test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai/test_serving_vl_rerank.py -f
```

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=99 hides the single GPU for these CPU tests; the current base has a separate test-utils import issue with an empty value.

Real-model comparison: Ubuntu 22.04, RTX 5090 32 GB, Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B BF16, FlashInfer, radix cache and CUDA graphs disabled. Compare /v1/rerank with /generate using the same rendered prompt and explicitly requested yes/no logprobs.

| Query / document | Before | Exact-label reference | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| France's capital / Bananas are yellow fruit. | 0 | 0.119202922 | 0.119202922 |
| Reverse a Python list / The moon orbits Earth. | 0 | 0.075858180 | 0.075858180 |
| 证明黎曼猜想 / 香蕉苹果橘子西瓜 | 0 | 0.191932786 | 0.191932786 |

All **15 text pairs and one real image request** match the exact-label reference after the fix (maximum absolute error 1.11e-16; image error 0). This checks API scoring against the same engine's logprobs, not overall model relevance quality or an independent forward implementation. No model-forward or kernel changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput claim. The request now retrieves only the two labels and omits unused prompt logprobs.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Route 512-expert softmax MoE routing through aiter topk_gating
body:
## Motivation

This is a ROCm performance change: it routes Qwen3.8's 512-expert softmax MoE router through aiter's `topk_gating` instead of the vendored `vllm::moe::topkGatingSoftmax` launcher it reaches today, worth **+1.48%** output tok/s without MTP and **+2.22%** with NEXTN MTP on 8x MI355X, TP8, geomean over 12 serving shapes. **Those numbers need aiter >= `02c94ca` (aiter#5334, merged 2026-09-20), and SGLang main still pins `acf8fdf`, so the aiter bump has to land before or with this PR.** On the current pin the dispatch still fires but reaches aiter's generic kernel, which is only marginally faster than today's launcher (see "Without aiter#5334" below). v0.5.20 ships aiter `4ad9983` and, per the profiler, still runs `topkGatingSoftmax` for Qwen3.8.

Qwen3.8 picks 10 experts out of 512 on every one of its 92 layers. On ROCm that pick is 0.878 ms per decode step, 4.8% of decode kernel time, against 0.440 ms/step for the B300 equivalent. `aiter.fused_moe.fused_topk` only hands off to its ASM router for `(experts, topk)` in `(128,4), (128,6), (128,8), (256,6), (256,8), (384,8), (640,8)`, and Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4 is `(512, 10)`. Calling `aiter.ops.topk.topk_gating` directly hits the E=512 kernel from aiter#5334.

sgl-project#28399 tried the same wiring in August and got nothing for it (ITL +3.7%, throughput -1.9% on Qwen3.5 TP2). aiter has since gained that E=512 kernel (aiter#5334) and learned to honour `need_renorm` for softmax (aiter#4460).

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`: `_use_aiter_topk_gating_softmax()` decides, and the `_use_aiter` softmax branch calls `topk_gating` when it says yes. Every other shape keeps `aiter_fused_topk`.
- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: `SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_TOPK_GATING`, default on, as the kill switch.
- `test/registered/amd/test_qwen38_moe_softmax_topk_gating.py`: agreement with the legacy launcher at 4, 128 and 1024 rows, plus every envelope boundary.

The dispatch is deliberately narrow: gfx95, AITER on, hidden size 8192, BF16 contiguous gating output, 512 experts, at most 4096 rows, no correction bias, no fused shared slots, no packed output. Two of those need a word.

**The 4096-row ceiling is where eager and graph timings agree.** aiter#5334's E=512 `prefill_n` kernel covers up to 1024 tokens; above that `topk_gating` uses a shared-memory path. Against `fused_topk`, `topk_gating` is faster on GPU time (CUDA-graph replay) through 1024 rows, ties at 2048-4096 and loses from 5120; with eager launch overhead included it wins through 6144. Decode, MTP verify and MTP draft are graph-captured, while prefill runs eager, so the row count that matters for the ceiling is prefill chunks, and there GPU time is what the chunk pays. This call site cannot tell prefill from decode, so without a ceiling a 16384-token chunk would take the slow path. MTP still fits: a NEXTN 3/1/4 verify batch is `batch * 4`, inside 4096 through concurrency 1024.

**The renorm probe.** Before aiter#4460, `topk_gating` accepted softmax and silently ignored `need_renorm`, returning weights that do not sum to 1. There is no capability flag to query, so the code inspects the signature and an older aiter keeps the old path instead of serving wrong weights. aiter#5334 is header-only and has no Python-visible marker, so it is not probed; without it the dispatch is still no slower than the legacy launcher inside the ceiling.

## Accuracy Tests

The AMD kernel test checks that `topk_gating` and `fused_topk` pick experts with identical logits, top-k weights within `1e-5` after sorting, and weights that sum to 1, at 4 / 128 / 1024 rows. It compares picked logits rather than positional IDs because BF16 ties can resolve to a different expert or order, which happens from 4 rows on an aiter without #5334 and at 2048+ rows with it (weight error ~1e-7 either way). It passes on MI355X both with an aiter that includes #5334 and with v0.5.20's aiter `4ad9983`. End to end this is a different reduction, not a different semantic, and MTP accept length is the sensitive detector for that: ~4.00 across all 12 shapes in every arm, baseline included.

Paired B0 vs E4 on one MI355X node (081), TP8, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4. GSM8K is 5-shot, 1314 items, thinking on. NIAH is `niah_single_2` at 65,536 / 131,072.

| Arm | GSM8K | NIAH 65k / 131k |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MTP baseline | 0.978 | 0.998 / 1.000 |
| MTP this PR | 0.978 | 0.990 / 1.00 |
| non-MTP baseline | 0.979 | 0.998 / 0.998 |
| non-MTP this PR | 0.978 | 0.998 / 0.994 |

No accuracy regression. MTP GSM8K is the same 1285/1314; non-MTP differs by one item.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8x MI355X, TP8, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4, SGLang v0.5.19 with aiter#5334, `chunked-prefill-size 16384`. 12 cells per arm: 8k/1k at concurrency 4 through 256, 60k/600 at 4, 16 and 64, 128k/1k at 4 and 16. Each table is one node and one allocation, and the two tables are different nodes, so read each against its own baseline. Geomeans of output tok/s.

Non-MTP:

| Arm | out tok/s geomean | TTFT geomean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline, `topkGatingSoftmax` | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| aiter `topk_gating`, no ceiling | 1.0142 | 0.9872 |
| **this PR** | **1.0148** | 0.9859 |
| [#39986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39986) Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024 | 1.0160 | 0.9891 |

NEXTN MTP, 3 steps / eagle-topk 1 / 4 draft tokens:

| Arm | out tok/s geomean | accept length | TTFT geomean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 1.0000 | ~4.00 | 1.0000 |
| aiter `topk_gating`, no ceiling | 1.0211 | ~4.00 | 0.9906 |
| **this PR** | **1.0222** | ~4.00 | 1.0009 |
| [#39986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39986) Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024 | 1.0199 | ~4.00 | 0.9966 |

MTP gains more because verify and draft-extend add router launches per accepted token.

In these runs decode graphs are captured for batch sizes 1 through 256 (`max-running-requests`), and the server logs `Disable prefill CUDA graph because cuda_graph_config resolved prefill.backend='disabled'`. The kineto traces agree: every decode, verify and draft router call is launched from `hipGraphLaunch`, and every prefill call is eager.

The ceiling is worth 0.06% non-MTP and 0.11% MTP, both inside run-to-run spread, so a kernel census is what justifies it rather than the geomean. Concurrency 4, TP0 kineto trace, `random-range-ratio 1`; counts are router launches, one per layer per forward, so every total is a multiple of 92:

| Arm | Cell | `topkGatingSoftmax` | E=512 kernel | aiter smem | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 8k/100 | 9476 | 0 | 0 | 9476 |
| baseline | 60k/100 | 10580 | 0 | 0 | 10580 |
| no ceiling | 8k/100 | 0 | 9200 | 276 | 9476 |
| no ceiling | 60k/100 | 0 | 9202 | 1380 | 10582 |
| **with ceiling** | 8k/100 | 276 | 9200 | 0 | 9476 |
| **with ceiling** | 60k/100 | 1380 | 9201 | 0 | 10581 |

Without a ceiling the prefill chunks land on aiter's shared-memory kernel: 276 launches at 8k is 3 chunks x 92 layers, 1380 at 60k is 15 x 92. With one, those go back to the legacy launcher while decode keeps the E=512 kernel. These census arms used a 4096-row ceiling, which is now the shipped gate.

Microbenchmark, gfx950, E=512, topk=10, softmax, `need_renorm=true`, bf16, median of 3 runs of 200 iters. Eager times each launch from the host; graph captures 20 calls in a CUDA graph and times the replay, which is what decode sees. The Triton column is #39986's router for comparison.

| rows | eager: legacy `fused_topk` | eager: `topk_gating` | eager: Triton | graph: legacy | graph: `topk_gating` | graph: Triton |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 14.70 | **11.47** | 20.50 | 9.26 | 4.74 | **4.20** |
| 1024 | 15.56 | **12.28** | 21.18 | 9.42 | 5.50 | **4.75** |
| 2048 | 15.57 | **11.98** | 21.18 | 9.44 | 9.73 | **6.57** |
| 4096 | 15.53 | **12.00** | 21.61 | 11.50 | 11.63 | **10.78** |
| 5120 | 14.86 | **12.53** | 20.66 | **11.51** | 12.92 | 12.66 |
| 6144 | 15.02 | **13.68** | 20.82 | **11.58** | 14.10 | 14.55 |
| 7168 | **14.88** | 15.16 | 20.84 | **11.58** | 15.18 | 15.95 |
| 8192 | **14.89** | 16.55 | 20.85 | **11.64** | 16.51 | 17.93 |
| 16384 | **18.74** | 28.20 | 32.30 | **18.56** | 28.58 | 32.60 |

Times in us. Under graphs `topk_gating` is about 45% faster than the legacy launcher through 1024 rows; eager, the gap is about 20% and mostly launch cost.

Without aiter#5334 (v0.5.20 image, aiter `4ad9983`, graph replay, us), `topk_gating` runs its generic kernel at every size:

| rows | legacy | `topk_gating`, no #5334 | `topk_gating`, with #5334 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 9.27 | 8.02 | 4.74 |
| 256 | 10.07 | 8.44 | 5.13 |
| 1024 | 9.40 | 9.24 | 5.50 |
| 4096 | 11.38 | 11.43 | 11.63 |

Not measured: other 512-expert models, which keep their current dispatch; rows above 4096, which stay on `topkGatingSoftmax`; short-prompt prefill end to end (every benchmark cell's prefill chunks were 5k-16k rows, so the eager <=4096 range rests on the microbenchmark); gfx942; anything outside TP8/EP1.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No user-facing docs change; the new env var is documented at its definition in `environ.py`, next to the other AITER switches.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

Draft for two reasons. The first is the aiter pin: this should land after, or together with, a bump to aiter#5334. The second is how it sits next to [#39986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39986). The two don't overlap today: #39986 gates on hidden size 4096 (Qwen3.5), this PR on 8192 (Qwen3.8). Extending #39986 to Qwen3.8 instead would be end-to-end neutral (+0.12% without MTP, -0.23% with it, both inside run-to-run spread). Under CUDA graphs the Triton kernel is ~0.5-0.75 us faster per call at <=1024 rows, but eager it is the slowest of the three, so it would need to stay behind a small-row gate. I'd keep both as they are unless you prefer one router per family. Happy to mark ready once the aiter pin includes aiter#5334.

title: [Spec] Add --speculative-draft-kv-ratio for all-SWA DFLASH drafts
body:
## Motivation

A DFLASH draft allocates one KV slot per target token, even when every draft layer is sliding-window attention and it can only ever read the last window of what it stores. On Qwen3.8-27B, for example, the draft pool is 8.6 GiB versus the target's 27.5 GiB, which represents a quarter of the KV budget held for rows outside the draft's 2048-token window.

We propose a flag to size the draft KV pool as a ratio of the target's capacity for all-SWA DFLASH drafts. For example, for Qwen3.8-27B on 1xH200 with a 5-layer all-SWA draft, draft window 2048, 8 running requests, and 0.8 mfs, we see:

| ratio | draft pool | target pool |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 (default) | 450,060 slots, 8.6 GiB | 450,060 tokens |
| 0.25 | 136,974 slots, 2.6 GiB | 547,899 tokens (+21.7%) |

## Modifications

- `--speculative-draft-kv-ratio` sizes the draft pool as a fraction of the target's token capacity. At the default of 1.0 nothing changes.
- Below 1.0 the draft's KV becomes the SWA side of the target allocator, which hands out a draft slot with each target slot and owns the full->SWA mapping.
- The radix cache takes its SWA component from the draft's window, so out-of-window draft slots are freed.
- Requires DFLASH. The window defaults to the draft's `sliding_window` unless `--speculative-draft-window-size` is set. Drafts with full-attention layers and targets with sliding-window layers are not supported yet. A ratio too small for the running requests is rejected with the smallest usable value.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/spec/dflash/test_dflash_draft_kv_ratio.py` on 1xH200 with Qwen3.8-27B and the `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` draft. Page size 1 and 64: 9 passed, with GSM8K run once since paging does not affect accuracy. GSM8K 0.98 with accept length 5.75.

`test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_pool_configurator.py` and `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`: 334 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: this reallocates KV between the target and draft pools and does not touch the compute path.

title: [DeepSeek-V4] Enable fused and overlapped mHC stats for small SM90 decode batches
body:
## Motivation

On SM90, DeepSeek-V4 previously used fused mHC stats only for `M=1`.
Small decode and target-verify graphs therefore ran:

```text
partial -> reduce -> split_sinkhorn
```

on the main stream for every layer. For small `M`, this work is independent
of the following attention or MoE computation and can be hidden on the
existing mHC stats stream.

## Modifications

- Add the opt-in JSON environment variable
  `SGLANG_OPT_MHC_STATS_OVERLAP_EXTRA_TOKEN_COUNTS`.
- For explicitly enabled SM90 decode/target-verify shapes with
  `1 < M <= 16`, use the existing fused stats path:

  ```text
  partial -> reduce_sinkhorn
  ```

- Submit attention stats before attention and FFN stats before MoE on the
  existing stats stream.
- Join the stats stream only immediately before `hc_post` consumes `post`
  and `comb`.

The default allowlist is empty, so existing SM90 behavior is unchanged unless
the optimization is explicitly enabled. `M=1`, prefill, Blackwell, and the
FP4 MoE operator are unchanged.

Suggested H20 setting:

```bash
export SGLANG_OPT_MHC_STATS_OVERLAP_EXTRA_TOKEN_COUNTS='[4,8,12,16]'
```

## Accuracy Tests

- Fused-vs-unfused stats numerics passed for `M=1/4/8/12/16` with
  `torch.testing.assert_close(rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-6)`.
- Maximum absolute error for every tested shape:
  `1.1920928955078125e-7`.
- Shape-policy checks passed:
  - Default: only the existing `M=1` path is enabled.
  - With `[4,8,12,16,20]`: `M=1/4/8/12/16` are enabled and `M=20`
    remains rejected by the hard cap.
- Existing mHC kernel test: 27 passed, 1 failed.
  - The failure is the existing BF16 tolerance boundary in
    `test_mhc_fused_post_pre_matches_unfused[False-17-7168]`.
  - One of 121,856 elements differs by `0.00390625` versus tolerance
    `0.002`; this test covers an unchanged operator.
- Full model accuracy evaluation was not run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Environment:

- Performance-tested base: `86cb4a0f97`
- 8x NVIDIA H20 (SM90, 97,871 MiB, 78 SMs/GPU)
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8/EP8
- PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, Triton 3.6.0, FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1
- `dsv4` attention, `flashinfer_mxfp4` MoE
- Full decode CUDA graphs; prefill CUDA graphs disabled

Method:

- Random token IDs, 100 input / 128 output tokens
- Concurrency `4/8/12/16`, `4 * concurrency` requests per case
- One warmup plus five measured runs per case and variant
- Order: baseline A1 -> optimized -> baseline A2, with a fresh server and
  graph capture for every variant
- Baseline is the median of 10 A1+A2 runs; optimized is the median of 5 runs

| Decode M | Baseline tok/s | Optimized tok/s | Throughput | Baseline TPOT ms | Optimized TPOT ms | TPOT |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 199.90 | 207.38 | +3.74% | 18.311 | 17.567 | -4.06% |
| 8 | 358.34 | 367.61 | +2.59% | 20.285 | 19.727 | -2.75% |
| 12 | 469.14 | 484.80 | +3.34% | 22.227 | 21.371 | -3.85% |
| 16 | 594.56 | 600.71 | +1.03% | 23.224 | 22.935 | -1.25% |

Baseline A1-to-A2 throughput drift was `+0.23%/+0.21%/+0.16%/+0.17%`.
Optimized throughput CV was at most `0.07%`.

TP0 trace at `M=8`:

| Path | Partial | Separate reduce | Separate Sinkhorn | Fused reduce+Sinkhorn |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline | 5,280 | 5,280 | 5,280 | 0 |
| Optimized | 5,280 | 160 | 160 | 5,120 |

- All 5,120 fused decode kernels overlapped work on another CUDA stream.
- Conservative interval overlap: 30.298 ms of 51.775 ms fused-kernel GPU
  time (58.5%).
- Frequent overlap partners include RMSNorm, FP8 quantization, W8A8 matmul,
  tiny-N GEMM, and router kernels.

The fused kernel is not faster in isolation. The E2E gain comes primarily
from moving dependency-independent stats ahead of attention/MoE and hiding
that work on the side stream, plus removing one launch and intermediate
handoff.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and static checks passed (`py_compile`, `git diff --check`, shell
  syntax check).
- [x] Existing relevant unit test was run; the one known BF16 boundary failure
  is documented above.
- [ ] Documentation update is not required for this opt-in experimental knob.
- [x] Kernel numerics, E2E speed benchmarks, and GPU traces are provided.
- [x] The change follows the existing model scheduling and environment-variable
  patterns.

title: [AMD] Reuse AITER DSA prefill metadata across layers
body:
# [AMD] Reuse AITER DSA prefill metadata across layers

**Depends on:** #39083

## Motivation

During an EXTEND forward pass, every DSA layer builds the same AITER work and
reduction metadata. The metadata depends on the sequences in the current
forward pass, not on the transformer layer. Building it again in every layer
adds unnecessary CPU and GPU work.

## Modifications

- Use the current `DSAMetadata` object to identify the forward pass.
- Build AITER metadata when the first DSA layer runs.
- Reuse that metadata in later layers of the same forward pass.
- Build new metadata when the `DSAMetadata` object changes.
- Keep the existing buffer size, dtype, and device checks.

Decode metadata is unchanged. The reused metadata belongs only to the current
forward pass.

## Accuracy Tests

Hardware: AMD MI355X.

The registered unit test checks that:

- one forward pass builds metadata once;
- a new forward pass builds new metadata.

The reused tensors also completed graph capture and two graph replays on
MI355X. The existing AITER BF16 and FP8 DSA prefill tests pass.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

For the tested long-context workload, AITER metadata generation decreased from
28.27 ms to 0.36 ms per 1,000 tokens.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and code-style checks pass.
- [x] Tests cover reuse within a forward pass and rebuilding for a new pass.
- [x] Graph capture and replay pass with reused metadata.
- [x] No user-facing documentation change is required.

title: [AMD] [GLM5] use tuned MXFP4 kernels for MLA absorbed BMM
body:
## Motivation

The absorbed K/V projections remain the largest dense-attention bottleneck in GLM-5.2 prefill because the existing path does not use the checkpoint’s MXFP4 weights. This change preserves those weights in MXFP4 and runs the absorbed BMMs on the matching gfx950 kernels.

## Modifications

- Preserve GLM MLA absorbed `w_kc` / `w_vc` weights and scales in packed MXFP4 behind `SGLANG_USE_MXFP4_MLA_BMM=1`.
- Dispatch A16WFP4 K/V BMMs with `NUM_KSPLIT=1`.
- Use `BLOCK_SIZE_K=64` for GLM K-up (`K=192`).
- Use `BLOCK_SIZE_M=128`, `BLOCK_SIZE_K=128` for V-up when `M>256`; preserve AITER's small-M decode buckets.
- Route the current `MLA_ROCM` K/V path through the tuned dispatch helpers.
- Write V-up output directly in batch-major layout.

## Accuracy Tests

| Test | Pre-tuning | This PR |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K, 20 examples | 0.950 | 0.950 |
| Focused unit tests | — | 14/14 |

## Speed Benchmarks

GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4 MI355X, 8192 input / 1024 output, `REPS=3`.

A. Pre-tuning A16WFP4:

| concurrency | TTFT (ms) | ITL (ms) | E2EL (ms) | output tok/s |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 996.05 | 11.825 | 13386.47 | 305.49 |
| 8 | 1610.50 | 13.583 | 16449.63 | 497.61 |
| 16 | 2871.90 | 15.943 | 21346.01 | 765.34 |
| 32 | 5405.12 | 19.817 | 30273.44 | 1081.76 |
| 64 | 10497.72 | 26.803 | 47538.85 | 1379.12 |

B. Tuned A16WFP4 (delta vs A):

| concurrency | TTFT (ms) | delta | ITL (ms) | delta | E2EL (ms) | delta | output tok/s | delta |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 1001.84 | +0.58% | 11.820 | -0.04% | 13357.40 | -0.22% | 306.13 | +0.21% |
| 8 | 1578.35 | -2.00% | 13.577 | -0.04% | 16397.56 | -0.32% | 499.28 | +0.34% |
| 16 | 2805.58 | -2.31% | 15.953 | +0.06% | 21287.72 | -0.27% | 769.49 | +0.54% |
| 32 | 5291.87 | -2.10% | 19.827 | +0.05% | 30107.75 | -0.55% | 1087.52 | +0.53% |
| 64 | 10344.29 | -1.46% | 26.823 | +0.07% | 47212.48 | -0.69% | 1388.12 | +0.65% |

**Baseline** = `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260804`, plus these 7 PRs
PR #30575: Triton sparse MLA prefill/decode
PR #30715: fused indexer query Hadamard + FP8 quant
PR #30808: gfx950 dense-MHA short-context fallback
PR #31323: fused shared-expert append
PR #31324: skip unnecessary dense-regime decode indexer work
PR #33602: FP8 dense GEMMs
PR #33620: pre-tuning A16WFP4 absorbed K/V BMM

**This PR** = Baseline + M128/K128 V-BMM tuning

title: [Qwen 3.8 Flash Next] Add sm120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell) support
body:
#36497 merged into `main` through #37500 on 2026-09-08, so this branch now sits on `main` (rebased at `9c8d4641f`) with no external dependency. The commits listed below are the whole diff.

On sm120 the model from #36497 does not serve as written. The QSA sparse decode path is gated on `is_sm100_supported()` and falls back to a packed gather plus a FlashAttention varlen call; the QSA MQA indexer scoring runs TileLang with a silent torch fallback; and the JIT modules are built during graph capture. The PLE host-load path also performs a wasted row-zero read on non-owner ranks (correct output, unnecessary PCIe traffic). This PR adds the sm120 paths: a direct-paged Triton sparse decode with a fused split-K merge, Triton MQA scoring, a fused small-row NVFP4 MoE kernel in the in-tree CUDA JIT, sm120 launch geometry for the hyperconnection mix, tuned FP8 fused-MoE configs for this GPU, NUMA-interleaved pinning for the offloaded PLE table, and correctness fixes for the items above. With this branch both checkpoints serve with CUDA graphs and NEXTN speculative decoding: FP8 at TP4/EP4 and NVFP4 at TP2/EP1.

## Motivation

sm120 is the workstation and consumer Blackwell architecture (RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090, GB10 at sm_121). The QSA decode kernels this model depends on exist only for sm100: trtllm-gen has no sm120 cubins, so the gate is closed and the fallback gathers the selected tokens into a packed buffer before every attention call. Two day-0 reports describe the same gap: #36531 (the QSA fallback selects the pip FA4 path on sm120 and fails at the MLIR build) and the GB10 comment on #36497 asking to widen the sm100 gate. #36532 (FlashInfer GDN wanted fp32 state on sm120 while flag validation accepted bf16) is covered on `main` itself now, which converts the prefill state to fp32 on sm12x and ships the pooled bf16 decode kernel with FlashInfer 0.6.18, so the GDN commit this PR carried before the rebase is dropped.

Widening the gate was measured and is not the right fix: `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` with `backend="auto"` routes compute capability below 10 to XQA, and forcing `backend="trtllm-gen"` fails at `fmhaRunner.cuh:37: Unsupported architecture`. XQA cannot address the paged pool directly, so it pays a page-aligned gather that costs more than the attention itself at large batch (measured below). The contribution here is a direct-paged kernel that skips the gather at large batch and splits along the top-k axis to reach XQA-class latency at small batch.

The irregular sparse-attention and gather paths are Triton: sparse decode, MQA scoring and the PLE gather have shape-dynamic index expansion where the compile keys are the fixed head and page tiles, not the sequence lengths. The quantized MoE GEMM is an in-tree sgl-kernel CUDA JIT kernel because it is a fixed-layout `mma.sync.kind::mxf4nvf4` grouped GEMM with the architecture and model shape as compile keys. FlashInfer stays in place everywhere it owns the full production contract on sm100, including the NVFP4 MoE above 16 tokens, which remains the fallback.

## Modifications

Eleven commits, oldest first (hashes omitted; see `git log`).

| Subject | What it does |
|---|---|
| [QSA] Add direct-paged Triton sparse decode on sm120 | Reads the selected tokens straight from the paged KV pool through the request table. `SGLANG_QSA_DECODE_BACKEND` selects `auto`/`triton`/`flash_attn`/`trtllm`; `auto` picks Triton on sm120 (excluding sm121) and trtllm-gen where it exists. The MQA counterpart `SGLANG_QSA_MQA_BACKEND` accepts `auto`/`tilelang`/`triton`/`torch`. |
| [sm120] Fix serving fallbacks and graph capture | Masks the PLE host load for non-owner ranks, makes the MQA path recoverable through `SGLANG_QSA_MQA_BACKEND` instead of dropping to torch silently, prewarms the Qwen4Exp JIT kernels before graph capture. |
| [MoE] Add tuned fused MoE configs for RTX PRO 6000 | Triton 3.7.1 FP8 blockwise configs for E=64/128/256 at N=640, the EP8/EP4/EP2 layouts of this model. |
| [QSA] Add split-K sparse decode for small batches | Two-stage split along the KV axis with the 12 grouped query heads packed into M; the split count is a static function of query rows so graph capture stays valid. |
| [QSA] Add Triton MQA scoring on sm120 | Packed-prefill and direct-paged decode/verify scoring for the indexer; default on sm120, sm100 keeps TileLang. |
| [QSA] Fuse split-K merge into sparse decode | The last program per row merges the partial softmax states with a graph-safe counter reset, removing the separate reduction launch. |
| [PLE] Interleave the pinned table across NUMA nodes | Allocates the offloaded PLE table with `mmap` + `numa_interleave_memory` + `cudaHostRegister` instead of `pin_memory=True` so it does not exhaust the NUMA node local to the GPU. Goes through the `allocate_ple_host_table` backend switch that `main` gained with the file-backed table (pinned branch only; the mapping is read back with `ple_pinned_mapping`). Opt-out env provided. |
| [HC] Tune sm120 Triton geometry by row bucket | Picks grid and tile from the static row count (1, 2-16, 17-64) on sm120; other architectures keep the previous choice. |
| [MoE] Add fused small-row NVFP4 kernel for sm120 | One cooperative JIT launch per layer for 1-16 routed tokens: W4A4 quantize, FC1, SiLU-mul with group-16 requantization, grouped FC2, routing-weight finalize, all in checkpoint layout. Falls back to FlashInfer CUTLASS when cooperative launch or occupancy is not provable; above 16 tokens CUTLASS is unchanged. |
| [QSA] Bound sparse indices and use 64-bit KV addresses | Prefill kernels bound the selected index by the request's own extent; decode, compaction and decode MQA compute slot-times-stride products in 64 bit. |
| [PLE] Select the prefetch buffer from capture state | Asks the driver for the capture state instead of trusting a runner flag that some graph runners never set; keeps the mmap reachable until device work finishes. The prewarm reads the resolved graph config and draft width from the runtime context bags, since the worker's record only carries the raw flag value (found by @detain while running the stack on `main`). |

New environment variables, all declared in `environ.py` with defaults that preserve non-sm120 behavior: `SGLANG_QSA_DECODE_BACKEND`, `SGLANG_QSA_MQA_BACKEND`, `SGLANG_PLE_OFFLOAD_NUMA_INTERLEAVE`, and `SGLANG_NVFP4_MOE_SM120` (a kill switch for the small-row kernel, default on; turning it off restores the FlashInfer CUTLASS path everywhere).

New registered tests: `kernels/ops/qsa/test_qsa_sparse_decode_triton.py`, `kernels/ops/qsa/test_qsa_mqa_triton.py`, `kernels/ops/qsa/test_qsa_sparse_index_bounds.py`, `kernels/ops/moe/test_nvfp4_moe_sm120.py`, `unit/models/test_qwen4_ple_prefetch_buffers.py`, `unit/utils/test_interleaved_pinned_table.py`, `unit/layers/moe/test_nvfp4_smallm_dispatch.py` (CPU), an extension of `unit/layers/moe/test_fused_moe_triton_config.py` (CPU), plus additions to the existing QSA, PLE offload, PLE table, hc_mix and cuda graph tests. The three kernel benchmarks live under `test/manual/kernels/benchmark/` (they need an sm120 GPU and, for the MoE one, local checkpoint tensors, so they are not registered CI jobs).

## Environment

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| CPU | 2x AMD EPYC 9355 |
| GPU | 8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition 96 GB, sm_120a |
| Driver / CUDA | 595.71.05 / 13.2 |
| torch / Triton / FlashInfer | 2.13.0+cu130 / 3.7.1 / 0.6.17 |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04.4, kernel 6.8 |

PCIe workstation host, no NVLink; measured GDDR7 bandwidth 1.459 TB/s; two unequal NUMA nodes (257.6 GB and 128.9 GB), which is why the NUMA commit exists.

## Accuracy Tests

Every serving and accuracy number below was measured at the branch tip. Sampling for `sglang.test.run_eval`: T=1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, max tokens 32768, thinking on. Server: CUDA graphs, NEXTN 3 steps / 4 draft tokens, PLE offloaded to host.

| Task | n | Checkpoint and layout | Score |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| GSM8K | 1314 | FP8, TP4/EP4 | 98.10% |
| GSM8K | 1314 | NVFP4, TP2/EP1 | 97.87% |
| AIME26, reference protocol (8 passes, 131k max tokens) | 30 | FP8, TP4/EP4 | 96.25% |
| GPQA | 198 | FP8, TP4/EP4 | 80.81% |
| GPQA | 198 | NVFP4, TP2/EP1 | 78.28% |
| IFEval | 541 | FP8, TP4/EP4 | prompt strict 0.9316, inst strict 0.9508 |
| IFEval | 541 | NVFP4, TP2/EP1 | prompt strict 0.9057, inst strict 0.9365 |

The NVFP4 model card publishes 98.75% for AIME26 under the 8-pass protocol; the 96.25% above is the FP8 checkpoint under the same protocol (per-pass spread 93.3 to 100; repeated 8-pass runs during development landed between 96.3 and 98.3). Multimodal observations exist but their protocols are not all matched to published ones, so they are not claimed as comparisons.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### QSA sparse decode

Isolated kernel benchmark at the model's full-attention shape: 24 query heads, 2 KV heads, head dim 256, bf16, 2051 selected-token slots per row, page size 64 for the gathered paths, ragged valid counts. CUDA events around the complete call, 10 warmups.

| Query rows | flash_attn packed fallback (ms) | XQA end to end (ms) | XQA kernel alone (ms) | Triton direct paged (ms) | + split-K (ms) | + fused merge, head (ms) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.0633 | 0.0377 | 0.0181 | 0.0901 | 0.0363 | 0.0318 |
| 4 | 0.0772 | 0.0374 | 0.0183 | 0.0912 | 0.0363 | 0.0314 |
| 16 | 0.0767 | 0.0417 | 0.0184 | 0.0917 | 0.0367 | 0.0361 |
| 64 | 0.5489 | 0.5476 | 0.1848 | 0.1985 | 0.1991 | 0.1992 |

The final column carries a 3-4 us cost at small rows over the pre-review revision of this kernel; it combines a defensive reinitialization of the split-K reduction generation with a retuned split schedule, and still beats every fallback at every row count. At 64 rows the split count is 1, so the last two columns both run the non-split kernel and their near-identical times are expected. The XQA column is what widening the sm100 gate would select: at 64 rows it spends 0.363 ms of 0.548 in the gather, and its 1-16 row numbers are optimistic because the gathered working set stays L2-resident across benchmark iterations. Numerics against an fp32 reference stay at the bf16 output-rounding floor (max abs 0.000477 to 0.007577 across 1-64 rows); eager calls are bitwise reproducible and captured graphs replay with zero drift. The split-K path is clean under Compute Sanitizer memcheck, initcheck, racecheck and synccheck with guard bands, across capture and replay.

### QSA MQA indexer scoring

Decode scores a 32k source sequence (8192 compressed keys); prefill is one causal packed sequence. CUDA events, 2 warmups.

| Point | Query rows | torch (us) | TileLang (us) | Triton (us) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| decode batch 1 | 1 | 95.7 | 16.6 | 17.7 |
| decode batch 16 | 16 | 130.3 | 15.5 | 16.6 |
| decode batch 64 | 64 | 727.1 | 37.9 | 29.4 |
| prefill 8k | 8192 | 1297.3 | 132.7 | 73.5 |
| prefill 32k | 32768 | 21841.9 | 3221.6 | 1083.4 |

TileLang keeps a 2-4 us edge at decode batch 1-16; Triton wins at batch 64 and both prefill points and removes both the third DSL and the silent torch fallback from the sm120 path. Max abs logit error against torch is 2.4e-6 and all selected top-k sets matched exactly, including rows below the 512-block budget.

### NVFP4 small-row routed MoE

Layer 0 real checkpoint tensors, TP2 rank 0, 512 local experts, hidden 2560, rank-local intermediate 320, top-k 10. One MoE call per captured graph, 30 repeats, 256 MiB L2 flush per sample.

| Tokens | FlashInfer CUTLASS median (us) | This PR median (us) | Median change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 72.1 | 45.1 | 37.4% faster |
| 4 | 111.6 | 84.5 | 24.3% faster |
| 16 | 216.1 | 195.1 | 9.7% faster |

Both GEMMs stay W4A4 group 16; relative L2 error against fp32-dequantized weights matches FlashInfer to the third decimal (0.1375 vs 0.1377 at 16 tokens). Graph capture replays all three shapes with stable workspace addresses.

### Hyperconnection mix and FP8 MoE configs

hc_mix: a captured graph of 97 mix calls with distinct weights runs 5.0/5.4/20.8% faster at 1/16/64 rows (13.93 us per call at one row); max abs error is unchanged and 10,000 replays show no drift. The tuned FP8 fused-MoE configs reduce the isolated TP4/EP4 chain from 37.05 to 24.04 us at one token and 0.5-3.3% at 16-2048 tokens; the same chain measures 22.94 us against 49.90 us on FlashInfer CUTLASS per-tensor FP8 and 57.39 us on the CuTe-DSL sm12x grouped MoE from flashinfer PR 4720. E=512/N=160 (TP4 without EP) is rejected by the FP8 quantization layer before any config selection: the per-partition gate-up output size 160 is not divisible by the weight quantization block size 128, so no config exists for it.

### End to end serving

`sglang.bench_serving`, random dataset, ISL 1024 / OSL 512, CUDA graphs on, PLE offloaded to pinned host memory. Each row issues more prompts than its concurrency window, so median TTFT includes scheduler queueing for the requests beyond the window: NEXTN drains the window roughly twice as fast at concurrency 16, which is why its TTFT drops there, while at concurrency 64 the draft-extend prefill overhead dominates and TTFT rises.

FP8, TP4/EP4:

| Concurrency | Spec | Output tok/s | TPOT med (ms) | TTFT med (ms) | Accept len |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | none | 115.8 | 8.41 | 101.1 | |
| 16 | none | 873.8 | 16.27 | 1066.7 | |
| 64 | none | 1682.2 | 32.42 | 2719.9 | |
| 1 | NEXTN 3/4 | 220.6 | 4.40 | 109.9 | 2.92 |
| 16 | NEXTN 3/4 | 1111.4 | 12.47 | 216.9 | 2.98 |
| 64 | NEXTN 3/4 | 1754.2 | 25.01 | 3836.6 | 3.05 |

NVFP4, TP2/EP1 (two GPUs matching the four-GPU FP8 numbers is expected here: decode is weight-bandwidth-bound, NVFP4 halves the streamed weight bytes, and tensor-parallel traffic over PCIe scales poorly, so fewer ranks lose little):

| Concurrency | Spec | Output tok/s | TPOT med (ms) | TTFT med (ms) | Accept len |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | none | 124.7 | 7.83 | 95.2 | |
| 16 | none | 855.7 | 16.84 | 974.8 | |
| 64 | none | 1666.7 | 33.18 | 2552.4 | |
| 1 | NEXTN 3/4 | 216.0 | 4.56 | 101.8 | 2.94 |
| 16 | NEXTN 3/4 | 1069.2 | 13.20 | 194.5 | 3.00 |
| 64 | NEXTN 3/4 | 1703.1 | 25.22 | 3711.8 | 3.02 |

Reference point at the #36497 head `73a255206` on the same host: FP8 TP4/EP4, eager, no MTP, concurrency 1, 17.4 output tok/s at 57.21 ms median TPOT; a baseline for "it serves at all", not a like-for-like graph comparison.

The NUMA commit is what lets the NVFP4 NEXTN configuration start with the PLE table offloaded: `pin_memory=True` put both TP2 ranks' 47.7 GiB on the 128.9 GB node local to GPUs 4-7, the node went into reclaim and the driver failed with Xid 31 MMU faults at a host address during the draft load. Interleaved, each rank spreads 23.8 GiB evenly across both nodes and startup completes; single-stream throughput is about 2 percent below a GPU-resident table, the expected cost of PCIe reads.

## Rebase notes (2026-09-16)

Rebased from the #36497 head onto `main` at `9c8d4641f`. Besides the GDN commit drop and the PLE allocation change described above, the QSA tests sit in `test/registered/kernels/ops/qsa/` following the test layout consolidation (#39966), and the tree is formatted with ruff-format as the pre-commit config now asks. CPU verification on the rebased tree: the touched CPU suites pass (61 tests, 51 subtests). GPU check of the rebased tree on a DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121) on 2026-09-17: file-backed PLE boots and serves with defaults, with the Triton QSA kernels forced on, and with NEXTN (table in the comments). The exact-sm120 numbers above are from before the rebase; @detain reports the pre-rebase stack running on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Workstation Edition together with #37275, #38144, #38209 and #36644 (see the #37275 thread). An sm120 re-run of the rebased tree follows when a card frees up.

## Not covered

- **FP8 KV cache.** `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` still asserts in the QSA path (#36545); neither checkpoint requests it. Separate PR.
- **QSA prefill.** Decode is direct-paged; prefix and chunked prefill still gather more than they need. Separate PR.
- **RealWorldQA.** Under the official Qwen3-VL protocol (exact prompt, 602K-4M pixel smart resize, thinking recipe, rule-plus-judge extraction, all 765 items) scores 86.4-87.2 against the published 88.5; runs with NEXTN off and with rejection sampling land in the same band, so speculative decoding is excluded as the cause and the residual gap is still being investigated as an evaluation-protocol or serving-numerics question, not claimed as a kernel result.
- **CI coverage.** The registered kernel and GPU unit tests use the `base-b-kernel-unit` suites, as the test taxonomy check asks, and those run on H100/B200/H200 runners, so the sm120-gated tests skip there; the architecture-independent parts do run. The `1-gpu-small` runner is a 5090 (SM120), but no kernel-unit suite is defined on it. If maintainers want the sm120 paths exercised in CI, a `base-b-kernel-unit-test-1-gpu-small` suite would do it and I can wire the registrations to it.
- **Other sm120 parts.** Only RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition was measured. RTX 5090 (sm_120) should take the same paths but is untested here. GB10 (sm_121) keeps upstream defaults everywhere: the backend auto-selection does not route it onto the new Triton QSA paths (the env vars allow an explicit opt-in), and the small-row NVFP4 kernel refuses it and falls back to CUTLASS.
- **Adoption instead of duplication.** sglang #28125, #36043, #34827 and flashinfer #4720/#4718 overlap with the FP8 MoE and NVFP4 GEMM area. The tuned Triton FP8 configs here are an interim path; when one of those lands with the checkpoint's scale format and wins on the full routed chain, it should replace them.
