title: [XPU] Enable fused QK-norm + RoPE for Qwen3-MoE
body:
## Motivation

Qwen3-MoE already has a fused QK-norm + RoPE path, but the gate in `Qwen3MoeAttention.__init__` requires `_is_cuda`. On XPU this falls back to two RMSNorm launches plus a separate RoPE launch per layer, even though `sgl-kernel-xpu` already ships the kernel AOT as `torch.ops.sgl_kernel.fused_qk_norm_rope` ([sgl-kernel-xpu#97](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu/pull/97)), with the same call signature as the CUDA wrapper.

This enables that kernel on XPU, cutting the q/k-norm + RoPE stage from 3 launches per layer to 1.

Related prior art: [#37323](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37323) (unmerged) does the equivalent wiring for another model.

## Modifications

Single file, `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py`:

- `_has_xpu_fused_qk_norm_rope()` — `lru_cache`d probe for the op, so older
  `sgl-kernel-xpu` wheels fall back to the split path instead of failing.
- `use_fused_qk_norm_rope_xpu` — gated on `--enable-fused-qk-norm-rope`, same as CUDA, and reusing the existing `compatible_with_fused_qk_norm_rope` check (`head_dim` in {64, 128, 256}, not `MRotaryEmbedding`).
- An XPU branch in `apply_qk_norm_rope` calling the op in-place, then splitting
  QKV. bf16 and fp16, matching the CPU branch's dtype set.

Kept opt-in behind the existing flag to match CUDA. The measurements below (+4-5% throughput, no accuracy change) would support making it an XPU default instead, as the CPU path already does implicitly. The existing `--enable-fused-qk-norm-rope` flag has no CUDA-only validation, so it is already reachable on XPU.

Subtle things to note: for non-YaRN configs `compute_yarn_parameters` returns `factor=1.0, low=0, high=0`. Passing
`low == high` would divide by zero in a YaRN ramp, but the SYCL kernel branches on `factor != 1.0f` and ignores the bounds entirely, so this is safe — the same values the CUDA path already passes.

KV-cache handling needs no change: when the fused path runs, `_used_fused_qk_norm_rope_last_call` makes `must_save_kv` true in `forward_core`, so `self.attn` performs the write that the fallback would otherwise do via `fused_set_kv_buffer`. That logic is device-agnostic.

## Accuracy Tests

**Kernel-level equivalence** against the split path, Qwen3-30B-A3B dims (`head_dim=128`, 32/4 heads, `theta=1e6`), over 1/7/128/1024 tokens:

| dtype | max abs diff | relative L2 |
|---|---|---|
| bfloat16 | 0.031 | 2.7e-3 |
| float16 | 0.004 | 3.5e-4 |

`v` is bit-exact, since the kernel does not touch it.

**End-to-end**, GSM8K 1319 examples (1314 scored), greedy, Qwen3-30B-A3B, TP=4.
Both arms verified via `/get_server_info` to have actually resolved
`enable_fused_qk_norm_rope` as intended before running:

| | baseline | fused |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K | 0.9475 | 0.9429 |

Records came out in identical order across arms, so they can be paired per
question:

| | count |
|---|---|
| both correct | 1223 |
| both wrong | 53 |
| baseline right, fused wrong | 22 |
| fused right, baseline wrong | 16 |

38 discordant pairs, net −6, **McNemar exact two-sided p = 0.42** — not significant. Flips are near-symmetric in both directions, which is the signature of bf16 rounding perturbing borderline chain-of-thought generations rather than a
correctness defect. 5.4% of extracted answers differ at all, expected for greedy decoding under a small numeric perturbation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**q/k-norm + RoPE stage**, per TP rank over 40 profiled decode steps, Qwen3-30B-A3B TP=4 on 4x Intel Arc Pro B60, launches / device ms:

| component | baseline | fused |
|---|---|---|
| q/k RMSNorm (3 instantiations) | 3,880 / 79.62 ms | 40 / 0.59 ms |
| RoPE (`FusedRopeCacheKernel`) | 1,920 / 23.19 ms | 0 / 0.00 ms |
| `FusedQKNormRopeKernel` | 0 / 0.00 ms | 1,920 / 56.66 ms |
| **stage total** | **5,800 / 102.81 ms** | **1,960 / 57.25** |

**−66% launches, −44% device ms.** Isolated microbenchmark of the stage shows 2.0x (8192 tokens) to 4.5x (8 tokens).

**End-to-end**, `bench_serving`, input 1024 / output 256, mean of two independent runs (baseline run-to-run spread ~1%):

| conc | baseline | fused | delta | TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 21.3 tok/s | 22.2 tok/s | +3.9% | 46.5 → 44.8 ms |
| 8 | 157.9 tok/s | 164.5 tok/s | +4.2% | 49.1 → 47.1 ms |
| 32 |554.9 tok/s | 575.5 tok/s | +3.7%| 54.9 → 52.9 ms |

**~4% output throughput** with TPOT down ~4%, consistent at every concurrency and reproducible across runs.

  Most of the end-to-end gain is indirect. The stage is a small share of device time, so cutting it saves only ~45 ms on its own. But `oneccl_allreduce_pcie` dominates at TP=4 over PCIe -- 2,010 ms of 5,713 ms rank-0 device time (~35.2%) -- and it is a spin-wait kernel, so its duration is mostly time spent waiting for peer ranks rather than moving data. Removing a launch per layer per forward cuts host-side submission work, so every rank reaches each collective sooner and the peers wait less: so allreduce falls to 1,893 ms in fused case. That is where the bulk of the improvement will show up in the e2e throughput. and total allreduce time summed across the four ranks is reduced from 5,961 → 5,636 ms. (−5.5%) 

cc: @rahulvijayaraghavan @rbabukv

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

No new unit test: kernel correctness is already covered upstream by `tests/test_fused_qk_norm_rope.py` in `sgl-kernel-xpu`, and a model-level test here would require the 30B checkpoint. Happy to add one if reviewers prefer.

title: Reduce decode bootstrap latency with request-owned speculative KV
body:
## Problem

Optimistic prefill reduces decode bootstrap latency by overlapping decode-side allocation with prefill. Under `write_through` HiCache, however, speculative KV follows the normal publication path before the bootstrap result is known, making ownership unsafe across retries and aborts.

## Changed

- Keep pending-bootstrap KV request-owned and out of the shared radix cache.
- Advance multi-chunk requests without publishing speculative KV.
- Release retry, bootstrap failure, and abort paths without inserting unfinished KV or releasing it twice.
```
before:
Request
  → Decode bootstrap and KV preallocation
  → Wait for decode readiness
  → Prefill computation
  → Publish KV to radix cache and async write-through L2
  → Transfer KV to decode
  → First token

after:
Request
  ├─ Decode bootstrap and KV preallocation
  └─ Prefill computation
       → Keep KV request-owned and unpublished while bootstrap is pending
       → Bootstrap succeeds: publish once and async write-through L2 and transfer to decode
       → Bootstrap fails/retries/aborts: release unpublished KV and requeue
```
## Validated


DeepSeek-V4-Pro was tested twice on MI355X with 1P1D TP8/DP8, concurrency 256.

- Baseline:  [InferenceX action 33837253408](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/33837253408).
- Basline+this PR : the same code and configuration + this PR with  `--optimistic-prefill-attempts 2`. 
(https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/34666940659)

| Metric | Baseline | Optimized | Change |
|--------|----------|-----------|--------|
| TTFT mean | 19.433s | 15.087s | -22.36% |
| TTFT p50 | 13.359s | 10.833s | -18.91% |
| TTFT p90 | 38.542s | 27.873s | -27.68% |
| TTFT p95 | 49.845s | 37.629s | -24.51% |
| Total throughput/GPU | 38,966.51 tok/s | 41,201.55 tok/s | +5.74% |
| Output throughput/GPU | 296.06 tok/s | 309.44 tok/s | +4.52% |

title: [Feature] Support Lark grammars with XGrammar
body:
## Motivation

XGrammar 0.2.7 provides `GrammarCompiler.compile_lark`, but SGLang currently sends the existing `ebnf` grammar input only to `compile_grammar`. As a result, XGrammar cannot accept Lark syntax through the established grammar API.

## Modifications

- Pin XGrammar to the stable 0.2.7 release.
- Keep the existing `ebnf` sampling parameter and public API unchanged.
- In the XGrammar backend, compile as EBNF first and fall back to `compile_lark` when EBNF parsing fails.
- Preserve the resolved grammar format in compilation statistics and report both parser errors when neither format is valid.
- Document that XGrammar accepts Lark syntax through the existing `ebnf` parameter.
- Add focused XGrammar unit coverage for EBNF compilation, Lark fallback, real compilation with XGrammar 0.2.7, and invalid input.

## Accuracy Tests

The tests include real compilation of both `root ::= "yes" | "no"` and `start: "yes" | "no"` through `XGrammarGrammarBackend.dispatch_ebnf` with XGrammar 0.2.7.

Not applicable. Existing valid EBNF inputs retain the same compilation and decoding path. Lark compilation occurs only after the EBNF parser rejects the input.

title: [Diffusion] Preserve per-sample rollout trajectories across multi-output merge
body:
## Motivation

Reported in #34000 (Bug 1). **This is a silent numerical corruption bug** — no exception, no warning; per-sample rollout log-probs are simply wrong.

A `num_outputs_per_prompt=K` request runs as K per-output forwards, each producing its own `rollout_trajectory_data` from its own `x_T` slice and per-step SDE noise. Two sites collapse those K distinct trajectories into K copies of output 0's:

1. `GPUWorker._merge_expanded_singletons` keeps the trajectory of the **first** per-output batch only:

   ```python
   if (
       merged.rollout_trajectory_data is None
       and output_batch.rollout_trajectory_data is not None
   ):
       merged.rollout_trajectory_data = output_batch.rollout_trajectory_data
   ```

   Note the asymmetry: `output`, `trajectory_latents`, `noise_pred` and `trajectory_decoded` are all concatenated along the batch dim in `_finalize_expanded_parts`. Only `rollout_trajectory_data` is treated as a singleton.

2. `DiffGenerator._result_common` slices `samples` and `metrics` per `output_index` but hands the whole trajectory to **every** `GenerationResult`.

So every sample in the group carries output 0's `rollout_log_probs`. For GRPO-style post-training the per-sample log-probs become identical, the mean-zero advantages cancel, and the gradient vanishes — reward stays flat with `grad_norm ≈ 0`.

Both entry points into the merge are affected, including the sequential path added in #30683: `_forward_group` and `_collect_sequential_outputs` both call `_merge_expanded_output_batches`.

**This also fixes `rollout_api` (the actively maintained rollout interface) without touching it.** `_slice_rollout_trajectory_for_sample` already slices per-sample, but every slice is guarded on `shape[0] == batch_size`. Against the collapsed `[1, ...]` tensor that guard doesn't match, so `_extract_single_sample_tensor` returns the tensor **whole** and the slicing silently no-ops. That existing code already expects a `[K, ...]` trajectory — this PR makes the merge actually produce one.

## Modifications

- `gpu_worker.py`: collect `rollout_trajectory_data` into `_ExpandedOutputParts` and concatenate it along dim 0 in `_finalize_expanded_parts`, alongside the other per-output tensors. New module-level `_concat_rollout_trajectory_data` handles the nested structure; `timesteps` / `sigmas` / `denoising_env` describe the shared schedule and conditioning, so they come from the first output.
- `diffusion_generator.py`: `_result_common` narrows the grouped trajectory to the requested `output_index`, keep-dim, so a grouped result carries the same `[1, ...]` shape as an unexpanded one.

`output` dim 0 and the trajectory dim 0 are produced by the same per-output loop, so they agree by construction for every K — which is what makes `rollout_api`'s existing `shape[0] == batch_size` guard start matching.

**One deliberate behavior change:** when only *some* outputs in a group carry a trajectory, the merge now yields `None` rather than the single present row. Labeling one sample's trajectory as the whole group's is the same broadcast bug in a different disguise, so dropping it is preferable to misaligning it. Happy to change this if you'd prefer it preserved.

## Accuracy Test

Observed with K=3, T=4, per-output values tagged 1/2/3:

```
                          merged log_probs   result[0]  result[1]  result[2]
before                        (1, 4)             1          1          1     <- all output 0
after                         (3, 4)             1          2          3
```

`rollout_api` path, with `_slice_rollout_trajectory_for_sample` unchanged:

```
collapsed [1,...] merge (before)  -> per-sample values ['1','1','1']  ALL IDENTICAL
concatenated [K,...] merge (after) -> per-sample values ['1','2','3']  DISTINCT
```

Unchanged paths, checked before/after: K=1 trajectory shape `(1,4)`; non-rollout requests `None`; `output` tensor merge `(3,3)`.

**Verification caveat, please read:** I could not run the pytest suite against `main` — the sglang install I have is `0.5.12.post1`, whose tree predates the current layout, and my only box is a CPU node where importing `sglang.multimodal_gen` off network storage takes >10 minutes. The numbers above come from extracting the real functions under test from both `main` and this branch via `git show` and executing them side by side against stubs. **The added unit test has not been executed under a real sglang install** — please treat it as unvalidated and let CI be the first real run.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code with pre-commit hooks (isort / black / ruff clean on the changed files)
- [x] Add unit tests (`test_multi_output_rollout_trajectory.py`) — but see the verification caveat above
- [x] Linked the tracking issue (#34000)

title: [NPU] Fuse DeepSeek-V4 decode compression metadata updates
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 prepares decode compression metadata through several separate PyTorch operations before each NPUGraph replay. This PR fuses these updates into one Triton kernel to reduce dispatch overhead.

## Modifications

- Add the fused implementation to the existing `dsv4/metadata_kernel.py`, covering C4/C128 cache location copying and tail clearing, compression boundary detection and stable position compaction, and `start_pos` and `seqused` updates.
- Update existing graph buffers in place on the current stream, with kernel warmup before graph capture.
- Enable fusion by default through `SGLANG_NPU_DSV4_FUSED_DECODE_METADATA`. Setting it to `0` restores the original PyTorch implementation.
- Add tests covering compression boundaries, padding, missing locations, strided inputs, buffer reuse, and graph consumption.

## Accuracy Tests

- Four CPU tests passed using an isolated source harness.
- Two NPU tests were added for kernel correctness and graph replay with stream dependencies; these were skipped locally because NPU hardware was unavailable.
- Model-level accuracy evaluation has not been run.
- Ruff checks, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

With NPUGraph enabled and 8 concurrent decoding requests, the median server-reported decode throughput improved by 1.72%.

| Metric | Fusion disabled | Fusion enabled | Improvement |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Median decode throughput (tokens/s) | 289.38 | 294.35 | +1.72% |

Computed from the captured server logs, using all samples with `#running-req=8`: 8 samples with fusion disabled and 14 with fusion enabled.

title: [MiniMax-M3][AMD] Fix EAGLE3 TARGET_VERIFY on MI350/355 + AITER MXFP8 MoE
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-M3 EAGLE3 on gfx950 (MI350X/MI355X) server starts with PR #36659 but output quality is bad.

This PR includes #36659 and adds gfx950 commits on top. It is kept separate as it touches another architecture.

This PR adds gfx950 fix for **MXFP8** MoE clamped-SwiGLU and MiniMax Quark loader mapping. (The analogous **Quark W4A4 MXFP4** clamped-SwiGLU fix is tracked separately in #34540.)


## Modifications

1. **`fp8.py`**: MXFP8 AITER MoE clamped-SwiGLU — `_aiter_clamped_swiglu_limit()`, `_aiter_runner_moe_config()` rewrite `silu`→`swiglu` when clamp limit > 0; pass `swiglu_limit` in `AiterMoeQuantInfo`. (Same *pattern* as #34540, implemented for the FP8/MXFP8 path only.)

2. **`loader.py`**: Quark `packed_modules_mapping`: `"index_qkv_proj": ["index_q_proj", "index_k_proj"]` only (MiniMax index value disabled).

Requires `SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=0` for MiniMax interleaved gate/up layout. Baseline serving on gfx950 also needs `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1` to avoid a ~65 GB legacy AITER workspace OOM at `--mem-fraction-static 0.85` when using aiter attention.

**Quark W4A4 MXFP4 MoE:** use #34540 — do not land duplicate changes in this PR.

## Validation

`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8` with `Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3` on **4× MI350X (gfx950)**, ROCm 7.2.0, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x-20260827`, editable install @ `ef3723f97e` 

Benchmark: 8k/1k random, 320 prompts, c=32 warmed up by sequential bench

### Throughput — run on a warmed up server

| Config | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT | Mean ITL | Accept len |
|--------|-------------:|----------:|---------:|-----------:|
| **EAGLE3 ** | **1096** | 831 ms | 26.7 ms | **3.79** |
| Baseline | 635 | 732 ms | 46.5 ms | — |

**Speedup:** ~**1.7×** EAGLE3 vs baseline with graphs (1096 vs 635 tok/s); Acceptance rate may be artificially high with the random data benchmark, prepare for slight disappointment when deploying to production.

The runs are with Triton as Aiter unified verify path runs but yields very low acceptance rate (12%)/accept length (~1.37) on MiniMax sparse layers — Investigation left as future work.

### Accuracy

EAGLE3 with both aiter and triton backends both give 95.5% accuracy on GSM8K.

### Launch command  for EAGLE3

```bash
export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1
export SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=0

  --trust-remote-code \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --quantization mxfp8 \

  --reasoning-parser minimax-m3 \
  --tool-call-parser minimax-m3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30047 \
  --watchdog-timeout 7200 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32 \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE3 \
  --speculative-draft-model-path Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3 \
  --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant
```

title: [Scheduler] Fix final chunked-prefill abort commit race
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #34149.
Related prior report: #34112.

While testing chunked-prefill cancellation on latest `main`, we independently reproduced the same user-visible symptom reported in #34112: a cancelled request can expose one token and then finish with `abort`.

The #34112 attachment used SGLang v0.5.9. Its negative batch-level output IDs were old FutureMap relay handles and are not the failure criterion or target of this PR. Current `main` no longer uses that `ScheduleBatch.output_ids` representation.

Our deterministic current-main reproduction isolates a final-prefill overlap race. An abort can arrive after the final chunked-prefill `EXTEND` is launched but before its delayed result is committed. At that point `scheduler.chunked_req` is already clear, `Req.output_ids` is empty, and the result is pending in `result_queue`.

## Root cause

There were two commit boundaries to protect:

1. `abort_request()` records `req.to_finish = FINISH_ABORT()`, but the prefill result processor previously appended the sampled token and token-derived metadata before `update_finish_state()` consumed the pending finish.
2. In the CUDA/HIP overlap loop, scheduling the next batch happens before processing the delayed final-prefill result. Without an admission guard, the pending-finish prefill request can enter optimistic decode, increment `decode_batch_idx` / the KV committed watermark, and perform an optimistic decode step and its associated allocation before the result is dropped (which may reserve multiple slots or pages under speculative decoding).

Filtering only in the output streamer is too late: request output, reasoning state, logprobs, hidden states, sampling metadata, grammar state, and KV accounting may already be mutated.

## Modifications

- When a delayed result is actually pending, exclude pending-finish prefill requests from the prefill-to-decode merge before optimistic decode preparation.
- Keep decode requests in mixed batches on their existing partial-output path.
- In the final-prefill result processor, promote the pending finish with `new_accepted_len=0` and reuse normal finished-request cleanup.
- Do not commit the dropped token's output ID, reasoning state, hidden state, customized info, sampling mask, returned logprob values, or grammar state.
- Still advance packed hidden-state and logprob cursors so later live requests in the same batch read their own slices.
- Preserve synchronous, MLX, and PP scheduling semantics by applying the merge guard only while `result_queue` contains a delayed result.
- Leave PD-prefill transfer lifecycle unchanged; it uses a separate scheduler/result path.

## Regression coverage

The scripted test deterministically waits for this window:

- the request has passed through chunked prefill;
- the final `EXTEND` is launched;
- `scheduler.chunked_req is None`;
- no middle chunks remain in flight;
- `Req.output_ids` is empty;
- the final result is pending.

It then aborts and verifies:

- finish reason is `FINISH_ABORT`;
- no token is appended;
- no optimistic decode step occurs;
- the request-pool row and KV object are released;
- reclaimable KV capacity returns to its baseline after the scheduler drains.

Additional CPU tests cover both sides of the scheduler gate (pending queue vs. already-processed result), mixed prefill/decode membership, and a two-request packed-logprob case where the aborted segment advances the cursor without attaching metadata to the aborted request.

## Accuracy Tests

Cancellation control flow only; normal token generation is unchanged.

Validated on top of `main` commit `7605529bdf98ded2815e48c7054b1bc4533256c9`:

```text
PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_chunked_req_gate.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_batch_result_processor_hidden_states.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_batch_result_processor_spec_grammar.py

11 passed, 2 subtests passed
```

```text
SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 PYTHONPATH=python .venv/bin/python \
  test/registered/scripted_runtime/test_scripted_runtime_core.py \
  TestScriptedRuntimeCore.test_abort_at_last_chunk_does_not_append_output

Ran 1 test in 129.234s
OK
```

Also passed:

- direct CI-style execution of the two modified CPU test files;
- Python compile checks for all touched files;
- registered-test and package-registration repository checks;
- Black 26.1.0, Ruff 0.15.1, isort 7.0.0, codespell 2.4.1, and `git diff --check`.

The packed-logprob test was mutation-checked: it fails both if the aborted request attaches returned logprobs and if its packed cursor contribution is skipped.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The new checks are scheduler control-flow predicates; the result-drop branch runs only for a request that is already finishing.

## Topology notes

The race is not caused by TP, DP, or PP. TP/DP use the same per-request result state. PP and MLX process their pending result before the relevant `last_batch` is reused, so the queue-gated admission change is a no-op there while the result-drop protection remains valid. PD-prefill is intentionally out of scope because it has a separate transfer and result lifecycle.

The registered end-to-end regression is TP=1 / DP=1 / PP=1. Multi-rank topology behavior was source-reviewed but not claimed as a multi-GPU runtime validation.

## Checklist

- [x] Rebased onto current `main`.
- [x] Added deterministic registered regression coverage.
- [x] Added focused scheduler and packed-metadata unit coverage.
- [x] Ran relevant unit and scripted-runtime tests.
- [x] Ran formatting, compile, and test-registration checks.
- [x] Documentation and performance benchmarks are not applicable to this abort-only correctness fix.

title: fix(dsv4): ship the fp8 unified_kv rope pool through the direct external linker
body:
## Problem

Under `SGLANG_DSV4_UNIFIED_KV_FP8=1` a unified_kv row is **two parallel pools** —
`unified_kv_pool.kv_buffer` (512 B packed fp8 nope) and `unified_kv_pool.kv_buffer_rope`
(128 B bf16 rope) — and one row index addresses both.

`_build_deepseek_v4_device_pool_group()` registers the compressed regions through
`_dsv4_compressed_region_buffers()` → `unified_region_buffers()`, which returns **the nope
pool only**. The direct external linker therefore offloads and restores 512 of every 640
bytes, and the rope half of a restored row keeps whatever the slot last held.

HiCache already ships the sibling (`_dsv4_rope_sibling` / `_build_dsv4_rope_entry` in
`hybrid_pool_assembler.py`); this is the linker-side mirror of it. It is backend-agnostic —
`umbp_direct_linker.py` and `mooncake_direct_linker.py` both resolve through
`resolve_hybrid_device_pool_group()`.

## Why nothing catches it

`DevicePoolEntry` derives its row stride and page size from the buffers it is handed and has
no view of the logical row width, so a short row is not a crash — it is wrong output. That is
what the pool's own docstring on `unified_rope_region_buffers()` warns about.

There is also no full-resolution fallback to mask it. With the unified layout the SWA pool is
a per-request ring, so `unified_cache_linker.py` sets `_skip_swa` and tombstones the range as
`swa_evicted_seqlen`. A linker-restored prefix therefore exists *only* as compressed c4/c128
rows, and `unified_kv_kernels/runtime.py` passes `unified_kv_rope` to both paged decode and
paged prefill as the prefix pool.

## Evidence

A plain before/after A/B **cannot** see this: `/flush_cache` frees device rows without
overwriting them, so a nope-only restore lands on rope that is still correct for exactly
those tokens. gsm8k accuracy was unchanged across five configurations up to 81.7% linker
exposure, including one that wrote 560k tokens of unrelated KV between the flushes.

To get a real signal, fill the compressed rope rows with a marker at flush time and count how
many still carry it after the next pass. DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MI355X (gfx950), TP8 +
DP-attention, `--page-size 256`, EAGLE MTP, UMBP direct external linker; gsm8k, 200
questions, temperature 0, warm → flush → measure:

| pass | marker written at flush | before this PR | with this PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 1 (cold) | none | 0.965 | 0.975 |
| 2 | rope pool | **0.775** | **0.955** |
| 3 | rope + nope pools | 0.825 | 0.975 |

Rope rows written during pass 2, mean per rank, of 181,136,962: **67,465 before** vs
**268,858 with this PR**. Without the fix only the extend fraction is written — 99.96% of
rows keep the marker, and the model reads them.

## Test

`test_unified_deepseek_v4_fp8_ships_the_rope_half` fails on `main` (and only that test) and
passes with the fix. The existing bf16 unified test gains an explicit
`unified_rope_region_buffers` stub returning `None`, pinning that the bf16 path ships exactly
what it did before. `test_linker_pool_assembler.py`: 10 passed before, 11 passed after.

## Scope

`unified_rope_region_buffers()` returns `None` on every non-fp8 layout, so bf16 unified and
all other layouts are untouched. For fp8 unified_kv the linker now moves the rope half as
well: 512 → 640 B per row transferred.

title: [ROCm] GLM-5.2 decode path: decode-shaped MoE/MLA tiles, split speculative softmax, and bf16 GEMM routing
body:
## Motivation

Four changes on the GLM-5.2 decode path on gfx950, found by profiling a
GLM-5.2-MXFP4 TP8/EP1 server at 104k context. They are all the same shape: at
decode batch sizes these kernels leave a 256-CU part mostly idle, and none of
them is made faster by doing less arithmetic.

- two of them launch a handful of workgroups because the tile or the reduction
  was sized for a regime decode never enters;
- one spends more time in launch overhead than in work;
- one lands on torch because a tuned table keyed on `(N, K)` has no entry for
  the shape and does not fall back to a neighbour.

Together they are **+5.7%** end to end on that configuration.

## Modifications

**`moe`: fold the padded-row fill into the shared-expert append kernel.**
`_post_process_topk_ids` bracketed the aiter shared-expert append with two
separate fills over the padded region -- one for the routed ids, one for the
weights -- three launches for a shape whose total work is a couple of
microseconds, once per MoE layer per step. The append kernel already writes
every one of those elements, so it fills the padded region itself. The id fold
requires EPLB remap off, since it relies on `pad_fill_id = 0` commuting with
`remap(0) = 0`; the weight fold additionally excludes the per-rank shared-slot
kernel, which has no shared-slot weights to zero. Where either precondition
does not hold, the separate fills run exactly as before.

**`mla`: size the absorb BMM tiles for decode.** aiter's config table has no
entry for the MLA absorb shapes, so decode falls into a bucket tuned for square
GEMMs (`BLOCK_SIZE_M=64, BLOCK_SIZE_N=256`). The grid is
`(heads, cdiv(M, BM) * cdiv(N, BN))`, so at 16 heads per rank and `N <= 512`
that launches 16-32 workgroups on a 256-CU part: starved of workgroups, not of
bandwidth or flops. This sizes the tile so the grid covers the machine and then
stops -- it does not keep splitting, because the kernel quantizes its own A tile
per token group, so every extra workgroup repeats that work (at M=200/N=512 an
unbounded split is 3.7x slower than the starved table entry).

**`spec`: split the vocab-wide speculative softmax across CTAs.** Speculative
sampling reduces across the vocabulary at every draft step and at verify. torch
reduces each row with one block, so at the row counts speculation actually runs
(1 to 32) a 154880-wide row occupies a handful of blocks, and it is read three
times. `temperature_softmax()` splits each row across CTAs -- partial
max+sumexp, an online-softmax merge, then normalize -- and folds the temperature
divide into the first pass, which drops the separate pass that materialized
`logits / temperatures`. It hands the call back to torch above the row count
where one block per row already fills the GPU, so callers use it
unconditionally.

`fast_sample`'s argmax gets the same treatment by routing it to the existing
`row_argmax()`, which already lands this optimization for the dspark accept
path. No second implementation is added: a split argmax written for this path
is 4.7-42% faster below 32 rows but 3x *slower* above it, where it fell back to
torch, and those are the verify row counts at higher concurrency.

**`linear`: route the bf16 decode shapes aiter's tuned table misses.** The aiter
tuned GEMM keys its table on `(N, K)` and does not fall back to a neighbour, so
a shape the table never saw lands on torch. A decode step hits one of those 79
times -- the MLA q up-projection, `(2048, 2048)` -- where torch runs at 8.4 us
against a 1.05 us weight-bandwidth roofline while aiter's own Triton a16w16
kernel does it in 5.0 us. What is missing is the routing, not a kernel.

The gate is `K` rather than a list of shapes: a list keyed on `(N, K)` is what
makes the aiter table miss these shapes to begin with, and a different tensor
parallel split moves every `N`. It is also bounded in the row count, because
what torch is slow at is the weight-bandwidth-bound regime decode lives in and a
prefill chunk is its opposite -- a 32768-token chunk is 1.25-1.44x *slower* on
the Triton kernel, so prefill must not be routed. `lm_head`, `(19360, 6144)`, is
1.33x slower there and stays where it was.

## Accuracy Tests

Every change is either bit-identical by construction or checked against a
reference before any timing.

| change | property | how it is checked |
|---|---|---|
| moe padded fill | bit-identical | the append kernel already writes those elements; folded only where the preconditions above hold |
| mla absorb tiles | bit-identical | same kernel, different tile; compared at every admitted M |
| `temperature_softmax` | fp32-accurate | vs a float64 reference, not vs torch, which is not ground truth at this width |
| `row_argmax` routing | bit-identical | vs `torch.argmax`, including the sampled index and the `gather` that consumes it |
| linear routing | bit-identical at M=1 | max rel diff 1.7e-4 at M=6, with the error against a float64 reference *equal* to torch's -- not accuracy traded for speed |

`temperature_softmax` against float64, MI355X, vocab 154880:

```
rows      this PR       torch       row sum deviation
   1     3.42e-11    3.42e-11                7.44e-08
   2     2.67e-11    3.27e-11                6.07e-08
   6     2.42e-09    2.89e-09                3.62e-08
  12     3.47e-10    3.47e-10                8.26e-08
  32     3.34e-09    3.34e-09                1.44e-07
  48     1.30e-09    1.30e-09                9.04e-08
  84     2.89e-09    2.89e-09                1.29e-07
```

`row_argmax` matches `torch.argmax` exactly at all seven row counts, and returns
the lowest index on an all-tied row, which ROCm's argmax does not guarantee
(#26358).

A GLM-5.2-MXFP4 TP8 server on an fp8 KV cache comes up and serves correctly with
`--dsa-decode-backend triton`, checked against prompts with verifiable answers
on both arms of every end-to-end run below.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Kernel level

`benchmark/kernels/bench_bf16_linear_routing.py` ships with this PR and needs no
server or model weights. It runs both arms in one process and interleaves them
ABBA, so the clock drift that moves kernels this small by ~10% lands on both;
the figure reported is the ratio's spread, not either arm's.

The speculative reductions, MI355X, vocab 154880, fp32, under CUDA graph replay
(the path decode runs on), us/call:

```
rows |  softmax: torch     PR    speedup  spread |  argmax: torch     PR    speedup  spread
   1 |           52.37   6.03      8.7x   23.36% |          12.00   4.61      2.6x    2.34%
   2 |           53.62   6.45      8.3x    0.79% |          34.48   4.71      7.3x    7.93%
   6 |           55.92   7.88      7.1x    0.45% |          34.65   5.24      6.6x    1.15%
  12 |           58.31   9.75      6.0x    1.51% |          34.04   5.75      5.9x    0.95%
  32 |           65.09  20.78      3.1x    0.75% |          33.98   8.70      3.9x    0.90%
  48 |           76.94  76.75      1.0x    0.29% |          36.97  11.19      3.3x    0.67%
  84 |           94.13  94.13      1.0x    0.22% |          45.80  12.28      3.7x    0.65%
```

Rows 48 and 84 in the softmax column are it handing the call back to torch above
its row limit: the harness measuring one implementation against itself, which is
the control for the rest of the column. The 23% spread at one row is the ratio's
own spread over six interleaved rounds on a 6 us kernel; every other point is
under 2%.

In eager the launch cost is not amortized and the softmax win shrinks to
1.1-1.4x; this is a graph-replay optimization and the docstrings say so.

The other two, from their own commits: the MoE append fold is 4.74 -> 1.61 us at
one row and flat in the row count, because what it removes is two launches
rather than work; the MLA `w_vc` absorb (N=256, K=512) goes from 18.1 to 3.6 us
at M=48, and `w_kc` from 12.9 to 3.1.

### End to end

Steady-state decode throughput per user, median over a 150 s window at
concurrency 1 and 2, geometric mean of the two. Base and patched arms were
interleaved across the session rather than run back to back, so linear drift
lands on both:

```
GLM-5.2-MXFP4 · TP8/EP1 · concurrency 1 and 2 · fp8 KV · 104k context
EAGLE 5/6 · --dsa-decode-backend triton · hierarchical cache off

                    vs base     read-to-read spread
base                      =     0.59%  (three reads)
three kernels        +3.94%     0.14%  (two reads)
+ linear routing     +5.67%     0.05%  (two reads)

geometric mean is over the two concurrencies; separately, at +linear routing
  concurrency 1     +4.95%
  concurrency 2     +6.39%
```

The effect is about ten times the baseline's own read-to-read spread. Within it,
the absorb tile accounts for +0.85% and the linear routing for +1.66%; the
softmax and the MoE fold make up the rest.

A trace replay of the same model (aiperf, 1800 s), one read per arm, covering
the three kernel changes only -- it was taken before the linear routing existed:

```
GLM-5.2-MXFP4 · TP8/EP1 · concurrency 1 · fp8 KV · 104k context
EAGLE 5/6 · --dsa-decode-backend triton · hierarchical cache off

per-user throughput, p90     +3.55%
per-GPU total throughput     +1.62%
```

Both arms completed the same number of profiled requests with no dropped
errors, so neither figure comes from a shortened or partly failed run.

Two harnesses with different workloads and different statistics -- a median over
a fixed-shape load and a p90 over a trace replay -- agree on the magnitude for
the part they both cover.

### What this does not claim

Neither figure is a position on a published curve. Both are paired A/B deltas on
one configuration, taken with hierarchical cache off, so they are not comparable
to a leaderboard point.

The end-to-end numbers were taken with the local split argmax described above
rather than with `row_argmax`; the difference between the two is ~1.5 us of a
12.6 ms decode step at these batch sizes, so the tables were not re-taken. The
trace-replay arms are one read each, so drift is not bracketed there; only the
first harness has repeat reads (0.59% on the base side) to bound its own noise.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [MiniMax-M3][AMD] Fix EAGLE3 TARGET_VERIFY on MI300 + AITER unquant MoE
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-M3 EAGLE3 server currently crashes during startup on gfx942 GPUs.

EAGLE3 speculative decoding runs a TARGET_VERIFY forward on MiniMax-M3 sparse attention layers. On ROCm, missing `extend_seq_lens` metadata caused crashes. Also, if metadata was present, verify was routed through the prefill sparse path and that produced garbage output.

As a separate issue, cuda graphs for speculative decoding fail with Triton MoE. Aiter MoE can be used, but bf16 MiniMax-M3 with `--moe-runner-backend aiter` and CUDA graphs enabled produced incorrect outputs because MiniMax declares `activation="silu"` with `gemm1_clamp_limit` (clamped SwiGLU), but the AITER unquant runner only applied clamp limits when `activation="swiglu"`. This issue seems to be already fixed for several datatypes, PR #34540 fixes this for Quark W4A4 MXFP4, and this PR has a fix for the bf16 model.

## Modifications

1. **`minimax_sparse_backend.py`**: Reconstruct `extend_seq_lens` on TARGET_VERIFY (mirrors NPU path from #32941). Route ROCm TARGET_VERIFY sparse layers through a decode-style verify path so causal KV lengths match draft-token verification. Enable HIP/CUDA graph capture for verify batch sizes 1–8.

2. **`unquant.py`**: Mirror #34540 for bf16 unquant — rewrite `silu` + `gemm1_clamp_limit` to `swiglu` in the AITER runner config and pass `swiglu_limit` in `AiterMoeQuantInfo`.

Requires `SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=0` for MiniMax interleaved gate/up layout.

## Validation

`MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` (bf16) with `Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3` on **8× MI308 (gfx942)**, ROCm 7.2.0, clean container, ROCm install (`setup_rocm.py` → `pip install -e python[dev_hip]`).

Hardware: `smc300x-clt-r4c9-26.cs-clt.dcgpu`, branch `amd/minimax-eagle-target-verify-v2` @ `bbffd029fe`.

### EAGLE3 (speculative, CUDA graphs ON)

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Output throughput (8k/1k, 320 prompts, c=32) | **343 tok/s** |
| Mean TTFT | 2394 ms |
| Mean ITL | 84 ms |
| EAGLE accept len / rate (during bench) | 3.78 / 0.93 |
| GSM8K (200 q, thinking) | **95.0%** |
| Sanity (2+2, Paris, prime) | PASS |

### Baseline (no speculative decoding, same MoE/attn/CUDA graph config)

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Output throughput (8k/1k, 320 prompts, c=32) | 183 tok/s |
| Mean TTFT | 2014 ms |
| Mean ITL | 163 ms |
| GSM8K (200 q, thinking) | **95.5%** |
| Sanity (2+2, Paris) | PASS |

**Speedup:** ~**88%** higher output throughput with EAGLE3 vs non-spec baseline (343 vs 183 tok/s). GSM8K accuracy unchanged within noise.

### Launch command (EAGLE3)

```bash
export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1
export SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=0

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --tp 8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --page-size 128 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --attention-backend triton \
  --speculative-draft-attention-backend triton \
  --moe-runner-backend aiter \
  --reasoning-parser minimax-m3 \
  --tool-call-parser minimax-m3 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30043 \
  --watchdog-timeout 7200 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE3 \
  --speculative-draft-model-path Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3 \
  --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 8
```

### Benchmark commands

```bash
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
  --backend sglang --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30043 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8000 --random-output-len 1000 \
  --num-prompts 320 --max-concurrency 32 --model MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3
```

title: [Unified Cache] Dedup replicated MLA/DSA KV in the UMBP direct linker
body:
## Motivation

The UMBP direct external linker suffixes every stored object key with `tp{rank}`:

```python
rank_suffix = f"tp{tp_rank}_cp{params.attn_cp_rank}_pp{params.pp_rank}"
self.storage.mla_suffix = rank_suffix
self.storage.mha_suffix = rank_suffix
```

For DeepSeek-V4 that stores `tp_size` byte-identical copies of every page. The DSv4/DSA device pools carry no `tp_size` term (`deepseek_v4_memory_pool.py` has no `tp_size`/`tp_rank` anywhere — per-token bytes are fixed, and MLA latent plus the DSA indexer are *replicated* across attention TP ranks rather than sharded), so all eight ranks in a TP8 run hold the same bytes and write them under eight different keys into one shared tier.

Nothing collapses them today:

- `offload()` -> `_run_offload()` calls `batch_put_ranges_from_ptr` with no pre-put existence check (`_page_exists` is wired only into the load path).
- `BackupKV` is dispatched from the replicated radix tree on every rank, so all ranks issue the write.
- The one dedup mechanism built for this case — the SharedSSDLeader/Follower scheme in `umbp_store.py`, gated on `is_mla_backend and tp_size > 1` — is deliberately disabled here via `per_rank_keyspace=True`, because a follower would look for keys the leader never wrote under the follower's own suffix.
- UMBP's own dedup is keyed on the key *string* (`RoutePutOutcome::kAlreadyExists`), so eight distinct keys never collide.

The per-rank suffix also makes the keyspace asymmetric against DP attention. `tp_cache_group` is the attention-TP group when DP attention is on (`kv_cache_builder.py`), which is size 1 for `tp8dp8`, so every DP rank already writes `tp0`. A DP-attention engine can therefore read what a plain-TP engine wrote, but not the reverse: ranks 1..7 look for `tp1..tp7`, which nobody wrote, and the MIN reduction in `UnifiedCacheLinkerWrapper._sync_restorable_prefix` (a 0/1 mask under MIN is an AND) then intersects the hit down to zero.

## Modifications

Add `_storage_suffix()`, mirroring the helper `MooncakeDirectLinker` already has: drop the `tp` term when `pool_group.rank_replicated`, so every rank names the same object. `cp` and `pp` always stay — CP shards the sequence and PP shards layers, so neither may be collapsed. The topology log line gains `rank_replicated` / `suffix`; its existing prefix is unchanged, since acceptance checks grep it.

**Only the key collapses — the write path is untouched, and every rank still writes.** `MooncakeDirectLinker` pairs its suffix helper with `offload_owner = not rank_replicated or tp_rank == 0`, which is safe there because MooncakeStore is always a shared external store. UMBP has deployment forms whose tier is *not* shared by the ranks that read it: a Local/embedded tier is in-process and private to its rank, and a standalone server is per node. Electing a single writer in those forms leaves the other ranks looking up a key that only exists in the owner's store, so they miss and the MIN reduction drives the hit to zero. Eliding the redundant writes needs a predicate for "this store is shared by exactly these ranks", which the linker cannot currently answer; that is left for a follow-up.

Ranks writing one key concurrently is not a new code path — DP attention already has every rank writing the `tp0` keyspace today.

Scope: `_build_deepseek_v4_device_pool_group` and `_build_dsa_device_pool_group` set `rank_replicated=True`, so this activates on the DSv4/DSA paths. Every other pool group keeps the default `rank_replicated=False` and is untouched — mamba/hybrid state *is* sharded per rank and keeps its per-rank key.

## Accuracy Tests

E2E A/B on MI355X (8x gfx950), DeepSeek-V4-Pro FP4, **TP8 with DP attention off** — the topology this patch actually changes, since `tp_cache_group` collapses to a size-1 attention-TP group under DP attention and every rank already writes `tp0`. `--attention-backend dsv4`, `--page-size 256`, `--max-total-tokens 524288`, UMBP standalone tier (128 GiB DRAM, no master), one 256K prompt at 100% hit, 5 reps. Both arms ran back to back on one node in one session; the two checkouts differ by exactly one file (`diff -rq` over the trees reports only `umbp_direct_linker.py`).

| | base (unpatched) | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| linker attach | `topology=StandaloneProcess+Distributed` x8 | same, x8 |
| `UMBPStore` ranks seen | `rank=0` .. `rank=7` | `rank=0` .. `rank=7` |
| object-key suffix | `tp0_cp0_pp0` .. `tp7_cp0_pp0` — **8 keyspaces** | `cp0_pp0` on all 8 — **1 keyspace** |
| `achieved_hit` | **99.9%** | **99.9%** |
| cached_tokens | 261888 / 262144 | 261888 / 262144 |

The functional result: collapsing the key does not break readback. All eight ranks attach, and all eight resolve their pages out of the single shared keyspace at the same 99.9% hit the per-rank layout gets (the missing 0.1% is the request's own last partial page, which is never cached). The 8-vs-1 keyspace split is visible directly in the server log via the `suffix=` field on the linker's attach line.

No task-accuracy benchmark (gsm8k or similar) was run — the change renames an object, it does not alter KV bytes, and UMBP returns a miss rather than copying when a stored object's size disagrees with the request.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same runs as above.

| | base (unpatched) | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| ttft (median of 5) | 260.2 ms | 260.3 ms |
| `dev_ms` (device-tree floor) | 161.5 ms | 167.7 ms |
| **`load_ms` = ttft - dev** | **98.6 ms** | **92.6 ms** |
| ttft spread | 1.3% | 33.2% |
| `warm_ms` (comparability gate) | 62040.0 ms | 61948.2 ms |

`warm_ms` is the arms-are-comparable gate — it is machine state, not arm state — and the two agree to **0.15%**, so the cells are comparable.

**Read this as "no regression", not as a speedup.** The 6 ms lower `load_ms` is well inside the patched arm's 33.2% spread, which comes from a single stalled rep (`[242.6, 252.8, 260.3, 261.9, 323.2]` vs the base arm's tight `[258.9 .. 262.3]`). Intermittent admission stalls are a known property of this cell. The honest conclusion is that load cost is unchanged.

The saving this patch targets is storage, not latency: for a rank-replicated pool group on a shared tier, the distinct objects stored per page drop from `tp_size` to 1. Read traffic is unchanged — each rank still needs its own copy delivered into its own device buffer — and a per-rank-private tier (Local mode) keeps one copy per rank, so it neither gains nor regresses.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (full `pre-commit run --files ...` clean, including the registered-test CI registry validators)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_umbp_direct_linker_rank_keys.py`, registered `register_cpu_ci`)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (no user-facing surface changes)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — E2E A/B on MI355X in the two sections above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: feat(flexkv): support hybrid cache with shared restore lifecycle
body:
## Summary

Extend FlexKV to DeepSeek V4's split C4/C128/SWA pools while preserving SGLang's admission and cache-ownership contracts. Ordinary models use the FlexKV radix adapter; hybrid models wrap UnifiedRadixCache for FULL/SWA bookkeeping. The connector and transfer implementation remain in the external FlexKV package.

- Share request identity, restore leases, reset reclamation, and prefetch lifecycle between both adapters.
- Keep asynchronous H2D destinations request-owned until normal cache commit; retain Store sources until transfer completion. Cross-rank polling stays in the synchronized scheduler hook.
- Support optional chunked storage prefetch and ordinary-cache duplicate-restore deferral. Deferred Store mapping is retained for supported ordinary-cache topologies; hybrid SWA keeps synchronous mapping.
- Include physical SWA eviction accounting from `a144fb1d23`, and merge upstream main `d4dcce12d4`.

## Review fixes and scope cleanup

- Fix abort releasing staged/launched Store source locks before DMA completion.
- Prevent token-only FlexKV keys from mixing LoRA/extra-key or cache-salt namespaces. These requests retain namespaced GPU caching and recompute misses; lookup, store, and prefetch skip FlexKV. Deployments that previously used these namespaces must start with a fresh host/remote cache pool.
- Make explicit `--radix-cache-backend=flexkv` load the factory, honor configuration, poll completions, and retry admission just like `--enable-flexkv`.
- Reject incompatible streaming-session and built-in HiCache combinations before connector initialization.
- Reject EAGLE-style bigram cache keys before importing or initializing the connector. This covers both selection flags and ordinary/hybrid adapters; EAGLE, EAGLE3, and FROZEN_KV_MTP currently use these keys. The token-only connector cannot preserve their extra boundary token.
- Remove duplicated lifecycle methods, unreachable hybrid async-mapping queues, the redundant MP/IP lookup wrapper, and the unused load stream. Remove unrelated process-wide SIGINT/watchdog changes.
- Replace stale setup/performance claims in the integration README with current contracts and validation boundaries.

## Validation

The main lifecycle refactor at `03647c0fb9` was validated as recorded below. CPU tensors and mocked transfers are used; the isolated container exposes no GPUs.

- **210 passed, 28 subtests passed**: restore/admission/abort/reset, prefetch, namespace isolation, registry, hybrid eviction, and the added physical-SWA accounting tests.
- **12 regression cases fail on the pre-refactor implementation and pass after the fix.**
- All applicable project pre-commit hooks pass.
- Local and validation-container hashes match for **8,036 tracked source/configuration/documentation files**.

The EAGLE guard follow-up at `8f5950ff75` passes the complete registry/routing suite: **28 tests and 10 subtests**. Four new rejection cases fail before the guard and pass after it; four non-EAGLE controls still reach connector loading. Both changed Python files match the CPU validation container by SHA256, and all applicable pre-commit hooks pass. Other features remain in this PR.

The GPU-registered unified-cache suite needs an available device; it could not execute in this CPU-only container. No current-head DMA, model-output, DeepSeek V4/SWA model, cross-node, or performance acceptance is claimed. The earlier `2ef249ef91` H20 TP2 Qwen3-0.6B run had 15/15 restore outputs match cold references; that is historical evidence for the previous adapter revision, not this refactor.

## Dependencies and merge gates

- The shared connector/Mooncake changes in taco-project/FlexKV#280 are merged.
- Optional chunked prefetch requires taco-project/FlexKV#291, which is still open; it remains disabled by default.
- DeepSeek V4 unified-KV, `--enable-hisparse`, and Mamba/SSM pools remain unsupported.
- Maintainer approval and the `run-ci` label are still required. Please run the required GPU CI on this head before merging.

title: [Intel][XPU]Enable chunked prefill scnearios for XPU with UT
body:
# Motivation

The chunked-prefill scripted-runtime suite under `test/manual/chunked_prefill/` could not run at
all on Intel XPU: the harness killed every engine during startup. Three argument-resolution paths
also ended in an unhelpful failure rather than a clear rejection. This makes the suite runnable on
`--device xpu` and reports honestly where a path cannot work there.

Rebased on `f1a512c51c`. 23 files, +389/-125.

# Modifications

## Engine startup and runtime

- **`test/scripted_runtime/http_server.py`** — kv-canary JIT-compiles its plan/verify/write kernels
  from `.cuh` against the arch reported by `torch.cuda`, so `install_canary` raised inside
  `ModelRunner.alloc_memory_pool`; the server died before the dispatch-loop handshake and the test
  side waited out `LISTENER_ACCEPT_TIMEOUT_S`. The harness now launches with the canary off wherever
  its kernels cannot build, and passes nothing rather than restating the `ServerArgs` defaults.
- **`managers/scheduler.py`** — `continue_generation` read `torch.cuda.memory_reserved()`, which
  returns 0 when CUDA was never initialized, so the reclaim log asserted a call that never happened.
  It now reads the active device module, and when the device exposes no allocator hook it says so
  instead of reporting a 0 MB reclaim.
- **`utils/common.py`** — new `device_memory_reserved`, next to the existing `empty_device_cache`,
  returning 0 where the device module has no `memory_reserved` (`torch.cpu` and `torch.mps` do not).
- **`layers/attention/{aiter,wave}_backend.py`** — both read value buffer 0, but the pool indexes as
  `layer_id - start_layer`, so a non-first PP rank read a negative index. Both now index from
  `start_layer`, reusing the wording of the same fix already on `main` in `triton_backend.py`.
  `wave_backend` uses the `self.token_to_kv_pool` reference the constructor already captured;
  `aiter_backend` keeps a local because its own attribute is not assigned until later.

## Argument resolution

- **`arg_groups/kv_cache_hook.py`** — a host KV pool resolves its page movers from
  `sgl_kernel.kvcacheio`, imported only under `if _is_cuda or _is_hip` with no `else` branch, then
  called unconditionally (`pool_host/mha.py:278,331,475,863`). So on XPU
  `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, `--disaggregation-decode-enable-offload-kvcache` and an explicit
  `--disaggregation-decode-retraction-backup=host_pool` each died minutes into startup on a bare
  `NameError`. All three are now rejected in `handle_cache_compatibility`, where the other host-pool
  combinations are already validated and which runs unconditionally.
- **`mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py`** — a decode server that leaves the retraction backup unset
  degrades to `cpu_tensor` on XPU instead of being rejected for a pool it never asked for, matching
  what HIP already gets. Keyed on the resolved device, not a hardware probe.
- **`arg_groups/overrides.py`** — deterministic inference fell through to `fa3`, which asserts
  SM 8x/9x in its own factory, so `--device xpu --enable-deterministic-inference` could not start.
  XPU now resolves to `triton`, which unlike `intel_xpu` is in
  `RADIX_SUPPORTED_DETERMINISTIC_ATTENTION_BACKEND` and so does not silently disable the radix cache.
  Two lines, inserted after the SM branches; no other device's fallback changes.
- **`layers/quantization/mxfp4.py`** — mxfp4 is registered on cpu and xpu, where the weight-load
  tail called `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` and freed nothing.

## Test-side fixes the above exposed

- **`scripted_runtime/background_http_poster.py`, `context/http_post.py`** — a rejected control POST
  surfaced only as an unrelated socket-arrival timeout. `submit_coro` now returns its future and the
  timeout handler interrogates that one future, so the server's own complaint is reported. This
  removes the process-global failure list, whose entries could be attributed to a later request, and
  restores `_log_coro_exception` as a `staticmethod` — which also unbreaks four pre-existing CI tests
  in `test/registered/unit/scripted_runtime/test_background_http_poster.py`.
- **`test_scripted_abort.py`** — a repeat abort is dropped at the `TokenizerManager` once
  `abort_sent` is set, so awaiting a second `AbortReq` could only time out; and reusing a rid needs
  the `TokenizerManager` to have released it, which no number of scheduler steps in the same yield
  can achieve.
- **`scripted_runtime_chunked_helpers.py`** — `_drain_until_released` had drifted into four copies,
  three byte-identical; it is now one `drain_until_released` helper that also waits on `lock_refs`,
  which drops an iteration after the KV pages. Call sites in `test_scripted_abort.py`,
  `test_scripted_lifecycle.py`, `test_scripted_regression.py` and `test_scripted_pp.py` are rewired to
  it (`test_scripted_pp.py` passes `max_steps=16` to keep its longer drain). The rid settle constant
  moved up with the other module constants and states where its value came from and how a slower
  device fails; `test_scripted_multi_req.py` loses a comment that duplicated it.
- **`test_scripted_regression.py`** — the abort-release regression guards read through
  `find_req_by_rid`, which stops seeing a req whether it released or leaked, so they passed on a
  leaked row. They now compare pool free counts, with the per-req probes kept only on the branch
  where they can still fail.
- **`test_scripted_special_case.py`** — the flashinfer and HiCache classes skip on devices that
  cannot run them, instead of each burning a 300 s listener timeout.

# Accuracy Tests

New CI unit tests, on CPU runners:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/server_args/ \
  test/registered/unit/scripted_runtime/ \
  test/registered/unit/utils/test_device_module_probes.py
# 331 passed, 99 subtests passed
```

Added as `test/registered/unit/utils/test_device_module_probes.py` (new file), plus cases appended to
`test/registered/unit/scripted_runtime/test_http_server.py` and
`test/registered/unit/server_args/test_server_args.py`. They cover the four runtime behaviours this
PR adds: the device-module probes
(`device_memory_reserved` / `empty_device_cache` with and without the hooks), the canary knobs per
device string, the host-pool rejection per opt-in path, and the deterministic attention fallback with
the platform pinned so the result holds on any runner.

The manual suite, on one Intel Arc Pro B60 (23.9 GiB):

```bash
source /opt/intel/oneapi/2026.1/oneapi-vars.sh --force
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD/python
ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=7 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 MASTER_PORT=29700 SGLANG_TEST_PORT_BASE=29720 \
  python -m pytest -v -ra --timeout=1200 test/manual/chunked_prefill/
```

302 collected. Latest full run on this branch: **301 passed, 11 skipped, 19 errors, 0 failures**
(baseline before this PR on the same hardware: 252 passed, 23 skipped, 27 errors). No test-body
assertion failures in either run.

## End-to-end output accuracy

The scripted tests verify bookkeeping (chunk counts, KV pages, lock refs, pool accounting); none of
them checks that the emitted tokens are correct, so a chunked KV write landing at the wrong position
would pass all 301. GSM8K covers that gap. The number that matters is chunked vs unchunked on the
same model and seed, not the absolute score.

`Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `--device xpu --attention-backend triton`, 200 examples, 32 threads:

| `--chunked-prefill-size` | GSM8K score | eval latency (s) | output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| 256 | 0.575 | 296.76 | 551.44 |
| -1 (off) | 0.605 | 320.56 | 536.68 |

Delta -0.030 against a standard error of 0.049 on the difference (0.61 sigma), i.e. indistinguishable
at this sample size; chunking is also 7 % faster end to end, consistent with the sweep above.

Two honest caveats on this figure. Only 11 of 200 requests actually spanned a chunk boundary, because
most GSM8K prompts are shorter than 256 tokens — so it is a weak probe of the chunked path. And
n=200 cannot resolve a difference smaller than about 0.10, so it rules out a gross corruption, not a
subtle one. The stronger measurement is the suite's own `test_mixed_prefix_gsm8k_chunked`, which uses
24-shot mixed-prefix prompts specifically so every request spans several chunks; it is currently
blocked on XPU by the `Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` failure described below, not by anything in this PR.

## Suite errors

The 19 remaining errors are environmental or out of scope, not chunked-prefill defects:

| Cause | Count |
|---|---|
| `openai/gpt-oss-20b` not cached (mxfp4 is registered on XPU upstream, so the SWA classes attempt the load) | 10 |
| Multi-card classes on a single-card run (`device index is out of range`) | 5 |
| `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` fails on XPU on current `main`: `RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (1x14336 and 2048x2048)`, raised from the plain model forward (`eager_runner._execute_extend`), with no LoRA in the stack. This PR touches no model or LoRA file, and it reproduces with these commits applied to the parent of #30345, so it is neither this PR's doing nor that commit's. It is the sole cause of the four `lora_overlap` errors and of every e2e GSM8K error | 4 |

# Speed Tests

This PR alters no kernel and no scheduling path, so it cannot move a number by construction. What is
worth showing for an enablement PR is that chunked prefill behaves sensibly on XPU once the suite can
run, so the sweep below is a characterisation of the feature on this hardware rather than a
before/after for this diff.

One Intel Arc Pro B60 (23.9 GiB), `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `--device xpu --attention-backend triton`,
`--mem-fraction-static 0.7`. 65 536 total input tokens in every row.

```bash
python -m sglang.benchmark.offline_throughput \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --device xpu --attention-backend triton \
  --dataset-name random --random-input 4096 --random-output 8 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --num-prompts 16 --chunked-prefill-size <N> --mem-fraction-static 0.7
```

`--random-input 4096`, 16 prompts:

| `--chunked-prefill-size` | duration (s) | input tok/s | vs chunking off |
|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 18.90 | 3467.58 | +9.3 % |
| **1024** | **18.66** | **3512.29** | **+10.7 %** |
| 2048 | 19.20 | 3412.92 | +7.6 % |
| 4096 (= input, one chunk) | 20.80 | 3151.15 | -0.6 % |
| -1 (off) | 20.66 | 3171.58 | baseline |

`--random-input 8192`, 8 prompts:

| `--chunked-prefill-size` | duration (s) | input tok/s | vs chunking off |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1024** | **33.14** | **1977.25** | **+16.7 %** |
| 2048 | 33.94 | 1931.09 | +13.9 % |
| 8192 (= input, one chunk) | 38.84 | 1687.22 | -0.4 % |
| -1 (off) | 38.67 | 1694.78 | baseline |

Chunked prefill is worth 10-17 % input throughput on XPU at these shapes, best around 1024, and the
benefit grows with prompt length. Setting the chunk size equal to the input length reproduces the
unchunked number to within 0.6 %, which is the expected degenerate case and a useful sanity check that
the sweep is measuring what it claims.

Note for anyone reproducing this: `sglang.benchmark.one_batch` is **not** usable here. It constructs a
`ModelRunner` directly and never enters the scheduler, so every `--chunked-prefill-size` yields an
identical number. `offline_throughput` drives a real `Engine`, and the scheduler log confirms chunking
engages (`Prefill batch, #new-token: 512 ... #pending-token: 3583`).

# Notes

- `test/manual/` is excluded from CI by `test/README.md`, so the runtime behaviours added here are
  covered by the `test/registered/unit/` tests above rather than by the manual suite.
- A median/MAD latency-outlier filter for `ChunkSizePredictor.fit` was considered and **dropped**.
  Replayed against the only real 127-sample XPU profile in the tree, it moved the quadratic
  coefficient from -1.24e-05 to -3.65e-05 — further from the `a > 0` acceptance test — by discarding
  the largest and most curvature-informative sample. On that sweep `corr(seq_len, latency)` is
  -0.108, so the quadratic term is unidentifiable and the problem is the sweep range, not outliers.
  `TestPPDynamic` therefore still cannot pass on XPU; a wider sweep or a linear fallback is the real
  fix and is not attempted here.

title: [ROCm] Fuse the MLA q absorb into the RoPE + KV-write kernel on gfx950
body:
## Motivation

On gfx950, the absorbed q BMM and the fused RoPE + cat + KV write are two
separate launches -- `rocm_absorb_q_bmm` in prepare, `_fused_rope_cat_and_cache`
in core. At decode shapes neither fills half the CUs, so they run back to back
with most of the machine idle.

aiter ships `fused_fp8_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache_mla`, which does all three in one
grid. It is present at the pinned `AITER_COMMIT_DEFAULT` (`4ad9983`).

## What this does

`_can_fuse_bmm_rope_cat_and_cache` enumerates the conditions under which the
fused kernel is exactly equivalent to the two it replaces: gfx95 with AITER, an
fp8 absorbed weight, a rope to fuse, the skip-rope DSA path (`tilelang` or
`triton` backend), an absorb-capable attention backend, and no deep-gemm BMM,
experimental LoRA, or active `kv_b` LoRA. The caller adds `not q_replicate_active`
-- DCP all-gathers `q_nope_out` before core runs, and the fused path has none to
hand it. Anything else falls back to the two-launch path unchanged.

It also guards the new aiter import behind `is_gfx95_supported()`.
`rocm_linear_utils` is imported wherever AITER is on, gfx942 included, but the op
is gfx95-only -- without the guard an aiter build lacking it would break every
DeepSeek import on those cards.

## Perf

MI355X, GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP8, EAGLE MTP 5/6, ISL 100k / 1k out, concurrency 1.
Same build in both arms with the gate as the only variable, two reps each.
Accept length is pinned (`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.61`) so the comparison
measures kernel time rather than divergence in which draft tokens get accepted.

`triton` DSA backend (the HIP default since #30575), ROCm 10 CI image:

| | fused | unfused | |
|---|---|---|---|
| median ITL | 3.40 ms | 3.45 ms | -1.45% |
| P90 ITL | 4.53 ms | 4.60 ms | -1.41% |
| mean TPOT | 3.76 ms | 3.81 ms | -1.18% |

`tilelang` backend, measured earlier on a ROCm 7.0 image:

| | fused | unfused | |
|---|---|---|---|
| median ITL | 5.570 ms | 5.640 ms | -1.24% |
| mean TPOT | 6.145 ms | 6.245 ms | -1.60% |

The saving is one kernel launch per layer, so it does not depend on which
attention backend consumes the output -- the two backends agree to within the
run-to-run spread.

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/models/test_rocm_mla_absorb_fusion_gate.py` (CPU, 4 tests /
6 subtests): each gate term independently disables the fusion, and off gfx95
nothing else is consulted.

`ruff`, `ruff-format`, `isort`, `codespell` clean.

title: fix(mimo-vl): keep multimodal features when capturing aux hidden states, and correct vision preprocessing
body:
## Motivation

MiMo-VL image understanding is silently broken on `main` whenever DFLASH/MTP aux capture is on (the normal serving configuration for MiMo-V2.6 with a DFLASH drafter). `image_tokens` look correct in the usage payload, but every image produces the same description or an "empty placeholder" reading.

Two additional vision-path mismatches vs the reference implementation shipped with the checkpoint (`modeling_mimo_v2.py` / `preprocessor_config.json`) scramble colors and collapse ViT features even when embedding splice runs.

## Modifications

1. **`MiMoV2ForCausalLM.forward`** (`srt/models/mimo_v2.py`) — **primary**
   `set_dflash_layers_to_capture()` sets `capture_aux_hidden_states`, and `forward()` took that branch first and called the language model directly, never `general_mm_embed_routine`. Image/audio placeholder tokens kept plain text embeddings. Now the multimodal embed routine always runs for multimodal models (matching `Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration`); aux hidden states are unpacked afterwards when capturing.

2. **`MiMoProcessor` pixel stats** (`srt/multimodal/processors/mimo_v2.py`)
   `standardize_batch` applied ImageNet mean/std to un-rescaled 0–255 tensors. `Qwen2VLImageProcessor` (`image_processor_type` in `preprocessor_config.json`) uses `OPENAI_CLIP` mean/std with `do_rescale=1/255`. Switched to CLIP numerics in 0–255 space.

3. **Vision patch merger `ln_q`** (`srt/models/mimo_vl.py`)
   Reusing `Qwen2_5_VisionPatchMerger` left `ln_q` as `RMSNorm`; the MiMo reference merger uses `nn.LayerNorm` over the pre-merge context dim. Restored `nn.LayerNorm(..., bias=False)` (checkpoint ships only `ln_q.weight`).

4. **Attention sink init** (`srt/models/mimo_vl.py`)
   `VisionAttention.sinks` is `torch.empty` at construction and `_post_init` only cleared `*bias*`. Checkpoints that omit individual `visual.blocks.*.attn.sinks` keys then ran those layers with uninitialized sink bias. Zero sinks at init.

Note: `VisionFlash4Attention` dropping `window_size`/`sinks` is tracked separately in #38871 / #38872.

## Repro (DFLASH serving, vision backend default)

1. Solid-color images (256×256 red/green/blue/white/black) asked for the fill color → identical answers (or "empty placeholder") before the fix; distinct colors after.
2. Black-circle-on-white vs white-circle-on-black → identical description before; opposite after.
3. `usage.prompt_tokens_details.image_tokens` is non-zero in both cases.

title: [Radix Cache] Sync Rust TreeCore and make it the default
body:
Use Rust as the default unified tree core and resolve unsupported configurations to Python in one central place. Synchronize these Python behaviors:

| Original Python PR | Rust change |
| --- | --- |
| [#38356 — Logical-page placement](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38356) | Preserve `rotation_base` through insertion and splitting, and reject incompatible grafts before transferring KV ownership. |
| [#37503 — HiCache accounting](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37503) | Count every unbacked Full-KV eviction within a native step, including cascades, and report `tracked_unbacked_tokens`. |
| [#37795 — Eviction-policy configuration](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37795) | Forward SLRU's `protected_threshold` and validate policy parameters. The cutoff orders probationary nodes before protected nodes while preserving LRU order within each segment; the original policy came from [#18843](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18843). |
| [#33777 — Write-back host pressure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33777) | Preserve insertion order when reclaiming Full host duplicates, including removals and new backups. Retain device-resident SWA host backups under SWA pressure, matching Python's Full-only duplicate prepass; ordinary host-only SWA eviction remains available. |
| [#38462 — Host-duplicate reclamation](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38462) | Honor `SGLANG_HICACHE_SKIP_HOST_DUPLICATE_RECLAIM` in native eviction. |
| [#38269 — SWA layout-aware reuse](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38269) | Use the allocator's actual request-ring capability for SWA matching. This preserves ring prefix reuse without HiCache and rejects paged-SWA hits without the required window, including DSV4.1 encoder replay + DSpark + HiCache configurations from [#38798](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38798). |
| [#39283 — SWA buffer-mode prefetch](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39283) | Port `swa_tombstone_ranges` and `attach_swa_window`, including repairs that split existing nodes, preserving KV ownership, locks, pending write-through actions and namespace/page offsets. |
| [#37507 — Unified-memory HiCache](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37507) | Preserve exact Full-row anchors for SWA load-back, including resident-row holes, and resolve current physical SWA rows before backup after compaction. |
| [#40680 — Internal Mamba write-back](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40680) | Back up internal Mamba state before eviction, wait for acknowledgment and retain resident Full KV. Reclaim host-state capacity first; preserve the legacy drop on allocation failure and device state on submission/acknowledgment exceptions. |

Centralized Python fallback applies to both default and explicit Rust selection for:

- Session-aware caching.
- T-LRU eviction, introduced by [#34012](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34012).
- C128 or other unsupported components.
- Custom component overrides.
- Non-Linux platforms.
- PyTorch versions outside 2.11–2.13, or unrecognized versions.
- Devices other than CPU or CUDA.
- Installations containing neither the Rust extension nor its sources.

The T-LRU fallback preserves its policy configuration. Supported configurations surface build, import and runtime errors. Native sessions, C128 and T-LRU remain outside this round. Shared inspectors replace Rust-specific test skips; configuration-applicability guards remain.

The Full duplicate collection preserves constant-time membership/removal and amortized constant-time insertion with an arena-indexed linked list. General device/host leaf sets retain their existing implementation. The SWA layout flag is captured at construction; these fixes add no controller protocol or per-token allocation.

Validation:

- Current head: `37cba17762e0f221459722c79050b715906de46d`. Local checks: 884 native tests passed (one existing ignored test), 165 integration tests passed (one existing CUDA-only skip), and 120 focused Python tests plus 22 subtests passed (two existing skips). Native extension fingerprints match this source. Formatting, Clippy, focused Python lint, spelling and test-registration checks pass. Fresh CI runs: [Base](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35840830520), [Extra](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35840830214), [Lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35840829751); results pending.
- Before the latest fixes, the new shared regressions produced five Rust failures and fifteen passes on `768b29dcbc`, covering both SWA match directions, repeated Full victim order/rebackup and SWA duplicate retention. Current integration validation passes all twenty new cases. Host-pressure controls also verify locks/pending DMA and that ordinary host-only SWA eviction still works after demotion.
- Earlier NVIDIA evidence belongs to `768b29dcbc` / tested merge `b5bcda1af5`: [Extra](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35794750100) passed all 19 GPU slots; [Base](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35794750266) passed 34 GPU slots and all eleven CPU shards / 683 planned files. Its final B300 and H20 retries were queued when the latest fixes were prepared. These results do not validate the new source.
- On that preceding source, both shared Python/Rust CUDA matrices passed all four Mamba write-back/load-back variants (page sizes 1, 4, 64 and 128) and four write-through controls, establishing residency, matchability and transfer completion. The separate [#37507 HiCache E2E job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35794750100/job/106971644017) passed eight methods across four models against a Rust resident-cache reference, including text/logprob gates. These checks do not establish exact Python/Rust numerical state equality. Fresh CI must cover the updated native core.

Rotation compatibility has simulated-rank/core coverage. Upstream #38468 supplies shared sizing/invariant helpers; production allocator selection and serving E2E remain unwired at this base. The DSV4.1 SWA regression is reproduced with real CPU allocators/cores and traced through the supported NVIDIA construction; no GPU output-corruption reproduction is claimed.
