title: [DSA] Add opt-in LiteTopK decode top-k path for SM100
body:
@DarkSharpness could you take a look at the speedup table below when you have a chance?

## Motivation

DSA models run a lightweight *indexer* before main attention: an fp8 multi-query attention scores KV positions against each query, and the **top-k** positions are selected so main attention only attends to those. At decode, this top-k runs once per step per layer, so its latency lands directly on top-k selection.

The existing path scores into a logits buffer and then runs a separate per-row top-k over it. This PR adds an experimental decode top-k that keeps a bounded candidate set instead, selecting the exact top-k from it — **the selection is exact FP32, not approximate**. **In particular, it maintains the histogram when the score is computing, and directly selects based on the histogram information.**

This is the decode-side counterpart to the prefill work in #32094 (SM100) and #40461 (SM90).

## Modifications

Everything lives under `python/sglang/kernels/experimental/litetopk_decode/` and nothing outside that directory is touched. A decode top-k call is two kernels: the DeepGEMM score + histogram producer, then one selector.

- `deepgemm/opt_in_histogram.patch` — companion patch to sgl-project/DeepGEMM main `1853080` (4 files, +130 / −18). It adds an optional `histogram=` argument to the existing `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits`; the paged kernel takes it as a `kWithHistogram` template variant that counts every live, non-NaN score into a 1024-bin histogram while scoring. No new kernel, runtime class or API is added; calls without the argument keep the native template instance. `deepgemm/build.py` applies the patch to a private build tree; the installed `deep_gemm` is not replaced.
- `selectors/selector.py` — the CuTe DSL selector. From the histogram it finds the bins that must contain the top-2048, gathers only the scores in those bins, and ranks them exactly in FP32. It returns the histogram and its workspace to zero, so no reset kernel runs between calls or CUDA graph replays.
- `build_fused.py` — reproducible AOT build of the selector's two routes from that one source (512 threads/CTA for batch ≤ 8, 1024 otherwise), with a SHA256 manifest. `--candidate-capacity` sets the per-row candidate limit (default 32768).
- `fused.py` — `FusedDecodePlan`, the explicit API. It verifies the artifact hashes, loads the private DeepGEMM build under a separate module name, and is CUDA graph capturable.
- `smoke_fused.py` — correctness smoke test.

## Scope
- SM100a / B200 (148 SMs).
- Decode Q=1, 32 heads, head dim 128, FP8 KV with page size 64, top-k 2048, batch 1–128, context up to 1,048,576.
- Input scores and final selection semantics: exact FP32. There is no silent fallback: a live NaN score, or more candidates than the build's capacity, raises a CUDA device error.
- Unsupported inputs are rejected by the API.

## Accuracy Tests

- Every cell of the speed table below is checked against the FP32 reference before and after timing for both paths.
- `smoke_fused.py`: every batch 1–128 × 6 length patterns, plus the default list (810 records), eager and graph replay. Each record checks exact top-k and physical KV slots, every histogram bin against a CPU model, and that the histogram and the whole selector workspace are zero again after the call.
- Edge suite at batch 1/2/5/8/9/128: 360/360 cases exact. The 12 inputs built to fail (one candidate over capacity, a NaN score) raise the expected device error.
- A captured real decode input that once failed (batch 1, 262,154 tokens, 3,398 candidates) is selected exactly.
- Stress: 300 graph replays × 8 calls over 59 cases, 3,996,000 row checks, 0 mismatches.
- DeepGEMM: with the histogram on, scores are bit-identical to unpatched main `1853080`. Without it, scores are also bit-identical, and 16 audited kernel instances have the same SASS as unpatched main.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Decode indexer score + top-k latency on B200. Each cell is **Ours / SGLang / Speedup**, with latency measured in **µs/batch** — lower is better.

| Batch | 131072 (128K) | 262144 (256K) | 524288 (512K) | 786432 (768K) | 1048321 (~1M) |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12.468 / 16.568 / **1.33×** | 14.494 / 20.703 / **1.43×** | 16.556 / 28.924 / **1.75×** | 22.899 / 41.700 / **1.82×** | 35.380 / 60.355 / **1.71×** |
| 2 | 14.490 / 18.647 / **1.29×** | 16.525 / 22.749 / **1.38×** | 23.887 / 38.514 / **1.61×** | 37.333 / 56.510 / **1.51×** | 48.540 / 74.097 / **1.53×** |

title: [CPU] Add available memory retrieval from cgroup memory.max config
body:
## Motivation

Re-submit of #38260.

On CPU, sglang auto-computes mem_fraction_static from total host memory and does not honor container cgroup memory limits. This makes a single server reserve a huge KV-cache pool regardless of the actual model size, and makes it impossible to run multiple sglang containers on one host safely.

## Modifications

Added a `get_instance_memory_status` function which tries to retrieve the cgroup memory limit from /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max and memory status from /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.current . Existing CPU mem acquisition approach  psutil.virtual_memory().total is used as a fallback.

title: [NPU][CI] Move the NPU attention-backend UTs to a CPU-only gate
body:
## Motivation

`base-a-test-1-npu-a2` is the stage-A gate for every a3 stage, but its entire contents are two NPU attention-backend unit tests. Both stub out `torch_npu` / `sgl_kernel_npu` in `sys.modules` before importing the backend, so they never touch an NPU: they need neither an a2 (910b) card nor the CANN image. Today an NPU card still has to come up and install the whole Ascend stack before any a3 job can be scheduled, purely to run two model-free unit tests.

## Modifications

- Register `test_npu_ascend_backend.py` and `test_npu_ascend_dsv4_backend.py` to a new suite `base-a-test-npu`, and list it in `PER_COMMIT_SUITES[NPU]`.
- Replace the `base-a-test-1-npu-a2` job with an inline `base-a-test-npu` job on a hosted `ubuntu-latest` runner, in the same stage-A gate position: the a3 stages' `needs` lists (5 base-b, 2 multimodal-gen, `analyze-failure-report`, `pr-test-npu-finish`) now point at the new job, so the fast-fail semantics are unchanged.
- The new job installs the NPU dependency set (`pyproject_npu.toml` swapped in, `python[dev_npu]`) plus the CPU torch wheel, and runs the same `check-pr-test-health` gate as the other stages so a lint failure stops before any NPU job is scheduled.
- `triton` is installed explicitly: `sglang.srt.utils.common` imports it unconditionally, and the CPU-only torch wheel -- unlike the PyPI torch wheel the CUDA CPU stages resolve -- does not pull it in. The NPU image gets `triton-ascend` from `npu_ci_install_dependency.sh` instead.
- Drop the now-unused `CANN_image_910b` output from `set-image-config`.

Note: this retires the a2 PR job, which is the same direction as #40524. This PR is the subset of that change which does not depend on the CANN 9.1.0 bump, so it can be reviewed and validated on its own.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A - CI configuration only. The two unit tests are moved between suites, not modified.

N/A - no inference path is touched. The stage-A gate itself gets faster and stops occupying an NPU card.

title: [AMD] Drop the unreachable vLLM fallback from ROCm FP8 activation quant
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #40557: The reviewer asked why `_has_vllm` is still kept.

`_has_vllm` in `fp8_kernel.py` is only ever set inside `if _is_hip:`, and only in the arm where `_use_aiter` is false:

```python
if _is_hip:
    _has_vllm = False
    if _use_aiter:
        from aiter import dynamic_per_tensor_quant, ...
    else:
        try:
            import vllm._C
            _has_vllm = True
        except ImportError:
            _has_vllm = False
```

So the vLLM arm is selected in exactly one configuration: **ROCm, `SGLANG_USE_AITER` off, and `vllm._C` importable**. Nothing shipped reaches it:

| configuration | `SGLANG_USE_AITER` | vLLM present | vLLM arm |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` | `1` | — | never selected |
| `docker/rocm-gfx1151.Dockerfile` | `0` | not installed | never selected (native path) |
| `nightly-test-amd.yml` | `1` | — | never selected |
| `python/pyproject.toml` | — | not a dependency | — |

And the one configuration that does select it **cannot complete a forward pass on current `main`**. `RMSNorm.forward_hip` calls `fused_add_rms_norm` with AITER's 6-argument out-of-place signature; with AITER off, `layernorm.py` binds that name to vLLM's 4-argument in-place op instead. Replaying layer 0's calls in execution order in that configuration:

```
fp8_kernel: _use_aiter=False _has_vllm=True
layernorm.fused_add_rms_norm bound to vllm._custom_ops.fused_add_rms_norm

  [ok]    input_layernorm      rms_norm(out, x, w, eps)                        [4 args]
  [ok]    qkv_proj fp8 quant   scaled_fp8_quant -> vLLM arm
  [ok]    o_proj   fp8 quant   scaled_fp8_quant -> vLLM arm
  [FAIL]  post_attention_norm  fused_add_rms_norm(out, x, r_out, r, w, eps)    [6 args]
TypeError: fused_add_rms_norm() takes 4 positional arguments but 6 were given
```

A real `RMSNorm` module called with a residual fails the same way, from the dispatch it actually takes:

```
TypeError: fused_add_rms_norm() takes 4 positional arguments but 6 were given
  at sglang/kernels/fused_op.py:659 in forward
  at sglang/srt/layers/layernorm.py:766 in forward_hip
```

So the vLLM FP8 arm runs twice in layer 0 and then the first residual norm raises. The `fused_add_rms_norm` signature is the same in vLLM 0.26.0 and 0.27.1.

## Modifications

- Remove `_has_vllm`, the `vllm._C` import probe, and the three `elif _has_vllm:` arms (dynamic per-token, dynamic per-tensor, static). The import guard becomes `if _is_hip and _use_aiter:`.
- With AITER on, nothing changes. With AITER off, the native path takes over — the path gfx1151 already runs.
- In the per-tensor branch both remaining backends take a `torch.empty` scale, so the allocation is hoisted. The comment added in #40557, which explained why only vLLM needed the pre-zero, goes with the vLLM arm.
- The native fallbacks' docstrings said "when vLLM is unavailable"; they now say "when AITER is disabled".

One file, +13/−36.

## Accuracy Tests

The native fallback against the vLLM ops it replaces, on all three call sites: 144 cases over bf16/fp16, six shapes from `1x4096` to `4096x4096`, and gaussian, heavy-tailed and zero-row inputs. Run against both vLLM 0.27.1 and 0.26.0 with identical results.

| call site | byte agreement native/vLLM (worst) | scale ratio native/vLLM | worst reconstruction-error gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| static, calibrated scale | **100%** | 1.0000 | 0 |
| static, scale saturating 224–240 | **100%** | 1.0000 | 0 |
| dynamic per-token | 93.73% | 0.9967 – 1.0033 | +1.6e-4 |
| dynamic per-tensor | 95.01% | 0.9971 – 1.0032 | +3.4e-4 |

Static is bit-identical, including scales chosen to push values between 224 and 240 — so vLLM caps `float8_e4m3fnuz` at 224 exactly as sglang does.

The dynamic gap is a dtype effect, not an algorithmic one. The native path divides in the input dtype, and the scale spread tracks that dtype's epsilon:

| input | native/vLLM max \|ratio−1\| | dtype epsilon | same formula in fp32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 | 3.33e-3 | 3.91e-3 | 5.0e-8 |
| fp16 | 4.18e-4 | 4.88e-4 | 5.1e-8 |

For scale: AITER, which every shipped ROCm image runs, divides by the type maximum 240 where vLLM and sglang divide by 224. Its scale is a constant 224/240 = 0.9333 of vLLM's and it agrees with vLLM on ~20% of dynamic-quant bytes. Bit-compatibility with vLLM is not something this code relies on today.

After the patch, the public `scaled_fp8_quant` is bit-identical to calling AITER directly with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, and to calling the native fallback directly with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`, on all three call sites (18 cases per mode).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**The native path is 2.4–11x slower per call than vLLM's fused ops.** µs per call on MI325X, bf16, vLLM 0.26.0, median of 7×300:

| call site | shape | vLLM (graph) | native (graph) | native/vLLM | AITER (graph) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dynamic per-token | 1×4096 | 3.68 | 29.46 | 8.0x | 2.40 |
| dynamic per-token | 64×4096 | 3.98 | 41.30 | 10.4x | 2.59 |
| dynamic per-token | 4096×4096 | 18.69 | 115.84 | 6.2x | 12.87 |
| dynamic per-tensor | 1×4096 | 10.92 | 26.52 | 2.4x | 6.06 |
| dynamic per-tensor | 64×4096 | 11.55 | 35.14 | 3.0x | 6.72 |
| dynamic per-tensor | 4096×4096 | 63.99 | 115.09 | 1.8x | 54.96 |
| static | 1×4096 | 2.41 | 11.57 | 4.8x | 2.31 |
| static | 64×4096 | 2.58 | 13.28 | 5.1x | 2.50 |
| static | 4096×4096 | 14.40 | 88.94 | 6.2x | 12.38 |

Eager timings show the same ordering (per-token 5.9–7.9x, per-tensor 1.7–3.0x, static 3.8–6.1x).

No working deployment pays this: the only configuration that reached the removed arm cannot serve a model (see Motivation), and gfx1151 was already on the native path. If the AITER-off + vLLM mode is ever repaired at `layernorm.py:766`, its FP8 activation quant should get a fused kernel rather than fall through to the native path.

## Not in scope

Left alone on purpose, each for a reason:

- `layernorm.py` `_has_vllm_rms_norm` — also set `True` when AITER is on, where it means "a fast rms_norm is available", so it needs restructuring rather than deletion. It is also where the AITER-off + vLLM breakage actually lives.
- `moe/.../fused_moe.py` `_has_vllm_ops` — gated on `not _is_cuda and not _is_hip and not _is_xpu`, so it serves other platforms, not ROCm.
- `rotary_embedding/base.py` — a previous attempt to drop the vLLM dependency there was reverted in #12028 after it broke GPT-OSS.

## The manual quant test under `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`

`test/manual/quant/test_custom_ops.py` (not run in CI) passes 6/6 with AITER on, before and after this change. With AITER off it exercises whichever fallback is selected, so it is worth being explicit about:

| host | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| AITER off, vLLM installed | 6/6 via the vLLM arm | native path |
| AITER off, no vLLM (e.g. the gfx1151 image) | native path | native path, unchanged |

On the native path it passed 11 of 60 across ten runs. That is the native fallback as it already is on any ROCm host without vLLM; this change does not touch its arithmetic. Two things fail:

- The per-tensor and per-token assertions require exact agreement with an fp32 reference, and the native path divides in the input dtype — the dtype effect quantified above. The test was adapted from vLLM's kernel test, where that bar fits a fused kernel checked against its own formula; for a fallback it is stricter than it needs to be, and AITER does not meet it either.
- `test_scaled_fp8_quant_with_padding` hits a genuine shape bug: with `num_token_padding` the native fallback copies an `input`-sized result into a taller `output` and raises. On ROCm, `apply_fp8_linear` pads compressed-tensors FP8 activations to at least 17 rows unless torch.compile is on, so a batch of fewer than 17 tokens reaches it on a host running without AITER or vLLM. It predates this change and is left for a separate one.

## Checklist

- [x] `ruff format --check`: clean. `ruff check`: 48 findings before and after the change on this file, none introduced.
- [x] No new unit tests: this removes a branch no working configuration reaches, and nothing references `_has_vllm`. The existing manual test is covered in the section above.
- [x] Accuracy and speed results above.

title: [Quant] ModelOpt mixed precision: dispatch block-FP8 MoE experts and derive the block size
body:
## Motivation

`ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig` dispatches both `FP8_PB_WO` and `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` for Linear layers, but only `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` for FusedMoE, and it hard-codes the block-FP8 block size to `[128, 128]` in two field-identical sub-configs.

`nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` labels its MTP experts (`mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts`) `FP8_PB_WO` (`group_size` 128) in the inline `config.json` and `FP8_BLOCK_SCALES` in `hf_quant_config.json`. Today the file copy wins only because the inline copy carries no KV-cache key and is discarded as incomplete (`weight_utils.py`). If the inline copy became authoritative, the FusedMoE branch would fall through to `return None`, FusedMoE would install the unquantized method, and the fp8 expert weights would be cast to bf16 with `weight_scale_inv` silently dropped — no error.

Mirrors vllm-project/vllm#55513 (`_BLOCK_FP8_MOE_ALGOS`, block size from `group_size`, conflicting sizes rejected).

## Modifications

- `_BLOCK_FP8_ALGOS = ("FP8_PB_WO", "FP8_BLOCK_SCALES")`; the Linear and FusedMoE branches both dispatch on it to the single block-FP8 sub-config `fp8_block_config`. The field-identical `fp8_pb_wo_config` that sat next to it is removed (constructor parameter, attribute, construction, kwarg).
- That sub-config's `weight_block_size` is derived from the checkpoint's block-FP8 `group_size` (default 128) instead of being hard-coded; a MIXED_PRECISION map whose block-FP8 layers disagree on it raises.

## Test

- `test_modelopt_loader.py::TestModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig`: both names dispatch to `Fp8MoEMethod` with `[128, 128]`; block size follows `group_size`; conflicting sizes raise. The full file passes (36 tests) and the repo's pinned pre-commit hooks (isort / ruff / ruff-format / codespell) pass on the changed files.

## Validation (Modal, 4x B300 SXM6 AC, `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` = v0.5.20 cu130, whose pins equal `main`; this branch `pip install -e --no-deps` on top)

Checkpoint `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` @ `fc694b54`. Serve flags = the cookbook datacenter cell plus `--mamba-ssm-dtype float32 --linear-attn-decode-backend triton --page-size 64 --context-length 262144`, no `--quantization` (resolved to `modelopt_mixed` from `config.json`; MoE runner auto-pinned to `flashinfer_trtllm`). Evals via `sgl-eval` 0.1.2.

**Sampling per the model card** (`temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, top_k=20, max_tokens=131072, reasoning_effort=xhigh`):

| Config | Bench | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `--tp 4`, no EP, no MTP | AIME26, 30 x 16 | **pass@1 98.54** (sem 0.43), majority@16 100, pass@16 100, **0/480 truncated**, 0 server errors |
| `--tp 4`, no EP, no MTP | GSM8K, 1319 x 1 | **97.80**, stop_rate 1.0, **0 truncated**, 356 s eval wall, 0 server errors |

**MTP path exercised by this PR** (`--tp 4`, no EP, `NEXTN` steps 3 / topk 1 / draft tokens 4, greedy):

- Starts **without EP**; draft `Qwen4ExpForCausalLMMTP` loads with `quant=modelopt_mixed` and its block-FP8 experts on `Fp8MoEMethod` (scale grid `[5, 20]` for `[640, 2560]` weights).
- Accept length **2.99** on GSM8K at 64-way concurrency (max 4.0), ~3.5 on AIME26 reasoning — a mis-scaled draft shows ~1.6.
- GSM8K greedy 97.35 with MTP vs 97.65 without (4 / 1319 questions, batch-numerics noise at `temperature=0`). GSM8K wall time 204 s vs 273 s.
- 8 generations ran to the 262k context ceiling with speculation on; no IMA / CUDA error.

Note for reviewers running greedy evals: at `temperature=0`, the `--tp 4` no-EP configuration produces early repetition loops on one AIME26 problem (5/120 and 8/120 truncated in two runs). It reproduces without MTP, does not occur at `--tp 1`, and vanishes under the recommended sampling above — a greedy-decoding artifact of that TP layout, independent of this change.

title: [mem_cache][PD] Fix decode radix cache ownership and allow EAGLE/EAGLE3 with decode radix cache
body:
## Motivation

Fix KV ownership during post-insert repointing and allow `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache` with EAGLE and EAGLE3. These combinations previously failed startup validation.

### Observed failure

Seen on a 1-prefill / 1-decode deployment of gpt-oss-120b (hybrid SWA, page size 64) with EAGLE3 (3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens) and `--disaggregation-decode-enable-radix-cache` on the decode server, with the speculative-decoding guard relaxed and a 65,536-token decode KV pool. Single-turn traffic, including 500 GSM8K requests at 16 concurrency, ran clean. Multi-turn traffic (second turn = first-turn prompt + first-turn output, so the prefix hit lands on KV the decode server generated itself) then killed the decode scheduler at the next idle moment, after every request had returned HTTP 200:

```
ValueError: pool memory leak detected! [full] total=65536, available=768, evictable=65152, protected=0, session_held=0, uncached=0
[swa] total=52224, available=19136, evictable=33152, protected=0, session_held=0, uncached=0
```

`available + evictable` exceeds `total` by 384 tokens (6 pages) in the full pool and by 64 (1 page) in the SWA pool. With `SGLANG_DEBUG_MEMORY_POOL=1` and a tree walk at the failure point: the tree's size counters matched the recomputed per-node sums and `sanity_check` passed, the allocator's free list held no duplicate page, but exactly 6 full pages and 1 SWA page were referenced by a tree node **and** present on the free list — real double ownership, not a counting drift. The first shared SWA page had been freed by `maybe_evict_swa` (called from `eagle_prepare_for_decode`) for a running request while a tree node still owned it. A later run tripped the pre-existing assertion directly, in `cache_unfinished_req` during decode-side admission: `AssertionError: new_prefix_len=256, len(new_indices)=0` — the insert had overlapped 256 tokens already in the tree, and the re-match returned nothing.

The same multi-turn loop reproduced the failure within 1–5 rounds in three of four runs on the base commit. Without speculative decoding, 12 rounds did not trigger it; the bigram key is what makes the short re-match likely, not what makes it possible.


### Root cause

The previous code re-matched the prefix after insertion. A normal SWA match requires a full live window, but disaggregated decode can allocate SWA slots only for the prompt's recent tail. EAGLE's bigram key can move the page-aligned insert boundary back one page, leaving less than a full live window inside the inserted range.

The re-match can therefore stop short even though the tree already owns the whole inserted range. This leaves `cache_protected_len` too small: subsequent SWA eviction or finished-request insertion can free tree-owned slots, corrupting allocator ownership and triggering the scheduler's idle pool check.

## Modifications


Repoint unfinished requests using canonical indices collected from the final insert node to the root, and assert that they cover the entire page-aligned insert. With this ownership fix in place, extend the speculative-algorithm allowlist and update the CLI help to match.

title: [MiniMax-M3][PD] Support heterogeneous TP state transfer with Mooncake
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-M3 maintains an auxiliary sparse index-K cache in addition to the standard KV cache.

This state has four logical index heads, while the physical attention TP size may be smaller or larger than four:

- TP2: each rank owns two logical index heads.
- TP4: each rank owns one logical index head.
- TP8: each logical index head is replicated across two consecutive ranks.

The existing Mooncake state-transfer path assumes matching physical layouts and explicitly rejects heterogeneous TP and PP>1 for MiniMax states. Removing that check without remapping the state would allow replicated source ranks to write the same destination buffer or copy the wrong byte range.

This PR adds a MiniMax-specific index-K transfer path for heterogeneous attention TP and PP deployments.

## What this PR changes

### MiniMax index-K layout metadata

The MiniMax KV pool now records:

- the number of index heads stored by the local rank;
- the global number of logical index heads;
- the supported index-K cache layout.

The local head count is derived from the logical head count and attention TP size instead of being fixed to one:

```python
local_index_heads = global_index_heads // min(attn_tp_size, global_index_heads)
```

This is required for TP1 and TP2, where one rank owns multiple logical index heads.

### Heterogeneous-TP index-K mapping

Mooncake now computes MiniMax index-K transfer blocks from logical head ownership rather than physical rank equality.

Supported mappings include:

- TP8 -> TP4: elect one writer from each replicated source-rank group;
- TP4 -> TP8: fan out one source head to all destination replicas;
- TP8 -> TP2: gather multiple logical heads into each destination rank;
- TP2 -> TP4/TP8: split the multiple local source heads into destination
  head ranges;
- equal TP: preserve the existing direct-transfer behavior when layouts are compatible.

The implementation currently supports the NHD index-K cache layout only. Other layouts fail explicitly.

### PP global layer pairing

MiniMax uses compact local layer lists on PP stages. Positional pairing is therefore unsafe when a PP stage transfers state to a PP1 decode worker.

This PR registers global layer IDs for:

- MiniMax main KV buffers;
- sparse index-K buffers;
- dense KV state when present.

Source and destination buffers are paired by global layer ID, with missing or duplicate layers rejected.

### Main KV staging

`MiniMaxSparseKVPool` wraps its standard attention KV cache in `main_pool`.

The heterogeneous-TP staging path now unwraps this pool and selects the K/V buffers by global layer ID. Sparse index-K remains on the dedicated state transfer path and is not mixed into the standard KV staging layout.

### Validation and mixed-version safety

The new path validates:

- source and destination TP/rank values;
- TP-to-logical-head divisibility;
- local and global index-head counts;
- NHD layout compatibility;
- item length and per-head byte width;
- source and destination index counts;
- global layer-ID pairing;
- negative or out-of-range page indices;
- source and destination buffer bounds.

A new and an old peer must not silently fall back when only one side advertises the MiniMax index-K layout metadata. This is especially important for TP1 and TP2, where the physical item size changes compared with the previous single-head allocation.

If only one peer provides the new layout metadata, registration or transfer fails explicitly instead of performing a potentially truncated or out-of-bounds RDMA copy.

## Compatibility

- The new behavior is limited to MiniMax state types.
- Existing non-MiniMax state transfer paths are unchanged.
- Equal-TP peers using the legacy layout continue to use the existing path when neither side advertises the new MiniMax layout metadata.
- One-sided new metadata is rejected to make mixed-version deployment safe.
- NIXL and MORI behavior is unchanged.
- The implementation is currently Mooncake-only and NHD-only.

## Tests

No new test file is introduced. Coverage is added to the existing disaggregation, Mooncake batching, MiniMax state, and staging test files.

The tests cover:

- TP8 -> TP4 writer election;
- TP4 -> TP8 replica fan-out;
- TP1/TP2/TP4/TP8 logical-head ownership;
- multi-head slicing for TP1 and TP2;
- invalid TP/head topology;
- item-length and buffer-bound validation;
- negative and out-of-range indices;
- missing and duplicate global layer IDs;
- one-sided metadata from new-to-old and old-to-new peers;
- equal-TP TP1/TP2 mixed-version rejection;
- MiniMax main-pool staging;
- PP global KV and index-state layer pairing;
- Mooncake registration wire compatibility.

Current branch validation:

```text
483 passed
1 skipped
219 subtests passed
pre-commit passed
git diff --check passed
```

## End-to-end validation

The feature was validated during development on two NVIDIA H20 nodes with the following topology:

```text
Prefill: MiniMax-M3-FP8, TP4 + PP2
Decode:  MiniMax-M3-FP8, TP8
Transfer backend: Mooncake
KV cache dtype: FP8 E4M3
Index-K layout: NHD
```

Correctness results:

- 32K input / 16 output tokens: generated text exactly matched the TP8-prefill baseline.
- 128K input / 16 output tokens: generated text exactly matched the TP8-prefill baseline.
- 3.5K input / 1500 output tokens / concurrency 32: 64/64 requests completed successfully.
- No silent fallback was used for heterogeneous TP state transfer.

## Performance observations

The index-K mapping itself is a correctness mechanism. The performance difference comes from the TP4+PP2 prefill topology that this PR enables.

In the tested H20 environment:

| Prefill workload | TP8 baseline | TP4+PP2 | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K input / C64 | 13,892.95 tok/s | 19,187.84 tok/s | +38.11% |
| 32K input / C16 | 13,018.51 tok/s | 18,140.99 tok/s | +39.35% |
| 128K input / C4 | 10,850.41 tok/s | 15,006.71 tok/s | +38.31% |

Single-request TTFT regressed for 3.5K-16K inputs, was close at 32K, and improved for 64K-128K inputs. This topology is therefore intended for long-context or throughput-oriented prefill workloads, not short-context latency-sensitive traffic.

These performance numbers are specific to the tested H20 configuration and are not claimed to generalize to other GPU architectures.

## Scope and limitations

This PR intentionally does not introduce a generic state-sharding framework.

Its scope is limited to:

- MiniMax-M3 sparse index-K state;
- MiniMax main-KV staging and global layer pairing required by PP;
- heterogeneous attention TP over Mooncake;
- NHD index-K cache layout.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: Add 8-node AllReduce/AllGather and MNVLS algorithm support to MSCCL++
body:
## Motivation

This PR extends the SGLang MSCCL++ integration to support 8-node deployments and adds support for NVLS-based algorithms when the topology and symmetric-memory requirements are satisfied, allowing MSCCL++ to take advantage of the NVLink fabric available on systems such as GB200.

## Modifications

The main changes are:

* Extended the MSCCL++ communicator and algorithm-selection infrastructure to support additional multi-node / multi-IPC-domain topologies.
* Added MSCCL++ AllGather and AllReduce 8 Node algorithm support.
* Added topology-aware configuration and tuning for AllReduce, AllGather, and ReduceScatter algorithms.
* Added support for NVLS-based native AllReduce algorithms when NVLS and symmetric memory are available.
* Added ReduceScatter + AllGather composition as an additional AllReduce candidate.
* Added `benchmark/kernels/all_gather/benchmark_mscclpp.py` to benchmark MSCCL++ AllGather against NCCL/PyNCCL in eager and CUDA Graph modes.
* Added support to symmetric memory mode on `benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/benchmark_mscclpp.py` benchmark.
* Updated the MSCCL++ Docker dependency from `sglang-v0.9.1` to `sglang-v0.10.1`.

## Accuracy Tests

Correctness was validated by comparing the MSCCL++ results against the PyTorch/NCCL reference implementation.

### AllReduce

AllReduce was validated using:

`benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/benchmark_mscclpp.py`

The benchmark uses BF16 inputs and compares both MSCCL++ eager and CUDA Graph outputs against the PyTorch/NCCL eager reference.

For the 8-node runs, I used:

```python
rtol = 2e-2
atol = 1e-5
```

instead of the default:

```python
rtol = 1.6e-2
atol = 1e-5
```

The slightly higher relative tolerance was needed because the BF16 reduction across 8 nodes can accumulate slightly different rounding error depending on the reduction order. The absolute tolerance was unchanged.

All tested message sizes passed with `rtol=2e-2, atol=1e-5`.

### AllGather

AllGather was validated using:

`benchmark/kernels/all_gather/benchmark_mscclpp.py`

MSCCL++ AllGather output was compared directly against the PyTorch/NCCL AllGather output, including validation that CUDA Graph replay uses updated input data.

All tested message sizes passed the correctness checks.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

All times below are in **microseconds (µs)**.

The most relevant comparison for inference using CUDA Graphs is **MSCCL++ graph vs. PyNCCL graph**.

title: [Bugfix] Fix unified-memory compaction gates and pending page reuse
body:
## Motivation

Unified-memory compaction can move pages while a disaggregation gate is closed, report stale schedulable capacity after a gate transition, or lose pending source pages when move batches share a completion event.

## Modifications

- Respect movement gates in FLOAT compaction.
- Cache schedulable capacity by allocator epoch and current gate state, including separate low/high states for FLOAT.
- Cache neighbor lookups and retain gated memo-consistency checks.
- Accumulate all pending source batches sharing a completion event.
- Add regression tests for gate transitions, memo reuse, neighbor lookup, and page reclamation.

**Labels:** Upstream = before the bug fixes; Initial fix = original lifecycle fixes with gated capacity recomputed on every query; Optimized fix = review follow-up that reuses the cache while gate state is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

### CPU

| Check | Optimized fix result |
|---|---|
| Selected regression suite | **249 tests + 1,513 subtests passed**, 0 failed; 10 GPU-only skips |
| 100 gate transitions | **0 stale values, 0 memo violations** |
| 2,000 queries with a stable gate | **1 recomputation, 1,999 cache hits** |
| Asymmetric FLOAT gates and neighbor-cache invalidation | Passed |
| Gated cache diagnostics and no-epoch neighbor fallback | Passed |

<details>
<summary>CPU test details</summary>

The regression suite covers 13 files in the local WSL environment. Stable-gate reuse and gated-diagnostic tests fail on Initial fix and pass on Optimized fix. The no-epoch fallback test catches a second-lookup failure in the initially supplied patch; the final local patch fixes it.

The separate three-version CPU campaign reproduces stale capacity on Upstream after closing a gate (`79 != 39`); Initial fix and Optimized fix pass the transition check.

</details>

### H100

| Model | Initial fix vs Optimized fix | Request errors |
|---|---|---:|
| Qwen3.5-4B | **Identical correctness results across 200 questions** (5/200 correct in both) | 0 |
| Mellum2-12B-A2.5B-Base | **100/100 output hashes match** across two runs per version | 0 |
| Inkling-0.6B-A0.6B | **100/100 output hashes match** across two runs per version | 0 |

<details>
<summary>H100 setup and scope</summary>

H100 80 GB, one server per GPU; unified memory, Triton attention, context length 8,192, chunked prefill 512, page size 1, CUDA graphs disabled.

Qwen: 200 GSM8K questions, five-shot, temperature 0, concurrency 4, maximum 2,048 output tokens; two normal runs per version. Pressure uses a 4,096-token budget. Mellum2 and Inkling: 100 prompts, temperature 0, concurrency 1, two runs per version.

Qwen's matching correctness sets do not imply identical generated text or high absolute accuracy.

Additional conditions: Qwen memory-pressure runs had zero request errors and differed on one question; the cause is not established. Two Optimized fix runs at concurrency 16 had zero request errors, without an Initial fix control.

These reported H100 runs tested the supplied review patch before the local rebase and no-epoch fallback correction. Serving was non-PD with no move gate installed; it does not validate distributed PD/RDMA safety.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### CPU

Host query cost in **µs/sweep**; lower is better. Each sweep queries every pool once. The three columns below come from the same CPU campaign.

| Layout | Gate | Upstream | Initial fix | Optimized fix | Initial fix → Optimized fix reduction |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FULL+Mamba | None | 0.205 | 0.691 | **0.364** | 47% |
| FULL+Mamba | Open | 0.205* | 1.916 | **0.392** | 80% |
| FULL+SWA | None | 0.163 | 0.274 | **0.244** | 11% |
| FULL+SWA | Open | 0.167* | 2.221 | **0.278** | 87% |
| FULL+SWA+Mamba | None | 0.202 | 0.698 | **0.354** | 49% |
| FULL+SWA+Mamba | Open | 0.212* | 1.889 | **0.379** | 80% |

*Upstream can return stale capacity after gate transitions; its gated timing is not a correctness-equivalent reference. These are allocator costs, not model-generation speedups.*

<details>
<summary>CPU benchmark setup and independent local confirmation</summary>

Three-version campaign: Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13; 200 warmup sweeps, then 20 samples of 2,000 sweeps, reporting medians.

PyTorch intra/inter-op thread, page size 1, lazy compaction. Each case uses 2,000 warmup sweeps and seven samples of 30,000 sweeps. Two sequential Initial fix/Optimized fix process pairs run in alternating order. Fresh-value and unchanged-state checks run outside timing.

| Layout / open gate | Initial fix (µs/sweep) | Optimized fix (µs/sweep) | Paired reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FULL+Mamba | 2.826 | 0.437 | **84.5%** |
| FULL+SWA | 2.870 | 0.434 | **84.9%** |
| FULL+SWA+Mamba | 4.466 | 0.825 | **81.5%** |

The local comparison uses both versions rebased onto the same upstream revision. Its results are separate measurements and are not pooled with the three-version campaign.

</details>

### H100

One hour per model at concurrency 32, covering three unified-memory pool layouts. Sustained-load results, not paired throughput gains.

| Model | Memory pool configuration | Successful requests | Request errors | Reported tokens/s | Retractions |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5-4B | FULL KV + Mamba state (2 pools) | 11,345 | 0 | 1,600 | 0 |
| Mellum2-12B | FULL KV + SWA KV (2 pools) | 7,995 | 0 | 1,130 | 0 |
| Inkling-0.6B | FULL KV + SWA KV + Mamba state (3 pools) | 77,199 | 0 | 954 | 0 |
| **Total** | **3 layouts** | **96,539** | **0** | — | **0** |

<details>
<summary>H100 load-test setup</summary>

One GPU per model, temperature 0.7, maximum 512 output tokens, five fixed GSM8K questions rotated with a 0.2-second interval. Monitoring runs every 60 seconds. All three servers remain alive at completion. The duration is three aggregate model-hours.

Zero request errors does not mean zero warning messages: Qwen logs include torchcodec/ffmpeg loading warnings.

</details>

title: [Bugfix] Harden DeepSeek V4 reasoning and DSML tool-call parsing
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek V4 streaming parsing can emit unstable non-string arguments, confuse protocol boundaries with literal text,
or report completion before malformed tool arguments are detected.

This PR preserves append-only argument semantics and validates actual tool frames. It does not repair arbitrary
generation or forbid protocol-related strings in otherwise valid content.

## Modifications

- Rebased onto `release/v0.5.20` (`94602c9c2b7cbdb8efd5c52802dac6a1c180089e`).
- Delay non-string DSML parameters until their values are complete; reject incomplete EOF rather than guess values.
- Validate DSML structure, duplicate parameters/JSON keys, non-finite JSON values, append-only prefixes, and the
  supplied tool schema by default. No coercion, missing-field insertion, or external schema retrieval.
- Preserve quoted/code literals and normalize redundant/orphan closers only at confirmed reasoning/tool boundaries.
- Remove the four experimental strict/schema/marker environment switches. Remove blanket marker-content rejection
  and its ordinary-text buffering, so legitimate protocol examples remain usable.
- Keep raw pre-parser output tracing independently opt-in: both `SGLANG_ENABLE_MODEL_OUTPUT_LOGGING=1` and
  `SGLANG_MODEL_OUTPUT_TRACE_DIR` are required. Output text is not redacted; request bodies and authentication headers
  are not copied directly into this trace.

Malformed or schema-invalid tool calls now fail explicitly instead of being forwarded as successful calls.
Ordinary text is not globally scanned for forbidden words. Middle-of-reasoning orphan markers remain outside the
confirmed-boundary cleanup scope.

## Accuracy Tests

No kernel, model-forward, or weight-quantization implementation is changed by this patch.

```bash
python3 -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/parser/test_reasoning_parser.py \
  test/registered/unit/function_call/test_deepseekv4_detector.py \
  test/registered/unit/test_model_output_trace.py
```

**230 tests passed, including 3,953 subtests**, on the v0.5.20 code and again inside the resulting image.
The final-image run copied test files only; runtime source hashes were verified unchanged.

Coverage includes chunk boundaries, EOF, malformed structure, mandatory schema checks, valid protocol literals,
reasoning boundaries, and disabled/enabled raw logging.

Live smoke validation on a four-GPU FP8 setup completed 5/6 fixed API probes successfully. A compound literal request
was rejected for incomplete DSML framing. Two additional, separately recorded diagnostics passed 1/2; one requested
literal string was generated with a different value. A separate opt-in trace run confirmed that the malformed frame
and changed string were already present in decoded output before the reasoning/tool parsers; replay reproduced the
observed parsing behavior.

These failures are retained rather than replaced with successful reruns. This is limited integration evidence, not
a model-accuracy claim. Earlier v0.5.18 task scores are not attributed to this revision.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No isolated TTFT, TPOT, throughput benchmark, or profiler run was performed. No speedup is claimed.
Validation and enabled tracing can add CPU/I/O work; tracing is disabled by default.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Black formatting and code-level documentation are updated. Full pre-commit, public-facing documentation, and

title: [3/N] elastic-ep: Recapture decode CUDA graphs after scale-up
body:
## Summary

This PR follows [PR #30553](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30553)
and adds FULL decode CUDA graph recapture after runtime Elastic EP scale-up.
Primary and joiner ranks rebuild their graphs for the expanded topology before
the new EP size is committed.

The existing scale-up API and EPLB lifecycle are unchanged.

## Changes

- Defer initial decode graph capture on joining ranks until they enter the
  expanded world.
- Finish the current sampling step, release the old graph state, and rebuild
  decode graphs with the expanded Mooncake WORLD and NIXL rank mask.
- Require primary and joiner ranks to resolve the same graph mode and capture
  configuration before recapture.
- Reuse SGLang's existing FULL decode graph initializer and synchronize all
  ranks before committing the scale operation.
- Add graph-stable FA3 MLA metadata for the validated DeepSeek path.
- Reject execution modes that do not use the supported decode finalization
  path.

## Configuration

Launch primary and joiner groups with the same resolved graph settings:

```text
--cuda-graph-backend-decode full
--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled
--cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16
```

The scale request and status API are inherited from the base scale-up PR.

## Known Limitations

- Only FULL decode graph recapture is supported. Prefill and piecewise graph
  recapture are outside this PR.
- Primary and joiner groups must use the same resolved CUDA graph
  configuration and effective capture sizes.
- Recapture is synchronous. Configuring more decode batch sizes increases the
  scale-finalization pause.
- The validated DeepSeek MLA path requires FlashAttention 3.
- Speculative decoding, embedding, diffusion, encoder-only execution, forward
  hooks, and PDMux split-prefill are not supported with Elastic EP recapture.
- The topology, scale-direction, and post-scale recovery limitations of the
  base scale-up PR still apply.
- Recapture releases the old decode graph pool before rebuilding. The deployment
  must still leave enough free GPU memory to capture the configured decode graph
  sizes; the manual tests use `--mem-fraction-static 0.5`.

## Test Plan

The manual Elastic EP tests cover direct, single-rank, mixed-cohort, and
repeated scale-up:

- `TestElasticScaleUp4To5CudaGraph`
- `TestElasticScaleUp4To6CudaGraph`
- `TestElasticScaleUp4To8CudaGraph`
- `TestElasticScaleUp4To5To6CudaGraph`

Each test captures decode batch sizes `1 2 4 8 16` and checks post-scale
generation, routed joiner traffic, input logprobs, and GSM8K correctness.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
python -m pytest -v -s \
  test/manual/ep/test_elastic_scale.py::TestElasticScaleUp4To5To6CudaGraph::test_scale_up_on_demand
```

The repeated 4-to-5-to-6 and direct 4-to-6 validations passed with all five
decode graph sizes captured on every participating rank.

## References

- [PR #30553](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30553) - EPLB after scale-up
- [PR #30164](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30164) - runtime EP scale-up
- [[RFC] Elastic EP Scale](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22788)

title: [NPU] Enable MXFP8 low-latency DeepEP dispatch for Fp8MoEMethod FP4 experts
body:
## Motivation

On NPU, FP4-expert models routed through Fp8MoEMethod ( is_fp4_expert=True , e.g. MiMo-V2.5-Pro with modelopt_fp4) delegate execution to NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod kernels via the ASCEND MoE runner. However, process_weights_after_loading only runs Fp8MoEMethod 's own body, so the DeepEP dispatcher quant config was never set — dispatch fell back to BF16 and a separate DynamicMxQuant kernel ran before every grouped matmul (~15ms/layer at 16K-token prefill).

The native FP4 path ( NPUW4A8MXFP4FusedMoEMethod , DSV4) already sets the same dispatcher config; the Fp8MoEMethod path was simply missing it.

## Modifications

- Declare the dispatch wire format as a DISPATCHER_QUANT_CONFIG class attribute on NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod ( low_latency=mxfp8 ; normal stays BF16 since A5 MXFP8 normal dispatch is intranode-only). The kernel that consumes the activations now owns the declaration, instead of each caller hand-writing platform-specific if/else patches.
- In Fp8MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading , pick the config up from the attached layer.w13_kernel when it declares one; otherwise keep the original checkpoint-dtype config. No _is_npu / is_fp4_expert branching — the attached kernel already encodes both.
- Reuse the same declaration in NPUW4A8MXFP4FusedMoEMethod , replacing its hand-written copy.
With this, A5 low-latency dispatch quantizes activations to MXFP8 in-kernel (with E8M0 block scales) and the GMMs consume them directly; the three previously duplicated config dicts collapse into a single kernel-owned declaration.

## Accuracy Tests

```
echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000
export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1

source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=300
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600
export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
export ASCEND_USE_FIA=1
export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=32
export DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2500
export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=20
export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=4096
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
export HCCL_HOST_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE=auto
export SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1

sglang serve \
        --model-path $MODEL_PATH \
        --served-model-name $MODEL_PATH \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --attention-backend ascend \
        --device npu \
        --mem-fraction-static 0.92 \
        --tp-size 8 --nnodes 1 --node-rank 0 \
        --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-total-tokens 600000 \
        --max-running-requests 32 \
        --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto \
        --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 \
        --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \
        --speculative-draft-model-path $DFLASH_PATH \
        --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8 \
        --dp-size 2 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
```

title: [NPU] Gate arch35 block-FP8 -> MXFP8 requantization behind SGLANG_NPU_ARCH35_REQUANT_BLOCK_FP8
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #39823. That PR made plain block-FP8 checkpoints (fp32 block scales) on arch35 (Atlas A5) requantize to MXFP8 at load time unconditionally, so dense linears run on the native quantized GEMM instead of the Triton emulation path.

As raised in the post-merge review of #39823: fp8 per-block quantization with fp32 scaling factors is semantically different from MXFP8. Only DeepSeek-style UE8M0 checkpoints can be converted losslessly (a 128×128 block's power-of-two scale can be duplicated to its 1×32 sub-blocks exactly). For plain fp32-scale checkpoints, the load-time conversion is a lossy re-quantization (dequant to BF16 → npu_dynamic_mx_quant , granularity 128×128 → 1×32, scales rounded to powers of two), which changes the checkpoint numerics:

- Dataset-level evals are largely insensitive to this error magnitude
- Training-time consumers are not: e.g. RL rollouts served by sglang vs. reference logprobs computed elsewhere can see importance-ratio drift from the systematic numerics change
The safe default should be to serve the checkpoint as-is; the native-GEMM path should be opt-in for deployments that have validated accuracy for their workload.

## Modifications

- environ.py : add SGLANG_NPU_ARCH35_REQUANT_BLOCK_FP8 (default False )
- Fp8LinearMethod.process_weights_after_loading : only enter process_npu_arch35_mxfp8_linear_weights for UE8M0 checkpoints (lossless re-layout, unchanged) or when the env var is set; plain block-FP8 checkpoints now fall through to the generic path and keep their original layout
- fp8_utils._dispatch_auto_backend : select npu_w8a8_mxfp8_linear under the same condition ( act_scale_ue8m0 or the env var) — this must stay in sync with the weight-layout gate, otherwise the kernel and layout mismatch. arch35 + plain block-FP8 now resolves to triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear
- w8a8_mxfp8.py : docstring updated to document the gate

## Accuracy Tests

No numeric output changes by design:

- Default path (env unset) restores the pre-#39823 bit-faithful serving path for fp32-scale checkpoints — Triton emulation on the untouched checkpoint layout
- UE8M0 checkpoints are unaffected (lossless path, unconditional)
- env=1 is opt-in and numerically identical to what #39823 shipped
Dispatch verified locally for all three combinations (mocked is_npu_arch35 ): env-unset + fp32 scales → triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear ; env=1 + fp32 scales → npu_w8a8_mxfp8_linear ; env-unset + ue8m0 → npu_w8a8_mxfp8_linear . Also verified the fall-through path stays clean: requant_block_scale_ue8m0_for_deepgemm is a no-op without DeepGEMM, and block_fp8_as_mxfp8 requires UE8M0 + 32-wide K blocks so it cannot mis-enable on plain block-FP8.

Behavior matrix on arch35:

| Checkpoint | Env var | Weight layout | GEMM |
|---|---|---|---|
| UE8M0 (DeepSeek V3.1+) | any | MXFP8 re-layout (lossless) | native (unchanged) |
| fp32 block scales | unset (default) | plain block-FP8 | Triton emulation (pre-#39823 behavior) |
| fp32 block scales | `=1` | MXFP8 (lossy requant) | native (perf path, as merged in #39823) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None — this PR adds no new fast path. The perf characteristics of each path are unchanged from #39823: native MXFP8 GEMM vs. Triton emulation (~100ms per large-M linear) applies only when the env var is explicitly enabled.

title: [feat][NPU] Add not needs_cpu_seq_lens for dsa modules
body: ## Motivation Currently, `AscendAttnBackend` inherits `needs_cpu_seq_lens=True`. However, for DSA models that don't actually require `seq_lens_cpu`, we can bypass this dependency to reduce—or even eliminate—the CPU-bound bubbles. This PR sets `needs_cpu_seq_lens=False` for `AscendAttnBackend` when running DSA models. ## Modifications - Added a `needs_cpu_seq_lens` member variable to both `AscendAttnBackend` and `AscendAttnMultiStepDraftBackend`. It is set to False when running DSA models without the HybridSWA feature, which enables the optimization introduced by this PR. - Added branches for `needs_cpu_seq_lens is False` at device synchronization points within `AscendAttnBackend`, allowing device-side tensors to be used directly in computations. - Moved the `all_reduce` communication in `EAGLEDraftNpuGraphRunner.can_run_graph` to the CPU to eliminate blocking waits. ~~This PR builds upon PR #36472 and should be merged after it.~~ The predecessor to this PR is #21895. Both aim to eliminate the CPU-bound overhead during Draft execution, and both are exclusively applicable to DSA models. title: [PP+PD] Fix #38206 Reduce bootstrap consensus latency
body:
## Motivation In current implementation, PP+PD bootstrap ready takes a full round-trip from PP0 to PP(n-1). This contributes to TTFT in large pipeline deployement, e.g. `pp_size=8`. This has been reported in #34815 and analyzed in depth in #38206. PR #36613 was a different solution to the issue. This PR proposes an alternative approach. It introduces `PPConsensusStore`, which is simply a `Dict` shared among PP ranks. All PP ranks update their bootstrap status into the map. PP0 collects others bootstrap status and determine bootstrap readiness. PP0 broadcast its decision to other PP ranks using `pp_sync`. This completely removes two-round consensus for bootstrap readiness. This PR is working in progress. Here are limitations: - Only works with mooncake transfer engine. Other transfer engine is not fixed yet. - ~~`TCPStore` lacks of batch and non-blocking operation. We may need to implement our own store.~~ - ~~Only bootstrap consensus is removed. Other consensus processes are kept unchanged.~~. This will be done in follow-up PRs. Discussion and advices are welcome. ## Modifications 1. Add `PPConsensusStore`, which helps PP0 to gather boostrap ready events from other PP ranks. 2. Add `MooncakeKVSender.poll_pp_consensus`. This function collects bootstrap events of other PP ranks, and 3. In `pop_bootstrapped`, PP0 calls `poll_pp_consensus` to collect bootstrap status from others, and then propagate decision to other PP ranks. 4. Remove two-round bootstrap consensus at prefill side. ## Accuracy Tests Tested SWE bench verfieid with DSv4 flash, pd disaggregation, P pp_size=4 tp_size=1, D pp_size=1 tp_size=4. Baseline: 387/500 This PR: 385/500

title: [core] Root the JIT kernel cache under SGLANG_CACHE_DIR
body:
## Motivation

#19612 asked for all JIT/precompilation caches to live under one configurable root. #32434 delivered this for Triton, Inductor, FlashInfer, the CUDA driver and DeepGEMM — but SGLang's **own** JIT kernel cache still falls back to the hardcoded `~/.cache/sglang/jit` (`build_key_dir` in `python/sglang/kernels/jit/utils/compile/cache.py`), so setting `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR=/mnt/persist` moves every third-party cache except this one. The env-vars reference doc also enumerates the compiled-kernel caches that follow `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR` without listing the JIT kernel cache, so code and docs currently disagree.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/jit/utils/compile/cache.py`: when `SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` is unset, derive the fallback from `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR` (`$SGLANG_CACHE_DIR/jit`); an explicit `SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` still wins. The default resolution stays byte-identical to before (`~/.cache/sglang/jit`).
- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: comment updated to match.
- `docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx`: `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`'s description now includes the JIT kernel cache; new row documenting `SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` with default `` `{SGLANG_CACHE_DIR}/jit` ``.
- `test/registered/kernels/test_jit_cache.py`: two tests — the unset-var fallback lands under `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`, and an explicit `SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` wins over it. (The file is already in the CPU-registered suite.)

Audit note (from re-reading the #19612 thread): outlines' own disk cache (there is a kill-switch `SGLANG_DISABLE_OUTLINES_DISK_CACHE`, but no location redirect) and `multimodal_gen`'s `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_CACHE_ROOT` (defaults to `~/.cache/sgl_diffusion`) also sit outside `SGLANG_CACHE_DIR`; both look like separate scope, but I'm happy to follow up if maintainers want them unified here.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — no model/kernel numerics touched; path resolution only.

title: [AMD] fix: Wan2.2 crash due to Triton kernel compilation
body: ## Summary On gfx1250 with the Triton that ships in the ROCm SDK, `fuse_scale_shift_kernel` silently computed `x * scale + shift` instead of `x * (1 + scale) + shift`, dropping the identity term from adaLN modulation in every DiT block of every diffusion step. Output was wrong but plausible-looking — no crash, no warning. This gates the affected modulation math to fp32 on gfx1250 only. All other targets keep byte-identical codegen. ## Root cause The bug is in Triton's instruction encoding, not in SGLang. gfx1250 is the only target where Triton lowers bf16 elementwise math to packed `v_pk_*_bf16`; every other target promotes to fp32 first. Comparing the two Triton builds for `bf16 + 1.0`: ``` upstream 76940ad3 (fixed): v_pk_add_bf16 v1, v1, 1.0 op_sel:[0,1] ROCm SDK 4cff872c (broken): v_pk_add_bf16 v1, v1, 1.0 op_sel_hi:[1,0] ``` The inline constant `1.0` is the **fp32** pattern `0x3F800000`. Its high half `0x3F80` is bf16 `1.0`; its low half is `0x0000`. The SDK build selects the low half for `src1` in both lanes, so the addend is bf16 zero and the operation becomes a no-op. This affects `+`, `-` and `*` against any AMDGPU hardware inline float constant — `±0.5, ±1.0, ±2.0, ±4.0` — and nothing else. Ordinary literals (`1.5`, `100.0`) are encoded as a packed bf16 pair and are correct; tensor operands are correct. In this kernel `scale_constant` is exactly `1.0`, so it hit the broken case. The bug is fixed in upstream Triton, and `3865efc` (`[AMD] support gfx1250 on ROCM 10`) already moved the gfx1250 image onto a build that carries the fix (`BUILD_TRITON=1`, `TRITON_COMMIT=76940ad3`). This change keeps SGLang correct on the SDK Triton as well, so correctness no longer depends on which Triton the image happens to ship. ## Why fp32 and not `tl.full` `tl.full` looks like it should keep the constant out of the immediate, but it does not — LLVM folds the splat straight back in. Measured on the broken build: | form | result | emitted ISA | |---|---|---| | `scale_constant + scale` | wrong | `v_pk_add_bf16` + inline const | | `tl.full(...) + scale` | wrong | `v_pk_add_bf16` + inline const | | fp32 promote | **correct** | no packed bf16 immediate | fp32 promotion was the only form that produced clean ISA. It also keeps a single rounding on store, matching what the layernorm scale/shift kernels in this same file already do. ## Scope Gated behind `is_gfx1250_supported()` and passed as a `tl.constexpr`, so Triton resolves the branch at compile time — no runtime branch, and the `else` arm is the original code verbatim. NVIDIA, XPU, gfx942 and gfx950 compile to exactly what they did before, including the `tl.full` splat, so their numerics stay bit-identical. `is_gfx1250_supported()` is `lru_cache`d and returns `False` on non-HIP builds without touching CUDA. The kernel is shared by 11 DiT families, so this is not Wan-only: `wanvideo`, `causal_wanvideo`, `hunyuanvideo`, `hunyuan3d`, `qwen_image`, `glm_image`, `joy_image`, `helios`, `lingbot_world`, `longlive2`, `mova_video_dit`. They reach it through `LayerNormScaleShift` / `RMSNormScaleShift` / `ScaleResidualRMSNormScaleShift` with the default `scale_constant=1.0`. The VAE is unaffected — adaLN is a transformer construct, and an ISA scan over a full Wan2.2 run (1307 kernels, 118 using packed bf16) found this kernel as the only affected one. ## Testing After this PR is applied, the video can be played. Extracted pic comparison as below: Tested on rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm10-mi45x-test-triton4cff872c-20260923. Existing unit test `test_scale_shift_4d_matches_torch`, run against both Triton builds: | Configuration | Result | |---|---| | ROCm SDK Triton (broken), with fix | 16 passed | | Upstream Triton (fixed), with fix | 16 passed — no regression | | ROCm SDK Triton, fix reverted | **3 failed** (the bf16 + `scale_constant=1` cases) | | ROCm SDK Triton, gate forced off | **3 failed** — confirms the `else` arm is the original path | End-to-end Wan2.2-T2V-A14B on the broken SDK Triton (720×1280, 193 frames, 8 steps, seed 42) completed cleanly and matches a known-good baseline generated on the fixed Triton: correlation **0.991**, PSNR **29.3 dB**, mean abs diff 4.3/255. A dropped identity term collapses structure, so this margin is rounding and sampling non-determinism, not lost conditioning. Performance is unchanged. `bench_scale_shift_4d.py`, 3 runs each way, medians: 117.7 vs 119.9 µs (wan), 16.23 vs 16.24 µs (longlive). Within-group spread was ±20% on the larger workloads, so those deltas are noise — the kernel reads three tensors and writes one with no reuse, so it is bandwidth-bound and the extra `v_cvt` ops hide behind memory latency. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. title: [AMD] [GLM5] Add opt-in PTPC FP8 projections on gfx950
body:
## Motivation

The `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` checkpoint keeps the q_a, kv_a, q_b, and o attention projections in BF16. They are represented by three modules: `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `q_b_proj`, and `o_proj`.

This PR adds a default-off PTPC FP8 path on gfx950 using per-token activation scales and per-channel weight scales. BF16 remains the default and fallback.

## Modifications

- Add `SGLANG_DSA_FP8_PROJ_GEMM` as the single opt-in switch; the path also requires Aiter, gfx950, and the GLM DSA model type.
- Cache bpreshuffled FP8 weights while retaining the original BF16 parameters for fallback, so enabled projections hold both copies.
- Fold q_b input quantization into the existing q/k RMSNorm. o_proj uses a standalone per-token quantization of the attention output.
- Keep `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` on tuned Aiter BF16 for M≤512 and use PTPC FP8 for M>512; the threshold was selected empirically on MI355X. q_b_proj and o_proj use FP8 whenever the flag is enabled.
- Fall back to Triton quantization helpers on Aiter builds without the HIP fused per-token RMSNorm kernel.
- Add CPU unit coverage for the enablement gate, default-off BF16 behavior, weight repacking, PTPC dispatch, rollback, and the M=512/513 boundary.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [AMD] [GLM5] Fuse the ROCm DSA indexer q/k prep into aiter's single kernel
body:
## Summary On ROCm the DSA indexer spends 11 kernels per decode layer on q/k prep. This PR collapses most of that into one aiter kernel. * `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache` does k LayerNorm + RoPE + fp8 quant + paged index-k store, q RoPE + fp8 quant, and the head-gate scale in a single launch — six kernels become one. Like the CUDA fused path it drops the Hadamard rotation, which is logit-preserving and only shifts fp8 quantisation error. Prefill drops it too, since prefill writes the index-K cache decode reads back and the two must agree on basis. * `wk` and `weights_proj` are folded into one `wk_weights_proj` GEMM. This needs only the concatenated weight, no fused kernel, but was gated on CUDA; it now runs on CUDA or HIP and is numerically identical to the split projections. * The aiter kernel is tuned for decode's one-token-per-sequence shape and costs about twice what it replaces at prefill widths, so it is gated to decode. It also requires gfx95x, `SGLANG_USE_AITER`, and an aiter build exporting the symbol — a capability probe, not a preference: anything outside the envelope falls back to the existing path. CUDA and NPU are unchanged. Decode indexer on GLM-5.2 / MI355X: **11 kernels / 70.8 us per layer → 5 kernels / 41.4 us (−41.5%)**, which closes the MI355X-vs-B200 indexer gap from 2.55x to 1.49x. Drive-by fix: define the module-level `_use_dsa_indexer_fusion` that `lora_manager.py` already imports but nothing defined, so an indexer-targeted LoRA adapter raised `ImportError` instead of the intended `ValueError`. ## Test plan MI355X TP4, GLM-5.2-MXFP4, fp8 KV, `chunked_prefill=16384`, DSA backend triton, i8192 / o1024, one run per point. Baseline is the same AMD GLM-5.2 stack without this PR (#30519, #30575, #30715, #30808, #31323, #31324, #32888, plus ROCm/aiter#4453). | conc | Output tok/s | Median ITL (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 4 | 323.3 → 335.9 (+3.9%) | 10.61 → 10.16 (−4.2%) | 366.7 → 367.6 (+0.2%) | | 8 | 465.3 → 482.3 (+3.6%) | 14.02 → 13.43 (−4.2%) | 379.1 → 379.8 (+0.2%) | | 16 | 731.5 → 762.9 (+4.3%) | 15.73 → 14.86 (−5.5%) | 378.0 → 383.3 (+1.4%) | | 32 | 1044.3 → 1081.1 (+3.5%) | 19.39 → 18.37 (−5.3%) | 393.7 → 389.5 (−1.1%) | | 64 | 1342.4 → 1382.2 (+3.0%) | 25.33 → 24.03 (−5.1%) | 631.6 → 615.6 (−2.5%) | ITL improves −4.2% to −5.5% at every concurrency, matching the 29.4 us/layer the kernel table predicts over the 21 layers that run the indexer (0.62 ms per decode forward). TTFT is flat, which is the check that matters given the kernel is decode-only. GSM8K (1200 questions): 0.928 baseline, 0.934 this PR. The index-K cache is bit-exact against the unfused path across both `preshuffle` and `scale_fmt`; the q fp8 payload differs by 1 ULP on 0.10% of elements, because aiter multiplies by the reciprocal rather than dividing.
Per-layer decode indexer kernels, and why the aiter kernel is decode-only | baseline | us | this PR | us | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `hgemm_16x64x128x3` (wk) | 6.59 | `hgemm_16x64x128x3` (merged wk_weights_proj) | 6.50 | | `hgemm_16x64x64x6` (weights_proj) | 5.30 | — | — | | `Layernorm2dFwd` | 4.19 | `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache` | 5.60 | | `kn_entry_2c_sbhd_cached_indirect` (RoPE) | 8.78 | | | | `fast_hadamard_transform_kernel` | 4.43 | | | | `_hadamard_quant_kernel` | 4.55 | | | | `indexer_k_quant_and_cache_kernel` | 4.19 | | | | `triton_poi_fused_mul_unsqueeze_0` | 4.18 | | | | `wv_splitk_small` (q proj) | 5.70 | `wv_splitk_small` | 5.95 | | `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle` | 4.34 | `fp8_paged_mqa_logits_preshuffle` | 4.46 | | `topk_transform_decode_kernel` | 18.60 | `topk_transform_decode_kernel` | 18.93 | | **total** | **70.8** | **total** | **41.4** | Of the 29.4 us/layer saved, 5.4 is the merged projection and 21.3 is six kernels becoming one; downstream topk and logits move by 0.1–0.3 us, which is noise. With the aiter kernel enabled for prefill too, the prefill indexer went from 1614.5 up to 1780.5 us/layer: the fused kernel alone costs 300.4 us/layer against the 162.8 of the six it replaces, and drags downstream topk and logits ~8% each. Gating it to decode gives prefill 1519.6 us/layer (−5.9%), since prefill still benefits from the merged projection and from dropping the Hadamard.

title: [MiniMax-M3] Fix PP tc_piecewise position padding
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax-M3 fails during pipeline-parallel prefill when using the
`tc_piecewise` CUDA Graph backend together with fused QKNorm/RoPE.

After a hidden state is forwarded to a later PP stage, its token dimension
contains only the actual local tokens, while `positions` may still retain the
tail padding of the CUDA Graph bucket.

For example:

```text
hidden_states.shape[0] = 3372
positions.shape[0]     = 3584
```

Passing tensors with these inconsistent token dimensions to the fused
QKNorm/RoPE kernel causes a shape mismatch.

## Changes

Trim tail-padded `positions` to the PP-local hidden-state token count before
calling the MiniMax fused QKNorm/RoPE kernels.

The normalization is applied only when:

- the prefill CUDA Graph backend is `tc_piecewise`; and
- fused QKNorm/RoPE or grouped fused QKNorm/RoPE is enabled.

```python
if positions.shape[0] > hidden_states.shape[0]:
    positions = positions[: hidden_states.shape[0]]
```

## Scope

This change is intentionally limited to the MiniMax-M3 fused QKNorm/RoPE
prefill path.

It does not affect:

- decode;
- non-`tc_piecewise` prefill;
- non-fused QKNorm/RoPE paths;
- the NPU-specific forward path;
- other model implementations;
- requests where `positions` and `hidden_states` already have matching lengths.

## Why trimming is correct

The extra entries are tail padding introduced by the CUDA Graph bucket and do
not correspond to real hidden states on the current PP stage.

Trimming removes only those padded entries and preserves every real token
position.

## Tests

No new test file is introduced. Regression coverage is added to an existing
MiniMax test file.

Validation:

```text
3 passed
pre-commit: passed for all modified Python files
git diff --check: passed
```

## Reproduction configuration

The issue was reproduced with:

```text
Model: MiniMax-M3
Prefill topology: TP4 + PP2
CUDA Graph backend: tc_piecewise
QKNorm/RoPE: fused
```

title: [Docs] Add tested Ascend A2 deployment and A3 reference for MiniMax-M2.5
body:
## Motivation

Add Ascend deployment choices to the MiniMax-M2.5 cookbook: a tested A2 eight-device configuration and a separately labelled A3 reference. Related task: https://github.com/Ascend/sglang/issues/1215

HiDevLab supplied A2 multi-card resources; A3 multi-card resources are unavailable for this contribution. The tested scope therefore uses A2. Hardware and performance equivalence to A3 is not implied; acceptance of the adjusted task scope remains subject to maintainer review.

## Changes

- Add an A2 selector for 8 x Ascend 910B4 / 32 GiB, TP8, ModelSlim W8A8 main weights, BF16, one request at a time, and no EAGLE3 draft model. Model/tokenizer directories are editable and shell-quoted.
- Use the verified A2 settings `--mem-fraction-static 0.96 --max-total-tokens 4096`, with context 4096, chunked prefill 128, and CUDA graph/radix cache disabled.
- Keep the A3 8-card / 16-die W8A8 + EAGLE3 recipe explicitly unvalidated, with separate prerequisites and reference evaluation instructions.
- Document launch settings, observed versions, successful requests, the earlier capacity failure and its verified correction, and interpretation limits.
- Add 13 command-generator regression tests for A2 settings, NVIDIA/AMD behavior, and platform transitions.

## A2 hardware validation

September 22: main weights loaded, eight-rank HCCL/BF16 checks passed, and three chat answers stopped naturally with a 512-token output budget.

September 23 baseline: static fraction 0.95 allocated only 896 KV tokens despite configured context 4096. Inputs of 1024 and 2048 tokens were rejected with a maximum input length of 890. A separate JSON answer exhausted a 128-token output budget; it was inconclusive rather than a correctness failure.

September 23 corrected run: static fraction 0.96 plus an explicit 4096-token pool cap produced an actual 4096-token KV pool on all eight ranks. TP0 reported 1.36 GB available after pool allocation. Two warmups and six simple answer checks completed; all six answers passed and stopped naturally with a 512-token output budget. Six native serial probes each generated exactly 128 tokens:

| Exact input tokens | Output tokens | Observed first output (s) | End-to-end (s) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 64 | 128 | 0.494 | 29.970 |
| 128 | 128 | 0.478 | 29.313 |
| 256 | 128 | 0.700 | 30.193 |
| 1024 | 128 | 2.103 | 32.165 |
| 2048 | 128 | 4.218 | 34.451 |
| 3500 | 128 | 10.055 | 39.803 |

The native probes intentionally ignore EOS and stop at the requested length. These are single client-observed measurements at concurrency 1, not standardized throughput or latency percentiles. First output is measured from SSE events; buffering and multi-token chunks affect its interpretation. Prompt plus output must fit the available context and KV capacity. No higher concurrency or larger context is claimed.

The complete client run finished in 394.3 seconds; post-test health returned HTTP 200. Raw streams, launch settings, runtime logs, and cleanup evidence were archived locally. The server process group exited, all eight NPUs had no running processes, and MiniMax1215A2 was shut down.

Runtime: SGLang 0.5.14.dev172+gf308abc05, Torch 2.10.0+cpu, TorchNPU 2.10.0, Transformers 5.8.1, kernel 2026.5.1, CANN 9.0.0, driver 25.5.2. The supplied source tree had packaging-file modifications. Image digest and immutable model revision were not captured.

## Accuracy and performance scope

No GPQA score is claimed. These simple answer checks do not establish general model accuracy. Standardized throughput, sustained stability, tool calling, and A3 hardware validation remain untested. The documented A3 50 ms TPOT and GPQA baseline are upstream references, not results of this PR. This remains a draft pending review of the adjusted task scope and remaining evaluation requirements.

## Validation

All 13 command-generator tests, the shared cookbook configuration check, applicable pre-commit checks, Mintlify build validation, and git diff --check pass for this revision. Local preview previously verified the A2 selector and generated command. Independent review checked numerical claims against the archived raw results and found no blocking issue.

The previous revision's GitHub Lint workflow passed. Extra CI stopped at `Block draft PR`; that is not a passing runtime test. Refer to the latest commit checks for this revision's status. Stock site-wide broken-link scanning on Windows has a reproduced path-separator issue; the Linux GitHub documentation checks are tracked separately.

title: [Docs] Fix three stale references: llama4 tool-call parser, --target-lora-modules, /update_weights route
body:
Three stale references in the docs, each directly checkable against current runtime sources:

- `tool_parser.mdx` lists `llama4` as a `--tool-call-parser` value, but `ToolCallParserEnum` has no such key and `server_args.py` builds the argparse choices from those keys, so `--tool-call-parser llama4` is rejected during argument parsing. It is not a deprecated alias (`deprecated_tool_call_parsers` maps only `qwen25`, `glm45`). Llama 4 uses `pythonic`, which the same table already documents; this drops the dead row.
- `lora.mdx` calls a flag `--target-lora-modules` in a comment; the real flag is `--lora-target-modules` (`server_args.py`). Surrounding prose already uses the correct name.
- `native_api.mdx` references `/update_weights`, which is not a registered route (`http_server.py` has `/update_weights_from_disk`, `_from_tensor`, `_from_distributed`, `_from_ipc`), so a POST 404s.
