title: [Spec] Let NEXTN and the DFlash2 selector reuse a packed target lm_head
body:
## Motivation

A compressed-tensors checkpoint that quantizes `lm_head` in the pack-quantized INT format stores the head as `weight_packed` / `weight_scale` / `weight_shape`; the module has no `.weight`. The target serves fine on its own, but both speculative paths that borrow the target head refuse it:

- `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN` dies at startup in `get_embed_and_head`: `AttributeError: 'ParallelLMHead' object has no attribute 'weight'`.
- `--speculative-algorithm DFLASH` with a DFlash2 draft dies on the server's own warm-up request, so the server never becomes ready: `DFlash2 selector requires a dense FP16/BF16/FP32 target lm_head or a supported lm_head.quant_method.`

Both come from `should_apply_lm_head_quant_method` refusing any head without `.weight`. That check arrived with #27906 to keep the ModelOpt `lm_head.weight.dtype` reads safe. A packed head is exactly the case where `quant_method.apply` is the only way to get logits, and the target's own `LogitsProcessor` already does that through its trailing fallback branch. #35496 added the quant-method path to the DFlash2 selector, but the gate never let a packed head reach it. GGUF heads (`qweight`, no `.weight`) sit in the same position.

Reproduced on main (525f140) with `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` quantized by llm-compressor so that `lm_head` is pack-quantized; the recipe is under Accuracy Tests.

## Modifications

- `layers/logits_processor.py`: `should_apply_lm_head_quant_method` no longer requires `.weight`. Only the three ModelOpt methods, whose branches read `lm_head.weight.dtype`, are refused when the tensor is missing. In `_compute_lm_head` a head without a dense weight now takes the `quant_method.apply` branch and keeps the fp32 activation cast the old fallback gave it under `--enable-fp32-lm-head` (that flag with a marlin-packed head was and stays unsupported); the old trailing fallback becomes an explicit error, since every head that used to reach it is now admitted by the gate. Only the second, bound definition of the gate is changed; #39707 removes the shadowed first copy.
- `models/qwen3_5.py`, `models/qwen3_5_text.py`: `get_embed_and_head` hands out `None` for a packed head instead of reading `.weight`. `EagleDraftWorker.init_lm_head` then shares the whole module through `set_lm_head_from_target`, which `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP` already implements.
- `speculative/spec_utils.py`: `lm_head_is_packed` (no `.weight`, and not a `PPMissingLayer`). `speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py`: when the target head is packed and the draft cannot take the module (no `set_lm_head_from_target`, or a hot-token map), fail with a clear error instead of decoding with the draft's own head; the PP+spec branch, which shares the tensor only, fails the same way.
- Out of scope: `dspark_draft_sampler.py`, `deepseek_v4_dspark.py` and `domino_utils.py` still read `lm_head.weight` and keep failing on a packed head as before. DSpark's `project_through_lm_head` goes through the gate and is fixed along the way.
- `speculative/multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py`, `speculative/frozen_kv_mtp_worker_v2.py`: these two share the head tensor only, so they fail with the same clear error on a packed target instead of handing the draft `head=None`. `qwen3_5_text.set_embed_and_head` accepts `None` for either half, matching what its accessor can now return.
- Tests: the two DFlash2 selector cases in `test_dflash_logits.py` are parametrized over a head that keeps packed bytes under `.weight` and one that has no `.weight` at all. New CPU file `test_spec_packed_target_lm_head.py` covers the gate (admission, and refusal of each ModelOpt method without a dense weight), the fp32 cast, the error path, the three accessors, and `init_lm_head` sharing the module, refusing when it cannot, and still accepting a pipeline stage without a head. On main 8 of the 23 cases fail; the rest pin behaviour that must not change.

## Accuracy Tests

Checkpoints, both built from the official weights with llm-compressor's model-free PTQ. The target has a W4A16 body and a W8A16 `lm_head`, both pack-quantized; the in-checkpoint MTP layer stays BF16:

```python
# llmcompressor==0.14.0, data-free round-to-nearest, runs on CPU
from compressed_tensors.quantization import QuantizationConfig, QuantizationScheme
from compressed_tensors.quantization.quant_scheme import W4A16, W8A16
from llmcompressor import model_free_ptq

model_free_ptq(
    model_stub="Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B",
    save_directory="Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16-lm_head-W8A16",
    config=QuantizationConfig(config_groups={
        "lm_head": QuantizationScheme(targets=["re:.*lm_head$"], **W8A16),  # first match wins
        "body": QuantizationScheme(targets=["Linear"], **W4A16),
    }),
    ignore=["re:.*visual.*", "re:.*mtp.*", "re:.*in_proj_(a|b)$", "re:.*conv1d.*",
            "re:.*norm.*", "re:.*embed_tokens.*"],
)
```

The reference is the same call without the `lm_head` group and with `"lm_head"` added to `ignore`, so its head stays BF16. DFLASH uses the official `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` draft.

One RTX 6000 Ada (48 GB, TP=1), `--disable-overlap-schedule`. NEXTN: steps 3, top-k 1, draft tokens 4. DFLASH: block size 8. Accuracy is SGLang's own GSM8K eval, one request at a time so completions can be compared across runs:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-threads 1 --temperature 0 --max-tokens 512
```

| target `lm_head` | branch | spec | result | GSM8K (200) | accept length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BF16 | main | none | serves | 0.960 | |
| BF16 | main | NEXTN | serves | 0.970 | 3.629 |
| BF16 | main | DFLASH | serves | 0.970 | 6.035 |
| W8A16 packed | main | none | serves | 0.965 | |
| W8A16 packed | main | NEXTN | `AttributeError: 'ParallelLMHead' object has no attribute 'weight'` at startup | | |
| W8A16 packed | main | DFLASH | `RuntimeError: DFlash2 selector requires a dense ...` on the server's warm-up request | | |
| W8A16 packed | this PR | NEXTN | serves | 0.965 | 3.629 |
| W8A16 packed | this PR | DFLASH | serves; the selector is folded into the draft CUDA graph | 0.970 | 6.035 |

Accept length is the mean of the scheduler's `accept len` over every decode-log window of the run, bonus token included. The `sglang:spec_accept_length` gauge only holds the last window, so it is not used here.

Speculative decoding matches non-speculative decoding only up to numerics, so completions are compared against the same checkpoint without speculation. With the packed head, 172/200 NEXTN and 167/200 DFLASH completions match the packed-head target decoding on its own. On main, the BF16-head target matches its own non-speculative run in 167/200 (NEXTN) and 166/200 (DFLASH) completions.

Unit tests (CPU): `test_spec_packed_target_lm_head.py` + `test_dflash_logits.py` 23 passed (8 fail on main); `test_eagle_draft_extend_logits.py`, `test_eagle_worker_v2_topk1_fastpath.py`, `models/test_qwen3_5_packed_weight_loader.py`, `models/test_qwen3_5_modelopt_fp4.py` 31 passed; the `lm_head_guard` cases of `model_loader/test_modelopt_loader.py` 4 passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change for dense or ModelOpt heads: the gate returns what it returned before and the same kernel runs. A packed head goes from refusing to start to serving; the draft calls the same `quant_method.apply` the target already runs for its own logits. I have no clean timing for it yet, since the GPU these runs used was shared with other jobs.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Spec] Build DFlash draft layers under their checkpoint names and refuse tensors the draft would drop
body:
## Motivation

A quantized DFlash draft is built from its quantization config by module name and loaded by tensor name, and the two did not see the same names. `DFlashDraftModel` gave every decoder layer an empty prefix unless the checkpoint was a Nemotron 3.5 draft, so quantization matching saw a bare `qkv_proj`, `o_proj`, `gate_up_proj`, `down_proj` for all layers. Name-based `ignore` entries such as `re:.*self_attn\.q_proj$` never applied, the attention projections were built as quantized layers, and `load_weights` then dropped the checkpoint's BF16 `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` tensors without a word because the fused module had no `.weight` to put them in. The packed weight went into attention uninitialized. With the W8A16 draft from the recipe below, built from the official `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`, main hits a device-side assert (`srcIndex < srcSelectDimSize` in `indexSelectSmallIndex`) on the server's own warm-up request, after a startup that only logged `DFLASH fused KV materialization disabled: quantized qkv_proj is not supported for this path`.

The second half of the same problem is `fc`: outside the Nemotron path it was a plain `nn.Linear`, so a checkpoint that quantizes `fc` (`fc.weight_packed` / `weight_scale` / `weight_shape`, or FP8 `fc.weight` + `weight_scale_inv`) had those tensors dropped the same way and `fc` kept its random init, so the draft would propose from a random projection of the target's hidden states. Several of the quantized DFlash2 drafts published on the Hub for Qwen3.8-27B quantize `fc` as well.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/models/dflash.py` only:

- Every decoder layer is built with `layers.{i}` (or `{prefix}.layers.{i}`), not just Nemotron drafts, so a quantization config matches the same names the checkpoint uses. Unquantized drafts are unaffected; the prefix only feeds quantization matching.
- `packed_modules_mapping` on the draft model class, which the loader already injects into the quant config, so an `ignore` list that names `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` or `gate_proj`/`up_proj` applies to the fused module. llm-compressor writes the shard names it was given, as in the recipe below. As for every other model with such a mapping, an ignore list that names a single shard now fails with the fused-layer scheme mismatch error instead of matching nothing.
- `fc` is a `ReplicatedLinear` with the quant config for every draft, as it already was for Nemotron; `project_target_hidden` uses `input_size` and unpacks the `(out, bias)` tuple unconditionally. The `fc.weight` shape check keeps the packed-aware form and `encoder.fc.*` vendor names alias to `fc.*`. The unquantized `fc` now runs through `UnquantizedLinearMethod.apply` like the Nemotron draft's, not `F.linear`, and starts uninitialized rather than randomly initialized, so `load_weights` refuses a checkpoint that fills the decoder layers but never `fc` (such a checkpoint produced unusable drafts before as well); a projector-only load, as Domino does, is unaffected.
- `load_weights` refuses a checkpoint tensor whose module the draft has, under a parameter name that module does not have (a dense tensor for a packed layer, or a packed tensor for a dense layer, under the draft's own or the vendor `encoder.` name), with the module's actual parameter names in the message. Tensors for modules the draft does not have are still ignored, and so are the ones that have no draft parameter by design: `.bias`, the `.inv_freq` / `.cos_cached` / `.sin_cached` rotary caches, and the `.input_scale` / `.output_scale` / `.k_scale` / `.v_scale` / `.kv_scale` activation and KV-cache scales.
- New CPU test `test/registered/unit/spec/test_dflash_quantized_draft_layout.py`: the layer names through the real decoder layer, the shard-only ignore list reaching the fused projection, `fc` quantized / ignored / dense, packed and dense `fc` loading (own and vendor name), the two refusals, and the tensors that must still be ignored. On main 8 of the 12 cases fail.

## Accuracy Tests

Unit tests (CPU): `test_dflash_quantized_draft_layout.py` 12 passed (8 fail on main); `test_dflash_logits.py`, `test_dflash_domino.py`, `test_oot_dflash_hooks.py`, `model_runner_components/test_spec_aux_hidden_state.py` 31 passed.

The quantized draft is built from the official `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` with llm-compressor's model-free PTQ: INT8 weight-only for the MLP, `o_proj` and `fc`, with q/k/v, the candidate selector and the convolution kernels left BF16:

```python
# llmcompressor==0.14.0, data-free round-to-nearest, runs on CPU
from llmcompressor import model_free_ptq

model_free_ptq(
    model_stub="z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2",
    save_directory="Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-W8A16",
    scheme="W8A16",
    ignore=["re:.*self_attn\\.(q|k|v)_proj$", "re:.*candidate_selector.*",
            "re:.*kernel_projection$", "re:.*norm.*"],
)
```

The target is `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` with a W4A16 body from the same tool and its `lm_head` left BF16, so that this change is tested on its own.

<details>
<summary>Target recipe</summary>

```python
# llmcompressor==0.14.0, data-free round-to-nearest, runs on CPU
from compressed_tensors.quantization import QuantizationConfig, QuantizationScheme
from compressed_tensors.quantization.quant_scheme import W4A16
from llmcompressor import model_free_ptq

model_free_ptq(
    model_stub="Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B",
    save_directory="Qwen3.8-27B-W4A16",
    config=QuantizationConfig(config_groups={
        "body": QuantizationScheme(targets=["Linear"], **W4A16),
    }),
    ignore=["lm_head", "re:.*visual.*", "re:.*mtp.*", "re:.*in_proj_(a|b)$", "re:.*conv1d.*",
            "re:.*norm.*", "re:.*embed_tokens.*"],
)
```
</details>

One RTX 6000 Ada (48 GB, TP=1), `--speculative-algorithm DFLASH --speculative-dflash-block-size 8 --disable-overlap-schedule`. Accuracy is SGLang's own GSM8K eval, one request at a time so completions can be compared across runs:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 200 --num-threads 1 --temperature 0 --max-tokens 512
```

| draft | branch | result | GSM8K (200) | accept length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none | main | serves | 0.960 | |
| `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (BF16) | main | serves | 0.970 | 6.035 |
| `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` (BF16) | this PR | serves | 0.970 | 6.035 |
| W8A16 from the recipe | main | device-side assert on the server's warm-up request | | |
| W8A16 from the recipe | this PR | serves, fused KV materialization back on | 0.970 | 6.031 |

Accept length is the mean of the scheduler's `accept len` over every decode-log window of the run, bonus token included.

With the BF16 draft, this PR's 200 completions are identical to main's. The W8A16 draft's completions match the BF16 draft's on main in 196/200. Against the target decoding on its own, the W8A16 draft matches 165/200 and the BF16 draft 166/200.

With #40883 applied as well, the same W8A16 draft also serves the target from that PR, whose `lm_head` is W8A16 pack-quantized: GSM8K 0.965, accept length 6.025, and 165/200 completions matching that target decoding on its own.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No change for unquantized drafts on most GPUs. Their only runtime change is that `fc` runs through `UnquantizedLinearMethod.apply` instead of `F.linear`, as the Nemotron draft's `fc` already did, and that method is `F.linear` itself unless the BF16 GEMM backend is cutedsl (the `auto` choice on sm100). There `fc` now uses the same GEMM as the rest of the draft's linears. The quantized drafts above go from not serving to serving; I have no clean timing for them, since the GPU these runs used was shared with other jobs.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).

title: Release the weight-checker snapshot once compare passes
body:
The WeightChecker snapshot is a host copy of every weight — tens of GB for a large model — and it stayed resident for the whole run even though compare is its only consumer. Two changes:

1. Back the snapshot with a single mmap arena (`alloc_mmap`) instead of per-tensor `.cpu()` copies. The per-tensor copies are mostly below glibc's mmap threshold, so freeing them never shrinks RSS (on Grace/64K pages even `malloc_trim` reclaims nothing); one mmap region is returned to the OS deterministically by munmap.
2. Release the snapshot (arena + views) once compare passes; a failed compare keeps it for debugging.

Verified on GB300 (DeepSeek-V4, 8 nodes): snapshot RSS returns to the OS after the first compare; unit tests cover the arena packing and release paths.

Port of #36561 (merged into `sglang-miles`) to main.

title: [HiCache] fast_file: stripe pages over several local disks and add parallel writes (write_workers)
body:
> **Stacked on #39880.** This branch is based on the head of #39880 (`a71c2814`), so until #39880 merges the diff against `main` also shows its commit. Only the last two commits belong to this PR:
>
> - `65cb6108` [HiCache] fast_file: parallel page writes with write_workers
> - `fb4e9a65` [HiCache] fast_file: stripe pages over several storage roots
>
> To review only this PR: https://github.com/briqt/sglang/compare/a71c281449420dab12cbd1a61128e53337d8d9a1...hicache-fast-file-striping-parallel-write
>
> It stays a Draft until #39880 merges. After that I will rebase onto `main`. If the design needs changes to fit #39880, I can split it or move it wherever the author prefers.

## Motivation

`fast_file` (#39880) writes to a single `storage_dir`. Hosts with several local NVMe drives therefore get one drive's bandwidth and capacity, unless the operator sets up RAID or LVM first. Backups (`batch_set_v1`) are also serial: `read_workers` only parallelises reads and existence checks.

This PR adds two opt-in extra-config keys to `fast_file`. When they are unset, behaviour is unchanged.

- `write_workers`: a write thread pool, separate from the read pool.
- `storage_dir` as a list: one root per disk. Each page file lives on exactly one root.

## Modifications

Only `fast_file_store.py`, `lru_file_evictor.py`, two docs paragraphs and one new unit test file change. The controller, the backend factory and `HiCacheFile` are untouched.

### Commit 1: `write_workers` and one task per slice

- `write_workers` (default 1) sizes a `ThreadPoolExecutor` that is **separate from the read pool**. A large background backup should never queue ahead of a latency-sensitive prefetch or its existence checks. Both the direct `readv`/`writev` path and the staged path use it.
- Both pools now submit **one contiguous slice of pages per worker** instead of one task per page. For small pages, handing off each task costs more than the I/O it overlaps (see the benchmark below).
- A batch still **waits for every task to finish before it returns or raises**, even after the first failure. The controller may release or reuse the host pages as soon as `batch_set_v1` / `batch_get_v1` returns, so no worker may still be reading from or writing to them. A test pins this.
- `read_workers` and `write_workers` share one validator that rejects non-integers, booleans and values below 1.
- GIL: `os.readv` / `os.writev` (and open, rename and stat) release the GIL during the system call, but the per-page Python work does not: building iovecs, evictor reserve/commit and the write-lock stripe all hold it. Workers therefore overlap device time, not Python time. The default stays 1 because each extra worker competes for the GIL with the scheduler thread in the same process (see the benchmark below).

### Commit 2: striping over several storage roots

- **Config.** `storage_dir` accepts a JSON list or a comma-separated string. Every root gets the **same namespace directory**, and the namespace name does not include the root list. Duplicate roots, including a symlink to the same directory, are rejected. Roots that share one filesystem log a warning, since striping them adds no bandwidth. `SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_STORAGE_DIR` is shared with the `file` backend, so it stays a single path.
- **Routing (`DiskRouter`).** The page file name (blake2b, 64 bit) picks one of 2^14 buckets. At startup, each bucket is assigned once to the root with the highest **rendezvous (HRW) score** for (bucket, root path). A lookup is one hash plus a table index (about 0.5 µs here). The assignment does not depend on the list order, and adding or removing a root only moves that root's share of the buckets.
- **A change in the number of roots is only a miss.** Keys are content hashes, so a page that now routes to another root reads as a miss and is never read wrong. At startup, each root's scan deletes the pages that now route elsewhere. They can never be read again, so this reclaims their space and stops them leaking when eviction is off. The scan runs even when eviction is off.
- **One evictor per root (`StripedEvictor`).** Each root is its own filesystem, so each root gets its own `LRUFileEvictor` with an independent LRU order, cap and background drain. `StripedEvictor` wraps them behind the single-root interface. `max_size` is split across roots by their bucket share. `min_free_space` applies to **each root's filesystem**, so a full disk does not stop writes to a healthy one; a test covers this. The per-root startup scans run in parallel.
- **No path bypasses the router.** Two methods that `fast_file` inherited from `HiCacheFile` built paths from `self.file_path`: `_get_component_path` and the metadata-cache seed scan. Both are now overridden, and the existence check also goes through the router. A guard test lists every `HiCacheFile` method whose source mentions `self.file_path` and fails if `HiCacheFastFile` does not override it with a version that avoids `self.file_path`. That catches a future inherited method that would silently use only the first root.
- **A single root keeps the existing layout, namespace name and a plain `LRUFileEvictor`.** All 53 existing `fast_file` unit tests pass unchanged.

### Docs

Two new paragraphs in `hicache_best_practices.mdx` and an updated module docstring list the new keys.

## Accuracy Tests

This PR does not change model code or kernels, and the page format on disk is unchanged. The PR's page-level correctness tests are listed below. I have **not** run an end-to-end accuracy or KL-consistency check on GPU (see "Not verified").

All tests below ran on CPU with a local import shim. I do not have a full SGLang install on this machine. The shim loads the real modules from this branch: `environ.py`, `hicache_storage.py`, `backend_factory.py`, the `fast_file` package and `LogicalHostPool` extracted from `memory_pool_host.py`. It stubs the modules that are not under test: `ci_register`, `CustomTestCase` → `unittest.TestCase`, `StorageMetrics`, `human_readable_int` and the `MHATokenToKVPoolHost` marker. **Nothing here ran in SGLang CI or on a GPU.**

| Test file | Commit 1 | Commit 2 |
|---|---|---|
| `test_hicache_fast_file_unit.py` (from #39880, unchanged) | 53 / 53 pass | 53 / 53 pass |
| `test_hicache_fast_file_striping_unit.py` (new) | 6 / 6 pass | 22 / 22 pass |

- I ran the new file 20 times in a row with no failures. The ordering checks use events with 5 s timeouts, not fixed sleeps. Only the assertions that the work spreads over at least two threads rely on short per-page sleeps (5-10 ms).
- **Mutation check.** I injected 9 faults, one at a time, into the new code. Each one made at least one new test fail:
  - the existence check reads only the first root;
  - direct writes run serially;
  - writes run on the read pool;
  - no cleanup of pages that route elsewhere;
  - `max_size` is not split across roots;
  - the `_get_component_path` override is removed;
  - `_map_on` returns before all tasks finish;
  - `clear` stops at the first root;
  - modulo routing replaces HRW.
- The new test file is registered like the existing one: `register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")`, `CustomTestCase` and a `unittest.main()` entry point, under `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/`.
- `pre-commit run` passes on all changed files: isort, ruff, ruff-format, codespell and the registered-test checks.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Environment:** Intel Core i9-12900 (24 threads), 20 GB RAM, WSL2 (Linux 6.18), ext4 on a virtual disk, and tmpfs. Python 3.12.3, torch 2.14.0+cpu. No GPU.

**Workload:** a synthetic page-first host pool of 1024 pages × 160 KiB (64 tokens × 1280 B, K and V). It is written with `batch_set_v1` and then read with `batch_get_v1`, in batches of 128. `read_workers = write_workers = w`. "per-page" re-creates the one-task-per-page submission for comparison; "per-slice" is this PR. All roots are directories on **one** filesystem, and the page cache is hot. This measures the per-page software path (system calls, GIL, task handoff), **not disk bandwidth**, and it says nothing about a multi-disk speedup.

GB/s write / read, best of 3, tmpfs:

| | w=1 | w=2 | w=4 | w=8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| roots=1, per-page | 3.35 / 4.97 | 1.59 / 2.48 | 1.17 / 1.68 | 1.21 / 1.73 |
| roots=1, per-slice | 3.27 / 4.93 | **4.29 / 7.22** | 1.55 / 2.65 | 1.37 / 1.95 |
| roots=4, per-page | 3.10 / 4.61 | 1.54 / 2.31 | 1.19 / 1.67 | 1.21 / 1.70 |
| roots=4, per-slice | 2.93 / 4.85 | **4.06 / 6.57** | 1.48 / 2.18 | 1.33 / 1.93 |

On ext4 (virtual disk, hot page cache) the pattern is the same. With one root and per-slice submission: w1 2.95 / 6.78, w2 3.34 / 8.28, w8 1.27 / 1.96.

What I read from this:

- One task per slice was never slower than one task per page, beyond run-to-run noise. At w=2 it is 2.3 to 3.5 times faster, because per-page handoff dominates when the "device" runs at memory speed. The per-page rows also show that the existing per-page `read_workers` pool from #39880 regresses on this setup.
- **More than 2 workers regress on memory-speed storage.** Each page still needs Python work under the GIL, so extra threads mostly add contention. This is why both defaults stay 1, and I do not claim a write speedup from this data. The pool is meant for the case where the device is the bottleneck: cold reads, writes throttled by dirty-page writeback, or several physical disks. I have not measured that case (see below).
- Striping adds no measurable cost on the hot path: roots=4 is within noise of roots=1, and one `route()` call costs about 0.5 µs.
- Routing, from 200k random keys over 4 roots: key shares were 24.8 % / 25.0 % / 25.7 % / 24.5 %. After removing one root, 0 of the keys on the other roots moved. Reversing the root order changed no assignment. Building the table takes about 21 ms at startup.
- A GIL probe confirms that a thread blocked inside `os.readv` / `os.writev` does not stop the main thread from making progress: about 4M loop iterations in 0.2 s.

<details><summary>Benchmark script (run with this branch installed)</summary>

```python
"""fast_file batch_set_v1 / batch_get_v1 throughput vs. worker count and roots.

CPU only, no GPU or model: a synthetic page-first host pool of 1024 pages x
160 KiB (64 tokens x 1280 B, K and V), written and read in batches of 128.
All roots are directories on the same filesystem, so this measures the
per-page software path (syscalls, GIL, task handoff), not disk bandwidth.
"per-page" re-creates the one-task-per-page submission for comparison.
Set BENCH_DIR to choose the filesystem (e.g. /dev/shm).
"""

import os
import shutil
import tempfile
import time

import torch

from sglang.srt.mem_cache.hicache_storage import HiCacheStorageConfig
from sglang.srt.mem_cache.storage.fast_file import fast_file_store as ffs

PAGES, PAGE_TOKENS, TOKEN_BYTES, BATCH = 1024, 64, 1280, 128


class Pool:
    layout = "page_first"
    page_size = PAGE_TOKENS
    dtype = torch.uint8
    size_per_token = TOKEN_BYTES

    def __init__(self):
        self.size = PAGES * PAGE_TOKENS
        self.kv_buffer = torch.randint(0, 255, (2, self.size, TOKEN_BYTES), dtype=torch.uint8)

    def get_page_buffer_meta(self, indices):
        base = self.kv_buffer.data_ptr()
        value_offset = self.size * TOKEN_BYTES
        page_bytes = PAGE_TOKENS * TOKEN_BYTES
        ptrs, sizes = [], []
        for index in indices[::PAGE_TOKENS].tolist():
            ptrs += [base + index * TOKEN_BYTES, base + index * TOKEN_BYTES + value_offset]
            sizes += [page_bytes, page_bytes]
        return ptrs, sizes


def per_page_map_on(executor, workers, fn, *iterables):
    calls = list(zip(*iterables))
    if executor is None:
        return [fn(*args) for args in calls]
    return [f.result() for f in [executor.submit(fn, *args) for args in calls]]


def run(base, pool, roots, workers):
    dirs = [os.path.join(base, f"root{i}") for i in range(roots)]
    config = HiCacheStorageConfig(
        tp_rank=0, tp_size=1, pp_rank=0, pp_size=1, attn_cp_rank=0, attn_cp_size=1,
        is_mla_model=False, enable_storage_metrics=False, is_page_first_layout=True,
        model_name="bench",
        extra_config={"storage_dir": dirs, "write_workers": workers, "read_workers": workers},
    )
    backend = ffs.HiCacheFastFile(config)
    backend.register_mem_pool_host(pool)
    keys = [f"k{i}" for i in range(PAGES)]
    batches = [
        (keys[s : s + BATCH], torch.arange(s * PAGE_TOKENS, (s + BATCH) * PAGE_TOKENS))
        for s in range(0, PAGES, BATCH)
    ]
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    for batch_keys, indices in batches:
        assert all(backend.batch_set_v1(batch_keys, indices))
    write_s = time.perf_counter() - t0
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    for batch_keys, indices in batches:
        assert all(backend.batch_get_v1(batch_keys, indices))
    read_s = time.perf_counter() - t0
    backend.clear()
    backend.close()
    gb = PAGES * 2 * PAGE_TOKENS * TOKEN_BYTES / 1e9
    return gb / write_s, gb / read_s


def main():
    base = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=os.environ.get("BENCH_DIR"))
    pool = Pool()
    sliced = ffs.HiCacheFastFile._map_on
    print("GB/s write / read, best of 3")
    try:
        for roots in (1, 4):
            for label, map_on in (("per-page", per_page_map_on), ("per-slice", sliced)):
                ffs.HiCacheFastFile._map_on = staticmethod(map_on)
                row = []
                for workers in (1, 2, 4, 8):
                    w, r = max((run(base, pool, roots, workers) for _ in range(3)), key=sum)
                    row.append(f"w{workers} {w:5.2f} / {r:5.2f}")
                print(f"roots={roots} {label:9s} " + "   ".join(row))
    finally:
        ffs.HiCacheFastFile._map_on = sliced
        shutil.rmtree(base, ignore_errors=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

### Not verified

I don't have these numbers; help from anyone with the hardware is welcome.

- Throughput on a real GPU host with several physical NVMe drives, and cold-cache prefetch (recovery) latency for combinations of roots × `read_workers` × `write_workers`, including GIL impact while the scheduler is busy.
- Startup scan time with millions of page files per root.
- The end-to-end KL / accuracy consistency check from #39880 with striping enabled, especially on hybrid-attention models such as DeepSeek-V4 (with the `page_first` layout).

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). The new file is `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_hicache_fast_file_striping_unit.py`, registered in `base-a-test-cpu`.
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). I updated `hicache_best_practices.mdx` and the module docstring.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). So far there is only a CPU micro-benchmark; GPU accuracy and multi-disk numbers are still missing (see "Not verified").
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [XPU][model] Intel XPU support for encoder embeddings (NomicBERT / ModernBERT) and InternVL3_5
body:
Intel XPU model support for encoder embeddings and InternVL3_5 — the XPU-specific
model-enabling changes. Backend-agnostic fixes (SEP-preserving truncation, Hunyuan
qk_norm, Step3 pad_token) are separated into #39754 for independent review.

## Motivation

- **nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5** (`NomicBertModel`) had no SGLang model, so the
  Transformers fallback raised `NotImplementedError: get_input_embeddings ...`.
- **ibm-granite/granite-embedding-english-r2** (`ModernBertModel`) fell back and
  crashed in the forward pass (`RuntimeError` in `set_kv_buffer`) — a bidirectional
  encoder routed through the paged decoder KV cache.
- **OpenGVLab/InternVL3_5-30B-A3B** (Qwen3-MoE backbone) crashed at load
  (`AttributeError: 'InternVLChatConfig' object has no attribute 'num_experts'`) and,
  once loading, hung/crashed the vision encoder under concurrent multimodal at tp>1
  (Level Zero USM-memcpy deadlock on a per-block device->host `.item()`; DEVICE_LOST
  batching ViT tiles).

(`BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5` needs no new model file — it is a `BertModel` served via the
shared encoder path + #39754.)

## Modifications

Encoder embeddings:
- `models/nomic_bert.py` (new): `NomicBertModel` — RoPE, SwiGLU, post-norm; SDPA,
  `AttentionType.ENCODER_ONLY`.
- `models/modernbert.py` (new): `ModernBertModel` — RoPE, local/global attention,
  GeGLU; SDPA, `ENCODER_ONLY`.
- `test/manual/prefill_only/test_xpu_encoder_embedding.py`: XPU embedding UT.

InternVL3_5 (XPU):
- `models/internvl.py`: read `num_experts` from `config.llm_config`; pass the host
  `max_seqlen` into the vision attention metadata; chunk the ViT forward to
  `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` tiles on XPU.
- `layers/attention/vision.py`: `VisionIntelXPUAttention` (XPU-only class) consumes
  the metadata's host `max_seqlen` instead of re-deriving it from GPU `cu_seqlens`.
- `environ.py`: add `SGLANG_VIT_MAX_TILES` (default 12 = InternVL per-image tile cap).

## Accuracy Test

Intel XPU (Arc Pro B60), vs the HuggingFace reference.

Encoders — MTEB SciFact NDCG@10 (300 queries / 5183 corpus), tp-1:

| Model | cosine vs HF | SciFact NDCG@10 | HF ref |
|---|---|---|---|
| nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5 | 1.00000 | 0.6803 | (prefix-sensitive) |
| ibm-granite/granite-embedding-english-r2 (ModernBERT) | 1.0 fp32 / >=0.9999 bf16 | 0.6720 | 0.6815 |

InternVL3_5-30B-A3B — tp-4 (61.7 GB bf16): loads with 0 skipped params, MoE
initialized, multimodal smoke (red image -> "Red"); P1 lmms-eval **mathvision_testmini
38.2, mmmu_val 27.4**.

## Speed Test and Profiling

New encoder models are small SDPA (no KV cache). InternVL removes a per-block
device->host sync on XPU and bounds the ViT forward; non-XPU paths are unchanged.

title: [AMD][Quark] Serve the Kimi-K3 MXFP4 checkpoint on ROC
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Loading [AMD Quark's Kimi-K3 checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/amd/Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8) (per-channel FP8 dense layers + MXFP4 MoE) on ROCm fails or runs incorrectly in several places:

- hipBLASLt needs the FP8 GEMM's N to be a multiple of 16. K3's KDA `b_proj` has 12 output channels at TP=8, so `torch._scaled_mm` raises.
- AITER's MLA absorb GEMM only takes a scalar `w_scale`, but Quark stores `kv_b_proj` with one scale per channel. Collapsing those into a single per-tensor scale gives ~2.3% relative error on real K3 weights.
- K3's fused KDA projection merge concatenates `.weight` only. On a quantized checkpoint this silently drops the scale tensors.
- AITER pads the MXFP4 MoE W2 width from 384 to 512 at TP8. That adds 33% zero work and stops the native-shape tuning table from matching. The SiTU activation path also expects a GU-interleaved preshuffled layout, which Quark's MoE scheme didn't produce.

## Modifications

- **`quark_w8a8_fp8.py`**: On ROCm, if an FP8 linear's output partition width isn't a multiple of 16, dequantize it to `out_dtype` at load time and serve it with a dense matmul. At that width the layer is memory-bound, so this costs little.
- **`kimi_k3_rocm_quant.py`** (new): `_k3_channel_fp8_to_bf16` converts a per-channel FP8 weight to bf16 using each channel's own scale (~0.12% error, compared with ~2.3% for a single per-tensor scale).
- **`kimi_k3.py`**:
  - On ROCm, fold `kv_b_proj`'s per-channel FP8 scale into a bf16 weight before the `w_kc`/`w_vc` head split. `w_scale` stays at its 1.0 default in that case, and also whenever the scale isn't a single scalar.
  - Add a `_merge_dtype_ok` check (bf16/fp16 only) so quantized weights skip the fused `b_proj`/`f_a_proj` and `qkvg` merges.
- **`quark_w4a4_mxfp4_moe.py`**:
  - When `SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT` is set, skip AITER's 128-alignment padding and keep the checkpoint's intermediate width.
  - For SiTU, when AITER selects the A8W4/A16W4 kernels, preshuffle into the GU-interleaved layout with `shuffle_weight_a16w4`/`shuffle_scale_a16w4`.
- **Tests**: Add CPU unit tests for the narrow-partition dequant fallback (including the aligned-width and non-ROCm cases where it must not run), the per-channel dequant, and the merge dtype check.

## Accuracy Tests

| Benchmark | Accuracy |
|---|---|
| GSM8K | 0.942 |


## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. Correctness fixes, except the opt-in `SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT` path, which removes 33% of the zero-padded MoE W2 work at TP8.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [ROCm][DSA] Enable AITER fused FP8 indexer writer
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

On HIP, the DSA FP8 indexer writer currently issues a chain of small kernels (K LayerNorm, joint Q/K RoPE, optional Hadamard, Q/K FP8 quant, and the paged index-K cache store). That launch overhead shows up on decode ITL, especially the tail.

CUDA already fuses the analogous indexer writer (`SGLANG_DISABLE_DSA_INDEXER_FUSION`, default on). This PR adds the ROCm counterpart via AITER `indexer_qk_rope_quant_and_cache`, so HIP can fuse RoPE + K LayerNorm + FP8 quant + cache write into one kernel. Hadamard is omitted, matching the CUDA fused writer (pre-quant logits stay aligned).

The path is **default-on** when AITER is available and indexer geometry matches (`head_dim=128`, `rope_dim=64`, `quant_block=128`, index-K LayerNorm). Models that do not match (including RMSNorm index-K) keep the legacy split writer. Set `SGLANG_AITER_FUSED_FP8_DSA_INDEXER=0` to force the split path.

Validated on GLM-5.2-MXFP4 (gfx950). Any DSA indexer with the same geometry can take this path; it is not hardcoded to a model name.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa/fp8_fused_writer_hip.py`: AITER adapter (geometry checks, RoPE table reshape, fused Q/K write).
- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer.py`: enable fused writer when HIP + AITER + geometry match; LayerNorm in fp32 only on the fused path; warn only if the env is explicitly set and unsupported.
- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: `SGLANG_AITER_FUSED_FP8_DSA_INDEXER = EnvBool(True)`.
- Tests:
  - `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_fp8_fused_writer_hip.py`
  - `test/registered/amd/test_fp8_fused_dsa_writer_gfx950.py`

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K via local `sglang.test.run_eval` (1314 questions), GLM-5.2-MXFP4, baseline = fused off (`SGLANG_AITER_FUSED_FP8_DSA_INDEXER=0`).

| | Baseline | Fused |
|---|---:|---:|
| Score | 0.935 | 0.936 |

No accuracy regression. Server log contains `Enabled AITER fused FP8 DSA indexer writer`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hardware: gfx950. Workload: InferenceX AgentX, **1200s** (not the 3600s publication window). Toggle only `SGLANG_AITER_FUSED_FP8_DSA_INDEXER`. Interactivity = output token throughput per user; TPOT = ITL.

### TP4 / EP4 / concurrency 8, HiCache DRAM

Request mix is aligned (510 vs 518 completed; ISL/OSL mean 103925/568 vs 104042/563).

| Metric | Baseline | Fused | Delta |

title: [Fix] Give the full prefill CUDA graph replay view the captured bucket's input_ids
body:
# Summary

Full prefill CUDA graph replay refreshes the attention metadata through `init_forward_metadata_out_graph` on a slot-padded shallow view of the live `ForwardBatch`. The view already carries the captured bucket's `batch_size`, `seq_lens`, `req_pool_indices`, `extend_seq_lens`, `extend_prefix_lens` and `max_seq_len_override`, but its `input_ids` was still the live batch's, i.e. fewer token rows than the captured kernels run over.

An attention backend that sizes anything in that hook from `forward_batch.input_ids` (a per-row plan, a scratch buffer, a token count) therefore planned for the real token count while the replayed kernels consume the padded one, and had to re-plan per call to stay correct. The view now takes `input_ids` from the static captured batch, so the hook sees the same token rows as the graph it prepares for. One line in `PrefillCudaGraphRunner._prepare_forward_metadata_for_replay`; no kernel or backend changes.

Beyond the port, the existing full-replay padding unit test now passes a distinct static batch and asserts the padded view's `input_ids` is the static batch's; without the fix that assertion fails on the 2-row live tensor.

# Test plan

- `PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest test/registered/unit/model_executor/runner/test_prefill_cuda_graph_padding.py`: **10 passed, 3 subtests passed** with the fix; the extended case **fails** with the production line reverted (`tensor([0, 1]) is not tensor([0, ..., 15])`).
- isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 (`check` and `format --check`) and codespell 2.4.1 on both files: **clean**.
- Not run locally: the GPU full prefill CUDA graph suite (`test/registered/cuda_graph/full_prefill/`); left to CI.

title: feat(kv-hints): add kv hint envelope to request transport
body:
## Motivation                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                        
 A KV hint is advisory routing metadata attached by a trusted orchestrator (a router or a scheduler) after it has picked a worker -- never by an application client. A KV-aware router already knows which worker holds a prefix; today there is no way for it to tell the worker it just picked. This adds the transport for that, and nothing else.                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                        
This is the transport-only half of #36224, split out on review feedback so the KVCR backend that consumes a hint lands as a purely additive follow-up.                        
                                                                                            
## Modifications                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                        
The envelope travels unchanged from the entrypoint down to the scheduler's `Req`, and nothing in the core reads a payload:                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                              
  GenerateReqInput (HTTP/Engine) and the gRPC KVHintsEnvelope message                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                                                                                                        
    -> normalization (single, per-batch-item, and parallel-sample expansion)                                                                                                            
    -> TokenizedGenerateReqInput over msgpack IPC                                                                                                                                                                        
    -> Req                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                     
 The envelope is a list of independent actions, each naming its own type and version, so a consumer implementing one action type ignores -- rather than rejects -- an action it                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                        
    -> normalization (single, per-batch-item, and parallel-sample expansion)                                                                                                            
    -> TokenizedGenerateReqInput over msgpack IPC                           
    -> Req                                    

The envelope is a list of independent actions, each naming its own type and version, so a consumer implementing one action type ignores -- rather than rejects -- an action it does not implement sitting next to it. The payload is therefore untyped here; the component that implements an action owns its schema and validates it. **No action types are defined by this change.**

 New module `python/sglang/srt/managers/kv_hints.py` holds the `KvHintAction` / `KvHintsEnvelope` msgspec structs and `decode_kv_hints_envelope()`.

 Wire-compatible with vLLM's `KVHintsEnvelope` (vllm-project/vllm#53423) so one orchestrator can address either engine with the same envelope.

 ## Accuracy Test

  No model behavior changes -- an absent or malformed envelope leaves the request on the existing path.

 ## Benchmarking and Profiling

 No hot-path change; the field is `None` for every request that does not carry a hint.

  ## Checklist

  - [x] Format your code according to the Code Formatting with Pre-Commit.
  - [x] Add unit tests (`test/registered/unit/managers/test_io_struct.py`, covering normalization, batch expansion, parallel-sample expansion, and rejection of a malformed envelope).
  - [x] Update documentation as needed.

title: [Fix] Reject Chat Completions streaming errors in bench_serving
body:
## Motivation

An OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint can send an `error` event after starting an HTTP 200 SSE response. SGLang emits this format for streaming generation failures.

The benchmark client currently treats that event as an empty-choices chunk, skips it, and marks the request successful at EOF. An error-only stream followed by `[DONE]` is reported as `success=True, output_len=64` for a 64-token request, despite producing no text. This inflates completed-request and output-token totals and can hide failed warmup requests.

## Modifications

Reject a non-null SSE `error` before processing usage or choices, using the existing exception-to-failed-request path. Add loopback HTTP regressions for errors before content, errors after partial content (including exclusion from aggregate metrics), and a valid chunk with `error: null`.

Only the benchmark client and its existing registered CPU test file change.

## Accuracy Tests

Based on `d4dcce12d4fcdb3eb694d54d6afd31628c2eb7ce`.

- Before the fix: the two error regressions fail because the client reports success; the null-error control passes.
- After the fix: **13 tests pass**, including existing reasoning-content, usage-only chunk and non-streaming tests.
- Actual-model smoke check on one RTX 5090: **16 streaming and 16 non-streaming requests complete successfully** using Qwen3-0.6B BF16, FlashInfer, and decode CUDA graphs. This validates the normal client path; generation failures are reproduced by the CPU loopback HTTP fixtures.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=99 python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/bench_fn/test_bench_serving_reasoning_stream.py
```

The invalid GPU ordinal hides the accelerator on the test machine. The current base's test-utils import fails with an empty CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES value, which is outside this change.

Environment: Ubuntu 22.04, Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. No model-forward or sampling changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance claim. This fixes benchmark success/token accounting; inference kernels are unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Applicable pre-commit hooks pass on both modified files.
- [x] Add concrete regression tests using the existing CustomTestCase and CPU CI registration.
- [x] Follow repository code style.

title: [AMD] [GLM5] Reland: Fuse shared-expert append into aiter grouped-topk
body:
## Summary

Relands #31323, which #35105 reverted after it failed `base-a-test-cpu (0)` on main. That failure is fixed here, along with two latent bugs found while re-testing on MI355X, and the optimization finally gets the test coverage it shipped without.

## What the optimization does

On GLM-5.2 with the non-EP aiter grouped-topk route, every decoder layer ran a separate kernel to append the shared expert into the top-k ids/weights. Instead, the shared columns are pre-populated **once** in a persistent top-k buffer and the aiter kernel writes only the routed columns via row stride, so the per-layer append kernel disappears (prefill and decode).

- **Bit-identical**: the shared column carries the same constant the append kernel used to write.
- **Safe fallback**: the buffer is sized to the max prefill batch; larger token counts take the plain append path.
- **Auto-enabled** when `moe_ep_size == 1` and `num_fused_shared_experts > 0`. Other archs, EP mode and non-applicable routes are untouched.

GSM8K on MI355X TP4 (GLM-5.2-MXFP4): 0.931 → 0.933. Throughput and TPOT move under 1% either way — the gain is one fewer kernel launch per layer, not raw speed.

## Fixes on top of #31323

**1. Read the sizing config through `get_schedule()`** — the actual revert cause. `base-a-test-cpu (0)` failed with `alias-form process-global config field reads grew: 2 > baseline 0`. The ratchet baseline dropped to 0 on Aug 5, after this branch last ran green against a baseline of 12, so the two `ServerArgs` alias reads only became a violation once merged against current main. 

**2. `biased_grouped_topk_cpu` accepts `fused_shared_experts_scaling_factor`.** `select_experts` passes the kwarg unconditionally, so on CPU + AMX the alias raised `TypeError` during argument binding even when the value was `None`. A non-`None` value is rejected, matching how `fused_topk_cpu` handles parameters it cannot serve.


## New test: `TestAiterGroupedTopkSharedFuse`

#31323 shipped with nothing exercising the fused path — `fused_shared_experts_scaling_factor` had no non-default coverage anywhere in the repo, which is why both latent bugs above had to be found by hand. `test/registered/moe/test_fused_append_remap_per_rank_shared_slots.py` now adds three tests:

- **The buffer must equal the plain append, bit for bit.** The same input goes through the pre-populated buffer and through the plain append (forced by patching the token budget to 0), and the ids and weights must compare equal under `torch.equal`, not merely close. Covered over a decode step and three prefill chunk sizes on the DeepSeek-V3 / GLM-5 routing shape, under both `fused_shared_experts_scaling_factor` spellings and four routed scaling factors.
- **Expert parallelism must not fuse**, since the pre-populated shared ids only hold when the shared experts live on every rank.
- **Reaching the path before the MoE EP group exists must fall back**, not raise — a regression test for fix 3.

## Validation

On MI355X everything related to this change is green: the new tests (7 passed, 16 subtests) and the ratchet suite.

title: [ROCm] feat: enable aiter allreduce fusion for GLM models
body:
## Motivation

Two problems, both around `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` on ROCm.

**The auto-enable never shipped, but the log announcing it did.** The ROCm
auto-enable for this fusion landed commented out in #13747, while the
`logger.info` that announces it did not. A single-node ROCm run without DP
attention has since reported the fusion as on with nothing actually setting it.
Two sites are affected: the DeepSeek-family HIP arm and the GptOss arm of
`handle_model_specific_adjustments`.

**The switch is all-or-nothing, but the fusion is not equally worthwhile in both
phases.** Fusing the post-MLP all-reduce into the next layer's residual+RMSNorm
pays off in decode, where the collective is latency-bound and the launch count
dominates. Prefill is a different regime, and there is currently no way to keep
the fusion where it pays and drop it where it does not — the operator only gets
one boolean for the whole run. For GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) we want it
on for decode and off for prefill.

## Modifications

### 1. Per-phase opt-outs under the existing master switch

`python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/fields/exec_.py` — two new resolvable fields next
to `enable_aiter_allreduce_fusion`:

- `disable_aiter_allreduce_fusion_in_prefill`
- `disable_aiter_allreduce_fusion_in_decode`

Both default to `False`, so `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` keeps meaning
"fuse everywhere" and a run that does not pass the new flags is unchanged.

### 2. Phase-aware gate

`python/sglang/srt/layers/communicator.py` — the master-switch read moves into a
helper, and `apply_aiter_all_reduce_fusion` now takes the `ForwardBatch`:

```python
def aiter_all_reduce_fusion_enabled_for(forward_mode: ForwardMode) -> bool:
    comm = get_exec().comm
    if not comm.enable_aiter_allreduce_fusion:
        return False
    if forward_mode.is_extend_or_draft_extend_or_mixed():
        return not comm.disable_aiter_allreduce_fusion_in_prefill
    return not comm.disable_aiter_allreduce_fusion_in_decode
```

### Compatibility

- All three switches default off; a run that passes none of them behaves exactly
  as before, on every platform.
- The new fields need no `field_order.py` entry. A name that is not listed there
  sorts after every name that is, which is the only backward-compatible
  position for a new field — so `ServerArgs`' positional signature is unchanged.
- The two `assert not cfg.enable_aiter_allreduce_fusion` guards in
  `parallel_hook.py` (context parallelism, `moe_dp_size > 1`), the
  deterministic-inference override in `attention_hook.py`, and the MiniMax-M3
  override in `model_overrides/minimax_m3.py` are all untouched and stay sound:
  they gate the master switch, and the new switches can only narrow it.
- `qwen3_5._fused_ar_quant_enabled` still reads the master switch. It feeds
  `LayerCommunicator(enable_fused_ar_quant=...)` at construction time, which
  decides whether the next linear receives an fp8 tuple or bf16, so it is not a
  per-phase decision and is intentionally left alone.

title: [Perf] Shard Kimi K3 latent front projection for TP8 decode
body:
## Motivation

Kimi K3's merged MoE front computes the full latent down-projection on every TP rank. For small decode batches, sharding its output columns reduces redundant weight reads and compute.

## Modifications

- Automatically select the TP8 sharded front for supported M8/M16 decode configurations: compute the shared/router outputs plus 448 local latent columns, then assemble the FP32 latent tensor through multicast.
- Reuse the existing communication workspace and extend its gather consumer to support FP32 payloads.
- Select this path using the existing hardware, weight-layout, dtype, and communication-workspace checks, with no new environment variable; retain the existing path for other shapes or unsupported configurations. The local weight copy adds approximately 3.54 GiB/GPU for the 92 MoE layers; full weights remain available for fallback.

## Accuracy Tests

- Eight-rank exact FP32 assembly checks with positive, negative and zero payloads, alternating M8/M16 gathers with push all-reduce; six CUDA Graph replays exercise all three payload types in both mailbox phases.
- Exact M8/M16 projection checks against an independent FP32 matmul under CUDA Graph replay, including rank-specific shared-expert weights.
- Misaligned input rejection before kernel launch.
- Existing BF16 GEMM all-gather and push all-reduce regression tests.
- Pre-commit checks on all changed files.

Model-quality evaluation is pending; the performance experiment uses dummy weights.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Performance results are pending a full-model comparison against the best measured configuration on the exact OSS base. The earlier development-branch result has been withdrawn from this PR because it did not establish the speedup over that baseline. title: [Fix]Account for DCP replication when sizing the EAGLE draft KV pool
body:
## Motivation

Under DCP the target KV pool is sharded across ranks, but the draft pool is **replicated** — it indexes the allocator's widened virtual location space raw. `KVCacheConfigurator` says so directly:

```python
@property
def loc_space_scale(self) -> int:
    dcp_size = get_parallel().attn_dcp_size
    return dcp_size if (self.is_draft_worker and dcp_size > 1) else 1
```

```python
# Draft pools are replicated, not DCP-sharded, yet consume the shared
# allocator's virtual locs in [0, max_total * dcp_size) untranslated.
loc_scale = self.loc_space_scale
max_total_num_tokens *= loc_scale
```

Both pool configurators price the EAGLE/STANDALONE draft term at **one** replica while `dcp_size` are allocated:

- `DefaultPoolConfigurator._compute_cell_size`: `draft_num_layers = int(eagle_draft_num_layers)`
- `HybridSWAPoolConfigurator.__init__`: `draft_layers = int(kvc.spec_aux_config.eagle_draft_num_layers)`

The DFLASH term in each of those same two places already scales — `int(draft_num_layers) * get_parallel().attn_dcp_size` in the first, and `_dflash_draft_cell_size` (which multiplies by `attn_dcp_size` internally) in the second. `_dflash_draft_cell_size` even carries the matching docstring: *"Under DCP, the target pool is sharded while the draft pool spans the allocator's widened virtual location space, so the draft term is replicated across DCP ranks."* Only the EAGLE branches were left unscaled.

So `max_total_num_tokens` comes out too large and the pool overruns the memory it was sized against, by a factor of `(L + d·dcp) / (L + d)` for `L` target layers and `d` draft layers. At 32 target layers and 1 draft layer that is +9.1% at `dcp_size=4` and +21.2% at `dcp_size=8`.

## Modifications

**`DefaultPoolConfigurator`** — scale where `draft_num_layers` is derived, so both the DSA and non-DSA branches below inherit it:

```python
draft_num_layers = int(eagle_draft_num_layers) * get_parallel().attn_dcp_size
```

**`HybridSWAPoolConfigurator`** — scale the three derived per-geometry counts instead of `draft_layers` itself, because `draft_layers` indexes real draft layer ids (`for layer_id in range(draft_layers)` against `mtp_local_layer_ids`) and bounds the SWA layer clamp; multiplying it there would corrupt both:

```python
dcp_size = get_parallel().attn_dcp_size
self._draft_full_layers_num *= dcp_size
self._draft_swa_layers_num *= dcp_size
self._draft_swa_full_layers_num *= dcp_size
```

At `dcp_size == 1` both are `* 1` — existing behaviour and existing tests are untouched, and the measurements below confirm the sizing is identical there.

### Scope note on the DSA indexer

Moving the multiplier up to the shared `draft_num_layers` assignment means the DSA indexer term (`_compute_dsa_indexer_cell_size(..., num_layers=draft_num_layers, allocate_all_layers=True)`) now also scales with `dcp_size`. I believe that is correct — `_derive_pool_sizes` scales the draft worker's `max_total_num_tokens` regardless of whether the model is DSA, and the draft worker has no equivalent of the explicit c4/c128/state zeroing that would exclude an indexer pool. But I did not trace the indexer pool construction to the end, so this is the one part worth a maintainer's eye. If the DSA indexer is sized differently, the multiplier should move down into the non-DSA `else` branch instead.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_pool_configurator.py`: **45 passed, 9 subtests passed.**

Two tests are added, one per configurator. Both assert the budget holds once the replicas are counted; the hybrid one covers a draft layer of each geometry so the full and the SWA draft terms are both exercised, and runs at `dcp_size` 1 and 4 so the unscaled path stays pinned.

Reverting both source fixes while keeping the tests shows they have power rather than merely running the code:

```
AssertionError: 10874880 not less than or equal to 10000000      <- DefaultPoolConfigurator, +8.7%
AssertionError: 19995648 not less than or equal to 10000000      <- HybridSWAPoolConfigurator, +100%
2 failed, 44 passed, 8 subtests passed
```

Exactly the two new tests fail and every pre-existing test passes, so nothing in the suite covered this before. The `dcp_size=1` subtest passes in both builds. (The hybrid figure is inflated by the tiny test model — 4 target layers against 2 draft layers — and is not a real-world severity estimate.)

## Pool sizing measurements

`Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` (32 layers) with the EAGLE3 draft (1 layer), `sglang.bench_one_batch`, MI355X. `max_total_num_tokens` and the target KV allocation reported at startup:

| tp | dcp | before (tokens) | after (tokens) | delta | before K size | after K size |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 1 | 6,842,949 | 6,842,949 | 0.0% | 104.42 GB | 104.42 GB |
| 4 | 4 | 1,684,034 | 1,543,698 | −8.3% | 102.79 GB | 94.22 GB |
| 8 | 8 | 1,679,771 | 1,385,811 | −17.5% | 102.53 GB | 84.58 GB |

The capacity correction matches the model exactly, to the token: at `dcp=4` the budget priced `32 + 1 = 33` layer-equivalents against `32 + 4 = 36` allocated, and `1,684,034 × 33/36 = 1,543,698`. At `dcp=8` it priced 33 against 40, and `1,679,771 × 33/40 = 1,385,811`. `dcp=1` is unchanged.

The reduction is the cost of the correction, not a regression: the previous capacity was one the allocation could not actually honour.

No end-to-end throughput or accuracy numbers. EAGLE + DCP does not run on the container I have: the aiter backend raises `RuntimeError: view size is not compatible with input tensor's size and stride` from `memory_pool.py::_set_kv_buffer_impl`, and the Triton backend raises `NotImplementedError: DCP Triton extend does not support custom masks`. Both reproduce on unpatched `main`, so neither is caused by this change, but they did stop me from measuring past pool construction.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — internal sizing correction, nothing user-facing to document.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: Use the 128-row query tile for head_dim <= 128 on gfx950
body:
## Motivation

On gfx950 the extend-attention kernel only takes the 128-row query tile when `128 < head_dim <= 256`:

```python
elif _is_gfx95 and 128 < Lq <= 256:
    BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N = (128, 64)
    num_warps = 8
else:
    BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N = (64, 64)
    num_warps = 4
```

Every workgroup in this kernel streams the whole prefix, so the KV bytes read per call scale with the number of query tiles: doubling `BLOCK_M` halves them. And `BLOCK_M / num_warps = 128 / 8 = 16` rows per warp is exactly one MFMA tile at `matrix_instr_nonkdim=16`, so the wider tile maps cleanly onto the hardware rather than leaving a partial tile.

Neither part of that reasoning depends on the head dim being above 128. Head dims 64 and 128 — which cover most dense models, including the Llama family — are left on the narrow tile for no stated reason.

## Modifications

Drop the lower bound on the condition:

```python
elif _is_gfx95 and Lq <= 256:
```

`BLOCK_N` stays at 64 in both branches, so the KV sweep per query row is unchanged and each row's online-softmax accumulates in the same order. `BLOCK_M` only changes how many query rows a program handles, and rows are independent. The output is therefore expected to be bit-identical, and it is — see below. Other AMD architectures, CUDA, and head dims above 256 are untouched.

## Accuracy Tests

**MI355X (gfx950), 256 CU, ROCm 7.2, torch 2.9.1, Triton 3.7.0.** `B=32, H_Q=64, H_KV=8`, bf16, causal, tensors from the repo's `_build_batch`.

12 configurations, head_dim {64, 128, 256} × N_CTX {1024, 2048, 4096, 8192}, run before and after. Each run hashes its inputs as well as its `o_extend`, so the output comparison is only accepted when the inputs provably matched.

**12/12 inputs identical, 12/12 outputs bitwise identical.**

`test/registered/attention/unittests/dense/test_triton.py` and `.../swa/test_triton.py`: 14 passed, 2 skipped, 55 subtests passed.

## Speed Tests

Minimum over 7 repetitions of `triton.testing.do_bench(warmup=100ms, rep=500ms, return_mode="median")`, one idle GPU. The baseline sweep was run twice, before and after the patched sweep; **maximum run-to-run drift was 0.33%**.

### head_dim 64 — `BLOCK_M` 64 → 128

| N_CTX | before (ms) | after (ms) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 0.4712 | 0.2588 | **−45.1%** |
| 2048 | 1.8496 | 0.8606 | **−53.5%** |
| 4096 | 5.9978 | 2.8041 | **−53.2%** |
| 8192 | 16.8052 | 8.0892 | **−51.9%** |

### head_dim 128 — `BLOCK_M` 64 → 128

| N_CTX | before (ms) | after (ms) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 0.6572 | 0.5349 | −18.6% |
| 2048 | 2.4469 | 1.8698 | −23.6% |
| 4096 | 8.0976 | 6.2074 | −23.3% |
| 8192 | 22.8645 | 17.4134 | −23.8% |

### head_dim 256 — control, tile choice unchanged

| N_CTX | before (ms) | after (ms) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 0.8084 | 0.8083 | −0.0% |
| 2048 | 2.8070 | 2.8060 | −0.0% |
| 4096 | 9.4010 | 9.3854 | −0.2% |
| 8192 | 26.3511 | 26.3371 | −0.1% |

All four control rows are inside the 0.33% drift, as they must be — the condition change cannot reach this head dim.

### Register pressure

A wider query tile costs registers, and this file has a history of Triton 3.7 gfx950 spill regressions, so wall-clock alone is not enough. From the compiled AMDGCN at `N_CTX=4096`:

| head_dim | sgpr_count | sgpr_spill | vgpr_count | vgpr_spill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 105 → 106 | 4 → 2 | 107 → 114 | 0 → 0 |
| 128 | 106 → 106 | 4 → 6 | 169 → 151 | 0 → 0 |
| 256 | 106 → 106 | 14 → 14 | 227 → 227 | 0 → 0 |

No VGPR spills appear at any head dim, the SGPR spill counts stay in the single digits and move in both directions, and head_dim 128 actually uses 18 fewer VGPRs on the wider tile. Nothing here resembles the scratch-spill regime that motivated the narrower tile for `Lq == 576`.

## What this does not cover

gfx950 only, and kernel-level only — no end-to-end serving numbers. The change is gated on `_is_gfx95`, so no other architecture is affected by construction.
