title: Skip fully-masked KV tiles in sliding-window extend attention
body:
## Motivation

On a sliding-window layer, the stage-2 loop in `_fwd_kernel` sweeps the extend KV from 0:

```python
for start_n in range(0, extend_end, BLOCK_N):
```

The window mask inside that loop keeps `(q, kv)` only when `q <= kv + SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE`, so every tile lying entirely below `cur_block_m * BLOCK_M - SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE` is fully masked and contributes nothing.

Those tiles do not read K/V and do not run the dot — `SKIP_TILE` already guards that. What they still pay, once per tile, is the cost of establishing that they contribute nothing: building `final_mask` (the causal compare, the window compare, the `&`), and then the `[BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N]` cross-wave `tl.max` reduction that computes `SKIP_TILE` itself.

On a long extend with a small window that is the majority of the loop. At `extend_len = 8192` and `W = 127`, the last M block's floor sits at roughly `8192 - 127`, so almost every iteration is spent proving that the tile is empty.

## Modifications

Start the loop at the `BLOCK_N`-aligned tile that contains the window floor:

```python
extend_start = 0
if SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE > 0:
    extend_start = (
        tl.maximum(cur_block_m * BLOCK_M - SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE, 0) // BLOCK_N
    ) * BLOCK_N
for start_n in range(extend_start, extend_end, BLOCK_N):
```

The bound is derived from the mask predicate rather than estimated. The kernel returns early when `cur_block_m * BLOCK_M >= cur_seq_len_extend`, so `offs_m = 0` is always a live row and the smallest query index in the block is exactly `m0 = cur_block_m * BLOCK_M`. A skipped tile satisfies `start_n + BLOCK_N <= floor_aligned <= m0 - W`, hence its largest key index `start_n + BLOCK_N - 1 < m0 - W`, so the window mask is false for every one of its elements.

It is also tight at tile granularity: the preceding tile would need `floor_aligned >= m0 - W + 1` to hold a surviving element, which contradicts `floor_aligned <= m0 - W`. Nothing that can contribute is skipped, for any `BLOCK_M`/`BLOCK_N`.

`SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE` is a `tl.constexpr`, so a full-attention layer loses the branch at trace time and its loop is unchanged. `extend_start` is a multiple of `BLOCK_N`, so `tl.multiple_of(start_n, BLOCK_N)` stays valid. A custom mask or the non-causal path only adds conjuncts, which narrow the mask further, so the bound remains sound there. Under the HIP compact grid `cur_block_m` is still the per-sequence tile index, so the derivation is unaffected.

## Accuracy Tests

**MI355X (gfx950), 256 CU, ROCm 7.2, torch 2.9.1, Triton 3.7.0.**

The existing SWA suite passes unchanged: `test/registered/attention/unittests/swa/test_triton.py` reports 6 passed, 1 skipped, 20 subtests passed.

Output is unchanged rather than merely close. Across 21 configurations (12 sliding-window, 4 full-attention, 5 bound-inert) at `B=32, H_Q=64, H_KV=8, D=128`, bf16, causal, `o_extend` is bitwise identical before and after. Each run hashes its inputs as well as its output, so the comparison is only accepted when the inputs provably matched: **21/21 inputs identical, 21/21 outputs bitwise identical.**

The second commit adds coverage for the bound itself. Every pre-existing SWA extend case keeps the extend length under `BLOCK_M`, so `cur_block_m` is always 0 and the loop always starts at tile 0, leaving this code path unexercised. The three new cases use extend lengths above `BLOCK_M` with windows below it -- no prefix, with prefix and a window that is not a tile multiple, and a window landing exactly on a tile boundary -- so some query tile starts past the window and the bound takes effect.

## Speed Tests

Minimum over 7 repetitions of `triton.testing.do_bench(warmup=100ms, rep=500ms, return_mode="median")`, one idle GPU. The baseline sweep was run twice, before and after the patched sweep; **maximum run-to-run drift was 0.23%**, so the deltas below are well outside noise.

Note on methodology: `benchmark/kernels/sliding_window_attention_triton/bench_triton_swa_kernel.py` does not run on current main — its `_run_triton` predates the required `k_scale`/`v_scale` parameters of `extend_attention_fwd`, and `sglang.benchmark.bench_utils` hard-imports `flashinfer`, which has no ROCm build. These numbers therefore come from a harness that reuses that file's `_build_batch` for input generation but calls `extend_attention_fwd` the way `triton_backend` does, including `extend_seq_lens_cpu` so the HIP compact ragged grid is exercised.

| N_CTX | window | before (ms) | after (ms) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8192 | 127 | 16.8210 | 10.2927 | **−38.8%** |
| 8192 | 256 | 17.8645 | 11.8675 | **−33.6%** |
| 8192 | 512 | 19.9542 | 14.9579 | **−25.0%** |
| 4096 | 127 | 6.0787 | 4.4118 | −27.4% |
| 4096 | 256 | 6.5772 | 5.1913 | −21.1% |
| 4096 | 512 | 7.6285 | 6.6601 | −12.7% |
| 2048 | 127 | 2.0689 | 1.7511 | −15.4% |
| 2048 | 256 | 2.3980 | 2.1632 | −9.8% |
| 2048 | 512 | 2.9954 | 2.8858 | −3.7% |
| 1024 | 127 | 0.7128 | 0.6672 | −6.4% |
| 1024 | 256 | 0.8542 | 0.8301 | −2.8% |
| 1024 | 512 | 1.0625 | 1.0500 | −1.2% (bound inert, `max_len_extend`=466 < 512) |

The gain tracks the fraction of the loop below the floor: it grows with sequence length and shrinks with the window, which is what the derivation predicts.

### End to end

`gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` (25 of 30 layers `sliding_attention`, window 1024, `head_dim` 256, so `BLOCK_M`=128 here), `sglang.bench_one_batch --attention-backend triton`, one MI355X. Prefill latency, minimum of 4 alternating runs per arm. Minimum rather than mean because one patched run hit a 1.3 s startup artifact at `bs=4, 2048`; across the other cells the run-to-run spread is 0.2–1.3% for the baseline.

| batch | input_len | before (s) | after (s) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16384 | 0.5173 | 0.4753 | **−8.1%** |
| 4 | 16384 | 1.9708 | 1.8210 | **−7.6%** |
| 1 | 8192 | 0.2041 | 0.1944 | −4.8% |
| 4 | 8192 | 0.7725 | 0.7381 | −4.5% |
| 1 | 2048 | 0.0501 | 0.0497 | −0.9% |
| 4 | 2048 | 0.1558 | 0.1557 | −0.1% |

This is whole-model prefill, MoE included, so the attention-only share of the win is larger than these numbers. The 2048 rows are near zero because `BLOCK_M`=128 against a 1024 window means the bound only starts firing at `cur_block_m >= 9`, i.e. past token 1152. A model with a tighter window, such as `gpt-oss` at 128, should gain considerably more; I have not measured that.

### Full-attention control

At `sliding_window_size = -1` the branch is constexpr-eliminated, so the two builds should be indistinguishable:

| N_CTX | before (ms) | after (ms) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 0.6566 | 0.6573 | +0.1% |
| 2048 | 2.4447 | 2.4423 | −0.1% |
| 4096 | 8.0970 | 8.0976 | +0.0% |
| 8192 | 22.8541 | 22.8669 | +0.1% |

Mean +0.02%, all within the 0.23% drift. Full-attention models and the global-attention layers of hybrid models are unaffected both by construction and by measurement.

### Cost where the bound never fires

A sliding-window layer whose every M block satisfies `m0 <= W`: `extend_start` always evaluates to 0 and the trip count is unchanged, yet the computation still runs. `_build_batch` draws extend lengths from `randint(1, N_CTX // 2)`, so `W >= N_CTX / 2` makes the bound inert; `max_len_extend <= W` was checked per configuration rather than assumed.

| N_CTX | window | max_len_extend | before (ms) | after (ms) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1024 | 466 | 1.1208 | 1.1082 | −1.1% |
| 1024 | 2048 | 466 | 1.1167 | 1.1051 | −1.0% |
| 2048 | 2048 | 913 | 4.3497 | 4.2907 | −1.4% |
| 4096 | 4096 | 1884 | 14.8614 | 14.6661 | −1.3% |
| 8192 | 8192 | 4072 | 42.3522 | 41.9029 | −1.1% |

No configuration regresses. The small consistent gain is above drift but I do not have an explanation for it, so I am reporting it rather than claiming it.

The AMDGCN metadata does **not** show this as free on gfx950, at `N_CTX=8192, W=127`:

```
sgpr_count:       106 -> 106
vgpr_count:       204 -> 204
sgpr_spill_count:  76 ->  80
vgpr_spill_count:   0 ->   0
shared:         16384 -> 16384
```

Four more SGPR spills. It does not show up in any measurement above, but I would rather flag it than assert the bound is free.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no user-facing behaviour change, nothing to document.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [NPU] Fix W4A8 MoE scale_bias sharding for tensor parallelism
body:
## Motivation

Fix incorrect down-projection compensation in the Ascend INT4-weight / INT8-activation W4A8 MoE path when `moe_tp_size > 1`.

The per-channel loader copies the complete checkpoint `w2_scale_bias` into each rank, while `w2_weight` is sharded along K. `_update_bias()` then sums all compensation segments on every rank. Each rank therefore applies compensation for K partitions it does not own. In the affected ModelSlim checkpoints the last dimension contains 16 compensation segments.

This reproduced as incoherent GLM-5.2-W4A8C8 output with EP1, including on both CANN 9.0 and CANN 9.1. It is related to the W4A8-without-DeepEP accuracy item in #22521; this PR does not claim to resolve the other items in that roadmap.

## Modifications

- Before reducing `w2_scale_bias`, select the contiguous segment range for `layer.moe_tp_rank` using `layer.moe_tp_size`. Reject a segment count that cannot be evenly partitioned.
- Use the actual **MoE** TP group, so mixed TP/EP layouts use the correct rank and EP with MoE TP=1 retains all segments.
- Preserve the existing reduction and `w13` behavior. The activation-clipping branch does not call `_update_bias()` and is unchanged. No checkpoint conversion, new flag, kernel change, or inference-time dispatch change is required.
- Add six regression tests registered in `stage-a-unit-test-npu`: every rank at MoE TP1/2/4/8/16, conservation across ranks, mixed TP/EP rank selection, MoE TP1 with global TP16, unchanged `w13`, missing compensation, and rejection of incompatible segment counts. Nonuniform segment values also rule out replacing the correction with `full_bias / tp_size`.

Both ModelSlim and the non-clipping compressed-tensors W4A8 scheme use this backend method and allocate the full compensation segment dimension. Hardware validation below covers ModelSlim; no compressed-tensors model-level run is claimed.

## Accuracy Tests

### Local regression tests on this PR

Base: `d4dcce12d4fcdb3eb694d54d6afd31628c2eb7ce`.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/unit/npu/quantization/test_w4a8_int8_moe_bias.py
# Ran 6 tests ... OK

pre-commit run --files \
  python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/moe_methods.py \
  test/registered/unit/npu/quantization/test_w4a8_int8_moe_bias.py
git diff --check
```

Executed with Python 3.12 / PyTorch 2.10.0 on macOS arm64, using CPU tensors and actual SGLang imports. The tests invoke the real `_update_bias()` method, without mocking its tensor operations. An in-memory negative control that substitutes the unpatched upstream method fails the partition regression checks. NPU CI has not yet run for this PR.

### Prior on-device A/B validation of the same correction

Model: [`Eco-Tech/GLM-5.2-w4a8c8`](https://www.modelscope.cn/models/Eco-Tech/GLM-5.2-w4a8c8/files), ModelScope `master` revision `67e2b7157ac7d8ce1d15d7251853ce146819ceb9`. All inference-relevant weights, configuration, quantization metadata and tokenizer files were SHA256-checked against that revision. Hardware: Ascend 910B2, 64 GiB per device, driver 25.5.5.

| Environment | Layout | Before correction | After correction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SGLang `242d8a70c05bce1aace1e361000bb2f8b4f85469`, CANN 9.0.0, TorchNPU 2.10.0 | 1 node, TP8 / EP1, full decode graph (batch 1) | Arithmetic and greeting return incoherent text | `2`, `Hello!`, `56`, `Paris` |
| SGLang `40048f6e51891e984258d34c33c5a9f2c1f542f6`, CANN 9.1.0, TorchNPU 2.10.0.post4 | 2 nodes, TP16 / EP1, graphs disabled | Incoherent output | `2`, `Hello!`, `56`, `Paris.` |

Each A/B pair kept the same image, weights, seed and computational settings; only the rank-local compensation selection changed numerically. Corrected runs passed `/health`, `/v1/models`, and all four chat requests with HTTP 200 and `finish_reason=stop`. Requests used `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=48`, and `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}`:

1. `Reply with only the result: 1+1=?`
2. `Say hello in one short sentence.`
3. Chinese request asking for only the result of 7 times 8.
4. `What is the capital of France? Answer with one word.`

The TP16 corrected run also produced a coherent Chinese introduction and the correct final arithmetic answer with the default thinking mode enabled.

These are focused accuracy smoke tests, not a GSM8K/MMLU evaluation. They used an equivalent diagnostic `narrow` correction on the two revisions above; a new full-model run on this PR's newer main base has **not** been performed. EP16 end-to-end correctness is also **not** claimed: separate trials were blocked by DeepEP/NPU errors before useful generation.

A single-expert NPU grouped-matmul experiment additionally compared the sum of K-partitioned outputs against the unpartitioned output, using real `model.layers.3.mlp.experts.0.down_proj` weights and fixed INT8 input (seed 52):

| Compensation handling | TP8 relative L2 error | TP16 relative L2 error |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full compensation on every rank | 0.971464 | 2.081729 |
| Matching compensation segments per rank | 0.002361 | 0.002371 |
| No-bias additivity control | 0.002343 | 0.002340 |

The corrected error is close to the no-bias partition/reduction rounding control. These numbers are for this single-layer experiment, not model accuracy scores.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the TP16 serving configuration and smoke request</summary>

Run in a configured CANN/PyTorch-NPU environment on both nodes. Set `MODEL_PATH` to the checked-out checkpoint above, `NODE_RANK` to 0 or 1, `LOCAL_HCCL_IP` to the current node's interface address, and `DIST_INIT_ADDR` to the reachable rank-0 rendezvous address and port. The recorded runs used `eno0`; use the interface configured for your cluster.

```bash
source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
if test -f /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh; then
  source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh
fi
export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7
export HCCL_IF_IP="$LOCAL_HCCL_IP"
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eno0 GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=eno0 TP_SOCKET_IFNAME=eno0
export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=400 HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=2
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" --trust-remote-code --dtype bfloat16 \
  --quantization modelslim --attention-backend ascend --device npu \
  --tp-size 16 --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --dist-init-addr "$DIST_INIT_ADDR" \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30052 --served-model-name glm-5.2-w4a8c8 \
  --context-length 65536 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 65536 \
  --max-running-requests 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --moe-a2a-backend none --disable-radix-cache \
  --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \
  --watchdog-timeout 9000 --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --random-seed 800245974
```

On rank 0 after startup:

```bash

curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:30052/v1/models
curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:30052/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"glm-5.2-w4a8c8","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with only the result: 1+1=?"}],"temperature":0,"max_tokens":48,"chat_template_kwargs":{"enable_thinking":false}}'
```

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput benchmark was run. The correction executes once during weight post-processing, before serving; it adds a view selection and reduces fewer compensation elements per TP rank. The inference kernels and forward path are unchanged. No speedup claim is made.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused regression tests added, registered for NPU CI, and executed locally.

title: feat(mooncake): propagate per-request context to store RPC for end-to-end request tracing
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation


  HiCache's KV read/query/writeback paths issue Mooncake store RPCs (`batch_get*`, `batch_exists`, `batch_set*`, …), but those RPCs carry  no request identity. As a result, the Mooncake master cannot attribute a given storage I/O to a specific request, so the `request → store  RPC` trace link is broken and there is no end-to-end request tracing/atrribution on the store path.

  This PR injects a per-request context (`request_id`, plus optional `trace_id` / `span_id` / `parent_span_id`) and propagates it as a  `coro_rpc` attachment on store RPCs. The Mooncake master records it, closing the request→store-RPC trace link.

## Modifications

  Final state carries `request_id` inside `HiCacheStorageExtraInfo.extra_info` without changing any store method signature. 
  - **`mooncake_store.py` (+107/−6)** — `MooncakeBaseStore` gains request-context support:
    - `set_request_context` / `clear_request_context` / `request_context()` context manager, delegating to the underlying
    `MooncakeDistributedStore` Python bindings.
    - Helpers `_extra_info_request_id`, `_request_context_from_extra_info`, and a `_has_request_context_support` `cached_property` guard.
    - The context is held in Mooncake C++ thread-local `g_current_ctx` and attached out-of-band to subsequent store RPCs; it is cleared after
    each request to prevent cross-request interference.
    - `MooncakeStore`, `MooncakeEmbeddingStore`, and `MooncakeDirectLinker` inherit it via `MooncakeBaseStore`.

  - **`cache_controller.py` (+9/−3)** — carry `request_id` in `HiCacheStorageExtraInfo.extra_info` on KV read/query store-RPC paths:
    - `_page_transfer` (`batch_get_v1`, and its KV-derived sidecar `batch_get_v2`);
    - `_storage_hit_query` (`batch_exists`).

  - **`hybrid_cache_controller.py` (+6/−2)** — same `extra_info` propagation:
    - `_storage_hit_query` (`batch_exists` / `batch_exists_v2`) + non-KV sidecar `batch_get_v2`.

  - **Not changed** — store method signatures are untouched (no `request_id` param added; the store reads it from `extra_info`). Write path  (`batch_set*`, backed by `StorageOperation`) carries no `request_id` and is left unchanged; the embedding path has zero net diff.

  - **Backward compatible** — `_has_request_context_support` guards every call; against older Mooncake wheels (no `set_request_context`  binding) it is a no-op (no error, no behavior change).
  
Related mooncake pr: https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/pull/3848


## Accuracy Tests

title: [Metrics] Log forward and forward+idle occupancy over total wall time
body:
# Summary

With `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1`, the prefill and decode log lines reuse the `fwd_occupancy` gauge. That gauge is windowed over `decode_log_interval` batches and starts each window at NaN, so an isolated prefill logs `fwd occupancy: nan%`, and sparse decode traffic logs close to 100% even when the cumulative forward counter says the device was busy a small fraction of the wall time.

Add a separate log window that starts before its first forward, includes the idle gap that preceded it, and resets after `decode_log_interval` processed batches or on an active-to-idle transition. Repeated idle polls retain the idle gap for the next request. The log lines now report two values over the entire wall time since the window started:

- `fwd occupancy` = device forward seconds / wall seconds
- `fwd+idle occupancy` = (device forward seconds + scheduler idle seconds) / wall seconds

Both log paths poll completed device events before formatting; no device synchronization is added. Scheduler time accounting now also runs when only the device timer is enabled, so the log values work without `--enable-metrics`; the Prometheus counters and the `process_time_ns` sampling stay gated on `--enable-metrics`. The existing `fwd_occupancy` / `stats.fwd_occupancy` gauge keeps its timing, initialization, and NaN-at-idle behavior, so `sglang:fwd_occupancy` readers such as the sanity kit are unaffected.

The new window is a `msgspec.Struct` rather than a dataclass, per `.claude/rules/no-dataclasses.md`. No production caller changes; the change is one file.

# Test plan

- `PYTHONPATH=python pytest -q test/registered/unit/observability/test_forward_pass_metrics.py test/registered/unit/observability/test_scheduler_stage_metrics.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_uno_token_accounting.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_pause_generation.py test/registered/unit/managers/test_disagg_idle_step_counters.py`: **60 passed, 53 subtests passed** (CPU, PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130 from the repository lock).
- A local controlled-clock probe with fake device events and `ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER` patched on, without `--enable-metrics`: an idle gap followed by one forward logs `fwd occupancy: 8.00%, fwd+idle occupancy: 98.00%`; an active-to-idle transition and a `decode_log_interval` boundary each reset the window; with `--enable-metrics` the forward and idle Prometheus counters still receive the same seconds as before.
- pre-commit hooks for the changed file (isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 check and format, codespell 2.4.1): **passed**.
- Not run locally: end-to-end serving with a real device timer; the sanity kit's gauge path is untouched by this change.

title: [AMD] Use packed AWQ GEMM for small batches
body:
## Motivation

The ROCm `AWQLinearKernel.apply` path expands the entire weight matrix with `awq_dequantize_triton`, then calls `torch.matmul` on every invocation. `awq_gemm_triton` already exists, but no runtime caller uses it.

This is expensive during decode. I encountered it while tracing the [official Ternary Bonsai AWQ checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-27B-AWQ-4bit/tree/7f49f5d23a09087131cd50627366967f013b9f9e). Its sampled attention and MLP weights use only codes 7, 8 and 9 with zero point 8, but the generic AWQ path still materializes a full floating-point matrix.

## Modifications

- Route gfx1151 ROCm AWQ batches of 1 through 16 rows to the existing packed Triton GEMM with a 16x64x32 tile and split-K 8. Larger batches, other HIP architectures, and CUDA/Marlin routing stay unchanged. CDNA does not take the new path without CDNA measurements.
- Accumulate in FP32 and retain FP32 split-K partials. The existing helper used the output dtype for both, which could overflow on FP16 inputs even when the final answer was finite.
- Reduce split-K partials directly into the activation dtype. Avoid the initial zero-fill and skip reduction for split-K 1.
- Allow BF16 activations on the ROCm AWQ path. Keep checkpoint weights, zero points and scales unchanged. No activation quantization or ternary-specific repacking is introduced.
- Add kernel tests, runtime dispatch coverage for strided/empty/batched inputs and bias, and a paired benchmark. Defer unrelated Quark AITER imports until the operations that need them, so AWQ runtime imports do not require AITER.

## Accuracy tests

On Radeon 8060S, gfx1151, ROCm 7.2.53211, Torch 2.14.0+rocm7.2 and Triton 3.8.0:

```sh
python -m pytest test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_awq_gemm.py -q
# 18 passed in 4.34s
```

Coverage includes FP16/BF16, group sizes 32/64/128/full-K, split-K 1/8, tail output columns, signed packed words, exact agreement between dequantization implementations, and a cancellation case that needs FP32 accumulation.

On the real Bonsai tensor panels below, relative squared error against FP32 matmul of the same dequantized operands was 2.64e-6 for the BF16 attention tensor, 2.75e-6 for the BF16 gate tensor, and 4.27e-8 for the FP16 gate tensor. The dequantize-plus-matmul reference has essentially the same output-rounding error. Reduction order changes, so outputs are not promised bit-identical.

The registered HIP `test_linear_dispatch` now passes on gfx1151, including packed rows 1/16, fallback rows 0/17, BF16/FP16, strided input and bias. A gfx942 architecture control checks that CDNA does not select packed GEMM. Sixteen more cases load both pinned Bonsai layer-0 matrix tensors and compare runtime outputs with FP32 decoded-weight matmul; relative squared errors are below 1e-4 with generated activations. These are layer-level checks, not a full Bonsai model forward. Quark AITER imports have been moved to their operation boundaries, without installing or stubbing AITER. This PR remains a draft pending complete-model or server accuracy acceptance. CDNA performance is unmeasured and CDNA retains the existing fallback, so no CDNA speedup is claimed.

## Speed tests and profiling

Paired GPU-graph timing, nine rounds with alternating arm order and 40 calls per graph, on the hardware above. Actual checkpoint weight tensors are pinned to revision `7f49f5d23a09087131cd50627366967f013b9f9e`; activation inputs are generated with seed 917, not captured model activations. Times include dequantization and matmul in the reference, and packed GEMM plus split reduction in the candidate.

| Weight tensor | M | dtype | K x N | Dequantize + matmul | Packed GEMM | Median paired ratio |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Layer 0 linear attention `in_proj_qkv` | 1 | BF16 | 5120 x 10240 | 1222.43 us | 169.60 us | 7.22x |
| Layer 0 MLP `gate_proj` | 16 | BF16 | 5120 x 17408 | 2116.53 us | 321.31 us | 6.65x |
| Layer 0 MLP `gate_proj` | 1 | FP16 | 5120 x 17408 | 2089.41 us | 279.21 us | 7.48x |

A synthetic 512x1024 ternary AWQ matrix at M=1 took 18.56 vs 6.42 us, 2.89x paired. General random 4-bit weights at 5120x5120 took 564.05 vs 87.43 us at M=1, and 559.33 vs 93.99 us at M=16.

Clock and package-power telemetry was retained with the local panels. The machine had other CPU work, roughly 2 to 3 busy host cores during the real-tensor panels, so these are paired measurements under shared-package load rather than quiet or fixed-clock results. These are linear-operation timings, not end-to-end serving throughput or a comparison with CUDA Marlin.

The included benchmark reproduces the comparison using generated AWQ weights, including the same ternary codes:

```sh
python test/manual/bench_awq_gemm.py --m 1 --k 5120 --n 10240 --dtype bfloat16 --ternary
python test/manual/bench_awq_gemm.py --m 16 --k 5120 --n 17408 --dtype bfloat16 --ternary
```

<details>
<summary>Raw real-tensor timings in microseconds, reference / candidate</summary>

Attention M=1 BF16:
```

1222.131 / 176.600

```
Gate M=16 BF16:
```

The measured kernel source SHA-256 is `fdc3173733796b53c940ec29f9b1279704b56075e65384b6d5de269bc475c55b`.

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Changed files pass the repository's isort/ruff formatting and lint settings, plus `git diff --check`.
- [x] Added focused kernel tests and runtime dispatch coverage. The 18 kernel checks and registered HIP dispatch test passed locally, as did 16 real-weight layer cases.
- [x] Added a standalone paired benchmark and reported exact scope and numerical errors.

title: [AMD][PD] enable mori transfer for PD decode DCP
body:
## Motivation

PD decode with DCP currently rejects the Mori transfer backend because Mori does not implement the token relayout required by round-robin DCP KV shards.

## Changes

- Add DCP rank and layer metadata to Mori peer registration.
- Transfer MLA KV at token granularity into each decode rank's DCP shard.
- Map PP-local KV and Mamba state tensors by global layer ID.
- Handle TP mismatch for replicated latent KV and reject unsupported head-sharded layouts.
- Skip cached-prefix early send when DCP relayout is required.
- Allow Mori in the PD decode DCP backend validation.

## Validation

- Mori DCP unit tests: 6/6 passed.
- ServerArgs DCP tests: 6/6 passed.
- Kimi-K3 PP8/TP1 prefill + TP8/DCP8 decode: both servers healthy, with no KV transfer errors.
- 31K long-context retrieval and arithmetic: 8/8 passed, with no errors or truncation.
- GSM8K: 39/40 (97.5%), with no errors or truncation.
- 32K input, 1 output token, concurrency 16, 128 requests: 16,699 input tok/s and 31.11s median TTFT.
- Pre-commit and lint checks passed.

The Kimi-K3 E2E validation used an AITER DCP-enabled stack; this PR only changes the Mori transfer path.

title: [RL] Keep DSA cuda-graph state and the graph pool intact across TMS pause/resume
body:
## Motivation

In RL colocation the engine releases the `GPU_MEMORY_TYPE_CUDA_GRAPH` torch-memory-saver region while the trainer runs and resumes it before the next rollout. Two things break on main:

1. The full-cuda-graph pool holds capture-time-initialized device state that replays read but never rewrite. Pausing discards it, so the first replay after resume reads garbage.
2. DSA's wide `page_table` (`max_num_tokens x max_ctx_len` int32) and the flashmla metadata stay resident during training even though they are rewritten in full before every replay.

## Modifications

- `FullCudaGraphBackend`: pass `enable_cpu_backup=True` to the memory-saver `cuda_graph` context so the pool is backed up on pause and restored on resume.
- `DeepseekSparseAttnBackend.init_cuda_graph_state`: allocate `page_table` and `flashmla_metadata` inside the pausable cuda-graph region (gated on `--enable-memory-saver` and `SGLANG_MEMORY_SAVER_CUDA_GRAPH`). The other decode metadata is written once at init and stays outside the region.

Squash of sglang-miles #32718, #33479 (authors credited as co-authors).

## Testing

pre-commit clean. Relying on CI for GPU: `test/registered/rl/test_release_memory_occupation*.py` and the DSA cuda-graph paths under `test/registered/rl/`.

title: [AMD] Optimize Qwen3.5 GDN prefill preparation and Triton recurrence on ROCm
body:
## Motivation

[#36267](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36267) removed Qwen3.5 GDN prefill projection unpack copies on CUDA by keeping Q/K/V/Z/B/A as strided views. ROCm still materialized those tensors despite already having stride-aware consumers. ROCm also split QKV and then launched `l2norm_fwd` twice per GDN layer.

This PR ports the view path to ROCm and folds Q/K normalization plus GDN gating into the QKV split. Profiling then showed that the recurrent `chunk_h`/`chunk_o` kernels dominated the remaining GDN time. Their fixed launch geometry under-filled MI355X, while NVIDIA can route GDN prefill through specialized FlashInfer/CuTeDSL backends. This PR therefore adds gfx95-aware Triton launch selection while preserving the original configuration for other platforms, KDA, and unsupported shapes.

The norm fusion differs from [#33290](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33290) and closed [#28361](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28361): those reduce two norm launches to one; this PR reduces them to zero by normalizing while Q/K are already in registers. [#37113](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37113) is the complementary decode projection/Conv1D fusion; its decode branch is mutually exclusive with this prefill path.

## Modifications

- Enable Qwen3.5's strided projection views on ROCm for non-speculative extend. Speculative extend/verify retain the existing unpack path.
- Add `fused_gdn_prefill_prepare`, which in one launch:
  - splits strided post-conv Q/K/V,
  - L2-normalizes Q/K in fp32,
  - passes V through unchanged,
  - computes fp32 GDN `g`/`beta` from strided A/B views.
- Surface `chunk_gated_delta_rule`'s existing `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel` switch through `TritonGDNKernel.extend`.
- Harden non-power-of-two TP-local Q/K head counts by padding both reduction axes and masking padded loads/stores.
- Select AMD GDN `chunk_h` BV from launch-grid coverage and use deeper pipelining for long per-sequence recurrences. Explicit env overrides remain available; non-AMD and KDA retain prior defaults.
- For AMD GDN `K=V=128`, tune `chunk_o` to `BK=64`, `BV=128`, two warps, and three stages. Replace its zero-filled output allocation with `empty_like`, since every valid output element is overwritten.
- Register the existing chunk launch overrides in `environ.py`. No new user-facing option.

## Accuracy Tests

On MI355X, `test_gdn_prefill_layout.py` passes **7 tests / 10 subtests**, covering:

- BF16 and FP16,
- Qwen3.5 TP2 dimensions,
- non-power-of-two Q/K heads,
- empty batches,
- transposed post-conv and strided A/B layouts,
- exact V/g/beta parity,
- Q/K agreement with `l2norm_fwd`,
- GDN-only `chunk_h`/`chunk_o` selector contracts and fallback behavior.

GSM8K, full 1,319-question split, 5-shot, greedy, TP2, two runs per arm:

| Arm | Run 1 | Run 2 | Pooled |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline (pre-PR) | 0.928 | 0.922 | 0.9249 |
| This PR | 0.917 | 0.922 | 0.9196 |

The 0.53pp pooled gap is 0.72σ and does not resolve an accuracy difference. After the new recurrence tuning, a separate no-thinking chat-mode confirmation scores 0.974.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Environment

- 8× MI355X (`gfx950`)
- `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.19-rocm720-mi35x-20260913`
- Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4
- AITER unified attention, Triton linear attention
- FP8 E4M3 KV, page size 16, radix cache disabled
- EAGLE: 3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens
- chunked prefill size 16,384
- InferenceX fixed-length synthetic workload shaped as 70K input / 300 output; this is not an AgentX replay

### Kernel benchmark and attribution

Matched TP2 70K torch-profiler traces contain 225 GDN-layer launches (45 layers × 5 prefill chunks):

| Kernel / shape | Before | After | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `chunk_h`, profile total | 236.08 ms | 123.11 ms | **−47.9%** |
| `chunk_o`, TP2 16K | 0.208 ms | 0.151 ms | **−27.5%** |
| `chunk_o`, TP4 16K | 0.109 ms | 0.076 ms | **−30.7%** |
| `chunk_o`, TP2/TP4 4,464-token tail | 0.052 / 0.031 ms | 0.045 / 0.027 ms | **−14.3% / −14.0%** |

The standalone gating kernel disappears. Its 3.63 ms trace cost is absorbed by a prepare kernel increase from 12.71 to 14.87 ms, for a net 1.47 ms saving over the 70K request.

### End-to-end serving

Each result compares the pre-PR upstream baseline with this PR. Throughput is total tokens per second per GPU (input plus output, divided by TP). C1 rows use mirrored same-GPU-pair ordering; negative TTFT and positive throughput deltas are improvements.

| TP | Conc | Baseline TTFT | This PR TTFT | Δ TTFT | Baseline tok/s/GPU | This PR tok/s/GPU | Δ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 1 | 2549.4 ms | **2471.7 ms** | **−3.05%** | 3312 | **3322** | **+0.31%** |
| 2 | 4 | 2650.2 ms | **2573.4 ms** | **−2.90%** | 7619 | **7755** | **+1.78%** |
| 2 | 8 | 4417.3 ms | 4416.7 ms | −0.42% | 9680 | **9882** | **+2.09%** |
| 4 | 1 | 1754.6 ms | **1685.0 ms** | **−3.97%** | 1759 | **1772** | **+0.70%** |
| 4 | 4 | 1845.3 ms | **1802.5 ms** | **−2.32%** | 4664 | **4734** | **+1.50%** |
| 4 | 8 | 3283.8 ms | **3176.9 ms** | **−2.77%** | 6327 | **6475** | **+2.35%** |

TP2 concurrency 8 pools four GPU pairs, with the two GPUs 2+0 runs averaged first. Its TTFT delta is the mean of the four pair ratios; the TTFT columns are the averaged medians, which sit 0.5 ms apart. Total throughput was higher on every pair. TPOT is within +0.56% at TP2 C1 and +0.03% at TP4 C1; flat decode metrics are expected for a prefill-only optimization. TP2 C4 includes the tuned `chunk_o` launch but predates the final `empty_like` cleanup. TP4 C4/C8 predate both `chunk_o` changes and are therefore conservative. TP4 C8 has substantial queue-order variance; the table reports the mirrored crossover.

title: [NPU] Skip fused gmm1+swiglu for swiglu_limit (SiLU-with-clamp) checkpoints
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #39881. The fused gmm1 kernel ( npu_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2 ) applies plain SiLU with no clamp , but _uses_fused_gmm1 selected it for W4A8 MXFP4 MoE based only on the kernel type and use_fused_gmm1 — it never looked at the activation configuration.

Checkpoints whose MoE activation is SiLU-with-clamp ( swiglu_limit , e.g. DSV4) therefore lost the clamp when the fused kernel was selected, producing incorrect numerics. This silently bypassed the clamp path ( NPUSwigluMxfp8Quant ) that #38420 had just added for exactly this case.

## Modifications

Single-file change in python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/ascend.py :

- _uses_fused_gmm1(kernel, config) now takes the runner config and returns False when config.swiglu_limit is set and > 0 :
  - W4A8 MXFP4 + swiglu_limit (DSV4): falls back to the unfused path — w13 gmm + NPUSwigluMxfp8Quant(config.swiglu_limit) , which applies the clamp. This restores the pre-#39881 behavior
  - MXFP8 + swiglu_limit : raises NotImplementedError at init — this method has no unfused gmm1 path, so failing loudly beats silently serving wrong numerics (no known checkpoint hits this combination today)
  - Plain-SiLU models ( swiglu_limit unset or 0 ): keep the fused kernel, unchanged
- Both call sites ( __init__ and run() ) now pass the same config, so the activation selection and the fused/unfused branch decision can never disagree

## Accuracy Tests

- Dispatch logic verified locally with mocked kernels for all combinations: W4A8 ± swiglu_limit, MXFP8 ± swiglu_limit, use_fused_gmm1=False , and non-fused kernels — all resolve as intended
- DSV4 on NPU (fp4 experts → NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod , swiglu_limit from HF config) now resolves to the unfused clamp path, bit-identical to the pre-#39881 serving path

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None — this PR intentionally trades the #39881 fusion gain back for correctness on clamp checkpoints. Plain-SiLU models (e.g. Kimi-K3 MXFP4) keep the full fused-path benefit (~15% per-layer MoE latency reduction from #39881). Recovering the fusion gain for clamp checkpoints would require adding a limit parameter to the fused kernel, which is kernel-side work out of scope here.

title: [NPU] Fuse FIA KV-cache K/V writes into one npu_scatter_pa_kv_cache call
body:
## Motivation
On the NPU FIA path ( ASCEND_USE_FIA=1 ), NPUMHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer writes K and V into the paged KV cache with two separate npu_scatter_nd_update_ kernels — one per tensor, indexed by the same out_cache_loc . That is two kernel launches per layer on the decode critical path.

MiMo-V2.5-Pro EP6 decode profiling (msprof, DeepEP LL, 57 MoE layers) shows the two aclnnScatterNdUpdate kernels cost ~11.1us/layer.

torch_npu provides npu_scatter_pa_kv_cache , which writes both K and V in a single kernel .

## Modifications
- environ.py : add SGLANG_NPU_USE_SCATTER_PA_KV_CACHE (default False )
- memory_pool_npu.py : gate the FIA branch of set_kv_buffer on the env var —
  - enabled: single npu_scatter_pa_kv_cache call (K+V in one kernel, cache_mode="Norm" )
  - disabled: the original two npu_scatter_nd_update_ calls, unchanged (fallback for older torch_npu/CANN or explicit opt-out)
- guards: fail loudly when the installed torch_npu lacks the op, and when the store dtype is outside the op's fp16/bf16/int8 contract
- slot_mapping is passed through in its native dtype (int32 or int64): the op accepts both, and the prefill/spec paths deliver int64 out_cache_loc — an unconditional .to(int32) would add a per-layer cast kernel, partially defeating the fusion

## Accuracy Tests
Bit-identical by construction — same flat-slot indexing, and verified at two levels on Ascend:

1. Op level : npu_scatter_pa_kv_cache vs two npu_scatter_nd_update_ writing the same K/V into identical paged buffers, with cross-page slot targets (page_size=4, slots spanning multiple pages) — final buffers torch.equal in both K and V
2. Pool level : full NPUMHATokenToKVPool constructed with ASCEND_USE_FIA=1 , set_kv_buffer executed with the gate off vs on (with an int64 loc , matching the dtype the prefill/spec paths deliver), all layer K/V buffers compared torch.equal — identical
3. int64 slot_mapping : verified the op accepts int64 indices directly and produces identical buffers vs the int32 form

```

sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0

export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600
export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
export ASCEND_USE_FIA=1
export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=32
export DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2500

title: fix: zero the default Qwen3 classification bias
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #38768. Standard Transformers Qwen3 sequence-classification checkpoints have `score.weight` but no `score.bias`. SGLang currently keeps the randomly initialized bias, so these checkpoints silently produce `W @ h + b_init` instead of `W @ h`.

## Modifications

Initialize the existing classifier bias to zero. Checkpoints that explicitly provide `score.bias` still overwrite it through the existing weight loader. Add a CPU CI regression exercising both checkpoint shapes through the real classification constructor and `load_weights`; the unit test isolates the unrelated backbone with `nn.Identity`.

## Accuracy Tests

- `PYTHONPATH=python python3 test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_classification_bias.py`: passed (missing-bias and explicit-bias subcases). The missing-bias case fails on upstream.
- Also instantiated the complete native one-layer Qwen3 model with a tiny config (`hidden_size=8`, `num_labels=3`) and a real single-rank Gloo process group, without mocking the backbone. Loaded `score.weight`, then compared classifier outputs on fixed hidden states with `torch.nn.functional.linear(..., bias=None)`. Maximum absolute logit error: **0.320134 before, 0.0 after**. The fixed model's classifier also passes on an RTX 5060 Ti (PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130).
- This validates head initialization/loading and head-output parity; it is not a full transformer-forward or model-server accuracy benchmark.
- Pre-commit checks passed for both changed files, including registered-test validation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The change only zeroes a small bias once during construction; the forward path is unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format checks passed for changed files.
- [x] Added a registered CPU regression test using `CustomTestCase`.
- [x] Verified bias-free output parity and explicit checkpoint-bias compatibility.
- [x] Followed the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [CPU][kernel] fix rope for VLA model on CPU
body:
## Motivation
`torch.ops.sgl_kernel.apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu` kernel only takes 3D `[num_tokens, num_heads, head_size]` inputs and had no `unsqueeze_dim` argument. Pi0.5 calls it with 4D `[batch, num_heads, seq_len, head_size]` q/k and `unsqueeze_dim=1`, so it failed on CPU:

```
"/python/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/vlas/pi05_core.py", line 382, in forward
    query_states, key_states = native_apply_rotary_pos_emb(
  File "//lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/_ops.py", line 1350, in __call__
    return self._op(*args, **kwargs)
RuntimeError: sgl_kernel::apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu() expected at most 4 argument(s) but received 5 argument(s). Declaration: sgl_kernel::apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu(Tensor query, Tensor key, Tensor cos, Tensor sin) -> (Tensor, Tensor)
```
- https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/vlas/pi05_core.py#L902C32-L902C59

## Modifications

- `apply_rotary_pos_emb_cpu` now takes `unsqueeze_dim` (default 1) and supports q/k of 3D and higher, with the head dim at `unsqueeze_dim` (e.g. `[B, H, S, D]` or `[B, S, H, D]`). It is out-of-place, matching `apply_rotary_pos_emb_native`.
- The neox rope path now handles float32 inputs, and the CPU graph fake op is updated for the new signature.

## Test Coverage

- pi0.5 model functionality

- `test_apply_rotary_pos_emb` in `test/registered/cpu/test_rope.py`. It compares against the native reference for:
  (1) 3D with GQA, 4D `[B, H, S, D]` with `unsqueeze_dim=1`, and (2) 4D `[B, S, H, D]` with `unsqueeze_dim=2`

title: [chore] surface the cookbook to users who pip install sglang
body:
## Motivation

#40818 pointed coding agents at the cookbook, but everything it added lives in `.claude/` rules and docs, and both are excluded from the wheel:

```toml
[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
exclude = ["assets*", "benchmark*", "docs*", "dist*", "playground*", "scripts*", "tests*"]
```

So for anyone who runs `pip install sglang` rather than cloning the repo — the majority of users — there was no path to the cookbook at all. The README had zero mentions of it, `[project.urls]` carried only Homepage and Bug Tracker, and no CLI help mentioned it.

## Modifications

Add the pointer where a pip user actually looks:

- **CLI help.** `sglang --help`, `sglang serve --help` and `sglang generate --help` now end with a one-line pointer. For `serve` it is printed once in the help branch after whichever backend help ran, rather than as each backend parser's epilog — the auto path prints both the LLM and diffusion help, so an epilog per parser would repeat it. This also covers an LLM-only install, where the diffusion parser never runs.
- **`[project.urls]`.** Adds `Documentation` and `Cookbook`, which render in the PyPI sidebar.
- **README.** One line in Getting Started.

The wording stays generic ("its cookbook page carries the recommended command for it: GPU count, parallelism, quantization and the flags that matter for that model") so it does not go stale as the cookbook grows.

## Accuracy Test

Not applicable — no runtime behaviour changes; the CLI additions only affect `--help` output.

Verified on an H200 devbox that every help path prints the pointer exactly once, at the end:

| command | occurrences |
| --- | --- |
| `sglang --help` | 1 |
| `sglang serve --help` (auto) | 1 |
| `sglang serve --model-type llm --help` | 1 |
| `sglang serve --model-type diffusion --help` | 1 |
| `sglang generate --help` | 1 |

title: [Score API] Setwise Scoring Support
body: # Setwise Scoring Support ## Summary Adds **setwise scoring** to the score API: a SequenceClassification deployment can read its classification head **at every occurrence of a caller-chosen extraction token** in each `query + item` sequence, instead of only at the last token. A candidate set is packed into one item with one extraction token per candidate, and the head is pooled at each of those positions in a **single forward pass**, so `scores` comes back as one `[N_i x num_labels]` matrix per item (nested per item). This is a generic multi-position pooling primitive (`token_indices_to_pool`) that setwise scoring is the first consumer of; it is designed to extend to token classification, multi-vector embeddings, etc. The feature works in both execution modes: - **Batched (default):** each item is scored as an independent `query + item` sequence in one batch. - **Fused (`--enable-mis`):** the items are fused into one multi-item sequence (block-diagonal mask, shared query-prefix KV). Both modes return the same nested per-item shape. ## Motivation Rerankers and listwise/setwise rankers score a *set* of candidates jointly. Without this feature a caller must issue one request per candidate (last-token pooling), paying the query-prefix cost N times and losing any cross-candidate context. Setwise scoring packs the whole candidate block into one prompt with one anchor token per candidate and returns all N scores from a single prefill, cutting redundant prefill work and giving the head a single fused view of the set. ## API ### Engine (in-process) ```python result = engine.score( query="", # optional shared prefix items=[prompt_with_anchors], # one item = one candidate set score_extraction_token_id=anchor_id, apply_softmax=False, return_pooled_hidden_states=False, ) # result.scores -> [num_items][N_i x num_labels] (nested per item) # result.pooled_hidden_states (optional) parallels scores: per-item, per-anchor vectors ``` `async_score(...)` takes the same `score_extraction_token_id` argument. ### HTTP (`POST /v1/score`) ```json { "query": "", "items": ["Rank the candidates. ... Scores:<|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|>"], "score_extraction_token": "<|object_ref_start|>", "apply_softmax": false } ``` - Request adds `score_extraction_token: Optional[str]` (resolved to an id in the tokenizer-manager process, which owns the tokenizer). - `ScoringResponse.scores` is now a union: `[num_rows x num_labels]` (pointwise) or nested `[num_items][N_i x num_labels]` (setwise). `pooled_hidden_states` follows the same nesting. ### Semantics & validation - SequenceClassification only, and specifically models whose forward routes the head through `score_and_pool` (per-position pooling) — an explicit allow-list (`is_score_and_pool_model`). Generation (CausalLM), cross-encoder (`CrossEncodingPooler`), reward, and embedding models are rejected **before** inference, and `item_first` is incompatible. - An omitted `query` is normalized by item type (`[]` for pre-tokenized items, `""` for text) so token-ID items with no query take the token-ID path. - Every item must contain at least one extraction token; the shared query prefix must not contain it (both raise a clean `400` before inference). - The fused (`--enable-mis`) path carries the standard MIS delimiter tokens, so its scores differ slightly from the independent batched path — the inherent MIS trade-off, not specific to score extraction. ## Deployment / server start Pooling positions are full-prompt coordinates and all positions must be processed in one prefill, so setwise scoring requires radix cache and chunked prefill to be off. These constraints are validated at request time. Batched setwise: ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --disable-radix-cache \ --chunked-prefill-size -1 ``` Fused multi-item setwise (adds MIS): ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --enable-mis \ --disable-radix-cache \ --chunked-prefill-size -1 ``` (`--enable-mis` already auto-disables CUDA graph / radix cache / chunked prefill.) `--allow-auto-truncate` is rejected, since truncation would leave pooling positions pointing past the truncated length. ## Worked example Serving a real multi-task setwise ranker (`num_labels = 7`): ```bash python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path /shared/public/elr-models/sjsmodels/downloaded_models/sps_l3_multitask_ranker_setwise_history_0_0_4_0_peoplesearch-oc_sps_l3_multitask_ranker_setwise_history/proxima/model_resources \ --attention-backend flashinfer \ --dtype float16 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --chunked-prefill-size -1 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.15 \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` Two items (candidate sets), each with three anchors → nested `[num_items][N_i x num_labels]` (2 items × 3 rows × 7 labels): ```bash curl -s http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/score \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "query": "", "items": [ "Rank the candidates. Candidate 0. Candidate 1. Candidate 2. Scores:<|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|>", "Rank the candidates. Candidate 0. Candidate 1. Candidate 2. Scores:<|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|><|object_ref_start|>" ], "score_extraction_token": "<|object_ref_start|>", "apply_softmax": false }' | python -m json.tool ``` ```json { "scores": [ [ [0.7158203125, -0.326171875, -2.576171875, -5.640625, -5.984375, -1.6240234375, -7.328125], [0.72314453125, -0.333984375, -2.560546875, -5.6015625, -5.8203125, -1.6318359375, -7.25390625], [0.7353515625, -0.35302734375, -2.587890625, -5.6171875, -5.6796875, -1.6337890625, -7.1875] ], [ [0.7158203125, -0.326171875, -2.576171875, -5.640625, -5.984375, -1.6240234375, -7.328125], [0.72314453125, -0.333984375, -2.560546875, -5.6015625, -5.8203125, -1.6318359375, -7.25390625], [0.7353515625, -0.35302734375, -2.587890625, -5.6171875, -5.6796875, -1.6337890625, -7.1875] ] ], "pooled_hidden_states": null, "model": "default", "usage": { "prompt_tokens": 42, "total_tokens": 42, "completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens_details": null, "reasoning_tokens": 0 }, "object": "scoring" } ``` (The two items are identical here, so their matrices match; each item independently yields one `[3 x 7]` matrix — one row per candidate anchor, seven task labels wide.) ## Implementation | Area | File | Change | |---|---|---| | Pooling kernel | `layers/pooler.py` | `pool_at_positions()` (pool AT positions, no `delimiter-1` shift, no discarded row) and a multi-position branch in `score_and_pool()`. | | Request plumbing | `managers/io_struct.py` | `token_indices_to_pool` on `EmbeddingReqInput` / `TokenizedEmbeddingReqInput`, split in `__getitem__`. | | | `managers/schedule_batch.py` | `Req.token_indices_to_pool`. | | | `managers/scheduler.py` | Partition prefill batches by pooling mode in `get_new_batch_prefill` so pooling-readout (setwise) and standard requests never share a forward batch — valid requests are never rejected based on concurrent traffic. | | | `managers/scheduler.py` (io), `managers/tokenizer_manager.py` | Thread the field through request construction. | | Forward batch | `model_executor/forward_batch_info.py` | Build per-request `token_indices_to_pool` CPU tensors in `init_new` (mirrors `multi_item_delimiter_indices`; read-only over the ScheduleBatch). | | | `model_executor/model_runner.py` | Skip the prefill CUDA-graph path when `token_indices_to_pool` is set. | | Score engine | `managers/tokenizer_manager_score_mixin.py` | Extraction-token resolution/scanning, omitted-query normalization, capability-based validation, per-item anchor bucketing for MIS, and nested per-item result grouping (`per_item_matrix`). | | | `configs/model_config.py` | `is_score_and_pool_model()` allow-list of SequenceClassification architectures that pool the head per position. | | Entry points | `entrypoints/engine_score_mixin.py` | `score_extraction_token_id` on `score()` / `async_score()`. | | | `entrypoints/openai/protocol.py`, `entrypoints/openai/serving_score.py` | `score_extraction_token` field, token→id resolution, recursive tensor→list conversion for nested `pooled_hidden_states`. | | Tests / bench | `test/registered/unit/...`, `test/registered/e2e/scoring/test_setwise_scoring.py`, `benchmark/prefill_only/bench_setwise_score.py` | Unit + HF-parity + MIS tests and an Engine benchmark. | 16 files, +2080 / -45. ## Review feedback addressed - **Mixed-traffic reliability (High).** Setwise and pointwise requests share the `/v1/score` endpoint and scheduler queue, so a client cannot guarantee homogeneous batches. Rather than reject setwise requests that happen to be batched with pointwise ones, the scheduler now **partitions prefill batches by pooling mode** (`get_new_batch_prefill`): a batch admits only the pooling mode of its first request, and the other mode runs in the next batch. The earlier traffic-dependent 400 abort is removed, restoring the additive/backward-compatible contract. Guarded by `test_mixed_setwise_and_pointwise_concurrent_batch`. - **Omitted `query` for tokenized input (Medium).** `query` now normalizes to `[]` for pre-tokenized items and `""` for text before path selection, so `engine.score(items=[[...token ids...]])` (and HTTP requests with no `query`) take the token-ID path instead of being rejected by the text builder. Guarded by `test_setwise_tokenized_items_omitted_query_match_hf`. - **Eligibility tied to `score_and_pool` (Low).** Validation now uses an explicit allow-list (`is_score_and_pool_model`) of SequenceClassification architectures that pool the head per position, so reward/embedding models (which pool a single vector and would ignore the readout positions) are rejected up front instead of after a wasted forward. Guarded by `test_validation_rejects_reward_model` / `test_validation_rejects_embedding_model`. ## Validation Environment: H200, `flashinfer 0.6.18`, `Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B-seq-cls` (anchor `<|object_ref_start|>`), engine `float16` on `flashinfer`. ```bash # CPU unit tests (no GPU / model needed) python test/registered/unit/layers/test_pooler_score_and_pool.py -v python test/registered/unit/managers/test_setwise_score_mixin.py -v # E2E (GPU); setwise uses a SequenceClassification checkpoint export TEST_CLASSIFICATION_BASE_MODEL=/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B-seq-cls python test/registered/e2e/scoring/test_setwise_scoring.py -v # Regression on the existing scoring paths export TEST_MODEL_NAME=/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct python test/registered/prefill_only/test_score_engine.py -v python test/registered/prefill_only/test_score_api.py -v python test/registered/prefill_only/test_serving_rerank.py -v ``` Results — all passing (106 cases): | Suite | Cases | Result | |---|---|---| | `test_pooler_score_and_pool.py` (CPU) | 12 | PASS | | `test_setwise_score_mixin.py` (CPU) | 44 | PASS | | `test_setwise_scoring.py` (E2E: HF-parity + MIS + mixed-batch + tokenized) | 10 | PASS | | `test_score_engine.py` (E2E regression) | 19 | PASS | | `test_score_api.py` (HTTP regression) | 8 | PASS | | `test_serving_rerank.py` (mock) | 13 | PASS | The E2E setwise tests assert **numerical parity** against a HuggingFace reference (gather the final hidden state at the anchor positions, apply the model's own classification head) — a wrong pooling position or head application changes the numbers, not just the shape. The MIS tests assert the nested per-item shape and block-diagonal set isolation (a set's scores are unchanged by other sets). ## Backward compatibility Purely additive. `score_extraction_token` / `score_extraction_token_id` default to `None`; when unset, the pointwise last-token path and its `[num_rows x num_labels]` shape are unchanged, as confirmed by the score-engine, score-api, and rerank regression suites. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #35742837071](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35742837071) Latest PR Test (Extra): :no_entry_sign: [Run #35742836922](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35742836922) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #35742837003](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35742837003)

title: [DeepSeek V4.1] Support encoder-only prefill for PD disaggregation
body:
## Motivation

Introduce an experimental encoder-only prefill path for DeepSeek V4.1 in prefill/decode disaggregation. This is intended to reduce redundant prefill-side work while preserving the state required by the decode worker.

Closes #39963.

This PR is intentionally opened as a draft while GPU end-to-end correctness and performance data are being collected.

## Modifications

- Add `--dsv41-encoder-only-prefill` and validate its supported deployment envelope at startup.
- Stop the prefill worker after the DeepSeek V4.1 encoder/global-cache producer boundary, without running the remaining layers or sampling.
- Add a cache-only disaggregation handoff that transfers the ratio-1/2 Main-KV state and owner Indexer-K state through Mooncake.
- Reuse decode-side preallocated KV slots and replay at most the final 128 prompt tokens once to rebuild request-local SWA/ratio-2 state and produce the first token.
- Add explicit cache-only wire and one-shot replay markers, including correct replay admission after priority scheduling reorders requests.
- Add focused unit coverage for the wire contract, priority scheduling, decode preparation, and compressed DeepSeek V4 memory pools.

Current limitations / fail-fast constraints:

- Mooncake transfer backend only.
- Pipeline, data, and context parallel sizes must all be 1.
- Overlap scheduling, speculative decoding, LoRA, and multimodal inputs are not supported in this mode yet.

## Accuracy Tests

- Added targeted unit tests for the new wire protocol, replay scheduling, and memory-pool behavior.
- Python compilation and AST validation pass.
- The targeted pytest invocation cannot complete collection in the current environment because `triton` is not installed (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named triton`; the subsequent `KeyError: sglang` is a follow-on import error).
- GPU end-to-end accuracy validation is still pending and will be added before marking the PR ready for review.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not available yet. No performance claim is made in this draft. GPU end-to-end benchmarks and profiling will be added before the PR is marked ready for review.

title: [HiSparse] Add speculative decoding support with multi-step KV cache swapping
body:
## Prerequisite

- Kernel implementation #32162 provides the multi-step gather/commit swap kernel, including cross-step miss deduplication, extra-page lookup, scratch-space management, cache commit, and device-location resolution. This PR focuses on integrating that kernel into the SGLang serving path.

## Motivation

This PR adds end-to-end HiSparse support for multi-step speculative decoding, currently targeting linear EAGLE/MTP decoding with multiple draft tokens. It integrates the multi-step swap kernel from #32162 into the HiSparse coordinator and speculative-decoding lifecycle, covering logical target-slot reservation, per-layer scratch and cache state, verify preparation, accepted-token commit, host backup, and request cleanup. Draft KV remains in its logical GPU address space instead of reusing the HiSparse target KV physical mapping, while the target KV continues to use HiSparse host/device placement. The PR also preserves speculative state when requests transition through HiSparse staging and, for Mooncake PD serving, carries separate target host/physical page indices and draft logical-device page indices. Together, these changes make HiSparse compatible with multi-step speculative decoding without falling back to sequential per-step LRU swapping.


## Accuracy Tests

- Model: GLM-5.2-W4AFP8
- Serving topology: 1P1D, TP8/DP8 with DP Attention
- KV cache: FP8
- Speculative decoding: EAGLE, 3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens
- CUDA Graph: enabled
- HiSparse: top-k 2048, 4096-slot device buffer, host/device ratio 4
- The only A/B variable was whether HiSparse was enabled.

| Benchmark | HiSparse ON | HiSparse OFF | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K 20-shot (200 samples) | 195/200 (97.50%) | 192/200 (96.00%) | +1.50 pp |
| GPQA-Diamond (198 samples) | 180/198 (90.91%) | 182/198 (91.92%) | -1.01 pp |

title: [Fix] Use cached prefix lengths for FlashInfer full-attention ragged prefill
body:
## Motivation

In a mixed sliding-window/full-attention model, FlashInfer ragged prefill plans the full-attention layer's paged read over `seq_lens`. The new K/V is not written to the cache until after attention, and the ragged wrapper already handles those tokens. Reading their cache slots can therefore mix stale K/V into the result.

## Modifications

- Plan the full-attention paged read over `prefix_lens` when ragged prefill is active. Use the host prefix total when available, retaining the existing device-sum fallback pattern.
- Add one deterministic GPU regression to the existing FlashInfer SWA suite. It poisons unwritten extend slots and checks the real attention output. No model checkpoint is needed.

Paged-only execution is unchanged. Two files; eight backend lines added.

## Accuracy Tests

On NVIDIA B300, using upstream `7b977ce5dcce6e61f0a5f8ef8b4235e42eb00299`, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, FlashInfer 0.6.18, and sglang-kernel 0.4.7+cu130:

- New regression on unmodified upstream: fails numerically, maximum absolute error **14.0** against tolerance **0.04**. The same test passes with the fix.
- FlashInfer SWA suite: **8 passed**. Dense suite: **8 passed**. No skips. The regression also passes with the optional host prefix list omitted.
- Public-model reachability: `unsloth/gemma-3-1b-it` at `5b11413a10db4e486ef16a20101fd028f8f2499c`, BF16, TP1, FlashInfer, page size 1, eager execution. Actual full-attention forwards use the ragged path. With a 384-token prompt and 257 cached tokens, the full wrapper plans 384 cache slots before the fix and 257 afterward.
- For three frozen prompts below the sliding-window boundary, full-vocabulary next-token KL between cold and cached prefill changes from **3.50e-5 / 8.75e-5 / 4.17e-7** to **1.89e-8 / 2.76e-6 / 6.55e-8**. This is numerical cache consistency, not a model-quality evaluation. A separate cold-versus-cached discrepancy above the sliding window remains outside this fix.

Reproduce the regression:

```bash
python3 test/registered/attention/unittests/swa/test_flashinfer.py \
  TestFlashInferSWAAttentionBackendCorrectness.test_full_layer_ragged_prefill_reads_cached_prefix_only -v
```

Changed-file pre-commit hooks pass. The all-files run passes its non-Rust hooks; four Rust hooks could not execute because the local host lacks cargo/rustup. No Rust files are changed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput improvement is claimed. The normal ragged-prefill path uses the existing CPU prefix lengths without adding a device-to-host scalar read.

title: [diffusion] fix: _accepts_mxfp8_input crashes on LoRA-wrapped linears (H3)
body:
## Problem

With a LoRA loaded on the MiniMax H3 diffusion pipeline, **every generation request fails on its first forward**:

```
AttributeError: 'RowParallelLinearWithLoRA' object has no attribute 'quant_method'
```

The LoRA itself loads and converts fine (LoRAFormatAdapter, 266 layers), and the crash is independent of quantization (reproduces with and without `kitchen_int8`).

## Root cause

`_accepts_mxfp8_input()` probes each linear for the mxfp8 fast path and dereferences `linear.quant_method` directly. When the linear is LoRA-wrapped, the module is a `RowParallelLinearWithLoRA` (a `BaseLayerWithLoRA`, not a `LinearBase`) and has no `quant_method` attribute — only the wrapped `base_layer` does.

Note this is a different call path than the one fixed by #24410: that PR guarded the merge-decision check (`base_layer` may not be a `LinearBase`); this crash happens later, at the mxfp8 probe during the denoise stage.

## Fix

`getattr()` with a `None` default, recursing into `base_layer` so the probe resolves the wrapped linear's real quant method (keeps semantics correct for LoRA-over-quantized bases):

```python
def _accepts_mxfp8_input(linear: nn.Module) -> bool:
    quant_method = getattr(linear, "quant_method", None)
    if quant_method is None and hasattr(linear, "base_layer"):
        # LoRA wrapper: recurse into the wrapped base linear
        return _accepts_mxfp8_input(linear.base_layer)
    return quant_method is not None and quant_method.accepts_mxfp8_input(linear)
```

## Verification

8x A800-SXM4-80GB (sm_80), MiniMax H3 Ref2VA, serving via `sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.launch_server` with `--num-gpus 2 --ulysses-degree 2 --layerwise-offload-components text_encoder --component-quantizations.transformer kitchen_int8 --lora-path <minimax_h3_turbo_v4_step600>`:

| Config | 10s 960x544 case | 4s smoke |
|---|---|---|
| USP2 + kitchen_int8 + turbo LoRA (12 steps) | **3.67 min wall (11 steps x 17.70 s/it)** — fastest known path for this workload | 2.34 min |
| USP2 + kitchen_int8, no LoRA (50 steps) | 14.51 min | 7.84 min |

Without this patch the LoRA configs fail 100% of requests; with it, generation completes end-to-end (mp4 with audio track) and 3-frame spot checks look correct.

## DCO

Signed-off-by: Jiang Lu <mail@jiang.lu>
