title: fix: align deterministic Triton GDN prefill chunks across scheduler paths
body:
> **2026-09-23 update:** The validated patch is [44b69115](https://github.com/sha7doww/sglang/commit/44b69115aa89122410b04c8422154c34928528fe), pushed to this PR's source branch. This PR is still closed: GitHub reports `viewerCanReopen=false` for the author and retains the old PR head. The implementation and validation described below refer to the updated commit, pending reopening by someone with permission.

## Motivation

Deterministic inference with Triton GDN prefill can produce different logprobs when scheduling changes the intermediate chunk lengths. This is reproducible on main `1d59ce7c9063edec20fd3f5a49a504b8c12acd23` with the public `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` model, FA3 full attention, and FP32 recurrent state.

Setting the configured chunk budget to a multiple of 64 is insufficient: concurrent requests consume part of the budget. With a 1024-token budget, observed first chunks were 1017 tokens in normal admission and 889 tokens in the cache-disabled `ignore_eos` path. The subsequent chunks preserve this displaced boundary. Serial repeats were exact, but concurrent responses could differ from their serial reference.

The constraint belongs to the dispatched Triton GDN prefill implementation, whose FLA chunk size is 64. It does not require imposing 4096-token chunks on every FA3 model.

## Modifications

- Expose an optional deterministic prefill chunk alignment on attention backends. Hybrid wrappers propagate the prefill/linear backend's requirement. GDN advertises the FLA chunk size when its actual extend implementation is Triton, including the CuTe DSL fallback on Hopper.
- Combine this requirement with existing FlashInfer/Triton full-attention alignment using LCM. Apply it only in deterministic mode, leaving dLLM outside this new constraint.
- Align intermediate chunks in normal admission, cache-disabled `ignore_eos`, and continuation admission. Preserve complete short tails and page allocation constraints. If the remaining budget cannot fit a legal chunk, defer without charging tokens or announcing a successful prefill.
- Keep a deferred continuation out of another request's batch accounting. Preserve the single unfinished-chunk slot while allowing a complete short request to run.
- Reject enabled fixed chunk budgets below the smallest legal chunk. Clamp dynamic predictions to that minimum so the same prediction cannot indefinitely park a continuation; memory admission can still defer it.

Related context: #10645 / #10694 introduced the existing full-attention constraints; #13309 discussed GDN chunk sensitivity; #35632 restricts deterministic GDN prefill to Triton. This change addresses scheduler chunk lengths, not the separate radix-prefix FA3 layout proposals in #25479 / #25481.

## Accuracy Tests

Environment: 4 × H20 96 GB, TP4, Python 3.10.10, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, sglang-kernel 0.4.7, FlashInfer 0.6.18, Transformers 5.16.1. Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`. Explicit `SGLANG_MAMBA_SSM_DTYPE=float32`, FA3 full attention and Triton linear attention. Overlap and CUDA graphs were disabled. Each chunk configuration used a fresh server.

### Cache disabled: current main versus candidate

Three synthetic prompt lengths (4127, 4224, 6151), normal and `ignore_eos` requests, two serial repeats and two rounds of three concurrent requests per mode: 24 responses per chunk budget. Exact means equality of returned input/output token logprobs, input/output top-5 logprobs, and text against the corresponding **main, unchunked, serial** reference. Per-request traces verified continuous coverage and the actual intermediate chunk lengths; concurrent prefill batches contained up to two requests.

| Chunk budget | Main: serial exact | Main: concurrent exact | Candidate: serial exact | Candidate: concurrent exact |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| disabled (`-1`) | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 |
| 1000 | 0/12 | 0/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 |
| 1024 | 12/12 | 5/12 | 12/12 | 12/12 |

Main: `1d59ce7c9063edec20fd3f5a49a504b8c12acd23`; candidate for this matrix: `6c5975cd1b2dfff10e78fecb3387383f1be8a881`. All candidate intermediate chunks satisfied the effective alignment. All serial repeats were exact within their own configuration, including on main. Generated text also agreed across the tested configurations: the observed regression here is in logprobs, not an observed greedy-token divergence.

Final head `44b69115aa89122410b04c8422154c34928528fe` adds the dynamic-budget minimum and completes the ignore-eos test fixture. A fresh run at budget 1000 repeated all 24 cold-cache responses (both modes, serial/concurrent): **24/24 exact** against the same main, unchunked reference, with all observed intermediate chunks aligned.

### Warm prefix cache

With `extra_buffer`, each serial request and each concurrent round was preceded by a cache flush and a 4097-token seed request. Normal admission was tested at budgets `-1` and `1000`; logprob scoring started after the seed prefix. On the candidate, all 24 measured requests had `cached_tokens=4096` and an observed prefill start of 4096. All signatures matched main's unchunked warm reference exactly. At budget 1000, the 6151-token request used 960-token continuation chunks; one concurrent schedule began with 832 tokens, followed by 960, and still matched.

Main's unchunked warm case also matched throughout. Its 1000-budget case differed, but its actual cache hits changed from 960 in serial execution to several different lengths under concurrency. Those main results therefore do **not** isolate continuation splitting from changes in the cached prefix state. The candidate's fixed-prefix result is the controlled warm comparison; it does not establish equivalence for arbitrary cold/warm transitions.

### Kernel scope and limitations

A direct FLA test compared single splits and periodic splits at 1000 / 1024 / 1088 / 4096, lengths 4127 / 4224, and three seeds. With FP32 recurrent state, all 36 aligned cases matched the unsplit output and final state exactly; all 12 unaligned cases differed. Unsplit repeat controls were exact. With BF16 recurrent state, aligned splits still did not consistently match: this scheduler change is not a complete determinism guarantee for reduced-precision recurrent state and adds no dtype restriction.

The service evidence covers these inputs and configurations. It is not an exhaustive numerical proof or a claim that changing the cached prefix state is equivalent to starting cold.

### CPU regression tests

Final head `44b69115aa89122410b04c8422154c34928528fe`: **54 passed, 57 subtests passed** on the environment above, with all GPUs hidden.

The added tests cover runtime configuration, backend wrappers, existing alignment LCM, fixed/dynamic minimum budgets, all three admission paths, temporary-budget deferral and resumption, short tails, page alignment, the unfinished-chunk slot, and deferred-request batch accounting. Existing chunked-request gate/abort tests are included in the regression command:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_prefill_adder.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_deterministic_gdn_prefill.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_chunked_req_gate.py \
  test/registered/unit/managers/test_scheduler_chunked_abort_race.py
```

<details>
<summary>Cold-cache reproduction commands and client</summary>

Run a fresh server for each budget (`-1`, `1000`, `1024`) on main and the PR head. Change `CHUNK_BUDGET` and the output filename for each run:

```bash
SGLANG_MAMBA_SSM_DTYPE=float32 python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B --tp 4 \
  --attention-backend fa3 --linear-attn-backend triton \
  --enable-deterministic-inference --disable-overlap-schedule --disable-cuda-graph \
  --disable-radix-cache --mamba-radix-cache-strategy no_buffer \
  --context-length 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.65 --max-running-requests 8 \
  --skip-server-warmup --chunked-prefill-size CHUNK_BUDGET
```

Save the following as `reproduce_client.py`, then run `python reproduce_client.py --output responses.json` once the server is ready. For each mode/length, compare every saved signature to the corresponding main, `-1`, `serial/0` signature. The compact client reproduces the numerical comparison; it does not collect the per-request scheduler traces used for the table above.

```python
"""Save cold-cache serial/concurrent signatures from a running SGLang server."""

import argparse
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import json
from pathlib import Path
from threading import Barrier

import requests
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument("--model", default="Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B")
parser.add_argument("--url", default="http://127.0.0.1:30000")
parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model)
lengths = [4127, 4224, 6151]
pattern = tokenizer.encode(
    "Record 17: the blue box contains 23 pencils. Record 18: the green box contains 31 pencils.\n",
    add_special_tokens=False,
)
full = (pattern * (max(lengths) // len(pattern) + 1))[: max(lengths)]
inputs = {
    length: full[:4097]
    + tokenizer.encode(str(i + 1), add_special_tokens=False)[:1]
    + full[4098:length]
    for i, length in enumerate(lengths)
}
keys = (
    "input_token_logprobs", "output_token_logprobs",
    "input_top_logprobs", "output_top_logprobs",
)


def generate(length, ignore_eos, barrier=None):
    if barrier is not None:
        barrier.wait(timeout=30)
    response = requests.post(
        args.url + "/generate",
        json=dict(
            input_ids=inputs[length],
            sampling_params=dict(temperature=0, max_new_tokens=8, ignore_eos=ignore_eos),
            return_logprob=True, logprob_start_len=length - 128, top_logprobs_num=5,
        ),
        timeout=600,
    )
    response.raise_for_status()
    data = response.json()
    assert data["meta_info"].get("cached_tokens", 0) == 0
    return dict(text=data["text"], **{key: data["meta_info"][key] for key in keys})


results = {}
for ignore_eos in (False, True):
    for execution in ("serial", "concurrent"):
        for repeat in range(2):
            if execution == "serial":
                values = [generate(length, ignore_eos) for length in lengths]
            else:
                barrier = Barrier(len(lengths))
                with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=len(lengths)) as pool:
                    futures = [pool.submit(generate, length, ignore_eos, barrier) for length in lengths]
                    values = [future.result() for future in futures]
            for length, value in zip(lengths, values):
                results[f"{ignore_eos}/{execution}/{repeat}/{length}"] = value
args.output.write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2) + "\n")
```

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput benchmark has been run. Rounding can leave part of a chunk budget unused or defer admission, so this change can affect batch packing. It adds no kernel implementation; that alone does not establish zero performance impact.

## Checklist

- [x] Format touched files with the repository's isort 7.0.0 and ruff 0.15.1 configuration.
- [x] Add CPU CI regression tests.
- [x] Document the tested scope and numerical limitations above.
- [ ] Provide both accuracy and speed benchmark results (accuracy above; throughput not measured).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [AMD][Bugfix] Route default aiter NEXTN draft extend off the faulting CK kernel
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

#39517 reports that NEXTN on Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 memory-faults on MI300X, MI325X, and MI355X when the attention backend is aiter (ROCm 10 nightlies, both fp8 and bf16 KV). A plain server is fine. The faulting kernel is CK `mha_batch_prefill` (`FmhaBatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheKernel`), with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`, on the first draft step.

#### Root cause

On HIP, Qwen3.5 MTP draft attention is `HybridAttnBackend` over `AiterAttnBackend`, and `supports_hip_draft_extend_graph` is false for that backend, so every `draft_extend` is eager. Eager `DRAFT_EXTEND_V2` builds a short `qo_indptr` (one entry per draft token) and an exact-sized page-id list, then stores them only on `ForwardMetadata`. The CK launch reads `self.qo_indptr[:bs]`, which the prompt extend just filled with the prompt length, and `metadata.max_kv_len`, which that branch leaves as `None`. The kernel trusts `cu_seqlens_q` and reads off the end of a 2-token Q. It also reads 128 page ids past the last token; the prefill updater pads that tail, `generate_attn_arg_prefill` does not.

#30105 already routes this step through `unified_attention` (GQA-packed + split-KV) and defaults `SGLANG_AITER_UNIFIED_DRAFT_EXTEND` on. The call site still AND-ed `_use_unified_verify`, which requires `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`. On the default aiter backend that kernel never runs. This PR does not add a kernel. It lets the existing one run, and it repairs the CK fallback for `topk>1` and for the env kill switch.

## Modifications

- `aiter_backend.py`: drop the `_use_unified_verify` conjunct on `draft_extend_v2`. Non-MLA `topk<=1` takes `unified_attention` even when prefill and target verify stay on their current kernels. `topk>1` stays on CK, because `unified_attention`'s causal flag does not represent a tree mask. The gate reads `speculative_eagle_topk`, not `AiterAttnBackend.topk` (the registry constructs that backend without the eagle topk).
- Same file, CK fallback: publish the short `qo_indptr` into the shared buffer, set `max_kv_len`, and pad the page-id tail by 256 with a live page id, matching `AiterIndicesUpdaterPrefill`.
- `environ.py`: document that `SGLANG_AITER_UNIFIED_DRAFT_EXTEND` now applies without `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN`. The default stays `True`. Target verify is unchanged.
- `test/registered/amd/test_aiter_draft_extend_metadata.py`: pad, max KV length, and the topk gate.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/amd/test_aiter_draft_extend_metadata.py` (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd`) covers the pad, the CPU-mirror length, and the decision to take unified attention. On `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm10-mi35x-20260920`:

```
Ran 5 tests in 10.219s
OK
```

End-to-end, the issue's NEXTN shape on the local Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 checkpoint (same eager `draft_extend_v2` path; no 122B download). TP=2, `--attention-backend aiter`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=0`, page size 16, fp8 KV, `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN`, topk 1, 2 draft tokens. MI355X, gfx950.

| Run | What the log shows | 32-token completion |
|---|---|---|
| default (`SGLANG_AITER_UNIFIED_DRAFT_EXTEND` unset) | `Aiter draft extend uses unified_attention` on both ranks; gfx950 asm verify kernel loads | HTTP 200, no `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT` |
| `SGLANG_AITER_UNIFIED_DRAFT_EXTEND=0` | that line is absent; aiter JIT-builds `mha_batch_prefill` | HTTP 200, no memory fault |

Server warmup itself is a generation, and it returned 200 on both runs before the explicit request.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No new kernel and no launch-geometry change. #30105 already measured the short-Q CK kernel at about 0.2% of HBM bandwidth; this PR is what lets that unified path run when unified attention is not also turned on for prefill and target verify. No throughput sweep in this PR.

title: [NPU] Avoid FP8 dispatch for INT8 MoE on A5
body:
## Motivation

W8A8 MoE inference with DeepEP fails on Ascend A5 with `x=DT_FLOAT8_E4M3FN, weight=DT_INT8` in `aclnnGroupedMatmulWeightNz`. Both an explicit `--deepep-dispatcher-output-dtype int8` and `auto` resolved from the W8A8 quantization config map to `use_fp8=True`. DeepEP resolves this flag to INT8 on A3, but to per-token FP8 on A5. The flag also takes precedence over the normal-mode `DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT=1` fallback.

## Modifications

Disable `use_fp8` only for INT8 dispatcher requests on NPU arch35. Normal dispatch can then use its existing INT8 environment fallback; otherwise BF16 activations are dispatched and the existing MoE quantizer converts them to INT8 before grouped matmul. Low-latency dispatch uses the same BF16 fallback. A3 and explicit FP8/MXFP8/MXFP4 requests retain their existing behavior.

The change is limited to 9 added lines in one file.

## Accuracy Tests

- Passed a local source-method harness with mocked device detection and tensor/kernel boundaries: 20 before/after routing cases covering A3/A5, `auto`/INT8/BF16/FP8 and A5 MXFP8/MXFP4, and normal-mode INT8 environment values 0/1. Both normal and low-latency routing are checked. The harness reproduces FP8 selection for the failing A5 INT8 requests before this change.

title: [DSV4.1] Enable Engram WKV projection sharding for TP4/TP8
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1 uses ReplicatedLinear for the Engram WKV projection. When token inputs are replicated across TP ranks, every rank stores the full projection weights and repeats the same computation during prefill and decode.

This PR partitions the projection's output dimension across TP4/TP8 ranks and gathers the projected activations before the existing Engram gate. This reduces per-rank projection weight storage and redundant computation while preserving the gate's full input layout. The optimization is enabled automatically for supported configurations in both PD-disaggregated and standalone serving, with ReplicatedLinear retained as the fallback.

## Modifications

- Automatically shard Engram WKV projections with ColumnParallelLinear and gather_output=True for TP4/TP8 with replicated token inputs.
- Support prefill and decode workers in PD deployments, plus standalone non-PD serving (disaggregation_mode="null"). No dedicated environment variable is required.
- Retain ReplicatedLinear for other TP sizes, DP attention, context parallelism, LayerNorm sequence parallelism, and scattered attention inputs.
- Fall back to ReplicatedLinear when output partitions do not align with weight quantization blocks. Reuse the existing linear weight loaders and leave Engram lookup and gating unchanged.
- Add unit coverage for full-weight reconstruction from rank-local slices for TP4 and TP8, topology fallback, and partition alignment.

## Accuracy Tests

### TP4 prefill correctness

In a cross-node PD deployment on H20-3e GPUs, projection sharding was enabled only on prefill. All 72 paired synthetic benchmark outputs matched exactly. Both deployments passed 24 additional arithmetic, retrieval, and JSON correctness samples; two paired responses differed only in JSON whitespace and matched after parsing.

### TP8 decode validation

All 2,160 requests in the decode sharding comparison completed successfully. Generated outputs differed between sharding-on and sharding-off runs, and also between repeated sharding-on runs. These runs confirm request completion but do not establish accuracy equivalence; no logits-level comparison was performed.

These checks and the performance measurements below used earlier development builds. GPU validation of the current PR revision, TP4 decode and standalone serving validation, and broader model accuracy evaluation remain pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### TP8 performance

Prefill and decode were measured with different workloads and cache settings. The decode experiment measures the incremental effect of enabling decode sharding while prefill sharding remains enabled. Results from the two experiments are not directly comparable and their gains cannot be added.

#### Prefill sharding

Cross-node 1P1D, 8×H20-3e GPUs per side, TP8/EP8, approximately 68K input tokens per request, and approximately 90% mean request-level prefix-cache hit rate. The table compares measurements before and after enabling prefill projection sharding. Input throughput counts uncached tokens only.

| Request rate | Input throughput change | Mean TTFT change |
|---|---:|---:|
| 40 RPM | Essentially unchanged | 18.1% lower |
| 50 RPM | 4.4% lower | 16.2% lower |
| 60 RPM | 8.4% higher | 3.2% higher |

#### Additional decode sharding

Cross-node 1P1D, 8×H20-3e GPUs per side, TP8/EP8, with DSpark and CUDA Graph enabled. HiCache and radix caching were disabled. Each request used approximately 43–51 input tokens and 512 output tokens. Prefill sharding remained enabled in both configurations; only decode sharding was toggled.

| Request rate | Output throughput change |
|---|---:|
| 60 RPM | 0.25% lower |
| 120 RPM | 1.40% higher |
| 180 RPM, two-run average | 1.81% higher |

Requests were launched for 120 seconds at each rate, then allowed to drain. Output throughput includes launch and drain time. At 180 RPM, the full-run completion rate was approximately 102–104 RPM, not sustained 180 RPM capacity. The small throughput changes and generation variability do not establish an isolated operator speedup.

### TP4 prefill performance

Cross-node 1P1D, 4×H20-3e GPUs per side, TP4/EP4, with DSpark enabled. HiCache and radix caching were disabled. Each rate used the same 24 synthetic requests in the same order: eight each at approximately 3K, 12K, and 52K input tokens, grouped by length, with up to 128 output tokens per request. Projection sharding was enabled only on prefill in the custom build.

The comparison is between the custom build and a compatible deployment of main at e332e1b84e643d02d6223542941030c03717f62c. Their code and kernel stacks differ, so the table reports overall deployment changes rather than the isolated effect of projection sharding.

| Request rate | Input throughput change | Mean TTFT change |
|---|---:|---:|
| 15 RPM | 12.6% higher | 39.7% lower |
| 30 RPM | 17.0% higher | 28.0% lower |
| 60 RPM | 25.2% higher | 32.0% lower |

RPM is the client request launch rate. Input throughput covers the full batch, including launch intervals and drain time, rather than peak prefill throughput. Each rate was measured once, and the synthetic outputs were favorable to speculative decoding.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Keep quantization for mixed Quark Qwen3.5 MTP checkpoints
body:
## Motivation

Speculative decoding is currently not working for amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4 (NEXTN, TP8, gfx950), because MTP does not load on mixed Quark MXFP4 Qwen3.5 checkpoints. This PR fixes the issue by addressing two separate problems:

`_mtp_quant_config` drops the draft's quant config as soon as any `mtp.*` layer appears in the Quark exclude list. That is correct for checkpoints whose MTP module is entirely bf16 (#23146), but here it builds the whole draft unquantized, so the MoE loader allocates bf16 experts that the MXFP4 checkpoint shards no longer fit.

`Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP` declares no `packed_modules_mapping`, which the loader reads off the model class so the quant config can expand `qkv_proj` into `q_proj`/`k_proj`/`v_proj` before matching the exclude list. Without it an excluded attention projection is allocated MXFP4 - half as wide once packed - against bf16 shards.

## Modifications

Two changes in `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`:

- `_mtp_quant_config`: the Quark branch now takes the whole-module skip only when the routed experts are excluded as well, rather than on any `mtp.*` entry. They are the bulk of the draft, and the ordinary per-layer exclusions keep attention, the shared expert and `fc` in bf16 on their own.
- `Qwen3_5ForCausalLMMTP`: declare `packed_modules_mapping`, aliasing the target model's as `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` already does. That is also what the `TODO` above the Quark block in `_get_quantization_config` asks for.

`test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_5_mtp_quant_config.py` is new, covered under Accuracy Tests below.

Nothing else changes behaviour. The `mtp.*` exclude lists of the two published AMD checkpoints are identical apart from the routed experts:

| checkpoint | `mtp.*` excludes | of which `mlp.experts` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 | 1546 | 1536 (= 512 x 3) |
| amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4 | 10 | 0 |

So the 397B still takes the skip and is unaffected. The only lists whose behaviour changes are Quark lists naming some `mtp.*` layers but not the routed experts, which is exactly the mixed case.

One side effect worth flagging: `_get_quantization_config` mutates the mapping it reads off the class, so a Quark run now adds `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` to `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM.packed_modules_mapping` process-wide. It is harmless here and `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` already aliases the same dict, but I can copy instead if you prefer.

## Accuracy Tests

The draft loads and serves on `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, NEXTN 3/1/4, TP8, MI350X; without this change it fails at load. New CPU-only unit tests cover both checkpoint shapes, using the real exclude entries, including a regression guard for #23146.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None; this only changes which weights are allocated quantized at load time.

title: Port chat_parsing core
body:
Port Transformers' standalone `chat_parsing` library into SGLang so checkpoint-defined response formats can be parsed without adding a Transformers runtime dependency.

## Context

Chat templates convert structured messages into the token sequence expected by a model. [Response templates](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/chat_response_parsing) describe the reverse operation: converting raw generated output back into structured reasoning, content, and tool calls.

Transformers implements this through `transformers.utils.chat_parsing`, a self-contained parser driven by tokenizer `response_template` metadata. The library is intentionally portable so serving projects can vendor it and integrate it with their own APIs.

## What this PR adds

- Vendor the `chat_parsing` package from Transformers commit `9cfd6ab7c95f080dc1f33bcc7f97725ce783876e`, preserving its organization and Apache license with SGLang lint and format wrappers.
- Include the declarative response-template loader, content parsers, transforms, prefix-aware response parser, and streaming region events.
- Preserve support for literal and regex delimiters, repeated fields, implicit content fields, structured content parsers, transforms, and required or optional fields.
- Require the prompt prefix when creating a response parser, matching Transformers behavior. This lets the parser understand assistant prefills or regions opened by the chat template before generation starts.
- Preserve Transformers' shallow argument coercion: strings may be converted using the declared top-level schema, while already-decoded nested values remain unchanged.
- Add registered CPU unit tests covering parser behavior and representative response-template fixtures.

## SGLang-specific adaptations

- Replace Transformers-specific logging with Python's standard `logging` module.
- Accept the OpenAI-style tool dictionaries already used by SGLang instead of depending on Transformers tool-schema helpers.
- Add the direct `regex` dependency required by the parser.

This PR only introduces the generic parsing library. The richer serving event contract and SGLang adapters are kept in the following stacked PRs so each layer can be reviewed independently.

title: [HiCache] Add the page-unified KV load-back JIT kernel
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
The load-back half of the page-unified HiCache layout, and the mirror of the staged write-back added in #39606. That PR writes a device pool out into host pages ordered

  MHA: (page, head_group, layer, 2, page_size, head_in_group, dim), K=0 V=1
  MLA: (page, layer, page_size, dim)

but stops at write-back; nothing could read those pages back. This kernel does, for one layer at a time.

Per-layer and unstaged, unlike its write-back mirror. The two directions are not symmetric in how the runtime drives them: write-back moves a whole page at once, so staging it on the device and handing the bulk copy to the copy engine costs nothing extra. Load-back is walked layer by layer by the L2 transfer engine, which unblocks the forward pass one layer at a time, so staging whole pages per layer would move num_layers times the bytes the layer actually needs. Instead the SMs read the pinned host mapping in place, the way every other layout's per-layer load already does.

Each thread moves 16 bytes; the linear index runs dim-fastest then item, so a warp's lanes read consecutive host bytes for the tokens of one (head group, layer, K/V) cell. The grid is capped by kBlockQuota as in HiCacheKernel: the load overlaps a forward pass, so extra blocks buy bandwidth by taking SMs from it.

Note that head_group == 1 is NOT page_first_direct's byte order -- the K/V axis sits inside the page block here, not outside the pool. The HG=1 cases in the test pin that.

Correctness: 123 cases pass on B200 -- 3 geometries x {uint8, fp16, bf16} x {int32, int64} indices x {0, 1, 8} tokens, for MHA and MLA, each sweeping every layer, compared for exact equality against a PyTorch-indexing reference including the rows that must keep their sentinel. Payload is seeded noise, not a counter: a counter is periodic in the layer stride, so a layer mix-up would compare equal.

Round-trip against #39606: running that PR's write-back and then this kernel over 9 configurations (including the head-cut cases) returns the device pool bit-identical, which is the actual contract between the pair.

Performance (B200, PCIe gen5, 61 layers x 8 kv heads x 128 dim, bf16, page_size 64, one layer of K+V, payload counted once):

block_quota | 1 group | 2 groups | 4 groups | 8 groups
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
2 | 15.4-16.2 GB/s | 16.2-17.1 GB/s | 16.7-17.8 GB/s | 17.3-18.2 GB/s
16 | 39.7-47.8 GB/s | 39.7-47.8 GB/s | 39.7-47.8 GB/s | 39.7-47.8 GB/s


against a 53.8 GB/s contiguous cudaMemcpyAsync ceiling. Bandwidth is flat in head-group count -- the run length does not matter, the grid cap does. The shipped default stays at 2; raising it is a measurement-led change that wants an end-to-end number, not a new-kernel PR.

title: [DFLASH] Support Qwen4-Exp hidden-state capture
body:
## Summary

Fix Qwen4-Exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) so it can emit DFlash aux hidden states again, unblocking DFlash/DSpark drafters (closes the three breakages diagnosed in #38589, following the GLM-5.3-Flash precedent from #36708).

## Root cause

As diagnosed in #38589, three pieces of the capture pipeline were broken on main (`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen4_exp.py`):

1. **Capture mechanism dismantled.** `Qwen4ExpLayerExtensionMixin._init_qwen4_exp_layer_extensions` deletes `layer_communicator`, and `layer_communicator.prepare_attn_and_capture_last_layer_outputs` (parent: `qwen3_5.py`) is the hook that actually appends to the captured-outputs list. With the communicator gone, nothing ever appended.
2. **Decoder layers swallowed the capture list.** `Qwen4ExpAttentionDecoderLayer.forward` and `Qwen4ExpLinearDecoderLayer.forward` fully rewrite the parent forward and push `captured_last_layer_outputs` into `**kwargs` without consuming it, so the `aux_hidden_states` list built by `Qwen4ExpModel.forward` stayed empty forever.
3. **Return protocol collision.** The second element of the `Qwen4ExpModel.forward` return tuple was unconditionally occupied by the hyper-connection stream (`hc_hidden_states`, consumed by the MTP drafter via `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration.forward` stuffing it into `output.hidden_states`). Even if aux states had been collected, they had no slot to ride in — and the HC stream would have clobbered the packed aux states that `DFlashWorkerV2` reads from `logits_output.hidden_states`.

## Fix

All changes are confined to `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen4_exp.py` (plus a new unit test), mirroring the approved #36708 / `glm5_next.py` pattern:

- **Model-level capture** (issue point 1): `Qwen4ExpModel.forward` now appends `self._prepare_aux_hidden_state(hidden_states, residual)` before running any layer whose index is in `layers_to_capture` — the exact point the parent's `prepare_attn_and_capture_last_layer_outputs` hook observes — instead of relying on the deleted `layer_communicator`.
- **Layer forwards** (issue point 2): the dead `captured_last_layer_outputs` kwarg plumbing is removed from the layer call site; the rewritten layer forwards are unchanged otherwise.
- **Return protocol** (issue point 3): when aux states were captured, they now own the second return slot, matching the standard `(hidden_states, aux_hidden_states)` contract. `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration.forward` unpacks it and the logits processor packs the aux states into `LogitsProcessorOutput.hidden_states` for `DFlashWorkerV2`. The HC stream is still returned unchanged whenever aux capture is off (MTP path preserved), and `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration.forward` no longer overwrites the packed aux states with the HC stream while capture is active. `Qwen4ExpVLModel.forward` distinguishes the two second-slot payloads (HC stream tensor vs aux list) and passes the aux tuple through to the outer unpack.

One deviation from glm5_next, noted for reviewers: qwen4-exp keeps the residual stream in the hyper-connection layout (`hc_count * hidden_size`) **between** layers (glm5's stream is only mhc-wide mid-loop and it gates contraction on a `dflash_capture` flag to preserve its legacy EAGLE3 behavior). Since qwen4-exp had no working aux capture before, `_prepare_aux_hidden_state` contracts the hc-wide stream back to `hidden_size` via `hc_contract` unconditionally whenever the width matches, and passes already-`hidden_size`-wide inputs (the first capture edge) through untouched.

## Precedent

- #36708 — "[DFLASH] Support GLM-5.3-Flash hidden-state capture" (jianc99, merged 2026-08-27): same class of bug, same fix shape (model-level capture loop, `hc_contract` for the hyper-connection layout, outer-model routing). This PR is deliberately symmetric with it.

## Testing

Hardware-verified on an 8×A800 (SM80) rig, TP8. The checklist below is now filled in:

- [x] After `set_dflash_layers_to_capture`, `aux_hidden_states` is non-empty and correctly
      shaped (`hidden_size`-wide) on both prefill and decode paths, including under CUDA
      graph capture. — **PASS.** 5 taps, `(num_tokens, 2560)` bf16, observed on prefill
      (64-token batch) and decode (1 and 4 tokens), with CUDA graphs **on and off**; zero
      aux-related asserts or warnings in the server logs.
- [x] DFlash drafter serves Qwen4-Exp end-to-end. — **PASS, with a caveat.** The server comes
      up and completes requests, but accept length is only ~1.06 in the configuration we
      could run: the model+draft pair wants a 7-token block while QSA's
      `_require_chain_speculation` clamps the draft window to the compression ratio (4) on
      compressed-QSA configs. The capture-chain facts are unaffected — this clamp
      interaction is a separate finding.
- [x] MTP (EAGLE) path regression check: with aux capture off, `output.hidden_states` still
      carries the HC stream and MTP serving is unaffected. — **PASS.** Capture off, the
      second return slot is the HC stream at its full 4×2560 width; MTP serving measured
      accept length 3.10 / rate 0.70 (normal range for this model).
- [ ] TP>1 with DeepEP/Mooncake a2a MoE. — **NOT VERIFIED: environment-blocked, not a code
      question.** `--ep-size 8 --moe-a2a-backend deepep` fails in both `low_latency` and
      `normal` modes with `cudaErrorSymbolNotFound (500)` inside DeepEP's prebuilt kernels.
      `cuobjdump --list-elf` on the installed `deep_ep/_C*.so` shows the embedded cubins are
      **sm_90 / sm_100 / sm_103 only — there are no sm_80 kernels in the wheel**. This needs
      H100-class hardware; it cannot be settled on an A800 box.

Also: the added `test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen4_exp_dflash_capture.py` **has now been
executed — 3 passed** (it was previously untested, since the authoring machine had no torch
environment).

Evidence (rig: 8× A800-SXM4-80GB, driver 550.144.03, CUDA 13.0 forward-compat,
torch 2.13.0+cu130, target Qwen3.8-Flash-Next BF16):
- tap-to-final-hidden cosine 0.03–0.46, rising monotonically with depth; tap-to-tap cosine
  0.05–0.76 — i.e. distinct per-layer tensors rather than one tensor replicated five times,
  which is the signature of the learned `attn_hyper_connection.mix` contraction being active.
- These numbers are my own measurements on the PR head, not claims inherited from the PR body.

title: Extend Qwen3-VL EAGLE3 draft support

## Motivation
Extend Qwen3-VL EAGLE3 draft model support to include draft models that ship with `Eagle3LlamaForCausalLM` as their `architectures` field (vLLM-style class name; e.g. [AngelSlim/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct_eagle3](https://huggingface.co/AngelSlim/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct_eagle3) ). title: [ROCm][Perf] aiter: page-level KV view for gfx950 fp8 page-64 asm prefill
body:
## Motivation

This is a ROCm performance change for gfx950 fp8 hd256 chunked prefill: at `--page-size 64` it hands aiter's paged-varlen ASM kernel ([ROCm/aiter#4971](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4971)) a page-level view of the KV pool, replacing the gather that main (#36758) runs on every layer to copy the prefix KV into a contiguous buffer, and is worth **+1.1% to +1.9% output tok/s at 60k/600 and +0.9% to +1.6% at 128k/1k**, with TTFT 2% to 7% better, for `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` on 8x MI355X, TP8, fp8 KV, measured on two nodes against the released `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19-rocm10-mi35x` image at its default `--page-size 1`.

The gather exists because without a page-level table aiter reads a page-64 call as `page_size=1` and this shape falls to CK. It works, but it pays for a copy and a scratch buffer sized by the total KV in the forward, not by the chunk. Reading the pool in place removes both. Per prefill call that is 1.04x to 1.22x faster than the gather (2.8x to 3.7x over CK), and the gap grows with context length and with the number of requests prefilling together. The gather's scratch peaks at 451 MB in the largest case measured, eight prefills over a 111k-token prefix; this path allocates none. At 8k/1k the end-to-end result is flat, -0.1% to +0.9% throughput.

The change is contained. It only engages on gfx95 at `--page-size 64` with fp8 KV, head dim 256, a power-of-two GQA ratio and the plain NHD pool (not the sliding-window or vectorized 5D pool). Everywhere else prefill runs exactly as on main, and `SGLANG_AITER_PAGED_PREFILL_ASM=0` restores main's behaviour even there. Page 64 is the only page size aiter's kernel is compiled for, so at `--page-size 16`, where #37465 puts the MTP ASM verify kernel, this path is a no-op. The two cannot both be active on one server until one of them supports the other's page size.

main's `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` pins aiter `acf8fdf` (2026-09-12), which already contains aiter#4971, so no aiter bump is needed.

## Modifications

**`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py`**

- `_build_paged_kv_view()` converts the token-level KV table into `(page_indptr, page_ids, last_page_len)`. The allocator packs each page contiguously, so a slot's page id is `slot // page_size`; the arithmetic runs off `seq_lens_cpu`, so only the gather touches the GPU.
- `ForwardMetadata.paged_kv_view` carries it. It is built once per batch in `init_forward_metadata`, and only where the whole batch can use it: gfx95, page 64, and the plain NHD pool. Off gfx95 there is no kernel for this shape, so the view is never built rather than built and discarded.
- `forward_extend` computes `paged_asm_available` once per layer (view present and power-of-two GQA ratio via `_paged_prefill_asm_supports_gqa()`). The #36758 gather branch requires it to be `False`; the paged branch requires it to be `True`, and then swaps in the 4D K/V views, the page-level indptr/table and `kv_last_page_lens`. One flag read at both sites keeps the two branches mutually exclusive. The guard mirrors aiter's own: there is no CK arm for 4D LINEAR page-64 fp8 hd256, so a call aiter rejects raises `no matching kernel found` instead of falling back.
- `SGLANG_AITER_PAGED_PREFILL_ASM` (default on) gates whether the view is built at all.

**`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`** - `SGLANG_AITER_PAGED_PREFILL_ASM = EnvBool(True)`.

**`docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx`** - documents the flag, including that it is inert at any page size other than 64.

**`test/manual/test_aiter_paged_kv_view.py`** - CPU-only. `TestAiterPagedKVView` checks the conversion against a shuffled allocation with a ragged last page, since an identity table would pass even if the arithmetic were wrong; `TestPagedPrefillAsmSupportsGqa` covers the GQA guard, including indivisible and zero/negative head counts.

The flag is a plain on/off rather than a context-length heuristic. The paged path wins at 60k and above and is flat at 8k, but the crossover sits inside this host's noise, so a threshold picked from this data would not be defensible. Default on because the long-context win is the larger effect.

## Accuracy Tests

`amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8 on MI355X (gfx950), gsm8k 200 questions, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size 512` (reduced from 16384 so gsm8k prompts actually get chunked), `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x`. All at `--page-size 64`:

| stock | main (#36758 + #36852) | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.985 | 0.990 | **0.995** |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Against the released image, two nodes

Stock `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19-rocm10-mi35x` at its default `--page-size 1` (#36758 gather) versus the same image with this PR at `--page-size 64`. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --disable-radix-cache`, TP8, everything else identical. Ratios are this PR over stock, ranges span both nodes:

| ISL/OSL | conc | output tok/s | mean TTFT | mean E2E |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8k/1k | 4 | 0.999 | 1.007 - 1.009 | 1.001 |
| 8k/1k | 8 - 256 | 1.002 - 1.009 | 0.887 - 0.970 | 0.991 - 0.998 |
| 60k/600 | 4 | 1.011 - 1.012 | 0.952 | 0.988 - 0.989 |
| 60k/600 | 16 | 1.014 - 1.015 | 0.933 - 0.935 | 0.985 - 0.986 |
| 60k/600 | 64 | **1.019** | 0.973 - 0.976 | 0.982 |
| 128k/1k | 4 | 1.009 - 1.012 | 0.966 - 0.969 | 0.989 - 0.991 |
| 128k/1k | 16 | 1.014 - 1.016 | 0.955 - 0.966 | 0.984 - 0.986 |

The two nodes agree on throughput to within 0.003 in every cell. Absolute throughput differs between them but the ratio does not, which is what running it twice was for. Per-cell numbers are in [the sweep comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36505#issuecomment-5662364516).

### Against main at the same page size

One node, one day, identical server args at `--page-size 64`; only the aiter build and the patch differ.

- Server: `--attention-backend aiter --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --tp-size 8 --max-running-requests 256 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --disable-radix-cache`
- Bench: `bench_serving --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0.8`

Output throughput, tok/s:

| ISL/OSL | conc | stock | main | this PR | vs main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1k/1k | 4 | 228.4 | 228.6 | 228.1 | 99.8% |
| 1k/1k | 16 | 668.7 | 672.6 | 671.6 | 99.9% |
| 1k/1k | 64 | 1509.9 | 1515.3 | 1504.7 | 99.3% |
| 8k/1k | 4 | 226.1 | 226.0 | 222.5 | 98.5% |
| 8k/1k | 16 | 576.1 | 576.3 | 567.0 | 98.4% |
| 8k/1k | 64 | 1086.4 | 1093.4 | 1092.4 | 99.9% |
| 60k/600 | 4 | 103.0 | 107.6 | 108.8 | 101.1% |
| 60k/600 | 16 | 145.3 | 157.1 (*) | 158.9 (*) | 101.1% |
| 60k/600 | 64 | 161.8 | 178.1 | 180.8 | 101.5% |
| 128k/1k | 4 | not run | 92.3 | 93.5 | 101.3% |
| 128k/1k | 16 | not run | 123.0 | 125.6 | 102.1% |
| 128k/1k | 64 | not run | 131.2 | 134.0 | 102.1% |
| **geomean, 1k-60k** | | | | | **99.9%** (102.6% vs stock) |
| **geomean, 60k** | | | | | **101.3%** (108.9% vs stock) |
| **geomean, 128k** | | | | | **101.8%** |

At 1k and 8k the two paths are the same code below the branch and land within 1.6%, inside this host's noise floor; the 8k cells here are the ones the two-node sweep resolves as flat. The 128k rows come from a separate sweep on the same node and day, which is why stock was not repeated there. TTFT at 128k: 8.4 s -> 8.1 s at conc 4, 22.6 s -> 21.8 s at conc 16, 239.8 s -> 234.9 s at conc 64.

The 60k trace confirms the swap: prefill attention is `aiter::fmha_fwd_hd256_fp8_causal_paged_varlen_gfx950` (299 calls, 465 ms) where an unpatched run runs `ck_tile::...FmhaBatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheKernel`.

Moving off `--page-size 1` costs nothing on its own: holding the code fixed and changing only `--page-size`, page 64 over page 1 is 99.9% for stock and 100.1% for main across the nine 1k-60k cells, and 99.1% to 99.6% at 128k.

<details>
<summary>(*) the 60k/16 cell, measurement noise, and two caveats</summary>

This host shows reproducible whole-server stalls: the scheduler stops logging and no requests complete for 13-18 s, roughly every 2-4 minutes, with occasional 30-55 s events. They cost 5-9% of wall time in every run and appear in every arm including unpatched stock, so they are not attributable to any patch. Aligned to each run's first scheduler log line, five runs taken hours apart share one schedule to within 2-3 s, so they are workload-driven and in-process rather than host noise. Per-cell deltas below a few percent are therefore not resolvable from a single run.

60k/16 is where they hit hardest, so it was run three times per arm. main: 155.4, 156.7, 157.1, none carrying a stall. This PR: 158.9 with no stall, 139.3 on a run that lost 47 s to one, and 135.5 on a run that lost 10 s and is not fully explained by it. The table shows each arm's stall-free run. Taking instead each arm's worst run would move the nine-cell geomean to 98.5% and the 60k geomean to 96.9%, so this cell alone spans the whole result.

Two caveats. At 128k conc 64 the KV pool saturates and the scheduler runs only 26-28 requests with 37 queued at 0.94-1.00 token usage, so that cell is capacity-bound rather than prefill-bound; conc 4 and conc 16 are the cleaner read. And the page-1 gather arm ran later on a different node, carrying 8k/16 and 60k/16 as anchors; those came back at 98.6% and 99.1% of the same cells on the original node, so cross-node page-1 comparisons in this table are directional only. The two-node sweep above is the clean version of that comparison.

</details>

### Op-level: why not just gather

Both paths reach the same ASM family, so the choice is measurable on one prefill call. aiter with #4971, page 64, hd256, GQA 8:1, causal, medians of three runs. Wall clock per call, so the gather's copy and index arithmetic are inside the timed region. The budget is held at 16384 new tokens, what `--chunked-prefill-size` caps, and split across the batch:

| prefilling reqs | chunk each | KV prefix | CK | gather + contiguous asm | page view + paged asm | ratio | gather scratch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 16384 | 0 | 1544 us | 570 us | **549 us** | 1.04x | +8 MB |
| 1 | 16384 | 43,616 | 9213 us | 2892 us | **2595 us** | 1.11x | +30 MB |
| 1 | 16384 | 111,616 | 21310 us | 6577 us | **5685 us** | 1.16x | +64 MB |
| 4 | 4096 | 0 | 432 us | 230 us | **203 us** | 1.14x | +8 MB |
| 4 | 4096 | 43,616 | 8185 us | 2673 us | **2355 us** | 1.14x | +95 MB |
| 4 | 4096 | 111,616 | 20354 us | 6527 us | **5523 us** | 1.18x | +230 MB |
| 8 | 2048 | 0 | 251 us | 176 us | **150 us** | 1.18x | +8 MB |
| 8 | 2048 | 43,616 | 8019 us | 2720 us | **2334 us** | 1.17x | +181 MB |
| 8 | 2048 | 111,616 | 22373 us | 6859 us | **5602 us** | 1.22x | +451 MB |

The scratch is the gathered K/V buffer, `2 * total_k * H_kv * D`, allocated and freed per layer, so the column is the transient peak. This path allocates none of it; both paths need the same 128 MB for q and the output.

<details>
<summary>Where the time goes, and two controls</summary>

Timed separately, the index arithmetic costs 74-152 us and the copy 102-514 us, so together they cover about a fifth of the 892 us gap at one request and about half of the 1257 us gap at eight. The rest is the kernel: the contiguous ASM kernel on a gathered buffer is slower on this shape than the paged ASM kernel reading the pool in place, so even with a free gather this path stays ahead. Those splits are upper bounds, since measuring them adds device syncs.

A device-side kernel-time measurement would show none of this - the copy runs as separate `index_select` kernels before the attention call and the index arithmetic is host-side - so wall clock per call is the framing that charges each path for what it does.

Controls: the gather is page-size-insensitive at long context, page 64 landing within 0.3% of page 1 at both 43k and 111k prefix, as it should since `kv_indices` is token-level at either page size; at no prefix page 64 is 8-12% faster, where the scattered page-1 allocation costs the copy its locality. The batch-1 cells reproduce within 4% on a second node.

</details>

## Checklist

title: [RL] Add /pull_weights: engine-side pull of published weights into a host-local checkpoint
body:
## Motivation

For disaggregated RL where the trainer and the rollout engines don't share GPUs or a fast interconnect, the trainer publishes weights to shared storage and each engine host pulls them locally before reloading. Full checkpoints per step are too big; a delta stream needs an engine-side applier that is idempotent across ranks and fails loud on corruption.

## Modifications

- New `sglang/srt/weight_sync/local_checkpoint.py`: `pull(local_checkpoint_dir, base_dir, source_dir, target_version)`.
  - A published version `weight_v{N:06d}/` is a full HF checkpoint, or a delta (index metadata carries `delta_encoding`) of zstd-compressed per-tensor payloads against N-1, `xor` or sparse `overwrite`, with per-tensor checksums (`adler32` / `xxh3-128` / `blake3`).
  - Seeds from the newest full version at or below the target (the engine's own `model_path` for a pure-delta stream), then applies the remaining deltas in place through mmap on a thread pool. Any checksum mismatch or out-of-order delta raises.
  - A per-host `flock` plus an applied-version marker make concurrent calls from co-located ranks collapse to one pull.
- `POST /pull_weights` (`local_checkpoint_dir`, `source_dir`, `target_version`) → `SchedulerWeightUpdaterManager.pull_weights`. Success is all-gathered across the TP group, so the reply only reports success once every host holds a verified checkpoint. The engine reloads afterwards via the existing `update_weights_from_disk`.
- `--custom-pull-weights-pre-read-hook`: import path of a `hook(source_dir, target_version)` called before reading, for object-store-backed mounts without cross-host read-after-write consistency.
- CPU unit test `test/registered/unit/weight_sync/test_local_checkpoint.py`: seed-from-base + xor delta, chained overwrite delta with idempotent re-pull, fresh host seeding from a later full version with stale-file pruning, checksum mismatch, out-of-order delta.

Squash of sglang-miles #30366 (author credited as co-author).

## Testing

pre-commit clean. The new unit test passes locally against the module (5 tests). No GPU path is touched beyond the RPC plumbing.

title: dp-attention: add prefix_affinity load balancing for routing-key/session affinity
body:
## TL;DR

`prefix_affinity` is an opt-in, routing-key-based affinity policy for single-instance DP
attention. It targets multi-turn / agentic workloads where independent sessions share a large
system/tools prefix but should not all be routed to the same DP rank. Compared with
`round_robin`, it preserves per-session radix-cache locality; compared with first-N-token prefix
hashing (#26612), it avoids collapsing all sessions whose distinguishing tokens appear after the
shared prefix window. An overload guard lets affinity degrade to load-aware routing when the
preferred rank becomes hot.

---

## Motivation

Single-instance DP attention (`--enable-dp-attention --dp-size N`) currently offers only
`round_robin`, `follow_bootstrap_room`, `total_requests`, and `total_tokens` — **none route by
request content**, so under `round_robin` a repeated shared prefix only hits a rank's radix
cache about once per `dp_size` requests. This is the known DPA cache-miss problem.

The open proposal #26612 (`prefix_match`) addresses the *sequential* case by hashing the first
~4K tokens and routing `hash % dp_size`. This PR covers an adjacent failure mode: for workloads
where the first hash window is dominated by a shared system/tools prompt (agentic / OpenCode /
Claude-Code-style traffic), first-N-token hashing cannot distinguish sessions. In the worst case,
independent sessions with identical leading tokens map to the same DP rank, creating a hotspot.

This policy was motivated by our production-like GLM5.2 agentic workload, where many concurrent local-agent sessions share a large system/tools prefix. Existing native-DPA policies either miss cache locality (`round_robin`) or scatter session turns under concurrency (`total_tokens`), while first-N-token prefix hashing cannot distinguish sessions when the shared prefix dominates the hash window.

### Why not just use SMG?

SMG is the right layer for production inter-instance routing. This PR fixes a different layer:
intra-instance routing among native DPA ranks. When a single SGLang server is launched with
`--enable-dp-attention --dp-size N`, requests are dispatched internally by
`DataParallelController`; an external gateway **cannot choose the internal DP rank**. Therefore SMG
does not address the native-DPA radix-cache locality problem unless users give up this topology
and run separate replicas instead. `prefix_affinity` is a small opt-in policy for users who need
native DPA's KV-capacity benefits and also need per-session cache locality.

## What this PR adds

A new `--load-balance-method prefix_affinity` for the single-instance `DataParallelController`
that routes by a **session-level key** and preserves affinity under load instead of collapsing:

1. **Routing key priority** — reuses the *existing* `req.routing_key` as the primary affinity
   key so callers can pin at the agent/session/project level. This PR **does not introduce a new
   public request field**: it consumes `req.routing_key`, which the native OpenAI-compatible
   entrypoints already populate from the `x-smg-routing-key` header via
   `OpenAIServingBase.extract_routing_key` (`serving_completions.py`, `serving_chat.py`, …) —
   so it works on native single-instance DPA **without SMG in front**.

   Selection order:
   1. If `req.routing_key` is present, use HRW affinity on that key.
   2. Else if token fallback is enabled and input tokens are available, use HRW affinity on the
      first `--prefix-affinity-hash-tokens` tokens.
   3. Else use `--prefix-affinity-fallback`.
2. **Rendezvous (HRW) hashing** instead of `hash % dp_size`: candidates are scored using the
   **stable DP rank ids**, not their position in a filtered live-rank list, so taking an offline
   rank out of the candidate set does not renumber the others. When a rank drops or `dp_size`
   changes, only keys that mapped to the affected rank move — everyone else keeps affinity.
3. **Overload guard** — walks the HRW-ranked candidates and picks the best rank whose active
   request count is within `max_load_skew ×` the average across live ranks. The guard uses
   `dp_budget.total_requests` (`running + waiting`) rather than resident token/KV footprint,
   so a long-context session is not treated as overloaded merely because its useful cache is
   large. The configured fallback policy remains independent.

### New flags
| Flag | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--load-balance-method prefix_affinity` | — | enable the method |
| `--prefix-affinity-fallback {round_robin,total_requests,total_tokens}` | `total_tokens` | method used when affinity can't be honored |
| `--prefix-affinity-max-load-skew FLOAT (>=1.0)` | `1.5` | per-rank load ceiling vs average before a rank is skipped |
| `--prefix-affinity-hash-tokens INT` | `4096` | leading tokens hashed for the fallback key |
| `--prefix-affinity-disable-token-fallback` | off | route keyless requests straight to the fallback method |

## Blast radius / compatibility

- **2 runtime files changed:** `managers/data_parallel_controller.py` (new enum value +
  scheduler method + helpers) and `server_args.py` (choice + 4 config fields + validation).
- **1 unit test file changed:** `test/registered/unit/managers/test_data_parallel_controller.py`.
- **No protocol / io_struct / scheduler changes** — reuses the already-plumbed `req.routing_key`.
- Fully opt-in; default behavior is unchanged. Fallbacks reuse the existing schedulers so
  budget accounting/status handling are identical.

## Benchmarks

8×H100 80GB, sglang 0.5.15 + this feature. `gsp` = shared-prefix agentic generator with
`--gsp-send-routing-key`. Baseline `round_robin` == current upstream DPA behavior.

### 1. `prefix_affinity` vs `round_robin` vs `total_tokens` — the PR's core A/B (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8)
_16 groups × 32 prompts, 4096-tok system prompt, q128/o256, 512 prompts, concurrency 64. Same seed, same server args except `--load-balance-method`._

| Metric | round_robin | total_tokens | **prefix_affinity** | Δ vs round_robin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Throughput (req/s) | 5.47 | 1.36 | **7.88** | **+44%** |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 3511 | 10632 | **789** | **−78%** |
| P99 TTFT (ms) | 27466 | 31718 | **6771** | −75% |
| P99 E2E (ms) | 35062 | 63577 | **12774** | −64% |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 31.81 | 141.41 | **28.60** | −10% |

**Win on the targeted DPA workload** — this is the contribution. The relevant native-DPA
baseline is `round_robin` for the common single-instance non-PD setup. `total_tokens` is the other obvious
baseline a reviewer may ask for: per issue #26611, `total_tokens` can *accidentally* approximate
locality under strictly sequential traffic but **falls apart under concurrency** — here it is the
worst of the three (1.36 req/s, ~4× slower than `round_robin`), because load-following with no
content awareness scatters each session's turns across ranks and thrashes every rank's radix
cache. `prefix_affinity` beats both by keeping each routing-key's turns resident on one rank while
the overload guard prevents hotspotting.

### 2. KV cache freed by DP attention (why DPA + this routing matters)
| Config | Aggregate KV capacity |
|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-122B (MoE/GQA), TP8-pure | 2.35M tok |
| Qwen3.5-122B, TP8+DPA8 | 8.41M tok (**3.6×**) |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash (MLA), TP8-pure | 2.04M tok |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP8+DPA8 | **13.3M tok (6.5×)** |

### 3. DPA + `prefix_affinity` vs TP-pure — DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 (MLA) showcase
_64 groups × 8 prompts, 8192-tok prefix, q256/o512, 512 prompts, concurrency 128._

| Metric | TP8-pure | **TP8+DPA8 prefix_affinity** | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Throughput (req/s) | 1.95 | **6.28** | **+222%** |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 20422 | **3960** | **−81%** |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 13173 | **1096** | −92% |
| Mean E2E (ms) | 64253 | **20268** | −68% |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 85.77 | **31.91** | −63% |

MLA has a single KV head, so pure TP **replicates** the full KV cache on every rank; DP
attention gives each rank its own pool (6.5× aggregate KV), and routing-key affinity keeps
shared-prefix sessions resident → improves all reported metrics for this workload.

### Honest scope note
For **MoE models with small active params** (Qwen), DPA frees KV and improves TTFT under
pressure but loses aggregate throughput/TPOT vs TP-pure, because each request decodes on
1/`dp_size` of the hardware. The DPA-vs-TP latency win is strongest for **MLA models**
(DeepSeek). Within DPA, the claim this PR makes is narrow and defensible: **for
repeated-prefix / multi-turn / agentic workloads where callers provide stable routing keys,
`prefix_affinity` beats `round_robin` in the DPA benchmarks reported here.** It is not claimed to
help random, non-repeating workloads. Without an explicit routing key, it uses token-prefix
affinity by default, or the configured load-aware fallback when token fallback is disabled or no
token key is available.

## Usage
```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <model> --tp-size 8 \
  --enable-dp-attention --dp-size 8 \
  --load-balance-method prefix_affinity
# Clients set a per-session key via the x-smg-routing-key request header, e.g.:
#   curl .../v1/completions -H 'x-smg-routing-key: <session-or-project-id>' ...
# The native OpenAI entrypoints already map this header to req.routing_key (no SMG required).
```

For workloads with a large shared system/tools prompt, callers should provide a stable
per-session or per-project routing key. Without a routing key, token fallback behaves like prefix
hashing and may not distinguish sessions whose first N tokens are identical.

## Tests

Added to `test/registered/unit/managers/test_data_parallel_controller.py` (CPU CI, no GPU),
following the existing `__new__`-fixture convention. **27/27 pass** (14 pre-existing + 13 new):

- **Routing key** — same `routing_key` selects the same HRW-preferred rank under balanced load
  (affinity); 256 distinct keys sharing an identical 8K prefix distribute across all 8 live ranks
  in the test setup (the anti-collapse fix vs #26612's first-N-token
  hash); a hot shared key under accumulating load **spills** across ranks via the overload guard
  instead of hotspotting one, while the first low-load request still lands on the HRW-preferred rank.
- **HRW stability** — taking a rank offline remaps only the keys that were on it (500-key check),
  unlike `hash % dp_size`.
- **Overload guard** — a preferred rank over the load-skew threshold spills to the next HRW
  candidate (and records the dispatch in the budget); a single live rank never deadlocks.
- **Fallback** — token-prefix fallback is deterministic; keyless + `--prefix-affinity-disable-token-fallback`
  defers to the load-aware fallback method; an explicit `routed_dp_rank` bypasses affinity entirely;
  a request without a `routing_key` attribute (e.g. `TokenizedEmbeddingReqInput` on the embedding
  path) falls through to the token/load fallback instead of raising.

The `x-smg-routing-key` → `req.routing_key` path is **pre-existing** plumbing
(`OpenAIServingBase.extract_routing_key`, wired into `serving_completions`/`serving_chat`/…), not
introduced here, so the unit tests inject `routing_key` directly on the request. An end-to-end
entrypoint test (assert the header reaches `req.routing_key` without SMG) can be added if
reviewers want belt-and-suspenders coverage.

## Local validation

- `pre-commit run --all-files` (black / isort / ruff / codespell) — clean on the changed files
- `pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_data_parallel_controller.py -q`
- 27/27 passed: 14 existing + 13 new

title: CPU device support for LTX, Hy and MOVA models
body:
## Motivation
This PR primarily addresses issues encountered when running the LTX-2.3, Hy-3 and MOVA models in a CPU environment.

CPU execution for the LTX vocoder path was not reliably preserving the expected float32 behavior, and device cache operations were still using backend-specific assumptions. 

Also, CPU execution for the MOVA path was not reliably preserving the expected float32 behavior. 

## Modifications

- Added `temporary_module_fp32_dtype` function in the LTX vocoder and MOVA to temporarily cast the module to float32 during the forward pass.  Added a `temporary_modules_fp32_dtype` function to handle type conversion for multiple modules in MOVA. A cache has been added to the function to reduce overhead associated with type switching during inference.
- Added the `empty_cache `and `synchronize `abstractions—matching those in SRT—under `current_platform`

## Accuracy Tests
No dedicated accuracy benchmark was added for this patch. The change is intended to preserve existing model behavior while fixing CPU compatibility and runtime stability.

title: [diffusion] cache: add opt-in DPCache step skipping
body:
## Motivation

This PR adds DPCache, a training-free step-skipping cache that uses an offline-calibrated schedule. It adapts [Denoising as Path Planning: Training-Free Acceleration of Diffusion Models with DPCache](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.22654); the algorithm is credited to that paper.

A request carries a schedule of `K` full steps. Those steps run the whole transformer block stack. On every other step, DPCache extrapolates the final block feature from the two most recent full steps and runs only the output head, using the current timestep. Every scheduler update still runs and the weights are unchanged, so this is approximate inference, not distillation or a reduced-step sampler.

On Qwen-Image 2.1 (1024x1024, 40 steps, one RTX 5090), `K=20` is **1.97x faster end to end** with mean LPIPS 0.0076 against native output. That is 10.9% less time than the conservative Cache-DiT preset, with lower mean and max LPIPS. `K=12` is **3.21x faster**.

DPCache plugs in the same way as Spectrum and TeaCache: a mixin on `CachableDiT`. Any DiT can opt in; Qwen-Image 2.1 is the first. A schedule is calibrated per deployment, so the server owns the schedules and a request only picks a budget. A calibration tool builds the schedules.

```bash
# 1. calibrate once per checkpoint and request configuration
python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.dpcache_calibrate record --model-path MODEL \
  --prompts-file prompts.txt --height 1024 --width 1024 --num-inference-steps 40 \
  --capture-dir captures
python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.dpcache_calibrate plan \
  --capture-dir captures --budgets 12 20 --out-dir schedules
# 2. serve; requests pick a budget with dpcache_budget, or use the default
sglang serve --model-path MODEL --dpcache-schedule-dir schedules --dpcache-default-budget 20
```

## Modifications

- `runtime/cache/dpcache.py`: a BF16 first-order predictor and per-request, per-CFG-branch state. Also PACT calibration costs, an exact DP planner over anchor pairs, and a versioned JSON schedule. The schedule records the checkpoint, scheduler class and config, timesteps and sigmas, resolution, guidance, attention backend and dtype, and a request that doesn't match it is rejected before denoising.
- Schedules belong to the deployment. `--dpcache-schedule-dir` loads the schedules a server serves and checks them against its pipeline, checkpoint and attention backend at startup, so a schedule built for another deployment fails the launch. A request sets `dpcache_budget: K` and the server picks the schedule with that budget calibrated for the request's resolution, step count, scheduler, guidance and dtype. If none fits, the request fails. `--dpcache-default-budget` applies to requests that set no budget and falls back to native where no schedule fits, and `dpcache_budget: 0` opts a request out. `sglang generate --dpcache-budget` and the image/video APIs (extra field) accept the budget.
- `DPCacheMixin` on `CachableDiT`: to opt in, a model sets `_supports_dpcache = True` and routes its block stack through `self.dpcache_blocks(run_blocks)`. The output head stays outside the callable. The model takes no extra arguments; the hook reads the current step and the branch's state from the forward context.
- `DenoisingStage.forward`: checks scope, selects the schedule, attaches fresh state for each CFG branch (`Req.dpcache_states`), and clears it after success or failure. Requests that use no budget take the native path unchanged. A requested budget outside the supported scope fails explicitly; only the server default falls back to native.
- DPCache requests are excluded from dynamic batching: a merged request carries several prompts, and DPCache is calibrated for one. Warmup requests run natively because they use fewer steps than any calibrated schedule.
- Qwen-Image 2.1: `_supports_dpcache = True`, and the block loop moves into `_forward_blocks` without changes.
- Calibration tool (second commit), `python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.dpcache_calibrate`:
  - `record` runs a prompts file natively with the new `dpcache_calibration` request field. The worker scores prediction errors online from each step's final block feature and writes one small capture per prompt; features never leave the worker. It can be sharded across GPUs and resumed.
  - `plan` averages the captures and writes one `K{n}.json` schedule per budget into the directory the server serves.
  - Online and offline scoring share one routine. `dpcache_calibration` writes a file on the worker, so the HTTP APIs do not accept it.
  - Also in this commit: the worker bootstrap's early-import warning no longer reports namespace packages. They run no code, and `python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.<tool>` imports `sglang.multimodal_gen.tools` in every spawned child.
- Docs: `dpcache.mdx` covers scope, the schedule format, the calibration API and how to add a model, and it is listed in the caching overview.

Supported scope for now: BF16, single-image text-to-image, one GPU, eager execution. The following are rejected: CFG, reference images, LoRA, dual-transformer models, torch compile or CUDA graphs, SP/TP/CFG parallelism, and combining DPCache with Cache-DiT, TeaCache, Spectrum, skip-softmax or attention-backend overrides. No calibrated schedule ships with this PR, because a schedule is bound to one checkpoint and request configuration. Operators build one per configuration with the calibration tool.

Review feedback is especially welcome on the serving API (server-owned schedules plus a per-request budget) and on the mixin hook as the integration point for more models.

## Accuracy Tests

- `test_dpcache.py`, `test_dpcache_calibrate.py` and the DPCache cases in `test_qwen_image21_cuda.py`: **158 passed**. The related regression tests (Qwen-Image 2.1, sampling params, SenseNova-U1 scheduler batching, Spectrum, MiniMax-H3 denoise loop, worker bootstrap), each file run on its own: **181 passed**.
- Requests without DPCache produce output identical to upstream `1d59ce7c9`: 8/8 final latents, decoded tensors and PNG bytes match on a real Qwen-Image 2.1 checkpoint.
- End to end on a real Qwen-Image 2.1 checkpoint:
  - The calibration tool, run on the 10 calibration prompts behind the schedules measured below, reproduced them exactly: identical full steps and calibrated costs for every budget from `K=12` to `K=39`. Recording took 2 min 53 s on one RTX 5090 including model load, and the 10 captures total 5 MB.
  - Serving those schedules from `--dpcache-schedule-dir` reproduced the measured held-out outputs bit for bit on 9 of 9 requests: `K=20` through the server default, `K=12` requested explicitly, and native through `dpcache_budget: 0`.
  - With the default budget, a 768x768 request (no schedule) ran natively. The same request with an explicit `K=20` was rejected with the available schedules listed.
- Quality with a schedule is reported in the table below.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Setup: Qwen-Image 2.1 BF16 (revision `790c9263`), 1x RTX 5090 32 GB, torch 2.13, 1024x1024, 40 steps, guidance 1.0, `torch_sdpa`, eager, DiT layerwise offload. DPCache schedules were calibrated on 10 prompts, `K` was selected on 8 different prompts, and the Cache-DiT presets were tuned on those same 8. Every choice was frozen before one measurement on 20 fresh held-out prompt/seed pairs. The prompt sets are disjoint.

| Config | Transformer blocks / image | DenoisingStage | E2E | E2E speedup | LPIPS mean / max | PSNR mean / min |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| native | 1280 | 13.26 s | 13.46 s | 1.00x | - | - |
| **DPCache `K=20`** | 640 | 6.63 s | 6.85 s | **1.97x** | **0.0076 / 0.035** | **41.5 / 28.2 dB** |
| Cache-DiT conservative | 710 | 7.47 s | 7.68 s | 1.75x | 0.0159 / 0.042 | 38.1 / 27.8 dB |
| uniform `K=20` (ablation) | 640 | 6.63 s | 6.85 s | 1.97x | 0.070 / 0.208 | 28.3 / 17.2 dB |
| **DPCache `K=12`** | 384 | 3.99 s | 4.20 s | **3.21x** | **0.085** / 0.220 | **27.6** / 17.1 dB |
| Cache-DiT stock | 443 | 4.77 s | 4.98 s | 2.71x | 0.102 / 0.176 | 26.2 / 20.7 dB |
| uniform `K=12` (ablation) | 384 | 3.99 s | 4.20 s | 3.21x | 0.155 / 0.280 | 22.3 / 16.2 dB |

- `K=20` takes 10.9% less time than conservative Cache-DiT and is closer to native on every quality column. `K=12` takes 15.6% less time than stock Cache-DiT and has the better mean, but a worse worst case (LPIPS max 0.220 vs 0.176).
- The uniform ablations keep DPCache's budget, first three steps and last full step, and spread the other full steps evenly. They take the same time and are clearly further from native, so the gain comes from the calibrated placement, not only from the budget.
- DenoisingStage is device time averaged over the 20 held-out images. E2E is client wall-clock for a warm generation (encode, denoise, decode, offload transfers), from interleaved paired runs over 4 held-out prompts. Speedup is the paired mean.
- LPIPS (AlexNet) and PSNR compare each image with the native output for the same prompt and seed, after compositing on white.
- With layerwise offload, predicted steps loaded no block weights, and peak memory rose by 154 MB (0.6%). Time scales almost linearly with `K`, because a predicted step costs only the per-step preparation and the output head.
- A low mean LPIPS does not guarantee that every image is preserved. `K=12` rearranged the chairs in a counting prompt and changed the lettering on a sign. `K=20` stayed visually close on every held-out pair.
- One-time cost: about 3 GPU-minutes of calibration per checkpoint and request configuration (10 prompts), plus choosing `K` on a separate validation set.

The benchmark harnesses, frozen corpora, published schedules, the full report and worst-case galleries are in [`fractalyze/sglang@experiment/qwen-image21-dpcache`](https://github.com/fractalyze/sglang/tree/experiment/qwen-image21-dpcache/benchmark/experiments/qwen_image21_dpcache). That branch is not part of this PR. It stacks on an earlier revision of this PR (`2754e6ecf`) that passed the schedule with each request. The inference path is the same, and the served-schedule outputs above are bit-identical to those measurements.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and lint changed code.
- [x] Add unit and CUDA tests for the hook, stage lifecycle, schedule loading and selection, scope checks, batching exclusion, warmup and calibration.
- [x] Update usage and scope documentation.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results on the current code.
- [ ] Complete maintainer review and upstream CI before merging.

Development used Claude Code for implementation and Astra for architecture review. Results come from local CPU/CUDA tests and real-model runs as described above.
