title: [XPU] Qwen3.8-flash-next enablement
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (generic model support merged into `main` via #37500)
introduces several architectural features new to SGLang — a sparse-attention
indexer (QSA), HyperConnection (gated multi-stream residual mixing), a
PLE/N-gram auxiliary embedding, and MTP/NEXTN speculative decoding on top of
a hybrid linear+full attention backbone. This work enables the model
end-to-end on the XPU backend, since the current implementation of these
new features assumes CUDA in several places.

## Plan

Staged enablement:
1. **Functionality ready** (this PR) — model runs E2E on XPU without errors, exercising every new feature at least once, using existing portable (Triton/torch) kernels where a custom SYCL kernel isn't required.
2. **Acceptable performance** (future) — remove the worst algorithmic bottlenecks (unbatched ops, Python-loop fallbacks) without necessarily writing new SYCL kernels.
3. **Peak performance** (future) — write/optimize dedicated SYCL kernels in sgl-kernel-xpu for any remaining hot paths.

This PR covers Stage 1.

## Current Status

Stage 1 (functional E2E correctness) is complete. Per-component implementation status:

| Component | Status | Implementation on XPU |
|---|---|---|
| QSA sparse-attention indexer | Fixed a real OOB gather bug in compressed-KV update (`update_key_state_and_compress`), plus added a `forward_xpu` dispatch | Reuses the existing device-generic Triton/torch fallback path (same code CUDA falls back to when its fast custom kernel isn't applicable); underlying dense attention math uses sgl-kernel-xpu's existing FMHA SYCL kernel |
| HyperConnection (gated residual mixing) | Fixed hardcoded `cuda` device selection | Pure torch-native, no custom kernel needed |
| PLE / N-gram embedding | Works out of the box, no changes needed | Pure torch embedding lookup + all-reduce |
| MTP / NEXTN speculative decoding | Fixed 4 device-portability bugs: hardcoded CUDA device in the Mamba state pool, hardcoded CUDA sync calls, a missing kernel arg in the GDN Triton wrapper, and an int64-overflow bug when packing XPU pointers into scatter-kernel metadata | Uses existing Triton GDN kernel and Triton-based Mamba-state-scatter kernel; no new SYCL kernel required |
| MoE (routed + shared experts) | Verified working | Existing sgl-kernel-xpu `moe_align_block_size` SYCL kernel |
| Vision encoder | Verified working | Existing sgl-kernel-xpu non-paged-prefill FMHA SYCL kernel |

Stage 2 (performance tuning) has not started yet.

Re-verified (all scenarios above, BF16 + FP8, 1×B60 + TP=4) after rebasing
onto `main` on two machines. One new requirement surfaced by the rebase:
QSA's forced `page_size=64` conflicts with the mamba radix-cache's
`no_buffer` strategy, and `extra_buffer` is currently unsupported on XPU
(`supports_mamba_cache_extra_buffer()` hardcodes `False` for XPU regardless
of model) — so `--disable-radix-cache` is required on XPU for this model
until that gap is addressed (tracked in `docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`).

## Upstream PRs to Track

- **#37500** — "Squash-merge Qwen 3.8 Flash Next integration into main":
  **merged** 2026-09-08. Supersedes #36497 (below); this is now our base.
- ~~#36497~~ — "Introduce Qwen 3.8 Flash Next": **superseded/closed** by
  #37500. Kept here for history only.
- **#36601** — "[AMD] Support Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on ROCm": parallel
  per-vendor enablement PR. Useful reference for how device-specific
  speculative-decoding/graph-replay code is layered on top of the generic
  model support.
- **#36644** — "[Qwen3.8] Fix FP8 KV cache support in QSA": still open; QSA
  correctness fix worth checking once XPU FP8 KV-cache support is tackled.
- **#36651** — "[Qwen3.8] Add PD state transfer for Flash Next": **merged**,
  inherited via the `main` rebase. Adds prefill/decode-disaggregation
  transfer of QSA/PLE recurrent state — out of scope for this PR, but
  required reference for a future XPU PD-disaggregation effort.
- **#38346** — "Fix QSA compress-group OOB gather clamp": **merged**,
  inherited via the `main` rebase. Superseded our own hand-rolled clamp in
  `qsa_indexer.py`; we removed our duplicate and kept upstream's fix.
- **#35051** — "Fix XPU USM pointer overflow via uint64 ptr tables":
  **merged**, inherited via the `main` rebase. Superseded our own
  `_signed_i64()` workaround in `mamba_state_scatter_triton.py`, which we
  removed since it became actively incompatible with upstream's fix.
- **sgl-kernel-xpu #341** — "[MoE] Add Xe2 FP8 W8A16 grouped GEMM support":
  adds a real, Xe2-native FP8 MoE kernel to sgl-kernel-xpu (dispatches FP8
  weights × BF16 activations internally, since Xe2/BMG has no native FP8×FP8
  MMA; reports 1.18x-2.15x speedup vs. the evaluated W8A8 path). This is the
  long-term/performant fix for XPU FP8 MoE, complementary to the Stage-1
  generic-Triton-fallback stopgap already implemented in this branch (see
  `docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md`). **Merged** on 2026-09-04.

### Design precedents (already merged, informational only)

Not dependencies — these are past XPU-enablement PRs for earlier
Qwen-family models, useful as coding-pattern references for Stage 2/3
kernel work (e.g. adding a fused sgl-kernel-xpu kernel, following the same
structure):

- #33354 — fused GDN kernel from sgl-kernel-xpu for Qwen3.5
- #32227
- #35775
- #24390

title: [AMD] Kimi-K3 - row-parallel LatentMoE tail
body:
## Motivation

The Kimi-K3 LatentMoE tail, after the MoE all-reduce, is fully **replicated**:
every rank runs the latent RMSNorm, the `routed_expert_up_proj` GEMM and the
`_add3` over all `T` tokens and keeps the same full result. At TP8 that means
7/8 of the GEMM is computed and thrown away on every rank, on every one of the
91 MoE layers.

The tail is **token-local** — there is no cross-token reduction anywhere in it
(RMSNorm reduces over the row; the up-projection is a per-row matmul; the adds
are elementwise). So each rank can compute its own `T/w` rows and the ranks can
exchange what they uniquely computed, instead of all of them recomputing the
same thing:

```
AR(buf) -> norm(full T) -> up_proj(full T) -> add3(full T)      before
AR(buf) -> norm(T/w)    -> up_proj(T/w)    -> add3(T/w) -> AG   after
```

This is the same idea as the existing SP-MoE family in `k3_sp_collective.py`,
applied one call-site over: that shards the attention-residual aggregation,
this shards the MoE tail. It deliberately leaves the all-reduce alone.

## Modifications

| file | change |
|---|---|
| `python/sglang/srt/layers/k3_sp.py` | **new**, 108 lines — the tail-shard closure only |
| `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` | `SGLANG_K3_TAIL_SHARD` + `SGLANG_K3_TAIL_SHARD_MIN_TOKENS` |
| `python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py` | one import + a 9-line branch in `_forward_fused` |
| `test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k3_tail_shard.py` | **new** correctness gates |

`k3_sp.py` is trimmed to what this feature uses — `tail_shard_enabled`,
`_tail_shard_armed`, `tail_shard_eligible`, `tail_shard_rows`,
`front_shard`/`qkva_shard` reuse `tail_shard_rows` and `tail_shard_all_gather`,
so a later PR adds them on top with no rework.

**No new kernel and no rebuild.** The only collective added is
`torch.distributed.all_gather_into_tensor` on the TP group.

**Off by default**, and gated three ways so an existing deployment is
bit-for-bit unaffected:

1. `SGLANG_K3_TAIL_SHARD = EnvBool(False)`.
2. A token floor, `SGLANG_K3_TAIL_SHARD_MIN_TOKENS = 4096` — below the
   crossover the all-gather's fixed cost exceeds the saving.
3. `num_tokens % world_size == 0` — a ragged batch has no row slice.

It is additionally skipped under `fused_norm`, where the fused AR+norm kernel
has already consumed the latent. The restructure is layer-local — every layer
still enters and leaves on the full batch — so the bank, the attention-side
aggregation, dspark capture and the PP wire are unaffected.

## Accuracy Tests

The all-reduce is untouched and the all-gather is unquantized bf16, so no value
passes through a codec the replicated path does not already use. RMSNorm and
both adds are strictly row-local, so they are exact by construction. **The only
step that can move a value is the up-projection GEMM, whose `M` drops from `T`
to `T/w`.**

### Where a difference comes from

That GEMM is the same arithmetic on a subset of rows. But bf16 accumulation is
order-sensitive, and the BLAS kernel selects its K-loop split from `M`, so the
last bit can round differently at one row count than at another. On a single
fixed tensor — every point a slice of the same data, so only the row count
varies — the disagreement appears in **eight disjoint bands of `T`, not a clean
threshold**. As a function of rows-per-rank:

```
M/rank   513-544  737-832  1153-1280  1345-1408  1537-1600  1633-1664  1825-1856  2081-2112
         differ   differ   differ     differ     differ     differ     differ     differ
```

Everywhere else in the gated range it is exact. **The two sizes this deployment
actually runs are outside all eight bands and are bit-exact.**

### Measured error

8x MI325X (gfx942), TP8, latent 3584, hidden 7168, bf16. Two independent runs.
Through the layer's own `ReplicatedLinear`:

| `T` | `M/rank` | differing | max ulp |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **19456** (tuned chunk) | 2432 | **0 of 139,460,608** | 0.00 |
| **16384** (`max_prefill_tokens`) | 2048 | **0 of 117,440,512** | 0.00 |
| 8192 | 1024 | **0 of 58,720,256** | 0.00 |
| 4096 (the gate floor) | 512 | **0 of 29,360,128** | 0.00 |

Where it does differ, the error is bounded and tiny. At `T=6144`
(`M/rank=768`), over the differing elements:

| | |
|---|--:|
| differing elements | 1862 of 5,505,024 (0.0338%) |
| **max ulp distance** | **1.00** bf16 ulp (mean 0.57) |
| **RMS(diff) / RMS(ref)** | **4.43e-05** |

That is last-bit rounding — one ulp, on 0.03% of elements, a relative error ~89x
below bf16's own resolution (2^-8 = 3.9e-3). It is the same magnitude everywhere
the disagreement appears: across all 480 differing points, `max ulp` is 1.00 and
`RMS(diff)/RMS(ref)` spans only 4.23e-05 … 4.57e-05.

**So:** bit-exact at the sizes this deployment runs; at most one bf16 ulp from
GEMM accumulation order anywhere else in the gated range. The new test asserts
the reference-shape comparison rather than assuming it, so a kernel-selection
change that widens one of these bands shows up there.

`SGLANG_K3_TAIL_SHARD_MIN_TOKENS` is a **performance** gate, not a numeric one:
it sits at the measured crossover where the all-gather stops paying for itself.
Lowering it changes speed, not correctness.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Per MoE layer, at the real shapes, through the layer's own `ReplicatedLinear`
(8x MI325X, gfx942; mean of 30 iterations after 8 warmup:

| `T` | replicated | row-parallel | delta | speedup |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **19456** (tuned chunk) | 2.3098 ms | **1.1814 ms** | **-1.1283 ms** | **1.96x** |
| **16384** (`max_prefill_tokens`) | 1.9217 ms | **0.9921 ms** | -0.9296 ms | 1.94x |
| 8192  | 1.0093 ms | **0.5443 ms** | -0.4649 ms | 1.85x |
| 4096 (the gate floor) | 0.5446 ms | **0.3174 ms** | -0.2271 ms | 1.72x |
| 128  | 0.0970 ms | 0.1157 ms | +0.0186 ms | **0.84x** |
| 64  | 0.0921 ms | 0.1614 ms | +0.0693 ms | **0.57x** |

Every row above is bit-exact through the layer.

Component breakdown at T=19456: latent norm 0.578 -> 0.099 ms, `up_proj` GEMM
1.934 -> 0.279 ms, bf16 all-gather of `[T, H]` costs 1.152 ms.

The token floor sits at the measured crossover; chunked prefill takes the path
and decode keeps the replicated one (the 0.57x and 0.84x decode rows are exactly
what the floor is preventing).

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [HiCache] Unify the linker mode entry under --hicache-host-memory-mode
body:
## Motivation

HiCache has two host-memory modes (`cache`, `buffer_only`), while the direct external linker (Mooncake / MORI direct L3) is a separate feature behind `--enable-unified-cache-external-linker` + `--unified-cache-external-linker-backend`, mutually exclusive with `--enable-hierarchical-cache`. This PR unifies the entry so HiCache has exactly three modes selected on one axis:

| mode | host tier | storage |
|---|---|---|
| `cache` | persistent host pool | optional `--hicache-storage-backend` |
| `buffer_only` | transient staging | required `--hicache-storage-backend` |
| `linker` | none, device pools link directly to storage | required `--hicache-storage-backend {mooncake,mori}` |

```bash
# before
--enable-unified-cache-external-linker --unified-cache-external-linker-backend mori
# after
--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-host-memory-mode linker --hicache-storage-backend mori
```

**Breaking change:** `--enable-unified-cache-external-linker` and `--unified-cache-external-linker-backend` are removed with no alias. `--hicache-storage-backend-extra-config` and `--enable-linker-mla-dedup` keep working as before (both linkers already read the extra config through the HiCache field).

## Modifications

- `arg_groups/fields/memory.py`: `linker` added to `--hicache-host-memory-mode`; the two linker flags removed (`field_order.py` follows).
- `arg_groups/hicache_mode.py` (new): `hicache_uses_linker(cfg)` / `hicache_has_host_tier(cfg)`, usable on both a resolving view and the published `memory` bag. It is a separate module because `overrides.py` and `hicache_hook.py` would otherwise import each other.
- `arg_groups/hicache_hook.py`: linker mode validates the backend (`mooncake`/`mori`) and skips the host-tier normalization (layout/io/DCP), which keeps today's linker behavior; `--enable-linker-mla-dedup` now requires linker mode with Mooncake.
- `enable_hierarchical_cache` is now true in linker mode, so every reader was classified:
  - any mode (unchanged or simplified): scheduler HiCache event drain / admission `batch_is_full` / `ready_to_load_host_cache`, DSA `index_k` retention, spec draft plan, `--disable-radix-cache` exclusivity, int8 Mamba / MiniCPM / beam-search rejections.
  - host tier only (switched to `hicache_has_host_tier`): `kv_cache_builder` staging + auto-sizing + draft sidecars + backup-only ratio, `registry.init_hicache`, scheduler `enable_hicache_storage` / decode HiCache / attach-detach-clear / `is_fully_idle` / host-pool metrics, piecewise CUDA graph gate, optimistic-prefill gate, Step3p5 SWA override, SM100 NVFP4 gate, Mooncake TE reuse.
- `mem_cache/registry.py`: the linker branch is selected by `hicache_uses_linker` before the host-tier branch, backend from `hicache_storage_backend`.
- Scheduler exposes `enable_hicache_host_tier`; unit fixtures that build a bare `Scheduler` set it where the tested path reads it.
- Existing tests moved to the new flags (unit + the two linker KL e2e tests). Docs: DeepSeek-V4 cookbook UMBP section and the Playground UMBP/HiCache axes emit and detect the linker recipe.

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward change. Verified:

- Unit suites `test/registered/unit/{managers,disaggregation,server_args,mem_cache}`: identical pass/fail set to `main` on the same machine (the remaining failures need the Rust workspace or the `parameterized` package and fail identically on `main`).
- Config resolution: linker+mooncake / linker+mori accepted; linker without backend, linker+`file`, `--enable-linker-mla-dedup` in cache mode rejected with clear messages; the old flag is an argparse error; cache and buffer_only recipes unchanged.
- E2E Mooncake direct linker via the new flags on a 5-layer DeepSeek-V3.2 checkpoint (single GPU): cold prompt 0 cached tokens, `/flush_cache`, replay hits 1984/2040 tokens with `Mooncake direct linker offload` / `lookup hit` in the log; server healthy throughout.
- Not run here: `test_unified_cache_linker_kl_dsv4.py` / `test_unified_cache_linker_kl_glm52.py` (multi-GPU), MORI backend, Playground JS.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Adds support for TRT-LLM XQA decode backend for SM90/120 speculative decoding, by building a causal mask it requires for the verify forward pass (more than 1 q token).

Agent generated summary:

Before: pure `--attention-backend trtllm_mha` + NEXTN on SM90/120 died at server startup during decode CUDA-graph capture — verify routes to the XQA decode kernel, which demands a mask for `q_len > 1` that the backend never passed:

```
  File "/SGL/flashinfer/flashinfer/xqa.py", line 332, in xqa                                                       
      assert mask is not None, "Mask is required for speculative decoding"                                         
  AssertionError: Mask is required for speculative decoding 
```

title: [KV Cache] Align additive KV event metadata with shared consumers
body:
## Motivation

Shared KV-event consumers reject SGLang `BlockStored` messages because the required nullable `lora_name` field is missing. Consumers that derive salted cache keys from `extra_keys` also cannot find SGLang's salt there.

This draft contains an implementation of **proposed Phase 1 of #39991**. Replay framing and LoRA adapter-name/hash propagation remain separate follow-ups, so this PR does not close the RFC.

## Modifications

- Always serialize nullable `medium` and `lora_name`; producers emit `lora_name=None`.
- Emit the cache salt in `extra_keys` only for block zero of a full prefix. Keep entries aligned with `block_hashes` when stores coalesce, including padding absent entries. Preserve the named `cache_salt` and `session_id` fields.
- Apply the same metadata rule to the Rust adapter using its existing parent hash, block count, and salt. No Rust binding tuple or native implementation change is needed.
- Document the wire metadata and add registered CPU regression tests for required nulls, legacy decoders, coalescing, prefix continuations, and Python/Rust parity after extension and node splitting.

A separate commit relocates the unchanged MXFP8 reserved-slot test added by #35351 from `test/registered/kernel/quantization/` to `test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/`. The latest upstream commit otherwise fails the repository's registered-test taxonomy check; the failure was reproduced on unmodified `main`. This is a path-only correction with no test-content changes.

Block hashes, storage-tier names, batch layout, and transport framing are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

No model-output changes. Validation used local Linux ARM64 CPU execution with the real compiled Rust extension, Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.13.0, and msgspec 0.21.1:

```bash
python -m pytest --noconftest \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_kv_events.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_kv_cache_events.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_radix_cache_unit.py \
  test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_rust_tree_core_integration.py \
  -k 'not test_memory_allocated' -q -rs -p no:cacheprovider
```

Result: **173 passed, 1 skipped, 1 deselected; 89 subtests passed**. The skipped test requires CUDA. The existing `test_memory_allocated` is deselected because it calls `torch.get_device_module().memory_allocated()`, which is unavailable on CPU.

The CPU suite, changed-line coverage, and full pre-commit checks were rerun after rebasing onto `main` at `0cb37c018c`. All passed after the path-only test relocation described above.

Additional checks:

- The same suite passed with `--cov --cov-config=.coveragerc --cov-report=xml`. `diff-cover coverage.xml --compare-branch=origin/main --fail-under=60` reported **100% of changed executable lines covered (13/13)**.
- `pre-commit run --all-files` passed with the repository's Rust toolchains.
- `mint@4.2.559 validate` and `mint@4.2.559 broken-links --check-anchors --check-redirects` passed.
- `node docs/scripts/check_cookbook_configs.mjs` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No inference-speed claim. This changes opt-in event metadata and does not modify model execution, kernels, or scheduling. No GPU inference benchmark was run.

title: [Elastic EP] Start a scale joiner at pipeline stage 0
body:
## Motivation

An elastic-EP scale joiner is required to run with `--node-rank 1`, and the launch path derived `pp_rank` from `node_rank`. With `--pp-size 1` that placed the joining cohort at pipeline stage 1, so every rank it claimed came out as

```
rank_offset + tp_size * 1 + tp_rank
```

one whole `tp_size` above the window it declared to the process group. Joining a world of size `rank_offset + tp_size` at rank `rank_offset + tp_size` is out of range, and mooncake 0.3.13 rejects it outright:

```
RuntimeError: rank out of valid range
```

Older mooncake did not range-check the rank, which is why this surfaced later and elsewhere — as a joiner that reached the paired expert-location broadcast and never came out of it.

The joiner is not a node of the deployment it joins. It owns a whole TP group on one machine and always starts at pipeline stage 0; its `--node-rank` only marks it as "not the primary's node 0", so reading it as a pipeline coordinate is the bug.

## Modifications

- Pull the `(pp_rank, tp_rank)` coordinate arithmetic in `DataParallelController.launch_tensor_parallel_group` out into a module-level `resolve_local_rank_ranges`, so the joiner reading and the ordinary multi-node reading are stated in one place and the joiner case is testable without launching schedulers.
- A scale joiner now resolves to pipeline stage 0 (`range(1)`) over its full local TP span, instead of inheriting a stage from `node_rank`.
- The helper takes plain scalars and reads no runtime context itself; the call site passes `get_parallel().{pp_size,tp_size,nnodes,node_rank}` and `get_exec().moe.is_ep_scale_joiner`, which are the same namespaces this call site already read (both within the `dp_controller` entry of `ROLE_NAMESPACE_SETS`, so nothing needs widening).
- Add `TestLocalRankRanges` to the existing registered CPU test file.

The non-joiner path is unchanged. I cross-checked the new helper against the replaced block over every combination of `pp_size` in {1,2,4} x `tp_size` in {1,2,4,8} x `nnodes` in {1,2,4} x every `node_rank` (84 shapes); all four return values are identical. The only behavioral change is the joiner branch.

## Accuracy Tests

Verified on 8xH100: a 4 -> 6 scale-up now completes, the joining ranks allocate their KV pool, and requests pinned to `dp_rank` 4 and 5 return output identical to `dp_rank` 0.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — this is launch-path coordinate arithmetic, outside any serving hot path.

title: [Docs] Add Qwen3 Ascend recipes and measured A3/A2 results
body:
## Motivation and scope

The Qwen3 cookbook lacks Ascend NPU deployment recipes. This adds seven selectable combinations: four A3 8B/30B-A3B recipes, A2 TP4 recipes for 32B BF16 and W8A8, and an A2 TP8 candidate for 235B W8A8. Related task: https://github.com/Ascend/sglang/issues/1216.

**Draft:** six recipes have measured performance. Five recipes have verified accuracy: A3 8B low latency, both A3 30B recipes, and both A2 32B recipes. A3 8B TP1 GPQA retesting and 235B hardware validation remain pending.

- Provide editable checkpoint paths, interfaces, service settings, and startup, inference, accuracy, and performance commands; require a draft checkpoint only when EAGLE3 is enabled.
- Label physical cards and logical NPU devices explicitly: one device per A2 card, two per measured A3 card. The shared component supports per-NPU throughput while preserving GPU defaults and hides the disabled Playground submission hint.
- Keep 235B BF16 outside the single-node selector: it requires two interconnected eight-card A2 nodes and storage for approximately 470 GB of weights. The 235B W8A8 recipe remains an untuned eight-card candidate.
- Document the 32B W8A8 source discrepancy: its A2 title says two cards but its command launches TP4; this recipe requires four actual A2 devices.

## Runtime and checkpoints

Documentation and A2 runs use SGLang source `b44e2486824e2fbde9cbcb09adad10bce5593c16`. A3 measurements are from **2026-09-12**, source `c389dd086340878934bf96bc209534f1fbb8440c`; A2 BF16 and the final W8A8 GPQA evaluation completed on **2026-09-23**. A3 results are not measurements on the newer documentation base.

- **A3:** one physical card exposing two 64 GB devices; CANN 9.0.0, PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu, torch-npu 2.10.0, sgl-kernel-npu 2026.9.0, triton-ascend 3.2.1.dev20260530, Transformers 5.8.1.
- **A2:** four 64 GB Ascend 910B3 devices; CANN 9.0.0, torch/torch-npu 2.10.0, official 910B/aarch64 kernel 2026.9.0, Transformers 5.12.1, memfabric-hybrid 1.1.4, memfabric-zbal 1.1.2. BF16 uses `--max-running-requests 8 --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8`, without EAGLE3. No additional host tuning was applied.
- **Checkpoints (main + draft):** 8B: `vllm-ascend/Qwen3-8B-w8a8` + `Zjcxy-SmartAI/Eagle3-Qwen3-8B-zh`; 30B: `Eco-Tech/Qwen3-30B-A3B-w8a8` + `vllm-ascend/Qwen3-a3B_eagle3`; 32B W8A8: `vllm-ascend/Qwen3-32B-W8A8` + `Zjcxy-SmartAI/Eagle3-Qwen3-32B-zh`; 32B BF16: `Qwen/Qwen3-32B`. A2 downloads passed recorded size/SHA-256 checks.

## Accuracy

| Recipe | Evaluation | Correct / evaluated | Accuracy | Successful requests |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A3 8B W8A8 low latency, TP2 | GSM8K, 5-shot completion, temperature 0, output budget 512 | 1157 / 1314 | 88.05% | 1314 / 1314 |
| A3 8B W8A8 high throughput, TP1; retest pending | GPQA Diamond, 0-shot, temperature 1, output budget 40000 | 121 / 198 | 61.11% | 197 / 198 |
| A3 30B-A3B W8A8, TP2 | AIME 2025, 0-shot, temperature 1, output budget 32768 | 23 / 30 | 76.67% | 30 / 30 |
| A2 32B BF16 low latency, TP4 | Full GSM8K, 8 client threads | 1139 / 1314 | 86.68% | 1314 / 1314 |
| A2 32B W8A8, TP4 | GPQA Diamond, output budget 38000 | 132 / 198 | 66.67% | 198 / 198 |
| A2 32B W8A8, TP4; retained historical attempt | GPQA Diamond, output budget 40000 | 139 / 198 | 70.20% | 197 / 198 |

The 30B workloads share one accuracy run. GSM8K excludes five prompt examples from 1,319 rows; all scored responses were nonempty with valid answer extraction. BF16 had no API errors, with 1136 `stop` and 178 `length` outcomes; all truncations remain scored. AIME had 27 `stop` and three actual `max_tokens` truncations, with all 30 requests successful. Recorded A3 GPQA/AIME used EvalScope 1.11.1, seed 42, and client concurrency 64/16.

**GPQA correction:** both historical 40,000-budget attempts rejected index 127 because 2,829 input tokens plus 40,000 requested output tokens exceeded the 40,960 context limit. EvalScope produced a synthetic `model_length` result with `error=null`; this was not an ordinary output truncation. The scores retain all 198 questions, including the failed request. The earlier A3 claim of 198 successful requests is corrected to 197. Public examples now use 38,000; neither historical score validates that revised protocol. The independent full A2 rerun completed with 198 HTTP 200 responses, 198 `stop` outcomes, no rejections, and no empty final answers. Its 132/198 result is reported separately without splicing or selecting the higher historical score. The changed output budget and stochastic sampling do not establish a controlled accuracy regression. A3 requires its own retest when resources are available.

## Performance

Each row is one complete formal run. A3 input/output lengths are 3,500/1,500; A2 W8A8 uses 3,584/1,536 and BF16 18,000/4,000. Runs use the random ShareGPT workload, seed 1, range ratio 1, cache flushing, and detailed output. BF16 performance client concurrency is 1, independently of the server limit of 8.

| Recipe | TP | Client concurrency | Successful requests | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Output tok/s, service | Total tok/s per logical NPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A3 8B low latency | 2 | 1 | 4 / 4 | 920.20 | 4.11 | 211.62 | 352.69 |
| A3 8B high throughput | 1 | 64 | 256 / 256 | 4578.23 | 29.94 | 1778.40 | 5927.99 |
| A3 30B-A3B low latency | 2 | 1 | 1 / 1 | 169.15 | 5.57 | 175.69 | 292.81 |
| A3 30B-A3B high throughput | 2 | 160 | 640 / 640 | 3619.48 | 46.05 | 3026.47 | 5044.12 |
| A2 32B BF16 low latency | 4 | 1 | 4 / 4 | 2888.82 | 32.96 | 29.69 | 40.83 |
| A2 32B W8A8 high throughput | 4 | 100 | 400 / 400 | 7326.95 | 73.59 | 1068.48 | 890.40 |

All 901 A3 and 404 A2 performance requests succeeded. Total throughput includes input and output tokens and is divided by the logical NPU count; A3 8B throughput uses one device of the allocated card. The one-request 30B low-latency row is not a latency distribution. Checkpoint/runtime/topology differences prevent controlled comparisons with the source TPOT references (A3: 5/37/10/50 ms; A2 W8A8: 55 ms).

- The Mintlify link check found zero failures after in-memory Windows separator normalization. The stock Windows CLI still has reproduced path-resolution false positives; its unmodified result is not reported as passing.

Final A2 W8A8 rendering also passed: **Verified**, GPQA 66.67%, mean TPOT 73.59 ms, and 890.4 total token/s/NPU; the historical 139/198 attempt is separate and the final 198/198 natural-stop explanation is correct. This is documentation-only work.
- A3 archive: CRC and all 178 payload length/SHA-256 checks passed. A2 resource-smoke archive: CRC and eight payload checks passed.

The model service is stopped and final NPU inspection found no processes on any of the four cards; platform UI confirmed `Issue1216QwenA2` shut down, and the bridge is stopped; other environments were unchanged.

title: [AMD][DSA] Extend Triton sparse-MLA prefill to gfx942 (MI308X) via 2-query merged programs
body:
## Motivation

The Triton per-query sparse-MLA prefill kernel (`SGLANG_DSA_TRITON_PREFILL=1`) is gated to **gfx950 + exactly 16 q-heads per card**: the per-query program places the head count `H` on the MFMA **M** dimension, and CDNA matrix cores require `M >= 16`. On **gfx942 (MI308X)** with GLM-5.3-class models at **TP8** there are only **8 heads per card**, so the fast path was unreachable and DSA prefill always fell back to TileLang (~3200 tok/s ceiling measured on this shape).

## Modifications

**`triton_sparse_mla.py`** — merge **2 query tokens per program**: `2 tokens × 8 heads = 16 rows`, so `M = 16` is legal with **zero wasted compute** (no head padding/duplication, which was tried first and measured 2× FLOP waste → −5.7% at C=64). The two tokens' topk KV sets are gathered into a single `NTOK*BLOCK_N` column block and kept disjoint via a structured **block-diagonal mask** (`row_tok == tok2`), so tokens never attend each other's KV. Odd `seq_len` boundaries are handled by load/store masks on the trailing token. The fp8 numerics (QK in fp8, `p` quantized to fp8 for the PV dot) are unchanged.

**`dsa_backend.py`** — gate changes:
- `_IS_GFX95` → `_is_hip` (gfx942 is also a HIP arch; the kernel itself remains shape-gated)
- `tp_q_head_num == 16` → `in (8, 16)`

## Validation

Hardware: **8× MI308X (gfx942, ROCm 7.2.0)**, GLM-5.3 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`, FP8 block 128×128), TP8, EAGLE 5/1/6, `fp8_e4m3` KV, random ISL 8192 / OSL 1024, `n = CON × 10`.

**Correctness (three layers):**
1. Kernel-level deterministic comparison vs `tilelang_sparse_fwd` on fixed fp8 tensors (seq=512, H=8, d_v=512, tail=64, topk=2048, fnuz): **max_abs_diff 0.001984**, `allclose(atol=0.03) = True` — bf16-output-level equivalent.
2. Standalone unit test (even `seq=128` and odd `seq=127` boundary cases) vs a dense softmax-over-topk reference with identical fp8 numerics: max_abs_err **0.02474 / 0.01365**, both PASS at `atol=rtol=0.03`.
3. End-to-end EAGLE accept length stays **6.00 / rate 1.00** (greedy), same as the TileLang path.

**Throughput — kernel level (primary claim):** on identical 8192-token prefill batches from the server logs (same host, same firmware `113-M3080202-101`, same selected autotune config `BLOCK_N=32/warps=2/stages=1`):

| Path | 8192-token prefill throughput (TP0, top-5 batches) |
|---|---|
| TileLang baseline | ~3205 tok/s (3223.93 / 3218.16 / 3202.79 / 3201.39 / 3200.86) |
| Triton 2-query | **~3370 tok/s** (3712.52 / 3370.69 / 3369.63 / 3367.09 / 3366.57) |

⇒ **~+5% on the isolated sparse-MLA prefill kernel at this shape (8K, H=8, topk=2048)**.

**End-to-end numbers (machine-specific context, not the primary claim):** an independent reproducer on a different MI308X host (same image/patches/driver, different VBIOS build `113-M3080101-100`) measured both backends within ~0.1–0.8% of each other at C1, and our own end-to-end table below turned out to straddle a firmware change on our host — so the end-to-end deltas are dominated by host/firmware drift, not the kernel. Kept for the record:

| Point | Metric | TileLang | Triton 2-query | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C=64 | Output tok/s | 283.45 | 365.03 | +28.8% |
| C=64 | TPOT ms | 160.4 | 123.7 | −22.9% |
| C=1 | TTFT ms | 3626 | 2266 | −37.5% |

## Notes for reviewers

- The 2-query merge also **unblocks the 8-heads-per-card shape on gfx950** (e.g. TP8 on MI350X), which the old `== 16` gate excluded.
- Serving-time autotune compilation of the merged kernel takes **~213 s** on first use (18 configs); pre-compile it during engine init or raise `--watchdog-timeout` for the first request. After the first compile the Triton cache hits and there is no recurring cost.
- A head-padding variant (pad 8→16 by row duplication) was built and measured first: correct but **−5.7%** at C=64 (50% wasted FLOPs) — the 2-query merge is the design that actually wins on this shape.

## Test plan

- [x] Standalone kernel unit test (even/odd seq, fp8-numerics-aligned reference) — PASS
- [x] Kernel-level deterministic diff vs `tilelang_sparse_fwd` — max_abs_diff 0.002
- [x] End-to-end EAGLE accept 6.00/rate 1.00 + exact output token counts
- [x] Full 7-point concurrency sweep (C=1..64) vs TileLang baseline
- [ ] gfx950 (MI350X) regression on the 16-heads path (TP4) — needs a gfx950 box
- [ ] Pre-compile / warmup integration so the 213 s autotune doesn't hit the watchdog on first request

title: Support unified memory decode host pools
body:
Original PR: [#36731](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36731) — previous reviews and comments.

## Motivation

Full and sliding-window KV caches share a device byte budget under unified memory, but independently sized host pools cannot redistribute free capacity between them. This PR adds a shared host arena with stable logical page IDs, safe compaction, and coordinated allocation/reclaim. It also enables the supported unified-memory decode offload and host-pool retraction paths.

#39477 is merged. This branch now includes main through `91c329cc866957a4750a929d158978a3ac69f45d`, including #37507's unified-memory HiCache support. Its remaining changes build on that implementation.

## Modifications

- Back compatible Full/SWA page envelopes with one byte arena, growing from opposite ends. Compact physical pages while keeping cache-visible logical IDs stable, and allocate/reclaim related transfers together.
- Hold host-layout leases across asynchronous L2 transfers and synchronous L3 storage access so compaction cannot move pages still in use. Discover UMBP page sizes without dereferencing unallocated logical pages.
- Use #37507's transfer contract: keep Full IDs virtual until L2 submission, retain kernel-facing SWA IDs, wait for the producer event before translation, then resolve host and envelope indices under the layout lease. Preserve main's batched write submission and sparse-layer transfer bounds.
- Preserve main's host capacity and RAM-budget accounting. Use the shared arena only for compatible two-ended Full/SWA pools; retain the existing host implementations for tri-pool/GDN, packed draft, buffer-only, and other layouts.
- Enable unified MHA decode offload with file storage and supported host-pool retraction. Keep unsupported MLA offload, hybrid SWA/Mamba decode offload or retraction, and decode-radix host-pool retraction guarded. Unified hierarchical HiCache support from #37507 remains enabled.

## Accuracy Tests

Local regression suites: **346 passed, 818 subtests passed, 1 skipped**, including real GPU L2 transfers, producer-event ordering, unified address translation, and strided-state coverage. Ten parameterized generic transfer cases were deselected in the focused kernel suite.

The existing `TestUnifiedMemoryHiCacheSWA` serving test was attempted but did not reach model startup. The local environment has PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130` and `sglang-kernel==0.4.4`; this main requires PyTorch `2.13.0` and kernel `0.4.7`. An isolated kernel 0.4.7 install exposed the expected Torch ABI mismatch (`common_ops` undefined symbol). Full serving accuracy and backend end-to-end validation remain unverified on this head.

title: [Fix] R-Fork remote_instance weight transfer defects
body:
## Motivation

Four defects found while running R-Fork (`--load-format remote_instance`) end to end between two Kimi-K3 instances of 32xH100 each, running a dspark draft. The Gemma-norm defect (2b) was reproduced separately on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, which has Gemma-style norms. Each one fails silently or hangs rather than reporting anything, so they are hard to tell apart in the field.

## Modifications

**1. Keep draft models off the publish side.** The engine-info bootstrap server keys entries by `tp_rank` alone, with no per-model dimension. A seed running speculative decoding had its draft `ModelRunner` publish under the target's key; initializing second, it overwrote the target's session id and weight layout, so the client pulled the draft model's memory regions for its target model. Gated on a new `RemoteInstanceWeightTransporter.publishes_weights` (target-only). Engine init is deliberately left alone — a draft loading under `--speculative-draft-load-format` still needs its own engine to *receive* weights; only publishing is target-only.

**2a. Deadlock from a group name spelled two ways.** `loader.py` derived the client id as `socket.gethostbyname(socket.gethostname())` while `load_model_utils.py` used `NetworkAddress.resolve_host(socket.gethostname())`. `init_custom_process_group` wraps the rendezvous store in `PrefixStore(group_name, store)`, so two spellings put seed and client in disjoint key namespaces and the NCCL unique-id handshake blocks forever — no timeout, no error. Both call sites now derive it through one `local_instance_id()`.

**2b. Gemma-style norms silently degrading to w = 1.0.** `GemmaRMSNorm` caches `weight + 1` in a non-persistent buffer that `forward` actually reads, and only `_weight_loader` filled it. Bulk loaders (dummy / sharded state / remote instance / remote fs) bypass those per-parameter hooks, and remote_instance additionally transfers only `named_parameters()`, which excludes buffers. A Qwen3.5-35B-A3B instance loaded over R-Fork came up healthy with all 101 norms still at their `ones_like` init, so each silently degraded to w = 1.0 while `weight` itself looked correct; greedy decoding diverged from the seed on 8/8 prompts with no error anywhere. `_post_load_weights` now rebuilds weight-derived buffers.

**3. IPv6-unsafe seed URLs and ephemeral group ports.** The seed address was interpolated straight into `f"http://{ip}:{port}"`, which is unparsable for a bare IPv6 literal — R-Fork could not be used at all on an IPv6-only host. Now expressed through `NetworkAddress` (bracketed). Separately, `--remote-instance-weight-loader-send-weights-group-ports` are *listened* on by the seed, but the kernel also hands ports in the ephemeral range to outbound connections, so an overlapping choice races and loses with `EADDRINUSE` some fraction of the time. `validate_remote_instance_group_ports` now rejects them at startup instead.

**4. Seed refusals surfaced.** Both trigger calls are fire-and-forget on a worker thread — they have to be, since the seed does not answer until the client has joined the barrier — so nothing downstream inspected the response. A seed that refused (port taken, unknown group name, mismatched model) left the client sitting in the group build until the process-group timeout fired tens of minutes later, with no log line naming a cause. `_raise_for_seed_refusal` logs the seed's own message.

Docs for the group-port choice and the speculative-decoding interaction are added to `rfork.mdx`.

## Accuracy Tests

Defect 2b is an accuracy bug by construction: before the fix, an R-Fork-loaded Qwen3.5-35B-A3B diverged from its seed on 8/8 greedy prompts while every weight tensor looked correct, because the buffer `forward` reads was never transferred. After the fix the two instances agree. `test_derived_weight_buffers.py` pins the mechanism (buffer stale after a bulk overwrite, refreshed in place so CUDA-graph captures keep their address).

CI on this branch additionally exercises the affected paths end to end: `test_load_weights_from_remote_instance.py` (the R-Fork e2e), plus `test_gemma4_mtp_31b_extra.py` and `test_gemma4_dflash_31b_extra.py`, which cover Gemma-style norms together with speculative decoding — both sides of changes 1 and 2b.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No effect on the serving path. Every change is on startup / weight-load, except `refresh_derived_weight_buffers`, which is one `torch.add` per Gemma-style norm at load time.

## Note on the port validation

The new startup check immediately caught a real bad configuration in this repo: the R-Fork e2e tests picked base port 60000, inside the CI hosts' ephemeral range (32768-60999). That is exactly the intermittent `EADDRINUSE` this check exists to prevent, and it argues for a hard error over a warning. The tests are moved below the range in a follow-up commit on this branch.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: disaggregation: Support Intel XPU for staging-buffer KV transfer
body:
## Motivation

PD disaggregation with staging-buffer KV transfer currently assumes CUDA in several parts of the Encoder/Prefill/Decode path. On Intel XPU, these assumptions can either fail immediately—for example, `torch.cuda.Event()` raises `RuntimeError: Tried to instantiate dummy base class Event`—or skip required synchronization because it is guarded by `is_cuda`.

This PR makes the staging-buffer path device-agnostic and enables the path end to end on Intel XPU, verified on 2x Intel Arc Pro B60.

Two issues exposed by XPU are not inherently XPU-specific:

* The encoder `/send` path synchronized only when `mm_embedding.is_cuda`. The synchronization is required because `transfer_sync` does not provide ordering with the device stream; without it, the transport can read a buffer before the device writes are complete.
* Staging initialization defaulted `device_type` to `"cuda"`, which allowed a non-CUDA backend to silently allocate staging buffers on CUDA.

### Depends on #39417

#39417 fixes the PD prefill early-send event handling and propagates the early-send wait event through NIXL and Mooncake.

This PR currently contains the one-line `prefill.py` event fix as well because the XPU staging path depends on it. Once #39417 merges, this PR should be rebased and that duplicate `prefill.py` change should be dropped.

There may also be textual conflicts around the `gather_all_layers_to_staging()` calls in `mooncake/conn.py` and `nixl/conn.py`, because both PRs modify the surrounding code. The final result should retain both changes:

* #39417: synchronize the early-send wait event before staging gather.
* This PR: pass the runtime device type through staging initialization / update the staging call arguments.

Without the event fix from #39417, the XPU staging e2e test fails when a cached prefix is reused under overlap scheduling.

## Modifications

### Device-agnostic device helpers

`sglang/srt/utils/common.py`

* Add `create_device_event` and `current_device_stream`.
* Use the device module associated with the runtime device instead of hard-coding `torch.cuda`.

### Staging buffers

`sglang/srt/disaggregation/common/staging_buffer.py`

* Support device-aware staging allocation for CUDA, XPU, and NPU.
* Resolve the device index from the explicit device string when present; otherwise fall back to `gpu_id`.
* Keep custom memory-pool allocation CUDA-only; XPU/NPU use their default allocator.
* Restrict Triton staging kernels to CUDA and use the Torch gather/scatter fallback on other supported accelerators.
* Avoid converting XPU device pointers to signed `int64`; XPU pointers can use bit 63, which is not representable as a positive `torch.int64` value.

### Stream ordering

* Resolve the current stream at gather time rather than caching it during initialization. The current stream is thread-local, while transfer workers execute on separate threads.
* Add an explicit ordering edge from the decode `schedule_stream` before reading `req_to_token`.
* This is required because XPU does not provide CUDA-style default-stream synchronization, and a dedicated CUDA stream also does not implicitly synchronize with unrelated work.

### Staging handler and transports

`sglang/srt/disaggregation/common/staging_handler.py`
`sglang/srt/disaggregation/mooncake/conn.py`
`sglang/srt/disaggregation/nixl/conn.py`

* Use the runtime `device_module` for `Event` and `Stream` creation.
* Thread the runtime `device_type` from `server_args.device` into staging initialization.
* Make `device_type` a required keyword-only argument.

This is a **breaking signature change for out-of-tree backends**. The previous `"cuda"` default is intentionally removed so that a backend cannot silently allocate staging buffers on the wrong accelerator. Omitting `device_type` now fails explicitly.

### NIXL

* Use `np.uint64` for transfer descriptors so high device pointers are not truncated or interpreted as signed values.

### Encoder

`sglang/srt/encoder/server.py`

* Select the transport according to the runtime device (`cuda_ipc` for CUDA and the existing CPU/default path otherwise).
* Allow `TensorWrapper` to copy from non-CPU devices.
* Synchronize `/send` for every non-CPU accelerator rather than gating the synchronization on `is_cuda`.

### DCP pack

`sglang/srt/disaggregation/common/dcp_pack.py`

* Order the gather against the staging buffer's producer stream rather than relying on `torch.xpu.default_stream`, which is not available.

### Metadata buffers and QK normalization

`sglang/srt/disaggregation/utils.py`
`sglang/srt/models/utils.py`

* Make tensor placement and stream handling device-agnostic.
* Keep the `INTRA_NODE_NVLINK` memory-pool path CUDA-specific.

### Prefill early-send

`prefill.py`

* Replace the CUDA-specific event creation with the scheduler's device module.

This change is duplicated with #39417 and will be dropped after rebasing onto the merged PR.

## Accuracy Tests

### XPU end-to-end

`test/registered/xpu/test_disaggregation_staging_xpu.py`

**8 tests passed in 106s** on 2x Intel Arc Pro B60 (`ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=5,6`), covering:

* single-request generation
* concurrent generation
* long sequences
* staging-buffer reuse across requests

The concurrent case is particularly important because it exercises `enable_overlap` together with a radix-cache prefix hit. This is the scenario that exposed the CUDA-only prefill event creation.

### Unit tests

`test/registered/unit/disaggregation/`

**379 tests passed**, including **2 new Mooncake staging-device tests**.

The new Mooncake tests verify that staging initialization receives the runtime device instead of implicitly using `"cuda"`. Both fail against the pre-fix implementation.

The tests specifically cover the configuration/device-selection regression; they do not claim to provide end-to-end Mooncake staging-transfer coverage.

The XPU e2e test is placed under the `xpu` vendor tree because the registered-test taxonomy rejects newly added paths outside the expected `<kind>/<subsystem>` structure, while the vendor directories are exempt.

The XPU e2e tests remain CI-disabled pending upstream NIXL/UCX support required by the test environment. They were run locally with NIXL/UCX builds containing the required patches.

### Remaining test gaps

The Mooncake staging transfer path is also not covered end to end on XPU; the end-to-end staging verification in this PR uses NIXL because that is the transport available on the test hardware.

## Performance

No CUDA-path performance regression is intended.

The changes are primarily device-selection and stream/event handling on initialization or correctness-critical paths. The gather now resolves the current stream per call instead of caching it; this was measured at approximately **0.3% overhead** on the affected path.

The per-call lookup is intentional because the current stream is thread-local and transfer workers run on separate threads.

title: Jeeja/fix pd early send wait
body:
## Motivation

This PR fixes two correctness issues in the PD prefill early-send path.

`SGLANG_DISAGG_PREFILL_EARLY_SEND_CACHED_PREFIX` defaults to `True`, so both issues affect the default PD path rather than an opt-in configuration.

### 1. CUDA-specific event creation crashes the prefill scheduler on non-CUDA devices

`maybe_send_cached_prefix_chunk` creates the early-send wait event using `torch.cuda.Event()`. On builds without CUDA support, this raises:

```text
Tried to instantiate dummy base class Event
```

As a result, the prefill scheduler can crash when a request reuses a cached prefix under overlap scheduling.

This was reproduced on Intel XPU with PD (NIXL transfer) and hierarchical cache: when the second request in a group reuses the shared prefix, the scheduler hits the CUDA-only event creation.

### 2. NIXL and Mooncake did not propagate the early-send wait event

The scheduler records a completion event on `forward_stream` and passes it to the sender so the transfer worker waits for the preceding prefill writes before reading the cached prefix pages.

Mori already consumed this event, but NIXL and Mooncake `add_transfer_request` did not accept or propagate `wait_event`. The event was therefore effectively dropped for those backends.

Without the wait, the transfer worker can read the prefix pages before the preceding forward has completed writing them. The transfer can still report success because the data movement itself succeeds, while the transferred KV may contain stale or partially written data. Transfer failure counters and performance benchmarks would not necessarily detect this; an output-correctness check is needed to expose the issue.

### Why the fixes are kept together

The two fixes intentionally ship together.

Fixing only the first issue makes the early-send path usable on XPU while leaving the missing synchronization in NIXL/Mooncake. That would replace an immediate scheduler failure with a potential correctness issue.

The fixes are kept as separate commits so they can be independently reverted, backported, and bisected.

## Modifications

### `75c7cb3f13` — Use the scheduler device for the PD early-send event

* `prefill.py`: replace `torch.cuda.Event()` with `self.device_module.Event()`.
* `self.device_module` is initialized from `self.device` during `Scheduler.init_overlap()` and is also used to construct `forward_stream`. This ensures the event and stream use the same accelerator.
* Using `torch.get_device_module()` without an explicit device could select the process-default accelerator rather than the scheduler device.
* Add a CPU unit test covering event creation through the scheduler's device module.

### `68a6dfed75` — Propagate the early-send event through NIXL and Mooncake

* `nixl/conn.py` and `mooncake/conn.py`: add `wait_event` to `add_transfer_request` and propagate it to the queued `TransferKVChunk`.
* The sender obtains the event through `_take_early_send_wait_event()`.
* The transfer worker synchronizes the event before reading/staging the KV pages.
* The parameter is trailing and has a default value, so existing call sites retain their current behavior.
* The Ascend backend inherits the common sender/event propagation change through its existing subclassing.

### Ordering requirement

The event must be synchronized **before** `gather_all_layers_to_staging()`, not only before posting the RDMA operation.

`gather_all_layers_to_staging()` synchronizes its own gather stream, which provides ordering between the gather and the subsequent transfer. It does not, however, establish ordering between the gather and the previous forward's writes.

Therefore, waiting only before the RDMA post would still allow the staging gather to read KV pages before the preceding forward has finished writing them.

The worker-side wait is intentionally blocking rather than deferring the chunk back onto the queue. Deferring would require additional bounded waiting/polling to avoid repeatedly retrying the same chunk. The trade-off is that the worker thread can be blocked while the covered forward is still running. This preserves the required ordering while retaining the purpose of early-send: the transfer can begin as soon as the required pages are ready rather than waiting for the entire current forward step.

### Common sender cleanup

* `common/conn.py`: declare `_early_send_wait_event` in `CommonKVSender`.
* Consume it through `_take_early_send_wait_event()` instead of using `getattr()` on backend subclasses.
* The accessor is one-shot so a later chunk cannot consume a stale event.
* `mori/conn.py` switches to the shared accessor.
* `common/utils.py` removes the Mori-specific wording from the `TransferKVChunk.wait_event` comment.

Total: 9 files, +289/-4, including 254 lines of tests.

## Unit tests

Eight CPU tests cover event creation, event propagation, one-shot consumption, and worker ordering. They run in `register_cpu_ci` using stubs/mocks, so no accelerator is required.

### NIXL

`test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_nixl_backend_basic.py`

* `test_early_send_wait_event_is_synchronized_before_the_pages_are_read`
* `test_early_send_wait_event_is_synchronized_before_the_staging_gather`
* `test_add_transfer_request_forwards_the_wait_event_to_the_queued_chunk`
* `test_taking_the_early_send_wait_event_clears_it`

### Mooncake

`test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_mooncake_transfer_batching.py`

* `test_worker_synchronizes_the_early_send_event_before_the_staging_gather`
* `test_worker_waits_on_the_early_send_event_with_staging_disabled`
* `test_add_transfer_request_forwards_the_wait_event_to_the_queued_chunk`

### Scheduler

`test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_abort_result_cleanup.py`

* `test_early_send_wait_event_comes_from_the_scheduler_device_module`

This test injects a stub device module and verifies that the scheduler creates the event through that module rather than through `torch.cuda`.

All eight tests fail against the pre-fix implementation.

The worker tests verify ordering by stubbing the downstream read and checking the recorded operation order. Each test bounds the worker queue with `side_effect=[chunk, SystemExit()]`, so an implementation that stops matching the expected sequence terminates the worker instead of re-dequeuing indefinitely. `SystemExit` is used rather than `AssertionError` because the NIXL worker loop catches `Exception` and would otherwise swallow the assertion.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [NPU][Quant] Fix ModelSlim W8A8 loading for Qwen3.8-27B-W8A8: resolve fused in_proj_qkvz scheme, quantize vision encoder, flatten 3-D inputs in NPU W8A8 kernels
body:
Summary ModelSlim W8A8_DYNAMIC checkpoints of Qwen3.5 (GDN hybrid, e.g. Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8) load incorrectly on Ascend NPU: the fused linear-attention projections and the whole vision tower silently fall back to unquantized loading (int8 weights copied raw into bf16 params → garbage output, with only not found in params_dict warnings), and once quantized, the first vision-tower matmul crashes the server at warmup with an ACL parameter error. Three independent bugs are fixed: 1. Unresolved fused-GDN scheme — the model side fuses in_proj_qkv + in_proj_z into in_proj_qkvz (and in_proj_b + in_proj_a into in_proj_ba) while the ModelSlim checkpoint records the unfused per-projection names. ModelSlimConfig._quant_prefix_candidates() now maps the fused names onto their shards, so in_proj_qkvz resolves to W8A8_DYNAMIC instead of falling through to UnquantizedLinearMethod (48 layers × missing weight_scale/weight_offset). 2. Vision encoder forced unquantized — Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration hardcoded quant_config=None for Qwen3VLMoeVisionModel, but ModelSlim checkpoints quantize the vision tower (attn.qkv/attn.proj/mlp.linear_fc1 are W8A8_DYNAMIC). The config is now forwarded when isinstance(quant_config, ModelSlimConfig) (same gating as kimi_vl_moonvit.py); GPTQ/AWQ/BitsAndBytes paths keep quant_config=None exactly as before. 3. NPU W8A8 kernels reject 3-D input — the vision tower feeds linears (seq, 1, hidden) activations (x.unsqueeze(1) in Qwen3VLMoeVisionModel.forward); the bf16 path broadcasts fine but npu_dynamic_quant/npu_quantize/npu_quant_matmul only accept 2-D (ACL error 161002). Both NPUW8A8Int8LinearMethod and NPUW8A8Int8DynamicLinearMethod.apply now flatten leading batch dims into m for the NPU ops and restore the layout afterwards. 2-D inputs (all language-model layers) are byte-identical. Changes python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/modelslim.py _quant_prefix_candidates(): add fused-GDN candidates (in_proj_qkvz → in_proj_qkv/in_proj_z, in_proj_ba → in_proj_b/in_proj_a) and model.visual. ↔ visual. prefix variants. python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py Forward quant_config to Qwen3VLMoeVisionModel when it is a ModelSlimConfig. python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/linear_method_npu.py Flatten 3-D inputs to 2-D in both W8A8 apply() methods and restore shape on output. Total: +54 / −13 lines across 3 files. Functional verification Real TP=1 server run on Ascend NPU with Qwen3.8-27B-w8a8 (--quantization modelslim): - 0 Unsupported Linear modelslim scheme warnings (was 48), 0 not found in params_dict (was 208+) - Server starts and passes warmup (quantized vision-tower forward) - Text generation correct (1+1=? → 2); multimodal request correctly describes the test image (objects and colors) - Radix cache hits observed
Accuracy bf16 w8a8
Performance (性能测试) bf16 w8a8
Scope Only the modelslim quantization path changes behavior; 2-D linear paths (all language-model layers) are byte-identical. The kernel change also benefits compressed-tensors W8A8 int8 on NPU, which shares NPUW8A8Int8DynamicLinearMethod. Other quantization methods (GPTQ/AWQ/FP8/MXFP4/bnb) are untouched. Fixes #36423 --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #35826070880](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35826070880) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #35826070683](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35826070683) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #35826070865](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35826070865)

title: fix(scheduler): abort over-length embedding requests before enqueuing
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #40459.

**Supersedes #21169 by @warren618**, who found and fixed this first. That PR and its issue #21168 were both closed by the inactivity bot rather than by review — #21168 on 2026-05-23 and #21169 on 2026-08-25. The original author has not responded to a reopen request, and I do not have the permissions to reopen either one, so this PR carries the same one-line fix forward with them credited as co-author. Please close #21169 as superseded if this lands.

`handle_embedding_request` does not call `req.set_finish_with_abort(error_msg)` when `validate_input_length()` returns an error, so the request is added to the waiting queue without ever being marked aborted:

```python
# python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py -- before this PR
error_msg = validate_input_length(
    req,
    self.max_req_input_len,
    get_serving().allow_auto_truncate,
)
if error_msg:
    self._add_request_to_queue(req)   # no set_finish_with_abort(error_msg)
    return
```

`handle_generate_request` does it correctly, and so do the three other early-return branches of `handle_embedding_request` itself (`mm_input_error`, multimodal input processing, post-expansion length). This branch was the only outlier.

`set_finish_with_abort` does two things: it sets `to_finish = FINISH_ABORT(...)`, and it replaces `origin_input_ids` with a single token ("set it to one token to skip the long prefill"). Skipping it means the over-length request is admitted at full length with no finish reason attached, so instead of the intended HTTP 400 the caller receives nothing and blocks until its own timeout. The scheduler logs the validation error, but it never reaches the client.

Note for anyone reading the original report: its Impact section claimed illegal memory access and a server crash, and linked the roadmap item #12780. That was wrong — there is no crash. #40459 has the corrected analysis.

The scheduler-side check is reachable because `TokenizerManager._validate_one_request` validates against `context_len` while the scheduler validates against `max_req_input_len`, so a KV pool smaller than the context length lets a request pass the first and fail the second. That split is a known issue, marked with a standing `FIXME: unify the length validation logic with the one in the scheduler.` in `tokenizer_manager.py`; unifying it is out of scope here.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py` — add the missing `req.set_finish_with_abort(error_msg)` in `handle_embedding_request`. `handle_batch_embedding_request` delegates to this handler, so it is covered by the same line.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — no change to kernels or model forward code. The touched branch is an input-validation error path.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable — the added call runs only on a request that is being rejected.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no documented behavior changes; the 400 response was already the documented contract.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — not applicable, see above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Metrics] Add request-level TPOT histogram (sglang:request_time_per_output_token_seconds)
body:
**Metrics PR stack** (merge bottom-up; each PR is based on `main` and includes the PRs below it)
1. #38600
2. #39706
3. #40275 ← this PR

Review only the last 2 commit(s); the earlier commits belong to the PRs below.

---

## Motivation

SGLang exports token-weighted inter-token latency but no request-weighted time per output token (TPOT). This adds `sglang:request_time_per_output_token_seconds`, observed once per qualifying request:

```text
TPOT = (finished_time - first_token_time) / (completion_tokens - 1)
```

This PR must not merge before #38600. Without it, non-streaming `first_token_time` is stamped late, so non-streaming TPOT is wrong; streaming TPOT is unaffected.

## Modifications

- Record TPOT for requests that finish with `stop` or `length`, have more than one output token, and have an observed decode interval. Skip aborts and PD prefill workers.
- When the first output is also the final one, stamp both times with the same timestamp so no false decode interval appears.
- Reuse `--bucket-inter-token-latency` buckets and label by `is_streaming`.
- `meta_info["decode_throughput"]` uses the same calculation (`APIServerReqTimeStats.get_time_per_output_token`).
- Docs: describe the metric and delete the stale `sglang:time_per_output_token_seconds` sample block. That metric is no longer emitted.

## Tests

- `test_req_time_stats.py`: formula and undefined cases (2 methods).
- `test_stat_loggers_di.py`: observation with the `is_streaming` label, and no observation when undefined (2 methods).
- `test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py::TestRequestTpotGating`, through the real `_handle_batch_output` (2 methods): a single-batch finish records nothing; across two batches, `stop` records one value while abort and PD prefill record nothing. Each of these mutations fails a test: dropping `ts=first_output_time`, making the stop/length filter always true, or making the prefill check always true.
- `test/registered/observability/test_metrics.py` (GPU e2e): checks that `sglang:request_time_per_output_token_seconds_count{is_streaming="true"}` is positive.

CPU: 115 tests pass across the stack's five affected unit files. Rebasing on current `main` clears the unrelated `logits_processor` lint failure (#40303).

title: [NPU][Perf] Run MiMo-V2.5 MoE router in bf16 and drop redundant topk_ids casts
body:
## Motivation

The MiMo-V2.5 MoE router kept its gate weight in fp32: every MoE layer cast `hidden_states` bf16→fp32 for the router matmul, then `fused_topk_npu` cast the logits back to fp32 for `npu_moe_gating_top_k` — two Cast kernels plus a non-Cube fp32 matmul per layer (57 layers). Separately, the DeepEP low-latency dispatcher converted `topk_ids` to int64 while the NPU DeepEP runtime takes int32 — an int32→int64→int32 round trip costing 2–3 more Cast kernels per layer.

## Modifications

- Keep `MoEGate.weight` / `e_score_correction_bias` in bf16 **on NPU**: the router matmul runs natively on Cube units and `npu_moe_gating_top_k` consumes bf16 logits directly. GPU keeps the historical fp32 gate.
- `fused_topk_npu`: dtype-alignment guard instead of unconditional fp32 casts — nothing is cast when logits and bias share a dtype; an fp32 bias promotes the logits to fp32 (downcasting the bias to bf16 reorders top-k routing, see the GLM-5.2 note in `deepseek_v2.py`). No bias → historical fp32 scoring, so sigmoid / `num_token_non_padded` models are unaffected.
- Skip `topk_ids.to(torch.int64)` in the DeepEP LL dispatcher on NPU; GPU keeps int64 (its native requirement).
- `topk_weights` stay fp32: `MoeLowLatencyCombineV2` requires DT_FLOAT expert scales — a hard requirement, not a leftover. The modelopt_fp4 + flashinfer_trtllm bias branch also stays fp32.

Other models: Qwen3-MoE-style (softmax, no bias) takes a different branch — unaffected; DeepSeek-family ends up fp32 either way — identical numerics; GPU behavior unchanged everywhere.

## Accuracy Tests

```

sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000

source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh
source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh

export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=300
export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV
export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True
export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32
export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT=600
export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1
export ASCEND_USE_FIA=1
export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=32
export DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2500
export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=20
export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=4096
export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
export HCCL_HOST_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE=auto
export SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1

sglang serve \
        --model-path $MODEL_PATH \
        --served-model-name $MODEL_PATH \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --attention-backend ascend \
        --device npu \
        --mem-fraction-static 0.92 \
        --tp-size 8 --nnodes 1 --node-rank 0 \
        --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-total-tokens 600000 \
        --max-running-requests 32 \
        --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto \
        --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 \
```


## Speed Tests and Profiling

Profiling (per MoE layer, decode, DeepEP LL, EP6):

| Kernel | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Router MatMulV3 | 13.84 us | 9.12 us (**-34%**) |

The single remaining cast is the hard-required bf16→fp32 `topk_weights` conversion (CombineV2 DT_FLOAT).

Benchmark (16k-input prefill-heavy workload, 128 prompts, request rate 0.4):

title: [Spec] Reuse K3 auxiliary outputs across decode CUDA graph sizes
body:
## Motivation

With DFlash/DSpark, every captured decode CUDA graph keeps its own packed aux hidden-state output alive, so reserved graph memory grows with the sum of captured sizes. One buffer sized for the largest graph is enough: the worker writes target hidden states into draft KV before the next target forward on that stream.

## Modifications

- `AuxHiddenStatePacker` (#37329) takes an optional `out=` buffer, checks its shape and dtype on the first `append`, and writes captures into it.
- `DecodeCudaGraphRunner` keeps one `[max_num_token, K * hidden]` buffer per stream (so PD-multiplexed streams don't alias) and gives each captured size a row slice through `ForwardBatch.aux_hidden_states_buffer`. The buffer is used only for DFlash-family target runners with `pp_size == 1`, and only for models implementing `SupportsSharedAuxHiddenStates.get_packed_aux_hidden_size()`.
- Kimi K3 now captures through `AuxHiddenStatePacker` (PP stages keep the list, since inherited captures arrive already concatenated) and is the first model to opt in. Other packer users (DeepSeek V2, MiMo V2) and EAGLE3 are unchanged.

## Tests

- `test_spec_aux_hidden_state.py`: packing into an external buffer gives the same result as the list-path concat, lands in the caller's storage, and raises on a buffer that doesn't fit.
- `test_decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`: graph sizes 64/8/32 share one buffer; a second stream gets its own; non-DFlash, draft, PP and non-opt-in models get no shared buffer.

GPU check, Kimi K3 colocated TP8 on 8xB300 with DFLASH (block size 8), GSM8K 5-shot on all 1,319 questions. The comparison is main + #40794 (K3 DFLASH) with and without this PR. Target-verify CUDA-graph memory per GPU goes from 2.215 GB to **1.756 GB** (−0.46 GB, −21%), and startup free memory rises by the same amount. Accuracy and acceptance are unchanged: 95.0% / average accept length 5.07 without this PR, 95.6% / 5.06 with it.
