title: [DSpark] Add MiniMax-M3 DSpark support
body:
## Summary

This PR adds MiniMax-M3 DSpark speculative decoding support, using MiniMax-M3 as the target model and MiniMax-M3-DSpark as the draft model.

MiniMax-M3-DSpark is a draft-only model and cannot be served standalone. Pairing it with MiniMax-M3 requires integration across auxiliary hidden-state capture, the VL wrapper, TARGET_VERIFY metadata, MiniMax sparse-attention geometry, DP padding, and DFLASH/DSPARK configuration loading.

This PR connects those integration points while preserving the existing MiniMax-M3 EAGLE3 and NPU behavior.

## Modifications

### MiniMax-M3 target model

- Add `set_dspark_layers_to_capture()` to `MiniMaxM3SparseForCausalLM`.
- Reuse the existing EAGLE3 layer-capture implementation so DSpark and EAGLE3 apply the same `L -> L + 1` mapping and `_is_layer_to_capture` marking.
- Require explicit DSpark layer IDs to provide deterministic auxiliary hidden-state capture points.
- Guard tuple unpacking because warmup and idle forwards may return a plain hidden-state tensor rather than `(hidden_states, aux_hidden_states)`.

### MiniMax-M3 VL wrapper

- Add `set_dspark_layers_to_capture()` to `MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration`.
- Reuse the same EAGLE3 layer-capture implementation.
- Forward captured auxiliary hidden states to the logits processor.
- Preserve plain-tensor handling for warmup and idle forwards.

### ForwardBatch TARGET_VERIFY metadata

- Add ragged TARGET_VERIFY metadata preparation for MLP synchronization.
- Populate `extend_seq_lens`, `extend_prefix_lens`, and `extend_start_loc` from `RaggedVerifyLayout`.
- Use `qo_indptr_device` as the graph-stable source of per-request start locations.
- Avoid reading replay-time verify lengths back from the GPU when no CPU mirror is available.
- Preserve and restore the original `ForwardBatch` metadata after MLP synchronization.
- Represent DP-padded request rows with zero-length verify geometry instead of treating them as real requests.
- Slice post-forward logits and hidden states using the real ragged token count when host metadata is available.

### MiniMax sparse attention

- Resolve `RaggedVerifyLayout` for TARGET_VERIFY and build sparse-attention geometry with `build_ragged_target_verify_geometry()`.
- Consume `geometry.cu_seqlens_q` and `geometry.cache_seqlens_int32` instead of reconstructing ragged geometry from a fixed request width.
- Continue using the regular `ForwardBatch.extend_*` path when explicit extend geometry is available.
- Restrict the fixed-width fallback to genuinely uniform, non-padded TARGET_VERIFY batches.
- Reject DP-padded or attention-TP sequence-sharded TARGET_VERIFY batches when per-request geometry is unavailable.
- Trim DP-padded `q` and `idx_q` rows before invoking the sparse kernel and restore the graph-sized output shape afterward.
- Use fixed query and context bounds during CUDA Graph capture to avoid deriving graph metadata from synthetic capture-time sequence lengths.
- Preserve the existing NPU sparse-attention paths, lazy GPU sparse-kernel import, index-cache behavior, and EAGLE3 compatibility.

### DFLASH / DSPARK configuration

- Read `sliding_window` from the local raw `config.json` when the loaded Transformers configuration exposes it as `None`.
- Reject `return_logprob` requests explicitly because DFLASH/DSPARK does not support that mode yet.
- Preserve MiniMax-M3-DSpark draft-model loading compatibility.

### Tests

Add unit coverage for:

- Rejecting DP-padded TARGET_VERIFY without per-request geometry.
- Rejecting sequence-sharded TARGET_VERIFY without per-request geometry.
- Building ragged sparse-attention geometry from per-request verify lengths.
- Trimming padded query rows before the sparse kernel and restoring the original output shape with zero padding.
- Handling explicit uniform `ForwardBatch.extend_*` geometry with zero-length padded rows.
- Reusing the EAGLE3 hidden-state capture setup for both the text and VL MiniMax-M3 wrappers.

## Error cases fixed

This PR addresses the following MiniMax-M3 + MiniMax-M3-DSpark serving failures:

```text
ValueError: DFLASH sliding_attention layers require config.sliding_window.
```

```text
ValueError: Model MiniMaxM3SparseForConditionalGeneration implements neither
set_dspark_layers_to_capture nor set_dflash_layers_to_capture, one of which is
required for DFLASH/DSPARK.
```

```text
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'device'
```

```text
ValueError: DFLASH target_hidden feature dim mismatch. Expected shape
[N, 36864] (num_context_features=6, hidden_size=6144), but got
shape=(..., 6144).
```

```text
RuntimeError: CUDA error: operation failed due to a previous error during capture.
```

It also addresses the TARGET_VERIFY geometry issue raised during review:

- Ragged TARGET_VERIFY now obtains `cu_seqlens_q` from the per-request verify lengths through `build_ragged_target_verify_geometry()`.
- DP-padded batches use explicit per-request extend geometry when available.
- The MiniMax sparse backend fails fast instead of interpreting padded or sequence-sharded rows as uniform real requests.

## Validation

### Unit tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_minimax_dspark_verify_geometry.py
```

Result:

```text
6 passed
```

### Static checks

```bash
python3 -m py_compile \
  python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/minimax_sparse_backend.py \
  python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py \
  python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py \
  python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py \
  python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3_vl.py \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_minimax_dspark_verify_geometry.py

git diff --check
```


### Two-node TP16 serving

Validated with MiniMax-M3 as the target model and MiniMax-M3-DSpark as the DSPARK draft model:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/MiniMax-M3 \
  --served-model-name MiniMax-M3 \
  --reasoning-parser auto \
  --tool-call-parser auto \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 16 \
  --nnodes 2 \
  --node-rank <0-or-1> \
  --dist-init-addr 192.168.1.81:20000 \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
  --speculative-draft-model-path /models/MiniMax-M3-DSpark \
  --speculative-dspark-block-size 8 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 31000
```
### End-to-end serving results
| Metric | Input 8K / Output 512 | Input 32K / Output 512 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Successful requests | 256 | 256 |
| Request throughput | 0.14 req/s | 0.05 req/s |
| Input token throughput | 1140.76 tok/s | 1518.18 tok/s |
| Output token throughput | 73.01 tok/s | 24.29 tok/s |
| Peak output throughput | 80.00 tok/s | 75.00 tok/s |
| Total token throughput | 1213.76 tok/s | 1542.47 tok/s |
| Effective concurrency | 15.76 | 15.91 |
| DSpark accept length | 3.39 | 3.40 |
| Mean E2E latency | 110538.41 ms | 335299.96 ms |
| Median E2E latency | 97803.34 ms | 286638.45 ms |
| P99 E2E latency | 266417.01 ms | 876994.82 ms |
| Mean TTFT | 7546.60 ms | 54129.68 ms |
| Median TTFT | 5068.49 ms | 42576.83 ms |
| P99 TTFT | 64566.62 ms | 239261.61 ms |
| Mean TPOT | 201.55 ms | 550.24 ms |
| Median TPOT | 177.17 ms | 444.06 ms |
| P99 TPOT | 511.15 ms | 1607.82 ms |

### Accuracy

| Benchmark | Examples | Sampling | Repeats | Score | Latency |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K | 1,314 | Default evaluation settings | 8 | 0.970 mean | 796.733 s mean |
| GPQA | 32 | `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `max_tokens=128000` | 8 | 0.992 mean | 11,345.289 s mean |

title: [fmha_v2] perf: use non-interleaved paged KV input for trtllm sm90/120 prefill
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Dependent on https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23112 and https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4124. Improves TRT-LLM SM90/120 prefill performance to beat FA3 by removing an expensive copy-operation that was previously needed to pass interleaved KV to the kernel API.

## Modifications

Allocate KV together (no functional change to any other backend), allowing us to use the new indexing mode to read data efficiently for fmha_v2.

> the below accuracy/perf data was collected and summarized by Claude

## Accuracy Tests

PQA Diamond, 198 questions x 8 repeats (1,584 rollouts per config), temperature 0.6,
top-k 20, max-tokens 81920.

**Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Thinking-FP8:**

| Config | KV dtype | Score | Repeat range |
|---|---|---|---|
| FA3 | bf16 | 0.725 | 0.712-0.742 |
| fmha_v2 (trtllm_mha) | bf16 | 0.723 | 0.702-0.753 |
| FA3 + MTP | bf16 | 0.734 | 0.712-0.758 |
| fmha_v2 prefill + MTP (fa3 verify) | bf16 | 0.721 | 0.707-0.732 |
| FA3 | fp8_e4m3 | 0.727 | 0.707-0.747 |
| **fmha_v2 (trtllm_mha)** | **fp8_e4m3** | **0.724** | 0.682-0.753 |

Per-repeat std is ~0.015, so every row is a tie. The fp8 fmha_v2 row ran the
**zero-copy path in this PR**, making it a 1,584-rollout validation of the new KV
addressing against the e4m3 kernel.

**Qwen3-32B-FP8, fp8 KV:**

| Config | Score | Range |
|---|---|---|
| FA3 | 0.630 | 0.606-0.677 |
| fmha_v2 | **0.630** | 0.606-0.657 |

Exact tie.

**MTP acceptance** (draft/target property -- matching rates show fmha_v2 prefill does
not perturb the target distribution):

| Config | Accept len | Accept rate |
|---|---|---|
| FA3 + MTP (bf16) | 2.37 | 0.46 |
| fmha_v2 prefill + MTP (bf16) | 2.45 | 0.48 |

<details>
<summary>Repro</summary>

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30000 --eval-name gpqa \
  --num-examples 198 --repeat 8 --num-threads 16 \
  --max-tokens 81920 --thinking-mode qwen-3 --temperature 0.6 --top-k 20
```

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Before/after on identical config** (Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Thinking-FP8, bf16 KV,
`--chunked-prefill-size 2048`). "Before" is the original `torch.stack([k_cache, v_cache], dim=1)`
full-pool copy; "after" is this PR's non-interleaved zero-copy path.

| ISL | metric | before (stack) | after (zero-copy) | FA3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1k | total tok/s | 11017 | **14940** | 14833 |
| 1k | median TTFT (ms) | 1696 | **719** | 841 |
| 8k | input tok/s | 13853 | **22266** | 22982 |
| 8k | median TTFT (ms) | 6566 | **2952** | 2713 |
| 128k | input tok/s | 14859 | **25506** | 29363 |
| 128k | median TTFT (ms) | 11215 | **5706** | 4764 |

**Root cause of the "before" column** (torch profiler, 2.7k-token request,
24 prefill / 384 decode layer-calls):

| | fmha_v2 (stack) | FA3 |
|---|---|---|
| prefill attention | 1.59 ms | 0.98 ms |
| decode attention | 15.4 ms (bf16 XQA) | 6.8 ms |
| KV-pool stack copy | **120.5 ms** (`direct_copy_kernel`, 1008 calls) | -- |

The stack copied the entire per-layer KV pool (~4 GB, ~5 ms) per prefill layer call,
per chunk, regardless of batch size. Causality check -- only the pool size varies:

| mem-fraction-static | KV pool per side | input tok/s @8k | median TTFT (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.8 | 24.0 GB | 13853 | 6566 |
| 0.55 | 15.0 GB | 19292 | 3809 |

**At the default chunk size** (fp8 KV, `--chunked-prefill-size 8192`; code pinned via
git worktrees, sglang@3c02143bb7 + flashinfer fmha_v2_test = perf_qtile@2a14301a +
cherry-picked 49b01545). Cells: input tok/s / median TTFT ms / median TPOT ms.

| ISL | FA3 | fmha_v2 zero-copy | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64k | 40368 / 2459 / 15.3 | **40918 / 2581 / 14.85** | 1.01 |
| 128k | 38643 / 3236 / 13.9 | **39309 / 3299 / 13.10** | 1.02 |

Confirmation trace (`wt_fmhav2_fp8_64k`): zero pool-sized `aten::cat` ops, GPU busy
1.38 s (FA3: 1.39 s), fmha_v2 kernel 81.6 ms.

**Dense model** (Qwen3-32B-FP8, 64 layers / 8 KV heads / head_dim 128, TP=4 -> 16q:2kv
per rank, YaRN x4 for 128k, chunk 8192, mem 0.85). Cells: input tok/s / TTFT ms / TPOT ms.

| ISL | FA3 | fmha_v2 |
|---|---|---|
| 8k | 21992 / 3473 / 16.5 | **23113 / 3471 / 15.4** (+5.1%) |
| 32k | 18661 / 5169 / 17.3 | **19324 / 4955 / 16.8** (+3.6%) |
| 128k | 12462 / 13869 / 27.7 | **13568 / 12662 / 25.4** (+8.9%) |

Full fp8 ISL sweep at chunk 2048 (1k-128k) is in the linked results doc; parity within
~1.5% for 1k-32k, -6% at 64k and -11% at 128k at that non-default chunk size only.

<details>
<summary>Repro</summary>

```bash
export PYTHONPATH=/SGL/sglang/python:/SGL/flashinfer
export FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1

python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model <MODEL> --tp 4 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
  --disable-radix-cache --mamba-ssm-dtype float32 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
  --attention-backend trtllm_mha --trust-remote-code --port 30000
# fp8 KV: add --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3

python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 \
  --model <MODEL> --dataset-name random --random-input-len <ISL> \
  --random-output-len <OSL> --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --num-prompts <N> --max-concurrency <C> --warmup-requests 2
```
Per-ISL (N, C, OSL): 1k=(200,64,256), 4k=(96,32,512), 8k=(64,32,512), 16k=(32,16,512),
32k=(16,8,512), 64k=(12,4,256), 128k=(8,2,256). The 64k/128k rows are latency-bound at
low concurrency (C=4/2), not throughput-saturated.

</details>

title: [Fix] Exclude added-vocabulary tokens from synthetic multimodal prompts
body:
## Motivation

Running the image benchmark dataset against MiniMax-M3 fails with HTTP 400 errors, because the randomly generated prompt text can contain a media placeholder token that the server then expects real video data for. The failures are silent — you only see them if you compare successful requests against the number you asked for — so multimodal benchmark results are unreliable. This PR fixes it by excluding those tokens from the random sampling pool. Technical details below: 

`--dataset-name image` builds the text half of each synthetic prompt by sampling random
token ids and decoding them. `get_available_multimodal_text_tokens()` excludes
`tokenizer.all_special_ids` plus the single `image_pad_id` the caller passes, so media
placeholders that live only in the **added vocabulary** stay sampleable.

For `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4`, neither placeholder is in `all_special_ids`:

| token | id | in `all_special_ids` | in `get_added_vocab()` | excluded before this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `]<]image[>[` | 200025 | no | yes | yes (as `image_pad_id`) |
| `]<]video[>[` | 200026 | no | yes | **no** |

When id 200026 is drawn, `tokenizer.decode` renders it verbatim into the prompt text. The
server matches that text to `Modality.VIDEO`, finds no video attached to the request, and
returns:

```
{"object":"error","message":"No data iterator found for token: ]<]video[>[",
 "type":"BadRequestError","param":null,"code":400}
```

The loss is quiet: only `Successful requests` drops below `--num-prompts`, and the error
body is discarded unless `--output-details` is set.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: this changes only synthetic benchmark prompt generation, not kernels or
model forward code.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable: no inference-path change. The pool is rebuilt once per `lru_cache` miss
exactly as before.

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Performance] Improve HyperConnection performance for Qwen-3.8-Flash
body:
## Motivation

Reduce HyperConnection (HC) kernel launches and intermediate memory traffic
in Qwen-3.8-Flash around attention/MLP, without changing the core computation.
Fuse Down and Inject, and reuse residual statistics across HC blocks instead of
materializing a normalized residual at each block.

This patch targets `main` and contains only the HC optimization changes across
18 production files; the previously merged model support is not part of this patch.

## Modifications

- **Fuse Down + Inject.** Fold the learned RMS scale into shared packed weights.
  Small T uses the custom GEMM epilogue to emit Down/SiLU and FP32 alpha;
  large T uses branch-batched GEMM with aligned output padding, followed by
  fused branch reduction, normalization, SiLU and sigmoid.
- **Reuse cross-block RMS statistics.** Carry the raw residual and FP32 square
  sums in `HCSumState`. Down and Up/Mix reconstruct inverse RMS where needed.
  Apply fuses the residual update with square-sum accumulation; Up/Mix resets
  the next sum buffer, avoiding separate normalization and reset kernels in
  steady state. Initial or invalidated state still requires bootstrap statistics.
- **Tune the remaining kernels.** Use register-only alpha output, configuration-
  sized shared memory, finer Up tiles, warp-shuffle post-processing and
  vectorized Apply. Runtime branch stride avoids exact-T JIT specialization;
  global address products use wide indexing.
- **Integrate with the framework and loaders.** Preserve the Tensor ABI for
  non-opted-in callers and keep checkpoint parameter names unchanged. The
  opted-in model carries `HCSumState` between blocks; packed HC uses a context
  object between `mix` and `combine`. Both token paths share
  prepared Down/Inject and RMS GPU layouts; canonical checkpoint values remain
  on CPU. Adapt weight updates, presharded loading, NCCL, IPC and RDMA to this
  storage model, including independent/repeated CPU IPC clients.

The dispatch boundary remains `T=24`. The optimized BF16/FP16 route validates
device/layout constraints and uses `C=4`; hidden size remains shape-derived.
Attention/MLP is not bypassed in production. Down and Inject must be updated
together. After any weight reload, recapture CUDA Graphs before replay: preparation
recreates derived small-T tensors even for in-place parameter updates. Generic
weight-update APIs do not automatically enforce this HC requirement.

This is tolerance-validated, not bitwise-equivalent to the original: statistics
use the FP32 residual update before its BF16/FP16 store, and folding RMS weights
changes rounding. Final alpha and carried statistics remain FP32; large-T
logits retain their activation-dtype rounding before the nonlinear operations.

### Known Limitation

`--enable-deterministic-inference` is **not supported by the optimized HC route**
in this PR and must remain disabled. Apply uses unordered FP32 atomic sums,
and the deterministic BMM replacement does not accept the required `out_dtype`
argument. Both will be addressed in a separate follow-up PR.

## Accuracy Tests

The results below compare HC commit `40d1499abe` with unmodified `main` at
`630b1ef322`.

- HC module validation: 32 BF16/FP16 numerical cases and 160
  changed-input CUDA Graph replays per implementation, including the 24/25 and
  32/33 boundaries and alternative shapes. Maximum relative-RMS drift versus
  unmodified main was 0.002847 for BF16 and 0.000357 for FP16, below unchanged
  limits of 0.008 and 0.0015.
- Focused regressions passed for shared weights, empty/aliased state,
  state-dict/direct/dummy loading, two-GPU NCCL and six independent/repeated CPU
  IPC clients, using the same final dependency environment as the module tests.
- Full-model GSM8K: unmodified main **1283/1319 (97.2707%)**, optimized
  **1282/1319 (97.1948%)**, a difference of one question (-0.0758 percentage
  points). Both had zero request errors and zero truncations. Paired results:
  1279 both correct, 4 baseline-only correct, 3 optimized-only correct, 33 both
  incorrect. This single run is not a statistical non-inferiority proof.

GSM8K used the same model checkpoint and complete dataset on four GB300 GPUs,
BF16, TP4/EP2, temperature 0, top-p 0.95, no-thinking, maximum 10240 generated
tokens and concurrency 32. Speculative decoding and service CUDA Graphs were
disabled; both runs used the same QSA Torch / vendored FA4 backend selection.
This does not validate the default backend combination.

Validation harnesses are separate from this production patch. Full-service
Graph/NEXTN testing below covers simulated-acceptance performance, not accuracy
under natural speculative decoding. Cross-node RDMA and the complete daemon
lifecycle remain untested; an unresolved CUDA IPC reference-count warning
remains at process exit.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### HC-only microbenchmark

Baseline: unmodified `main` at `630b1ef322`; optimized: `40d1499abe`. GB300; BF16;
`C=4, H=2560, L=320`; CUDA 13.3 / Torch 2.13; sglang-kernel 0.4.7 and
FlashInfer 0.6.18. Nsight Compute 2026.2.1 pure-kernel duration, strict application
replay, cache-control none and base clocks. Sources and compiled artifacts were
frozen; compilation is excluded from timing. Two reversed-order rounds, 20
samples per T per round; each sample measures two consecutive HC shells,
with per-shell totals aggregated by median.

Units: **µs per steady-state HC shell**. `T` is HC token count. The harness
bypasses attention/MLP; timings exclude bootstrap/final special cases and host
overhead, but include all retained HC stages. These are **HC-only**, not
end-to-end model speedups.

| T | Kernels: original → optimized | Original (µs) | Optimized (µs) | Speedup |
|---:|:---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 5 → 3 | 21.416 | 15.504 | 1.381× |
| 2 | 5 → 3 | 21.636 | 15.600 | 1.387× |
| 4 | 5 → 3 | 21.780 | 15.620 | 1.394× |
| 5 | 5 → 3 | 22.144 | 15.684 | 1.412× |
| 8 | 5 → 3 | 22.452 | 15.788 | 1.422× |
| 10 | 5 → 3 | 26.800 | 18.116 | 1.479× |
| 16 | 5 → 3 | 27.524 | 18.212 | 1.511× |
| 20 | 5 → 3 | 32.684 | 21.220 | 1.540× |
| 24 | 5 → 3 | 33.004 | 21.304 | 1.549× |
| 25 | 8 → 5 | 32.300 | 22.376 | 1.444× |
| 32 | 8 → 5 | 33.056 | 22.508 | 1.469× |
| 33 | 7 → 5 | 33.272 | 22.560 | 1.475× |
| 40 | 7 → 5 | 33.600 | 22.696 | 1.480× |
| 80 | 7 → 5 | 36.016 | 25.020 | 1.439× |

Geometric-mean speedup across these 14 workloads: **1.455×**.

### End-to-end serving

Measured on 2026-09-22 with the same revisions and model checkpoint: **2×GB300,
BF16, TP2/EP2, 8192 input / 1024 output tokens**, Triton MoE and `trtllm_mha`.
NEXTN uses 3 steps, top-k 1 and 4 draft tokens, with decode CUDA Graphs enabled.
`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.6` enables fixed-token, simulated-acceptance testing;
these are not natural speculative acceptance-rate or accuracy results.
Radix caching and overlap scheduling are disabled; `max-running-requests=72`.
Both versions use identical launch arguments and client settings.

The official `sglang.benchmark.serving` HTTP benchmark ran three rounds per
concurrency, with `max(32, 5 * concurrency)` requests per round. Throughput is
the median of the three round throughputs; latency columns are medians of the
per-round means. Warmup/compilation are excluded, and no profiler is active
during these measurements. All **10,512 requests** across both versions
succeeded with the requested lengths; matched prompt/output/verify counters
exclude differing simulated acceptance as the source of the gain.

| Concurrency | Baseline (tok/s) | Optimized (tok/s) | Throughput gain | TTFT (ms), baseline → optimized | TPOT (ms/token), baseline → optimized |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 347.757 | 354.064 | +1.81% | 205.16 → 202.26 | 2.677 → 2.629 |
| 8 | 1433.624 | 1471.807 | +2.66% | 896.42 → 879.57 | 4.703 → 4.574 |
| 16 | 2005.595 | 2072.988 | +3.36% | 1611.35 → 1583.77 | 6.400 → 6.167 |
| 64 | 3079.837 | 3146.780 | +2.17% | 5880.49 → 5784.53 | 15.023 → 14.673 |
| 256 | 3193.079 | 3261.558 | +2.14% | 59344.79 → 58104.83 | 16.028 → 15.655 |

Output-throughput speedup is **1.0181–1.0336×**, with a **1.0243× geometric
mean** across the five concurrency levels. Concurrency is not HC token count
or running batch size: concurrency 256 reaches a maximum decode request batch
of 72, with the remaining requests queued. TTFT includes queueing.

### Why the end-to-end gain is about 2%, rather than the HC-only gain

A separate concurrency-1 Nsight Systems capture confirmed the optimized HC
path on both TP ranks. HC, including its generically named Down/Up GEMMs,
accounts for approximately **16% of baseline summed decode kernel duration**;
this is not a serial wall-clock fraction. MoE, attention, other projections,
communication and framework overhead are outside this PR's optimization scope.

The baseline Gate also uses programmatic dependent launch (PDL): it can start
before the preceding AllReduce completes and then wait for its dependency.
About **63–65% of its recorded duration overlaps that AllReduce** in this trace,
so removing the Gate does not remove an equal amount of critical-path time.
The observed interval from AllReduce completion to Apply completion decreases
from approximately **2.92 to 1.67 µs**, rather than saving the whole roughly
4.5 µs Gate interval. The overlap is not an instruction-level wait measurement.
These observations explain why HC-only improvements translate into a smaller,
but measurable, full-model gain; they are not an exact E2E cost decomposition.

The single-request node traces are diagnostic only, separate from both the NCU
table and the unprofiled HTTP results. Both had shutdown flush warnings, but
every decode Graph kernel node was verified across all 284 replays on both
TP ranks. They are not used to derive the reported E2E speedups.

## Checklist

All applicable pre-commit checks passed for the 18 changed production files.

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [Spec] Enable split-KV EAGLE verify on CUDA for the Triton backend
body:
## Motivation

`verify_splitkv_fwd` (the flash-decode style EAGLE target-verify kernel for the Triton backend) is currently gated behind `is_gfx95_supported()`, so it only runs on AMD MI35x. On CUDA the Triton backend's target-verify falls back to `extend_attention_fwd`, whose grid is `(bs, head_num, cdiv(max_len_extend, BLOCK_M))`. At `topk=1` with 4 draft tokens that is **one program per (seq, head)** that walks the whole prefix serially in `BLOCK_N` steps — for a 24-head model, 24 programs vs. the `num_kv_splits=8` × 24 = 192 the regular decode kernel uses for the same prefix.

The consequence is that verify cost grows linearly with prefix length and speculative decoding becomes **slower than no-spec beyond ~32k context**, even with a healthy accept length. On a 27B hybrid-GDN model at 128k we measured decode dropping from 31 tok/s (no spec) to 10 tok/s (NEXTN), which is easy to misattribute to the SSM state handling.

The kernel itself is already NV-safe (HIP-only launch kwargs are gated on `is_hip()` inside `verify_splitkv.py`, and its own docstring says so), and `test_verify_splitkv.py` is registered on the CUDA CI lane. This PR simply drops the gfx95 gate. `SGLANG_ENABLE_SPLITKV_VERIFY=0` remains as the opt-out.

### Why the gate is gfx95-only today

The gate is historical, not technical. In #27382 the kernel originally shipped with **no platform gate**; the NVIDIA CI lane then failed (`test_basic_sanity_eagle3.py`, `KeyError: Keyword argument waves_per_eu was specified but unrecognised`) because the AMD-only Triton launch hints were passed unconditionally. The author fixed that in f7622c0 by making the kwargs HIP-conditional — and at the same time narrowed the dispatch to `is_hip()`, later to `is_gfx95_supported()` at review request ("scoped to where it's validated"). So the kernel has been NV-safe since before merge, and its numerics test has been running on the CUDA CI lane the whole time; only the dispatch was left closed. #35521 makes the same observation for gfx942 ("the kernel is arch-neutral Triton"). This PR supplies the CUDA validation that was missing at the time.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py`: remove `is_gfx95_supported()` from the `use_verify_splitkv` condition; keep the `topk == 1` and env-var gates. Comment updated to explain why.
- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: doc comment for `SGLANG_ENABLE_SPLITKV_VERIFY` now says ROCm and CUDA.

`_should_use_verify_shared_kv` (the grouped-head MLA / single-KV-head kernel) is left gfx95-only; this PR only touches the per-head split-KV path that `can_handle()` already validates.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/attention/test_verify_splitkv.py` on CUDA (sm_80, Triton from the 0.5.19 wheel): **9 tests, OK** (parity vs `extend_attention_fwd` across head dims / GQA ratios / prefix lengths / KV scales, plus the `can_handle()` rejection cases).

End-to-end: served a Qwen3.5-27B-class checkpoint with `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --attention-backend triton`; accept length stayed at 3.0–3.5 before and after (only the verify kernel changed), tool-call parsing and reasoning parsing unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen3.5-27B (hybrid GDN: 48 linear-attn + 16 full-attn layers, GQA 24/4, head_dim 256), compressed-tensors W4A16, 1× sm_80 GPU (64 GB), `--mem-fraction-static 0.80`, `--attention-backend triton --mamba-backend triton`, batch 1, cold prefix cache, 128 output tokens. Decode tok/s:

| prompt tokens | no spec | NEXTN s3/k1/d4 **before** | NEXTN s3/k1/d4 **after** |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 69.6 | 209.4 | **217.5** |
| 8,192 | 65.0 | 94.7 | **162.8** |
| 32,768 | 53.4 | 38.9 | **131.3** |
| 131,072 | 31.1 | 10.1 | **57.7** |

Before this change spec decoding is a net loss past 32k; after it is +86% over no-spec at 128k. Prefill / TTFT is unaffected by this PR (verify is a decode-side kernel).

Concurrency 4 at 32k (sum of per-stream decode tok/s) is flat vs. no-spec (156 vs 172), as expected once the GPU is saturated; the win is at low concurrency / long context.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (Existing `test_verify_splitkv.py` already covers the kernel on the CUDA lane; no new kernel code.)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing flag change; env var comment updated.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [model] Backend-agnostic fixes: encoder SEP-truncation, Hunyuan-A13B qk_norm
body:
Backend-agnostic fixes needed to serve several models, split out of the XPU
model-enabling PR #35304 so the shared / non-XPU changes are reviewed on their own.
None of these are gated behind a specific backend.

## Modifications

**1. Encoder embedding truncation preserves the trailing separator** (`managers/`)
Encoder embedding models (BERT / RoBERTa / ModernBERT / NomicBERT) rely on the
trailing `[SEP]`; a plain head-slice on over-length inputs drops it and shifts the
pooled embedding.
- `managers/utils.py`: the auto-truncation helper takes an optional
  `preserve_last_token_id`; re-append it after the head-slice when present.
- `managers/scheduler.py`: resolve `sep_token_id` once (only when `not is_generation`)
  and pass it through.
- `managers/tokenizer_manager.py`: same preservation on that truncation path.
Gated on `not is_generation`, so generation models are unaffected.

**2. Hunyuan-A13B qk_norm shape** (`models/hunyuan.py`)
`use_qk_norm` reshaped q/k to `(tokens*heads, head_dim)` for the per-head RMSNorm and
never restored the flat `(tokens, heads*head_dim)` layout, crashing the non-CUDA
(triton / XPU) `o_proj` (`mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied`); CUDA hid it via
flashinfer's token-count recompute. Restore the shape after qk_norm.

## Accuracy Test

- Encoders (with `[SEP]` preserved), Intel XPU Arc Pro B60, tp-1, MTEB SciFact NDCG@10:
  nomic-embed-text-v1.5 0.6803 (cos 1.00000); granite-embedding-english-r2 0.6720
  (cos 1.0 fp32 / >=0.9999 bf16, HF 0.6815).
- Hunyuan-A13B (XPU tp-8): loads with 0 skipped params; gsm8k (lm-eval) exact_match
  **66.87**.

title: [AMD][DI][CI] Use a node-local model cache on the SPUR cluster
body:
## What

Nightly DI CI on the SPUR MI355X cluster loads weights over shared storage.
It cannot serve 16 ranks pulling the same shards at once: a 1.5 TB checkpoint
took 16-24 minutes to load against a 50 minute health wait, so every model
over ~400 GB timed out. Failures split exactly by checkpoint size.

Adds `MODEL_LOCAL_ROOT`. When set, the container loads from the node-local
copy of the model cache while the snapshot hash is still resolved against the
shared root, which is the only one the driver node can read. Unset by default,
so no other cluster changes behavior.

Also adds a preflight: `/tmp` does not survive a reboot, and without a check
the container silently falls back to the shared root and the only symptom is a
health-wait timeout 50 minutes later. And drops `SLURM_EXCLUDE`, which names
two nodes from the old cluster.

## Needs one env change

The runner also needs `MODEL_LOCAL_ROOT=/tmp/model_coverage` in its `.env`,
next to the existing `MODEL_ROOT`. @bingxche - only you can edit those files.

## Validation

Snapshot hashes and shard counts verified against the shared root for all 8
checkpoints on all 4 nodes. Preflight tested both ways. Confirmed the
mi355x/slurm path is untouched when the variable is unset. Full accuracy run

title: [Diffusion] Apply latent-ids and packing to caller-provided initial latents
body:
## Motivation

Reported in #34000 (Bug 3).

`LatentPreparationStage.forward` runs two different preparations depending on where the latents came from:

```python
if latents is None:
    latents = randn_tensor(...)
    latent_ids = server_args.pipeline_config.maybe_prepare_latent_ids(latents) ...
    if latent_ids is not None:
        batch.latent_ids = latent_ids.to(device=device)
    if spec.pack_latents:
        latents = server_args.pipeline_config.maybe_pack_latents(latents, batch_size, batch)
else:
    latents = latents.to(device)     # <- no latent_ids, no packing
```

For packed models this is fatal. `Flux2PipelineConfig` supplies both hooks, and `FluxPipelineConfig.get_freqs_cis` later does:

```python
img_ids = batch.latent_ids
if img_ids.ndim == 3:
```

so an injected `x_T` reaches the denoising loop with `latent_ids` still `None` → `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'ndim'`. The latents also stay unpacked `(B, C, H, W)` where the transformer expects the packed `(B, H*W, C)` layout.

The grouped path already funnels provided latents into `forward`: `run_grouped_requests` falls back to per-request `self(batch, server_args)` when `any(batch.latents is not None ...)`, so fixing `forward` covers both paths.

## Modifications

Hoist the shared preparation so provided latents can run it too, **gated on the provided tensor matching the layout the randn branch would have produced** (`spec.shape`).

The gate is load-bearing, and I'd appreciate a maintainer sanity-check on it. The ComfyUI executors assign `Req.latents` in the already-packed `[B, S, D]` layout (`apps/ComfyUI_SGLDiffusion/executors/flux.py:54`, `req.latents = hidden_states  # Set as [B, S, D] format directly`), and those requests **do** reach this stage — `ComfyUIFluxPipeline.create_pipeline_stages` installs `ComfyUILatentPreparationStage`, which inherits this `forward` and pairs it with `FluxPipelineConfig`. Packing such a tensor a second time leaves the element count unchanged, so `_pack_latents`' `view` succeeds and **silently permutes** the caller's latents rather than raising. Latents in a layout this stage would not have drawn are therefore passed through untouched, exactly as before.

Corroborating evidence that this is the intended split: `ComfyUILatentPreparationStage.forward` saves `original_latents_shape` before calling `super().forward()` and restores it after, commented "before any potential packing/conversion (e.g., 4D spatial -> 3D sequence) to ensure proper unpadding later" — i.e. the parent packing provided latents is an expected outcome for the 4D case.

No-op for models that don't pack: the base `PipelineConfig` returns `None` from `maybe_prepare_latent_ids` and returns the latents unchanged from `maybe_pack_latents`, and stages that set `prepare_latent_ids=False` / `pack_latents=False` on their spec (realtime, LongLive2) skip both hooks as before. The randn path is unchanged.

## Accuracy Test

With a packed-model config stub whose `maybe_pack_latents` reshapes off the spec dims (mirroring the real `view`-based `_pack_latents`):

```
case                            latent_ids   packs   out shape
before  randn (drawn)           (1, 64, 4)     1     (1, 16, 16)
before  provided, drawn-layout        None     0     (1, 4, 8, 8)   <- unusable downstream
before  provided, PRE-PACKED          None     0     (1, 16, 4)

after   randn (drawn)           (1, 64, 4)     1     (1, 16, 16)
after   provided, drawn-layout  (1, 64, 4)     1     (1, 16, 16)    <- fixed
after   provided, PRE-PACKED          None     0     (1, 16, 4)     <- byte-identical, 0 pack calls
```

The pre-packed row is checked with `torch.equal` against the input, not just by shape.

**Verification caveat, please read:** I could not run the pytest suite against `main` — the sglang install I have is `0.5.12.post1`, whose tree predates the current layout, and my only box is a CPU node where importing `sglang.multimodal_gen` off network storage takes >10 minutes. The table above comes from extracting the real `forward` from both `main` and this branch via `git show` and executing them side by side against stubs. **The added unit test has not been executed under a real sglang install** — please treat it as unvalidated and let CI be the first real run. Given the ComfyUI interaction, an E2E run on a ComfyUI Flux workflow would be the most valuable check you could add here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code with pre-commit hooks (isort / black / ruff clean on the changed files)
- [x] Add unit tests (`test_provided_latents_preparation.py`, incl. a pre-packed passthrough case) — but see the verification caveat above
- [x] Linked the tracking issue (#34000)

title: [AMD] Fix Quark block-FP8 loading in DeepSeek loader
body:
# Fix Quark block-FP8 loading in DeepSeek loader

## Summary

Enable `amd/GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8` (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) on
SGLang/ROCm by completing the DeepSeek-family weight-loading path for Quark
checkpoints that combine:

- globally quantized OCP MXFP4 experts; and
- explicitly configured block-FP8 attention linears.

SGLang PR #38546 already provides the shared Quark `layer_quant_config`
resolution and block-FP8 linear/MoE dispatch. It also handles scale names in
the `glm5_next.py` loader used by GLM-5.3-Flash. 

However, the non-Flash `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` architecture instead loads through
`DeepseekV2WeightLoaderMixin`, where three compatibility gaps remained.

## Bug

### Quark block-scale parameter name

Quark serializes block-FP8 scales as:

```text
*.weight_scale
```

The shared `Fp8LinearMethod` registers the corresponding runtime parameter as:

```text
*.weight_scale_inv
```

Consequences in the DeepSeek loader included missing parameters for ordinary
attention projections and fused `q_a_proj + kv_a_proj_with_mqa` scales.
MXFP4 scales cannot be renamed unconditionally because they legitimately use
`weight_scale`.

Reproduced on SGLang `main` without this change:

```text
Scheduler hit an exception:
  File "sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py",
       line 464, in do_load_weights
    param = params_dict[param_name]
KeyError:
  'model.layers.0.self_attn.fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa.weight_scale'
```

The runtime parameter at that point is
`fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa.weight_scale_inv`; the checkpoint name has already
been fused correctly, but its Quark scale suffix has not been adapted.

### Fused indexer scale classification

`_load_fused_indexer_wk()` recognized only the `_inv` suffix as a scale. A
Quark `weight_scale` tensor could therefore be treated as a projection weight.
This is a silent-corruption path rather than a guaranteed startup failure.

### MLA absorption used the global configuration

`post_load_weights()` derived `kv_b_proj` block geometry from the global
quantization configuration. For this mixed checkpoint, the global configuration
is MXFP4 and does not describe the block-FP8 `kv_b_proj`. The exact scheme is
already available on `kv_b_proj.quant_method`.

## Changes

### `deepseek_weight_loader.py`

1. Add `_resolve_quark_fp8_block_scale_name()`.
   - Rewrite `weight_scale` to `weight_scale_inv` only when the original
     parameter is absent and the `_inv` parameter exists.
   - Genuine MXFP4 `weight_scale` parameters remain unchanged.
2. Apply the alias after fused QKV-A name resolution and in the ordinary
   parameter-loading fallthrough.
3. Recognize both `weight_scale` and `weight_scale_inv` in the fused indexer
   path.
4. Add `_resolve_layer_weight_block_size()`.
   - Prefer the constructed layer's resolved quantization method.
   - Retain the existing config-level fallback for compatibility.
5. Use the resolved per-layer block size for MLA absorption and UE8M0 handling.

No model-name or checkpoint-name gate is added. The compatibility behavior is
driven by the registered parameter and resolved quantization method.

## Files

Production:

```text
python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py
```

Tests:

```text
test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_quark_block_fp8_loading.py
```

## Tests

The new CPU regression coverage verifies:

- conditional `weight_scale` to `weight_scale_inv` mapping;
- genuine MXFP4 scale names remain unchanged;
- fused QKV-A Quark scales concatenate and load into the registered parameter;
- ordinary attention scales load into `weight_scale_inv`;
- Quark indexer scales are not misclassified as weights; and
- per-layer quantization geometry takes precedence over a config-level summary.

Focused validation:

```text
24 passed
3 existing GLM tests passed, 27 subtests passed
13 existing Quark utility tests passed
```

Formatting and repository checks:

```text
isort: passed
ruff: passed
ruff-format: passed
codespell: passed
registered-test validation: passed
git diff --check: passed
```

## MI355X validation

Configuration:

```bash
sglang serve \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --model-path /models/GLM-5.3-MXFP4 \
  --tp 4 \
  --ep-size 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend triton \
  --dsa-decode-backend triton \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 131072 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.80 \
  --watchdog-timeout 1200 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8000
```

Observed:

- all 141 target-model shards loaded;
- the EAGLE/NextN model loaded;
- target-verify, draft-decode, and draft-extend graphs captured;
- health endpoint returned HTTP 200; and
- no missing-parameter warnings were observed.

GSM8K, 400 questions:

```text
Accuracy:          0.912
Invalid:           0.000
Latency:           24.621 s
Output throughput: 1569.041 token/s
```

The measured accuracy is consistent with the checkpoint's reported result.

## GLM-5.3-Flash regression validation

`amd/GLM-5.3-Flash-Quark-MXFP4` was also tested to verify that deriving MLA
block geometry from the resolved `kv_b_proj.quant_method` does not regress the
Flash path.

Current `main` loaded all 62 shards successfully, then failed during decode
graph capture in the independent CUDA-only `IndexerKPool` path:

```text
NotImplementedError: kpool indexer is only supported on CUDA
```

The loader change was therefore also applied to the ROCm Flash support branch
(`amd_glm5.3_flash` at `2fa010a4fb`), which contains the ROCm k-pool
implementation used by the validated Flash deployment.

Observed on 4× MI355X:

- all 62 shards loaded;
- decode graphs captured;
- health endpoint returned HTTP 200;
- internal chat-completion warm-up returned HTTP 200; and
- no missing-scale or loader errors were observed.

GSM8K via `benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py`, 400 questions:

```text
Accuracy:          0.920
Invalid:           0.000
Latency:           74.894 s
Output throughput: 497.087 token/s
```

This benchmark invocation is not directly comparable to the model card's
thinking-enabled `sgl-eval` recipe, but it provides a focused before-merge
serving and generation regression check.

### Flash performance A/B

The concurrency benchmark was repeated on the same support-branch revision,
hardware, checkpoint, and launch configuration with only this loader change
removed. Workload: random 8,192 input tokens and 1,024 output tokens.

| Concurrency | Baseline total tok/s | With fix total tok/s | Delta | Baseline median E2E | With fix median E2E | Delta |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2 | 1,978.39 | 1,972.94 | -0.28% | 9,318.61 ms | 9,325.65 ms | +0.08% |
| 4 | 3,631.30 | 3,625.18 | -0.17% | 10,146.22 ms | 10,169.20 ms | +0.23% |
| 8 | 6,336.93 | 6,327.30 | -0.15% | 11,635.31 ms | 11,647.49 ms | +0.10% |

Median ITL differed by only 0.01-0.02 ms across all three points. The observed
throughput and latency differences are below 0.3% and consistent with normal
run-to-run measurement noise; no material Flash performance regression was
observed.

## Scope

This is a follow-up to the Quark mixed-precision support in #38546. It does not
replace or modify GLM-5.3-Flash's MoE/AITER layout, clamp, padding, or
model-specific loading logic. It completes the separate DeepSeek loader path
used by `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`.

- Add padding mechanism for vision part of `pixtral` modules to support TP6.

## Accuracy Tests

Server launching example commands:

```
sglang serve --model-path mistralai/Ministral-3-8B-Instruct-2512 --device cpu --tp 6 --disable-overlap-schedule

sglang serve --model-path mistralai/Ministral-3-14B-Instruct-2512 --device cpu --tp 6 --disable-overlap-schedule

sglang serve --model-path mistralai/Devstral-2-123B-Instruct-2512 --device cpu --tp 6 --disable-overlap-schedule

Tested with demo request script in [Devstral-2 cookbook](https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Mistral/Devstral-2#4-1-basic-usage-openai-compatible-api):

Output makes sense:
```
Here's a Python function that implements a request with exponential backoff using the `time` module and `requests` library. This function will retry a request if it fails, with a delay that increases exponentially each time.

```python
import time
import requests
from requests.exceptions import RequestException

def retry_with_backoff(
    url: str,
    max_retries: int = 3,
    initial_delay: float = 1.0,
    backoff_factor: float = 2.0,
    status_forcelist: tuple = (500, 502, 503, 504),
    method: str = 'GET',
    **kwargs
) -> requests.Response:
    """
    Retry a request with exponential backoff.

    Args:
        url: The URL to request.
        max_retries: Maximum number of retries (default: 3).
        initial_delay: Initial delay in seconds (default: 1.0).
        backoff_factor: Multiplier for the delay between retries (default: 2.0).
        status_forcelist: Tuple of HTTP status codes to trigger a retry (default: (500, 502, 503, 504)).
        method: HTTP method (default: 'GET').
        **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments for the `requests` function.

    Returns:
        requests.Response: The response object.

    Raises:
        RequestException: If all retries are exhausted.
    """
    delay = initial_delay
    for attempt in range(max_retries):
        try:
            response = requests.request(method, url, **kwargs)
            if response.status_code in status_forcelist:
                raise RequestException(f"Retrying due to status code: {response.status_code}")
            return response
        except RequestException as e:
            if attempt == max_retries - 1:
                raise RequestException(f"Request failed after {max_retries} retries: {e}")
            time.sleep(delay)
            delay *= backoff_factor

    raise RequestException("Unexpected error: max_retries exceeded unexpectedly.")
```
```

title: [quant] fix: accept a pre-quantized input in FlashInfer's block-FP8 GEMM
body:
## Motivation

**Problem:** a block-FP8 linear layer whose GEMM runs on FlashInfer's groupwise runner crashes if its input is already FP8-quantized.

**Background:** a block-FP8 linear layer usually receives a bf16 input and quantizes it to FP8 itself before the GEMM. `Fp8LinearMethod.apply` also accepts an input that the caller already quantized, as an `(fp8 q, scales)` tuple. In that case the layer skips its own quantization and passes the pair to the GEMM runner as `input` / `input_scale`. This lets a producer kernel fuse the quantization into its own epilogue and save a full read/write pass over the activation. For example:
- a fused `silu_and_mul` + quant kernel;
- a fused norm/modulation + quant kernel;
- a tensor-parallel all-gather that moves FP8 rows instead of bf16, half the bytes.

**What breaks:** the Triton, torch and SGLang CUTLASS runners all accept `input_scale`. The FlashInfer groupwise runner (`flashinfer_gemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback`) starts with `assert input_scale is None`. On Blackwell GPUs with FlashInfer installed (SM100/103 and SM120), auto dispatch picks this runner whenever DeepGEMM is not enabled, for example when `deep_gemm` is not installed, or an installed build predates its SM120 kernels, or `SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=0` is set. It is also used when `--fp8-gemm-backend` is `flashinfer_cutlass` or `flashinfer_trtllm`. In those configurations, a pre-quantized input fails the assert, and none of the fusions above can be used.

**Impact of this PR:** no code in `main` passes a block-FP8 tuple to this runner today, so no current behavior changes. This PR makes the FlashInfer runner accept the same input the other runners already accept, so such fusions can be added.

## Modifications

`flashinfer_gemm_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback` in `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py`:
- When `input_scale` is given, it uses `input` (which must be `float8_e4m3fn`) and `input_scale` directly instead of calling `sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8`.
- `input_scale` must have shape `(m, k // block_k)` in fp32. It can be row-major or column-major. It is laid out the way each backend reads it:
  - CUTLASS (`scale_major_mode="MN"`): transposed to a contiguous `(k // block_k, m)`, the same path the runner's own quantizer output takes.
  - TRTLLM: column-major `(m, k // block_k)`, the layout the runner requests from its own quantizer with `column_major_scales=True`.
  - TRTLLM's Triton fallback (K < 256): row-major, which is what `triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` expects for a pre-quantized input.
- The output is bf16, matching the Triton, torch and SGLang CUTLASS runners for a pre-quantized input.
- A wrong dtype or scale shape now fails with an explicit message.
- The path without `input_scale` is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

The requirement is bit-exactness. A layer given `sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8(x, 128)` must return exactly the bits it returns for `x`, since that is the quantization the runner does internally.

- `test_fp8_blockwise_linear_backends.py::TestFp8BlockwisePrequantizedInput` (GPU) checks `torch.equal(layer((q, s)), layer(x))` with both row-major and column-major `s`, over the existing `FP8_BLOCK_SHAPES`, on `flashinfer_cutlass` (SM100/SM120) and `flashinfer_trtllm` (SM100).
- `test_flashinfer_trtllm_fp8_fallback.py::TestFlashinferPrequantizedInput` (CPU, mocked GEMMs) checks four things:
  - the scale layout each backend receives;
  - that the quantizer is not called;
  - the Triton fallback for K < 256;
  - that a wrong scale shape is rejected.

Without the change, all of the new tests fail on the `assert input_scale is None`.

Results on an RTX 5090 (SM120): both files pass (15 passed, 23 subtests), and the existing `triton` and `cutlass` backend tests are unaffected. I had no SM100 GPU, so the TRTLLM path is covered only by the CPU tests here. The GPU test for it will run on the B200 CI runner.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This PR has no speed impact: no existing call path changes. It enables fusions that skip a separate quantization pass. 

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [LMCache] Support lmcache unified radix cache
body:
# Support LMCache in UnifiedRadixCache ## Summary This PR adds LMCache as an external KV-cache backend for SGLang's `UnifiedRadixCache` path. The integration keeps the existing radix-cache lookup, store, reuse, and flush behavior while allowing reusable KV blocks to be persisted and restored through LMCache. Overall flowchart: The validation covers: - prefix reuse across requests; - repeated warm requests; - cache flush followed by a cold request; - accuracy on `gsm8k` and `mixed_prefix_gsm8k`; - write-path overhead with no cache hits; - filesystem restore performance with reusable prompt KV loaded from storage; - comparison with the existing HiCache filesystem path. ## Related PRs - Design doc: https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/5041 - `UnifiedLMCacheMPConnector` implemention: https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/4828 ## Functional validation The request sequence below was exercised on both model families. | Step | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Qwen-3.5-27B | Purpose | |---|---:|---:|---| | Initial request | 716 input / 512 output tokens | 726 input / 512 output tokens | Populate the cache | | Longer request sharing the same prefix | 1,021 input / 474 output tokens | 1,025 input / 512 output tokens | Verify prefix reuse | | Repeat the longer request | Tested | Tested | Verify the warm path | | Flush radix cache and repeat | Tested | Tested | Verify flush and cold fallback | ## Accuracy Evaluation configuration: - 200 examples; - 32 threads; - 5-shot prompting; - temperature `0`; - maximum output length `2,048` tokens. | Model | Evaluation | Baseline | LMCache cold | LMCache warm | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | GSM8K | 0.975 | 0.96 | 0.97 | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Mixed-prefix GSM8K | 0.985 | 0.985 | 0.975 | | Qwen-3.5-27B | GSM8K | 0.745 | 0.73 | 0.75 | | Qwen-3.5-27B | Mixed-prefix GSM8K | 0.86 | 0.865 | 0.85 | The observed score variation is at most 1.5 percentage points across the sampled runs, with no consistent degradation between cold and warm LMCache paths. ## Serving benchmark Benchmark configuration: | Parameter | Value | |---|---:| | Dataset | Random | | Requests | 256 | | Input length | 32,001 tokens | | Output length | 128 tokens | | Request rate | Unlimited | | Maximum concurrency | 4/8/16/32 | | Seed | 42 | | Warm-up requests | 0 | ### DeepSeek-V4-Flash ### Qwen-3.5-27B ## Reproduction commands

title: [Diffusion] Add a permanent lifetime for layerwise resident layers
body:
Follows #40590 / #40592 / #40593 (all merged), which name and document the
lifetime the resident set has today; this one adds the other lifetime, which is
what the flag was designed to mean. `main` is merged in (`a5e7f87`), so the diff
is exactly this change.

## What the flag does today, and what it was meant to do

`--layerwise-resident-layers` keeps a set of a component's layers on the GPU
instead of streaming them. Today that set lives for the component's run: it is
pinned by the layer-0 pre-hook when the component starts its forwards for a
request, released by `finish_use → release_all()` when it finishes, and a
pinned host copy of every resident layer is kept for the next request.
`finish_request` forces `preferred = False` for any module that holds
residents, so nothing keeps the set past the request.

That is the right shape when several components' resident sets have to share
one budget: only the running component holds its set, so the peak is the
largest single set rather than their sum. It is the wrong shape when the sum
fits -- the layers are transferred again on every request, and host memory is
pinned for a reload that never had to happen. The original intent of the flag
was the second case: place the layers once, at load, keep no host copy, never
release them.

Both shapes are real, on adjacent consumer cards, for the same model and the
same flag value. Qwen-Image-2.1 with DiT+VAE resident (14.5 GiB) and the
text encoder's resident set at 0.8 (~9-11 GiB): the sum fits on an RTX 5090
(31.4 GiB) and keeping the set was measured faster (14.136 → 13.737 s); it does
not fit on an RTX 4090 (23.5 GiB, ~6.9 GiB free once DiT+VAE are resident), and
keeping it left the server unable to start. So the lifetime cannot be a
constant, and it is not the same knob as *which* layers are resident.

## The change

A lifetime axis beside the existing policy axis, in the same two-flag shape:

```
--dit-layerwise-residency-lifetime {forward,permanent}       # group default
--layerwise-residency-lifetime transformer=permanent,video_vae=forward
```

| lifetime | placed | host copy | released | transfers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `forward` (default, today's behaviour) | when the component starts running its layers for a request | kept, pinned | when it finishes | once per request |
| `permanent` | at load, before any forward or warmup | none | never | once, for the life of the server |

`forward` stays the default, so no existing command changes behaviour. Whether
`permanent` becomes the default when the sum fits is a placement decision; it
belongs with the residency planner (#37917 already carries a
`permanent_residency` field on `ResidencyTarget` and splits its option keys
into `permanent` / `stage`), not in a constant here.

### Manager

- Permanent layers are split out of `layer_groups` before the hosting plan
  runs, so they take no host store and spend none of the pin budget. They are
  placed with a layout-keeping device copy -- a transposed FP8 view has to stay
  transposed, the same reason the strided host store exists -- shared by the
  CUDA and MPS load paths.
- Residency is armed from construction, so `_head_of_stream` starts at the
  first streamed layer rather than layer 0.
- `release_layer` returns early for a permanent layer regardless of `force`.
  That single check covers `release_all`, the `disable_offload → enable_offload`
  round trip the compile-warmup and LoRA paths take, skip-gap and wraparound
  releases alike. `sync_layer_to_cpu` has nothing to sync;
  `iter_materialized_weights` reads them from the module as it does any
  non-offloaded parameter. `prepare_for_next_req` no longer visits them.
- A permanent lifetime with zero resident layers warns and streams everything.
- The readiness log names the lifetime:
  `resident=53/66 (permanent), policy=leading`, and placement logs what it
  put on the device: `placed 29 permanent resident layers (10.42 GiB) on the
  device at load; no host copy is kept.`

### Server args and help

One group default plus one per-component map, validated in the CLI (`choices`)
and in the Python API (`ValueError`), with the same "has no effect" warnings the
policy knob gives. The two resident-layer help strings now describe the default
lifetime instead of the permanent one they used to promise, and point at the
new knob; the CLI reference and the deployment cookbook gain the lifetime and
the rule for choosing it (sum fits → `permanent`; otherwise `forward`).

Wording is the user's, not the runtime's: "while the component runs for a
request", "released when it finishes", "for the life of the server". No
`ComponentUse` vocabulary on any user-facing surface.

## Validation

**Unit tests, on an H200 devbox at this head (`2bb100d`)**:
`test_layerwise_offload.py` 170 passed (158 on `main` + 12 new);
`test_server_args.py -k "lifetime or residency"` 21 passed + 13 subtests.
The new tests pin: placement at load without a host store and with layout kept;
survival through `release_layer(force=True)`, `release_all`,
`sync_all_layers_to_cpu`, and a `disable_offload → enable_offload` round trip;
`prepare_for_next_req` not touching the set (same `data_ptr`, no prefetch
issued); the hosting plan receiving only the streamed layers;
`iter_materialized_weights` yielding every parameter exactly once; the
zero-resident warning; rejection of unknown values in both the manager and
`layerwise_tuning_for`; the readiness log; and the help text's claims.

**End to end, Qwen-Image-2.1 on one H200**, the 5090 recipe's shape
(`--component-residency dit=resident text_encoder=layerwise-offload
vae=resident --layerwise-resident-layers text_encoder=0.8`), only the lifetime
flag differing; 1024², 40 steps, seed 42, `generator_device=cpu`; one warm
request then five measured:

| | `forward` | `permanent` | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| e2e p50 | **4.778 s** `[4.752 4.767 4.778 4.799 4.786]` | **4.547 s** `[4.546 4.547 4.543 4.556 4.555]` | **−0.231 s (−4.8%)**, ranges disjoint |
| worker RSS after load | 18.19 GiB | **6.87 GiB** | −11.3 GiB: the host copies are gone |
| placed at load | — | 11.19 GiB (29/36 + 22/27 + 2/3 layers) | = 53/66 |
| VRAM peak during requests | 36447 MiB | 36485 MiB | +38 MiB |
| output PNG md5 | `1db98827…` | `1db98827…` | **bitwise identical** |

The −0.231 s is the per-request transfer it removes: 11.19 GiB at this card's
~48 GB/s host-to-device is ~0.23 s. The peak is unchanged because the DiT is
resident in both runs, so the text encoder's set sits on top of the same
footprint either way -- on a card where the sum fits, `permanent` costs nothing
in peak. `nvidia-smi` cannot show the `forward` release at all: the caching
allocator keeps the freed blocks reserved, which is why "VRAM after load" reads
the same in both modes (36437 vs 36473 MiB) and why host RSS, not `nvidia-smi`,
is the number that moves.

Run again in the opposite order (`permanent` first, then `forward`, each a
fresh server) to rule out order effects: `permanent` p50 **4.547 s**
`[4.545 4.545 4.547 4.554 4.549]`, `forward` p50 **4.785 s**
`[4.789 4.785 4.789 4.764 4.772]`, Δ −0.238 s (−5.0%); RSS 6.87 vs 18.12 GiB;
the same md5 from all four servers. Across both orders every one of the ten
`permanent` samples is below every one of the ten `forward` samples (max 4.556 s
vs min 4.752 s). The one thing order did move was the first request of the
first server on the box (6.9 s vs ~4.6-4.8 s everywhere else): a cold page cache
on a freshly downloaded checkpoint, not a lifetime effect, so it is not claimed
above.

## CI guard

`wan2_1_t2v_1.3b_encoder_permanent_residents` (1 GPU): the existing 1.3B case
with `--layerwise-resident-layers text_encoder=0.8
--layerwise-residency-lifetime text_encoder=permanent`. Baseline seeded by CI on
the H100 pool (`b2fefd5822`):

| | streamed sibling `wan2_1_t2v_1.3b` | this case |
|---|---|---|
| TextEncodingStage | 534.89 ms | **171.56 ms** |
| load_peak_vram | 7814 MiB | **17792 MiB** |
| avg denoise step | 148 ms | 148 ms |

The guard is the stage: with the set on the device the stage is compute plus the
streamed 20%; if the lifetime ever regresses to per-request transfer, the stage
lands near the sibling's 535 ms, 3.1× this baseline, against a
`non_denoise_stage` tolerance of 1.8×. `load_peak_vram` carrying the set pins
that placement happens at load. Removing the transfer from the measured stage
also makes this case less sensitive to runner disk speed than its `forward`
siblings.

CI's first run of the seeded case reproduced the baseline (`load_peak_vram`
17792 MiB to the MiB) and failed only on the consistency check: no ground truth
exists under the new case id. The case now sets `run_consistency_check=False`
(`bd8caa64d6`): the lifetime moves weights, not math, the output is the base case's,
`wan2_1_t2v_1.3b` already guards it, and the H200 runs above showed it bitwise
identical across both lifetimes. A GT copy under a second name would turn this
into a ci-data revision bump for the whole suite.

## Not in this PR

- Making the planner choose `permanent` when the sum fits (#37917 / #37918).
- Loading permanent layers straight from the checkpoint to the device; they
  still pass through host memory once at load, as every layer does today.
- `_h2d_bytes_a_pin_would_save` ranks components for the pin budget by whole
  module bytes; permanent layers never move, so it slightly over-ranks a
  component that has them. A priority heuristic, not a correctness issue.
- MPS: the path is symmetric with CUDA but was not run here.
- Warning when a `component=value` map names a component the pipeline does
  not have. Today `--layerwise-resident-layers dit=4` is silently ignored
  (the maps take `transformer`, not the group alias); the CLI reference now
  says so, but a startup warning from the module-level configure, which sees
  every component, would catch it at the source. Separate change.

## Relationship to the merged PRs

#40590 (`release_after_use` / `release_all` split) and #40592 (`retain_resident_layers`)
change what `finish_use` calls; this PR puts its invariant one level lower, in
`release_layer`, so it composes with both unchanged. #40593 rewrote the same two
help strings and the readiness-log line; the merge keeps its user vocabulary and
adds the lifetime on top, and the log now names the lifetime (`(forward)` /
`(permanent)`) where #40593 wrote `(per request)`.

Churn: existing production files +220/−25 over 3 files (`layerwise_offload.py`
+122/−10, `server_args.py` +91/−15, `layerwise_offload_components.py` +7); new
production files 0; tests +308/−1; docs +10/−6.

title: [Refactor] Read parallel placement in consumers
body:
## Motivation

Parallel ranks, sizes, and groups already belong to the published runtime context, but consumers still receive copies through launchers and intermediate helpers. Resolve the current placement in the consumer to remove redundant arguments and avoid stale values when the active parallel scope changes.

## Modifications

- Remove redundant parallel arguments from scheduler initialization, derived-rank launcher plumbing, PD queues, embedding cache, model/runner helpers, and metrics components. Remove unused rank fields and the corresponding call-site arguments.
- Read DynamicChunkSizer's PP/WORLD groups in `profile_and_fit()`. Read prefill-delayer widths, all MLP-sync dimensions and its TP group, CUDA-graph trace rank, and remote-weight-transporter rank in their consumers; the transporter retains its construction-time rank for later registration.
- Keep the spawn boundary explicit: `run_scheduler_process` and Ray actors need TP/PP/DP placement before `publish()`. Preserve runner-owned placement across draft scopes and explicit inputs used to describe other nodes or hypothetical layouts. EPLB recovery keeps its explicit rank because post-scale rebalance supplies a global rank including the join offset.
- Retain two focused regressions for multi-node rank ranges and logits reassembly under an active TP override. Update existing consumer tests for the simplified signatures.

## Accuracy Tests

Current base: main `91c329cc866957a4750a929d158978a3ac69f45d`, which includes [#40707](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40707). This PR contains one commit. `git range-diff` confirms the patch is unchanged from `77d4827a4e`; pre-commit passes on the rebased diff. Runtime tests were not repeated for this history-only rebase.

Before #40707 merged, its encoder fix at `be149425e8` passed **210 tests and 149 subtests** across runtime context, layernorm SP, and parallel state, plus a four-process Gloo reproduction using the actual Qwen3 vision MLP at TP=4/CP=2.

Previous focused unit validation at stacked head `daa3485135a8e653b6eb7b51c253eae703883f9a`: **246 passed, 153 subtests passed**. The eight files cover runtime context, runtime overrides, parallel-state groups, layernorm SP, scheduler DP attention, PP/CP rank offsets, parallel consumers, and draft per-runner configuration.

The broader unit and serving-smoke results below were collected before the latest rebase; GPU serving smoke tests were not repeated for this rebase.

- Focused existing unit suites plus the two retained regressions: **394 passed, 2 skipped**, with 159 passing subtests. Coverage includes runtime context/draft scopes, parallel groups, launch/rank ranges, DP scheduling, metrics, embedding cache, graph buffers, and trace export.
- Two-H200 serving smoke tests with Qwen3-0.6B dummy weights, token-oracle sampling, KV canary, metrics, and NCCL prewarm: **TP=2, PP=2, attention-DP=2 with TP LM-head all-to-all, ordinary DP=2, PP=2 with dynamic chunking, and attention-DP=2 with prefill delayer**. Each completed four requests. Both PP stages fitted the dynamic-chunk predictor.
- The dynamic-chunk smoke used `--chunked-prefill-size 512 --context-length 1024 --max-running-requests 768`: profiling emits up to 640 tokens, so the canary needs more than the 512-entry capacity of the smaller launch. Canary checks remained enabled.
- Follow-up verification for the remaining MLP-sync arguments: **36 unit tests passed**, and two-GPU **attention-DP with Gloo** and **attention-DP with NCCL (overlap disabled)** smoke tests each completed four requests.
- An additional attention-CP=2 mock/canary smoke hit a `SimplePhaseChecker` device assertion (`caller_tag=4 expect=3 actual=1`). The same failure reproduces on upstream main at `2261c2e6188a4a8e11f077eee7bd0edbbdc738a1`; it is outside this mechanical refactor and is not counted as a passing smoke test.
- The [LTX-2 encoder component-accuracy CI failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662705674/job/106543345637?pr=40638) was reproduced on the earlier main base: encoder TP folding leaves a stale attention TP group in the runtime context. The fix landed separately in [#40646](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40646) and is included in the current main base.
- Pre-commit and stale-call-site checks pass.

Real-weight model accuracy and a live Ray cluster were not exercised.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance claim; no dedicated throughput benchmark. This changes configuration plumbing rather than kernels.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit formatting and static checks pass.
- [x] Focused unit coverage and existing consumer tests run.
- [x] Follow the repository's code style.
- [ ] Full model accuracy and speed benchmarks (not run).

title: [Lint] Reject methods shadowed by a later def in the same class
body:
## Motivation

Python binds the last definition in a class body, so an earlier method with the same name never runs. It is usually a merge artifact — two branches each add the method, both land, and the survivor silently drops whatever the other one did. Nothing flags it, and the dead copy still reads as live code.

`HybridAttnBackend.forward` is what motivated this. #20812 proposed reverting #19369 in March 2026 precisely because it left a duplicate `forward`, that revert was auto-closed after 158 days, #32541 later added a third variant, and #34303 tried again in August and was closed unreviewed. Six months, three attempts, and it is still on `main` — @haosenwang1018 is fixing that one in #40840, so this PR excludes the file rather than duplicating the work.

It also does not stay fixed. Scanning a week apart, `UnifiedMambaTokenToKVPoolAllocator.clear` had been repaired and `HybridLinearAttnBackend.get_indexer_metadata` had appeared. That is what makes this a gate rather than a one-off cleanup.

## Modifications

`scripts/lint/check_no_shadowed_defs.py`, wired into pre-commit next to the other AST checks. Only same-class collisions count, so a nested class keeps its own namespace. `@overload`, property accessors and `functools.singledispatch` registrations legitimately repeat a name and are skipped — matched on the decorator's exact attribute, so an unrelated `@register_custom_op(...)` does not exempt a method.

Removed the five shadowed definitions it finds. All are unreachable today, so behaviour is unchanged:

| class | method |
|---|---|
| `HybridLinearAttnBackend` | `get_indexer_metadata` |
| `DeepseekV4ForCausalLMDSpark` | `shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason` |
| `Gemma4ForCausalLM` | `get_embed_and_head` |
| `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration` | `get_embed_and_head` |
| `TestSeparateReasoningExecution` | `tearDown` |

The first four keep the definition Python already bound, byte for byte — `ast.unparse` of the surviving def equals `ast.unparse` of the last def on `main`. The two `tearDown` bodies are the same three statements written twice, so that one keeps the documented copy rather than the terser one.

## Two things worth a maintainer's eye

**The dspark one had an NPU guard that was never running.** The shadowed copy returned a disable reason under `_is_npu`, saying ModelSlim weight loading cannot map shared experts into fused expert slots. The bound copy has no such branch, so on NPU that fusion is currently *not* disabled. Restoring it is a behaviour change, so it is not in this PR — but if that guard was meant to be live, it needs its own fix.

**A test is not testing what it names.** In `test_scripted_runtime_core.py`, `test_get_all_node_lock_refs_held_during_run_released_after` and `test_lock_refs_held_during_run_released_after` both call `self._script_lock_refs_held_then_released`, and that name is defined twice. The first script — the one that exercises `get_all_node_lock_refs()` — is the shadowed one, so it never runs and both tests execute the same script. Fixing that means renaming rather than deleting, and confirming it needs a GPU run, so I left the file excluded and flagged it here instead.

## Exclusions

Three pre-existing offenders are excluded, each with a note in the config so they are easy to retire:

- `qwen3_5_text.py` — being fixed in #38096
- `hybrid_attn_backend.py` — fixed separately in #40840; drop this line once that lands
- `test_scripted_runtime_core.py` — the coverage gap described above

## Test Plan

`scripts/lint/test_check_no_shadowed_defs.py`, 12 cases: shadowing detected for sync and async methods, every extra definition reported, and no false positives for a single def, same name in sibling classes, same name in a nested class, property setters, `typing.overload` stubs, module-level redefinition, or an unparsable file. The existing `check-lint-script-tests` hook picks it up automatically.

```
$ pre-commit run check-no-shadowed-defs --all-files
reject methods shadowed by a later def in the same class...............Passed

$ pre-commit run check-lint-script-tests --all-files
unit tests for lint checkers...........................................Passed
```

Full pre-commit chain is green on every changed file. Verified on macOS/arm64, Python 3.12; nothing here needs a GPU.
