title: [deepep_v2] support GLM-5.3-Flash (Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration)
body:
## Motivation

`--moe-a2a-backend deepep_v2` cannot be used with GLM-5.3-Flash
(`Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`). There are two independent blockers.

**1. The architecture is not registered as v2-eligible.**
`moe_model_registry._DEEPEP_V2_MODELS` does not list it, so
`validate_deepep_v2_model_architecture()` rejects the server args before the
engine starts.

**2. `glm5_next.py` gates the a2a path on a v1-only predicate.**
`MoeA2ABackend.is_deepep()` is true only for `deepep`, not for `deepep_v2`, so
even past the first gate the model silently runs the non-a2a path:

`Glm5NextModel.__init__` computes
`enable_a2a_moe = is_deepep() or is_mooncake()`, which stays `False` under v2,
so the MoE layers never route through the dispatcher.

`deepseek_v2.py` — an already-validated v2 model — includes `is_deepep_v2()` in
that predicate. This change mirrors it.

> **Edit after review:** the first version of this PR also touched the
> `gemm_output_zero_allocator` sizing predicate and the
> shared-experts-fusion rejection reason. @mmangkad correctly pointed out that
> neither does anything here, and both are reverted as of 442125ed — see the
> Modifications section below.

## Modifications

Two lines, both load-bearing:

- `configs/moe_model_registry.py`: add `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` to
  `_DEEPEP_V2_MODELS` (`silu_mul_keep_fp32=False`, same as the other entries).
- `models/glm5_next.py`: include `is_deepep_v2()` in `enable_a2a_moe`.

Reverted after review (442125ed), both no-ops:

- the `is_a2a_moe` sizing predicate. Its enclosing block is gated on
  `_use_aiter_gfx95 and config.n_routed_experts == 256 and
  self.embed_tokens.embedding_dim == 7168`. Beyond being AMD gfx95 only,
  GLM-5.3-Flash is 288 routed experts with `hidden_size` 4096, so the block is
  unreachable for this architecture on any device.
- the `is_deepep_class_backend()` switch in
  `shared_experts_fusion_disable_reason`, plus its import. The
  `get_parallel().moe_ep_size > 1` check immediately above already returns for
  every DeepEP-family configuration.

## Accuracy Test

Hardware: 2x `p5.48xlarge` (8x H100 80GB, EFAv2), model GLM-5.3-Flash,
`--moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`, `deepep_v2_mode=direct`.

Both arms reach `The server is fired up and ready to roll!` and produce
correct output; before this change the server either fails server-arg
validation or runs without the dispatcher.

**TP=8 / EP=8, 1P1D PD-disaggregated (Mooncake over EFA):** PD warmup
completes; 7/7 requests correct, zero KV-transfer errors on either side.

**TP=16 / EP=16 across both nodes** (so dispatch/combine genuinely crosses the
network, not just NVLink):

```
$ curl .../v1/chat/completions -d '{... "用中文写三句话介绍长江..." , "temperature":0}'
长江是中国第一长河，全长约6300公里，也是亚洲第一、世界第三长河。它发源于青藏高原的唐古拉山脉，
自西向东流经11个省级行政区，最终在上海注入东海。长江流域物产丰富、经济发达，孕育了灿烂的中华文明，
被誉为中华民族的母亲河。
```

- 8 concurrent arithmetic prompts (`N * 13` for N in 3,5,7,9,11,13,17,19):
  8/8 exact.
- 4424-token prompt (3 chunks at
  `SGLANG_DEEPEP_V2_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=2048`): correct summary.
- zero errors/asserts in either node's log.

## Benchmark & Profiling

Not included — this change is about functional enablement, and the runs above
were correctness-focused. Happy to add throughput numbers if useful.

## Notes for other EFA users (deployment, not part of this change)

DeepEP v2's `ElasticBuffer` asserts on a non-NONE NCCL GIN
(`csrc/kernels/backend/nccl.cu`) even when EP fits inside a single NVLink
domain. On H100 + EFAv2 there is no GDAKI, so the aws-ofi-nccl GIN plugin
(self-reported type 5) is unusable and `NCCL_GIN_TYPE=2` (PROXY, layered over
aws-ofi-nccl via `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN`) is the only working setting. Separately,
`deep_ep/__init__.py:check_nccl_so()` matches the bare substring `libnccl`
against `/proc/self/maps`, so pointing `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN` at
`libnccl-net-ofi.so` trips its "Duplicate NCCL runtime" assert; a copy under a
name not containing `libnccl` avoids it.

- [x] Update documentation as needed, or state why it is unnecessary.

title: [Hisparse] fix: account for MiniMax HiSparse full-pool memory
body:
## Motivation

MiniMax HiSparse allocates dense KV and index caches at `size * host_to_device_ratio`, while sparse main KV stays at `size`. The memory estimator currently budgets all three at `size`, so automatic token capacity can exceed available GPU memory and fail during cache initialization. This fixes the capacity accounting introduced by #31446.

## Modifications

Apply the HiSparse ratio to dense layers and index-cache bytes when computing the MiniMax per-slot cost. Sparse main KV keeps its original cost; disabling HiSparse or using ratio 1 preserves the existing estimate.

For a 3-dense/57-sparse layout with one KV head per rank, 128-dimensional bf16 main/index caches and K-only index layers, ratio 2 changes the estimate from 45,312 to 61,440 bytes per slot.

## Validation

- All applicable pre-commit checks passed.
- Ran 648 local arithmetic/layout checks against the changed calculation, covering ratios 1/2/4, dense/sparse layer counts, KV heads, element sizes, and K-only/mixed/KV index layers. No test files added.
- Prior H200 A/B E2E on the original #31446 review head (`d0fb09af10ad36fc9b2458e6672f710bae387e9a`), with an equivalent formula fix: at `mem_fraction_static=0.80` and ratio 2, automatic capacity dropped from 2,629,667 to 1,939,380 slots. The original failed with CUDA OOM during index K allocation; the corrected budget completed startup, decode CUDA graph capture, and six HTTP generation requests (short, longer than the working set, and concurrent).
- That E2E used a small random-weight M3 fixture preserving the 60-layer KV layout, not the full pretrained model. GPU E2E has not been rerun on this main-based branch.

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward or kernel changes. The earlier E2E checked execution and output lengths, not numerical accuracy.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run; the change only affects startup capacity estimation.

Also fix large CP prefill batches entering the sparse prefill path through the query-count heuristic, despite its environment switch being disabled. That path builds global query offsets against CP-local buffers, which can cause out-of-bounds writes. Route active CP batches through paged attention and validate sparse metadata buffer capacity before launching kernels. ## Validation - Passed 8 isolated CPU regression checks covering configuration eligibility, capture buckets, replay buffer stability, output gathering, metadata lengths, and sparse prefill routing and bounds checks. - Passed Python syntax and diff whitespace checks. - Observed successful GPU graph capture and small-request replay before the final sparse prefill routing fix. title: Resolve HF LoRA targets through model-aware normalization
body:
Allow `--lora-target-modules` to carry full HF paths and normalize them after the base model is available. Replace the fixed CLI leaf-name list with validation of normalized runtime buffer types.

Use the same model-aware normalizer for engine initialization, adapter loading, and memory-pool compatibility. Inkling derives its target names from the existing tensor-loader mappings; GDN split projection aliases map to `in_proj_qkvz`, matching the existing tensor loader. Normalize each adapter’s target set once instead of repeating the work for every tensor.

For automatic Qwen MoE backend selection on SM100, use Triton when BF16 LoRA is enabled: the fused TRT-LLM path cannot inject expert LoRA deltas. Explicit backend choices are unchanged. Tensor packing is unchanged.

Accumulate virtual-expert LoRA shrink split-K atomic additions in FP32, then cast once before expansion. On the full GPT-OSS-20B service, six repeated identical single-token requests had logprob span 0.573 before and 0 after this change; two additional prompt sizes also had zero repeat span. Stable differences across batch shapes remain; this is not a general determinism guarantee. Performance has not been benchmarked.

Dependency for radixark/miles#3318 and radixark/miles#3584.

Validation:
- Changed-file pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.
- The Inkling cleanup was checked by executing the source-extracted normalization functions: 128 before/after cases match, and two mapping-extension cases confirm that target selection follows the loader tables. No permanent test file was added.

title: [AMD] Add diffusion (Wan2.2) extras to gfx1151 Docker image
body:
## Motivation

`docker/rocm-gfx1151.Dockerfile` (added in #33939, "[AMD] Add gfx1151 (Strix Halo / Ryzen AI MAX+) Docker image") only installs the `runtime_base`, `runtime_common`, and `srt_hip` pyproject extras. It never installs `diffusion_common` / `diffusion_hip`, so any image built from it is missing `diffusers`, `imageio`, `cache_dit`, `accelerate`, etc. `sglang generate` (Wan2.2 / `multimodal_gen`) fails immediately with `ModuleNotFoundError` on that image — reproduced live inside a gfx1151 container built from this Dockerfile, then fixed step by step with `pip install` before porting the fix back here.

Separately, `diffusers.loaders.peft` needs `accelerate` at import time (triggered via `cache_dit`'s patch functors, which `sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/cache/__init__.py` imports unconditionally), but `accelerate` was missing from the `diffusion_common` extras group in `pyproject_other.toml`. This affects every platform's diffusion install (CUDA and CDNA too), not just gfx1151.

## Modifications

- `python/pyproject_other.toml`: add `accelerate` to the `diffusion_common` extras group.
- `docker/rocm-gfx1151.Dockerfile`: install `diffusion_common`, plus the pure-Python subset of `diffusion_hip` (`cache-dit`, `peft`, `runai_model_streamer`). `st_attn` and `vsa` are deliberately left out — they're prebuilt CUDA-oriented wheels (`manylinux2014_x86_64`, no ROCm tag) of unverified gfx1151 compatibility, so this follows the same posture the file already takes with aiter's compiled CDNA kernels (`SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`).

title: [Fix] Keep Inkling automatic tool grammar active across the response
body:
## Motivation

With reasoning enabled, `ReasonerGrammarObject` defers constraints until the encoded reasoning-end marker is observed. Inkling emits the native `END_MESSAGE` token (`200010`), while encoding its printed spelling as ordinary text produces a different token sequence. The wrapper can therefore remain in its reasoning phase and never apply the automatic tool-call grammar, even after a thinking or text block.

For example, this synthetic token stream leaves the outer JSON object open (the marker spellings below represent native framing tokens):

```text
<|message_model|><|content_invoke_tool_json|>{"name":"tool","args":{}
```

Previously, both native `END_MESSAGE` and `CONTENT_MODEL_END_SAMPLING` remained allowed at this point. With this change, both are masked until the JSON is complete; adding the missing `}` permits the tool block to close and the response to terminate.

## Modifications

- In non-strict mode, return the canonical Inkling automatic tool grammar directly so it sees the entire response. This schema permits reasoning and ordinary text outside native tool triggers and owns the tool payload's boundaries.
- Identify that exception by comparing the complete decoded schema with the existing canonical builder. Matching only `token_triggered_tags` would be too broad: modified schemas can require a tag, exclude a reasoning terminator, or trigger on ordinary text. Those schemas retain reasoning deferral, as do other answer constraints.
- Resolve the scheduler's reasoning-end IDs through the reasoning detector, using Inkling's native ID and preserving the existing tokenizer encoding for other detectors. Ordinary text tokenization is unchanged.
- Add real XGrammar mask regressions for direct, thinking-prefixed, and text-prefixed tool calls; incomplete and complete JSON; plain text and literal marker strings; and modified schemas. Preserve strict-thinking behavior, the `full_assistant_ebnf` bypass, and the existing CPU CI registrations; use `CustomTestCase` for the registered test file.

This change covers the canonical automatic tool schema in non-strict mode and native reasoning-end ID resolution. It does not change required/named tool schemas or claim to fix the separate no-thinking `reasoning_tokens` overcount tracked in #34634.

## Accuracy Tests

Revalidated on PR head `01b8d93ebd6b3341a0f64f892886c2187eef0e76` (including upstream `367e3700cfb6a0b03b2fa41a4524febf18ec1f15`) on 2026-09-22, using Python 3.13.13, PyTorch 2.13.0, and XGrammar 0.2.1 on macOS/Apple Silicon. These are CPU component tests with a synthetic vocabulary; no model weights or serving process were used.

**Before:** on upstream `791c7850d0960fd768102f71e7d999b036bb75ba`, with only the new test file applied, this selection reported four failures: the three reasoning-enabled tool-mask subcases allow premature termination, and scheduler initialization returns the printed marker's token sequence instead of native ID `200010`.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/constrained/test_reasoner_grammar_backend.py \
  -k 'inkling_tool_masks_cover_the_whole_stream or inkling_scheduler_uses_native_reasoning_end' \
  -q --disable-warnings --tb=short
```

**After:** all **183 tests and 114 subtests pass** across the three suites, including those regressions:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/constrained/test_reasoner_grammar_backend.py \
  test/registered/unit/parser/test_reasoning_parser.py \
  test/registered/unit/parser/test_inkling_renderer.py \
  -q --disable-warnings --tb=short
```

The direct-file CI entry point also passes **34 tests** with fail-fast enabled:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python \
  test/registered/unit/constrained/test_reasoner_grammar_backend.py -f
```

All applicable pre-commit checks pass, including formatting, lint, syntax, and test registration:

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  python/sglang/srt/constrained/reasoner_grammar_backend.py \
  python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py \
  python/sglang/srt/parser/reasoning_parser.py \
  test/registered/unit/constrained/test_reasoner_grammar_backend.py
```

GPU execution, live serving, full-model generation, and end-to-end accuracy evaluations were not run.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run. Schema comparison occurs during grammar dispatch; the canonical grammar now also applies its masks during the reasoning prefix. No throughput, latency, or profiling results are claimed.

- [x] Add focused regression tests using the public CPU test conventions and verify failure before the fix.

title: [AMD] Make host Mamba cache size configurable for Qwen3.5 on gfx950
body:
## Motivation

Qwen3.5 sizes its host Mamba pool with the same ratio as KV. Under high concurrency, this can evict reusable Mamba state while CPU memory is still available. Later turns then repeat prefill work. This PR adds a separate host Mamba capacity setting so it can retain more state without enlarging the KV pool.

## Modifications

- Add `--hicache-mamba-size`, in decimal GB per rank. Default `0` preserves existing sizing.
- Put the initial `gfx950 + Qwen3.5` restriction in a separate helper so the model gate can be relaxed later.
- Require HiCache in `cache` mode and an explicit `--hicache-ratio`. The override applies only to `MambaPoolHost`; automatic sizing and a nonzero `--hicache-size` are rejected.
- Add configuration and allocation tests, plus the parameter documentation.

For a selected high-concurrency deployment, add `--hicache-mamba-size 104` alongside `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 1.5`. 

## Accuracy Tests

TBD.

## Benchmark

`amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2` (revision `e17e5f0`), MI355X TP2/EP1, C32, HiCache. Both configurations used 10 warmup requests per lane and a full 3600-second AgentX window on the same GPU pair.

The baseline used `--hicache-ratio 1.5`. The candidate increased only host Mamba capacity from 33.46 to 104.04 GB/rank after slot rounding. Host KV and GPU KV/Mamba capacities were unchanged; total host HiCache allocation was 227.44 → 368.60 GB within the original 599 GB budget.

title: Fix NIXL transfer of MXFP8 KV block scales
body:
## Motivation

Prefill/decode disaggregation with NIXL rejects MXFP8 KV caches when transferring their block scales:

```
PD Disaggregation via NIXL does NOT support StateType.BLOCK_SCALE hybrid models yet.
```

The block-scale buffers and page indices are already exposed through the disaggregation state interface, but NIXL's extra-state dispatch does not handle their state types.

## Modifications

Route `StateType.BLOCK_SCALE` and `StateType.BLOCK_SCALE_SWA` through the existing page-indexed KV transfer path, matching the Mooncake connector. This transfers scales for full-attention and sliding-window KV caches and retains the existing equal-attention-TP and index-length checks.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated the equivalent patch in a downstream integration with MXFP8 target KV, FP8 draft KV, and prefill HiCache:

- Inkling-Small NVFP4 with DSpark: 52 successful requests.
- Inkling NVFP4 with DFlash: 52 successful requests.
- Each run included known-answer chat requests, a streamed response, and 48 long-prompt generations at concurrency 16 across cold/warm rounds (approximately 33K–36K prompt tokens).

These are integration smoke tests, not an accuracy benchmark or an end-to-end run of this upstream checkout. The downstream runs also included launcher and network configuration fixes.

Re-ran the downstream block-scale transfer regression: 1 test and 6 subtests passed, covering both state types, source/destination transfer descriptors, mismatched TP, and mismatched index lengths. No test file is added in this minimal dispatch fix.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance comparison or profiling was performed. This enables a previously rejected transfer; it does not change the transfer algorithm.

title: [Diffusion] Sensenova bf16 rope npu main
body:
## Motivation

SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT applies RoPE to query and key tensors in every attention layer. Using an NPU fused operator reduces this work and improves end-to-end generation latency. RoPE table precomputation also needs to handle decoder layers wrapped by Cache-DiT; directly accessing `layers[0].self_attn` causes warmup to fail.

## Modifications

- Add a SenseNova RoPE path that calls `torch_npu.npu_rotary_mul` for query and key tensors using `rotary_mode="half"`.
- Enable it with `SGLANG_SENSENOVA_NPU_FUSED_ROPE=rotary_mul`. The default remains the original implementation, which is also used when the fused path’s conditions are not met.
- Resolve the attention module inside a Cache-DiT wrapper before precomputing shared RoPE tables, and add a unit test for this case.
- Merge the existing `sensenova-release` history into a branch based on the updated `upstream/main`. The resulting PR diff includes earlier SenseNova changes from that branch.

## Accuracy Tests

- Python syntax checks and `pre-commit` passed.
- A unit test was added for the Cache-DiT wrapper case. Local pytest stopped during test collection because `orjson` is missing from the environment.
- **Pending:** Compare generated outputs and numerical error between the original and fused RoPE paths on the target NPU.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

End-to-end measurements for SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT with Cache-DiT enabled:

| RoPE path | Test configuration 1 | Test configuration 4 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Original | 299.6 s | 299.7 s |
| `npu_rotary_mul` | 280.09 s | 279.93 s |
| Latency reduction | ~6.5% | ~6.6% |

Cache-DiT settings: `FN=4`, `BN=2`, `WARMUP=8`, `RDT=0.10`, and `MC=1`.

**Pending:** Add an NPU profiler trace to confirm fused operator calls and operator-level latency.

title: [AMD] Support DeepSeek-V4.1 on gfx950 with DSpark and fused kernels
body:
## Motivation

Run DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on AMD gfx950 with HIP attention, quantization, MoE and DSpark paths. This continues the AMD work from #39186 on a branch targeting `main`.

**Dependency stack:** main now includes the compression/KV metadata extraction (#39652). This branch still carries the remaining V4.1 prerequisites from `dsv4.1`, including #38798 and #39666, which are open. Those shared model, vision/chat, CUDA and Engram changes explain the larger main-relative diff. Keep this PR draft until those prerequisites land, then rebase to expose the AMD-only diff. They should not be reviewed as newly authored AMD ports.

## Modifications

- Add HIP low-ratio attention/indexing, KV stores, RoPE fusion and gfx950 dense/MoE kernels; preserve FP32 router output and deterministic reduction behavior where required.
- Port BF16 WO-A decode/verify, mHC split-H, and TP4 all-reduce/mHC fusion with shape/backend fallbacks.
- Integrate graph metadata, context-parallel ownership and DSpark device-side length preparation. Preserve main's legacy prefill graph path alongside V4.1.
- Preserve BF16 bits in sharded Engram reconstruction, including signed zero and subnormals.
- Keep performance-sensitive alternatives opt-in where model measurements were mixed or slower: Engram prefetch, shared-expert multistream, adaptive attention splits, compact KV, BF16x3 prefill and fused WO-A MXFP8 quantization. Bounded replay remains opt-in and follows upstream's approximate numerical contract.
- Retain the AITER synchronization and BF16 SiLU patches plus EP4 tuning CSV. Synchronization and tuning upstream drafts: ROCm/aiter#5561 and ROCm/aiter#5562. Remove downstream copies when the pinned AITER incorporates them.
- Clean comments and docstrings without changing executable model/kernel behavior. No workflow changes or benchmark artifacts are included. Outside runtime/tests, the diff contains four Docker/AITER files and two documentation changes inherited from the prerequisite stack.

## Accuracy Tests

On MI350X, ROCm 7.2.4, with isolated patched AITER:

- Publication revision `f5cd9c791c`: AMD, main prefill-graph, DP scheduling and model-guard suite **203 passed, 40 skipped, 302 subtests**. All-files pre-commit passed.
- At `0171bde4f2`: 203 tests and 302 subtests passed, 40 skipped. Focused quantization/KV/C2/WO-A tests passed on all eight GPUs. Eight-rank entrypoints passed: DSpark 36 tests/36 NVLink-only skips, Engram 5 tests, all-reduce/mHC 35 tests (rank-zero report counts, all ranks exited successfully).
- Four-GPU TP4/EP4 serving smoke and five-shot GSM8K, all 1,319 questions: DSpark off **1,193 correct (90.45%)**, on **1,190 correct (90.22%)**, zero invalid answers in both.

Serving used `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, FP8 KV, page size 256, radix cache disabled, shared-expert fusion disabled, DSpark block size 5. Environment: `TRITON_HIP_USE_ASYNC_COPY=0`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, `SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0`, `ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=NONE`, `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0`.

DSpark-off serving was measured at `629d905531`; DSpark-on at `0171bde4f2` after a raw-verification metadata argument fix. Model/kernel executable ASTs/tokens remain equivalent on the publication branch; the fresh regression results above supplement those serving runs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Four MI350X GPUs, TP4/EP4, 4,096 input / 1,024 output tokens, `ignore_eos`, six timed runs after a discarded warm-up. Median output tokens/s from first to last streamed event, cache flushed per run. **Real DSpark acceptance; no acceptance simulation.**

| Workload | Batch | DSpark off | DSpark on | On/off |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Random token IDs | 1 | 155.73 | 641.88 | 4.12x |
| Real text | 1 | 155.88 | 335.11 | 2.15x |
| Real text | 8 | 951.67 | 1,446.53 | 1.52x |
| Real text | 32 | 2,182.16 | 2,241.87 | 1.03x |

These are overall DSpark benefits, not incremental gains attributable to this PR. Random-input DSpark throughput was unchanged across the rebase: 641.89 → 641.88 tokens/s. Real-text changes versus the prior revision were +2.64%, +2.65%, and −1.15%, with acceptance lengths also changing. One launch per mode; this is not an interleaved noise-controlled comparison.

The random prompt is reconstructed at seed 42; the original blog `prompt.json` was unavailable. The original PR's 548–556 tokens/s used simulated acceptance fixed at 5.5 and is **not directly comparable** to these real-acceptance measurements.

Not executed: CUDA or ROCm 10 validation, a fresh Docker build, and full-model CP/EAGLE configurations blocked by existing guards. title: [Bugfix] Make top-k/top-p filtering consistent across sampling paths
body:
## Motivation

SGLang normally computes the top-p cutoff from the original probability distribution and intersects that support with top-k. Some sampling paths instead applied top-k, renormalized the remaining probabilities, and then applied top-p. That applies top-p to whatever probability mass happens to remain after top-k, making its effect unpredictable and inconsistent with other sampling paths using the same parameters.

The affected paths are the FlashInfer min-p path, the shared EAGLE-family/standalone/n-gram verifier, and the target-distribution builder shared by DFlash, DSpark, and UNO.

## Modifications

- Apply top-p before top-k in the FlashInfer min-p path.
- Apply the same ordering in the shared EAGLE-family, standalone, and n-gram verifier.
- Correct both the dense and sparse target distributions shared by DFlash, DSpark, and UNO.
- Preserve the sparse top-k path by translating the top-p cutoff into the renormalized top-k distribution using the top-k support's original probability mass.
- Reject `min_p > 0` for built-in speculative decoding, where it is not currently applied.
- Add focused CUDA regression tests for each corrected implementation.

## Accuracy Tests

The regressions use probabilities `[0.35, 0.25, 0.20, 0.05, 0.03, ...]`, `top_k=4`, and `top_p=0.82`.

The original top-p nucleus includes token 3 because the probability mass before it is `0.80`. Applying and renormalizing top-k first changes that mass to `0.80 / 0.85`, causing token 3 to be incorrectly removed.

- Baseline FlashInfer regression: failed with the expected support mismatch.
- Focused CUDA regressions: `4 passed` (FlashInfer, EAGLE, and both dense and sparse modes of the target-distribution builder shared by DFlash, DSpark, and UNO).
- All pre-commit checks pass on the rebased branch, and the upstream lint workflow passes.
- Full upstream GPU CI has not run because it requires the maintainer-controlled `run-ci` label.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No end-to-end benchmark has been run.

The FlashInfer and EAGLE changes reorder existing filtering operations. The corrected sparse DFlash/DSpark/UNO path adds a full-vocabulary `logsumexp` reduction to recover the original probability mass represented by its top-k support.

- [x] Format the code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [x] No documentation change is required.
- [ ] Provide speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: fix(attention): drop the shadowed HybridAttnBackend.forward
body:
> **Scope note (updated):** this PR originally also touched `hybrid_linear_attn_backend.py`. #38810 already covers that file plus `gemma4_causal.py` / `gemma4_mm.py` and adds a lint gate for the whole class of bug, so I dropped that hunk. What is left is the one shadowed definition #38810 does not touch.

## Motivation

`HybridAttnBackend` defines `forward` twice in the same class body. Python keeps the last definition, so the first one never runs:

| line | added by | body |
|---|---|---|
| 161 | `73d272bddb6` (2026-03-05) | accepts `mixed_qkv` / `a` / `b` and routes linear-attention calls to the child backend |
| 231 | `5b2e2750b55` (2026-03-04) | plain `q, k, v` delegation |

The two commits landed a day apart and each added its own `forward`. The plain one at line 231 wins, so a caller that passes `mixed_qkv=...` has it absorbed into `**kwargs` while the wrapper still forwards `q=None, k=None, v=None` to the child backend. The linear-attention support added at line 161 has never executed.

`ruff check --select=F811` flags it. That rule is not in this repo's pre-commit `--select` list; #38810 proposes a dedicated `scripts/lint/check_no_shadowed_defs.py` gate for exactly this, and its description calls `HybridAttnBackend.forward` "the clearest example" — but the file is not in its diff, so this definition survives either way.

I am aware of the history here (#20812 proposed reverting #19369 over this duplicate and was auto-closed; #32541 added a third variant; #34303 tried again in August and was closed unreviewed). If the preferred resolution is different from "keep the superset", say so and I will rework or close.

## Modifications

Delete the plain `forward` at line 231 and keep the one that handles linear attention.

To keep the diff behavior-preserving for the non-linear path, the surviving `forward` delegates with keyword arguments (`q=q, k=k, ...`), exactly as the definition that was live before this change did, instead of positionally.

The surviving definition is a strict superset of the deleted one, so the only behavior change is that `mixed_qkv` / `a` / `b` now reach the child backend instead of being dropped into `**kwargs` next to `q=None, k=None, v=None`.

No kernel or model forward math is changed. The change restores a branch that could not be reached.

title: [PD] Honor gracefully_exit in disaggregation event loops and keep non-zero-rank launchers alive on SIGTERM
body:
## Motivation

In PD disaggregation, graceful shutdown is driven by rank 0: the tokenizer manager drains in-flight requests and dispatches `ShutdownReq`, and the scheduler broadcasts it to every TP rank on every node, which sets `gracefully_exit` on each scheduler. Two gaps break that for PD deployments:

- The four disaggregation event loops (`event_loop_{normal,overlap}_disagg_{prefill,decode}`) never read `gracefully_exit`, unlike `event_loop_normal` / `event_loop_overlap`, so the schedulers keep looping after the broadcast until the tokenizer watchdog SIGKILLs them.
- A `node_rank >= 1` launcher has no SIGTERM handler. When the orchestrator signals every node at once, that launcher exits immediately and `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` SIGKILLs its own schedulers while rank 0 is still draining; the surviving ranks then crash inside `broadcast_pyobj` with gloo `Connection closed by peer`.

Fixing those exposes a third gap that the SIGQUIT path used to hide: a clean return from `block_until_scheduler_exits()` on `node_rank >= 1` fell through into `_setup_and_run_http_server` with `tokenizer_manager=None` and exited 1.

## Modifications

- `disaggregation/decode.py`, `disaggregation/prefill.py`: break out of each of the four disaggregation event loops on the iteration that sees `gracefully_exit`, the same check `event_loop_normal` / `event_loop_overlap` already make.
- `entrypoints/engine.py`: on `node_rank >= 1`, install a SIGTERM handler (main thread only) that logs and keeps `block_until_scheduler_exits()` running, so the node waits for the rank-0 `ShutdownReq` broadcast instead of exiting under its schedulers. The orchestrator's kill timeout is the backstop, which is the same unbounded-drain contract rank 0's `sigterm_watchdog` already has.
- `entrypoints/http_server.py`: `launch_server` returns right after `_launch_subprocesses` on `node_rank >= 1`, since that call already blocked until the schedulers exited.
- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_disagg_idle_step_counters.py`: `make_scheduler` now sets `gracefully_exit = False` for every loop fixture, since the disaggregation loops read it; the MLX case set it locally before.

Behavior change worth knowing: a SIGTERM delivered only to a non-zero-rank node now waits for the orchestrator's termination grace period instead of exiting right away.

Out of scope: `event_loop_pp*` and `event_loop_pdmux` still ignore `gracefully_exit`.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: no change to model forward or sampling.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

Verification:

- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_disagg_idle_step_counters.py` passes on this branch (12 tests, 51 subtests). Without the test-file change, `test_disagg_idle_gap` fails on the production hunks with `AttributeError: 'Scheduler' object has no attribute 'gracefully_exit'`.
- End to end on an internal two-node PD deployment (one prefill and one decode gang, TP16/EP16): when the orchestrator SIGTERMs every node, all schedulers on every node exit 0 through the rank-0 `ShutdownReq` broadcast within about 1 s of the drain finishing, a decode request in flight at the SIGTERM finishes before rank 0 exits, non-zero-rank launchers that receive SIGTERM before the broadcast log it and keep waiting, and no gloo `Connection closed by peer` tracebacks or exit-137 tasks remain. Before the change, the same stop produced the gloo crash on every surviving scheduler whenever the rank-0 node died first.

- `58173421a4`

title: fix(janus): rename the Normalize class shadowed by a same-named function
body:
## Motivation

`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_janus_pro.py` binds the name `Normalize` twice at module level:

```python
class Normalize(torch.nn.Module):                  # line 1096
    def __init__(self, mean, std, inplace=False): ...

def Normalize(in_channels, norm_type="group"):     # line 1793
    assert norm_type in ["group", "batch"]
    ...
```

The `def` wins, so the class is unreachable and its only call site cannot work:

```python
# CLIPVisionTower.__init__, line 1167
if pixel_mean is not None and pixel_std is not None:
    image_norm = Normalize(mean=pixel_mean, std=pixel_std)
```

Minimal repro of the same shape:

```
TypeError: Normalize() got an unexpected keyword argument 'mean'
```

`MultiModalityCausalLM.__init__` builds the vision tower straight from the checkpoint config:

```python
vision_config = config.vision_config
vision_cls = model_name_to_cls(vision_config.cls)
self.vision_model = vision_cls(**vision_config.params)
```

so a checkpoint whose `vision_config.params` carries `pixel_mean` / `pixel_std` — which the upstream Janus `CLIPVisionTower` accepts — fails at model load with that `TypeError`. The published Janus-Pro configs do not set those keys, so **this is latent rather than a live crash today**; I am not claiming a user-visible regression. What is certain is that the class has been dead since the collision was introduced, and nothing can use it while the name is taken.

Found by `ruff check --select=F811`, which is not in this repo's pre-commit `--select` list.

## Modifications

Rename the class to `ImageNormalize` and update its single call site. The five other `Normalize(...)` call sites in this file (VQ encoder / decoder, lines 1494, 1578, 1712, 1716, 1753) all want the `def` and are untouched.

Nothing outside this module imports either name — the only cross-module imports from this file are `DropPath` (`models/internvl.py`) and `MultiModalityCausalLM` (`multimodal/processors/janus_pro.py`).

`ruff check --select=F811,F821` is clean on the file after the change.

## Accuracy Tests

No math changes. The renamed class was not reachable before this PR, so nothing that runs today changes behavior.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

title: fix(logging): repair two logging calls whose message never reaches the log
body:
## Motivation

Two logging calls pass arguments the format string cannot consume. Python's `logging` interpolates with `msg % args` inside `LogRecord.getMessage()`, so both raise `TypeError: not all arguments converted during string formatting`, the handler prints `--- Logging error ---` plus a traceback to stderr, and **the intended message never appears**.

**1. `python/sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/quick_all_reduce.py:177`**

```python
logger.warning(
    "Custom quick allreduce:",                      # format string, no %-spec
    f"Invalid quantization level: {regime_str}. "   # ...but here is an argument
    "Supported levels: "
    f"{list(QuickReduceRegime.__members__.keys())}",
)
return
```

A user who sets an invalid `ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION` gets a logging traceback instead of the list of supported levels, and quick allreduce then silently stays off — exactly the case the warning exists for.

**2. `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/utils.py:64`**

```python
logger.debug("Function {} has already been called.", fn.__name__)
```

Brace placeholders are not interpolated by stdlib logging; the extra argument triggers the same `TypeError`.

Reproduced with plain stdlib logging:

```
>>> log.warning("Function {} has already been called.", "set_default_server_args")
--- Logging error ---
...
  File ".../logging/__init__.py", line 400, in getMessage
    msg = msg % self.args
TypeError: not all arguments converted during string formatting
Message: 'Function {} has already been called.'
Arguments: ('set_default_server_args',)
```

and after the fix:

```
>>> log.warning("Custom quick allreduce: Invalid quantization level: %s. Supported levels: %s", "FP8", ["NONE"])
WARNING:demo:Custom quick allreduce: Invalid quantization level: FP8. Supported levels: ['NONE']
```

## Modifications

- Rewrite both calls in the lazy `%s` form.
- Add `PLE1205,PLE1206` to the ruff `--select` list in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`. Those are the two rules that catch a logging format string and argument count that disagree, and they are what found these two. They are report-only (not auto-fixable), so the existing `--fix` behavior is unaffected.

The tree is clean for both rules after this change:

```
$ ruff check --select=PLE1205,PLE1206 benchmark docs examples python test sgl-model-gateway
All checks passed!
```

so turning the rules on does not add any new pre-commit failures.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable — log statements only.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests — the new `ruff` rules are the mechanical check and they run in pre-commit.

title: fix(rocm): restore the missing return in use_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_unrolledx4
body:
## Motivation

`use_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_unrolledx4` in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py` computes its predicate and then discards it:

```python
if _is_hip:

    def use_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_unrolledx4(M, N, META):
        # Use manually unrolledx4 kernel on AMD GPU when the grid size is small.
        # Empirical testing shows the sweet spot lies when it's less than the # of
        # compute units available on the device.
        num_workgroups = triton.cdiv(M, META["BLOCK_SIZE_M"]) * triton.cdiv(
            N, META["BLOCK_SIZE_N"]
        )
        num_workgroups <= get_device_core_count()      # <- no return

    def select_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_kernel(M, N, META):
        if use_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_unrolledx4(M, N, META):
            return _w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_unrolledx4
        else:
            return _w8a8_block_fp8_matmul
```

The helper always returns `None`, so the `if` is always false and `_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_unrolledx4` is never selected. On AMD GPUs the W8A8 block-FP8 Triton GEMM always runs the generic kernel, including in the small-grid regime the unrolled kernel was written for.

**Provenance.** #3306 (`[ROCm] Logic to decide whether to used manually unrolled kernel.`, 2025-02-04) added the heuristic inline and it worked:

```python
kernel = (
    _w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_unrolledx4
    if (is_hip_ == True and num_workgroups <= get_device_core_count())
    else _w8a8_block_fp8_matmul
)
```

#5993 (`[refactor] slightly tidy fp8 module`, 2025-05-07) moved that expression into the helper above and the `return` was lost in the move. The unrolled kernel has been dead on ROCm since then.

`ruff check --select=B015` reports it as *"Pointless comparison at end of function scope. Did you mean to return the expression result?"*. That rule is not in this repo's pre-commit `--select` list, which is why it has gone unnoticed.

## Modifications

One line: `return num_workgroups <= get_device_core_count()`.

This restores the exact predicate from #3306. `_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_unrolledx4` itself is unchanged and has been in the tree the whole time.

## Accuracy Tests

The two kernels compute the same GEMM; only the launch/unrolling differs, and `_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_unrolledx4` is the kernel #3306 validated. No math is changed by this PR.

I do not have an AMD GPU, so I cannot run the ROCm accuracy job myself. This one line does re-enable a code path that has been dormant for 17 months, so a ROCm reviewer's sign-off is worth having before merge — happy to hold for that.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This is the point of the change: on ROCm, small-grid W8A8 block-FP8 GEMMs (`num_workgroups <= device CU count`) should now use the unrolled kernel again, which is what #3306 measured as faster. I cannot produce the numbers without an AMD GPU; if someone on ROCm runs `benchmark/kernels/quantization/` before/after I will add the results here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests — one-line restore of a `return`; `ruff --select=B015` is the mechanical check.
- [ ] Update documentation — not applicable.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — needs ROCm hardware, see above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

---

title: fix(spec): accept pp_proxy_tensors in the UNO and frozen-KV-MTP workers
body:
Fixes #40155.

## Motivation

The scheduler's non-overlap speculative path always passes `pp_proxy_tensors`:

```python
# python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:4514 and :4527
batch_result = self.model_worker.forward_batch_generation(
    batch, pp_proxy_tensors=pp_proxy_tensors
)
```

Two spec-v2 workers do not declare the keyword, so any model served through them dies on the first scheduler step that takes that path:

```
TypeError: UnoWorkerV2.forward_batch_generation() got an unexpected keyword argument 'pp_proxy_tensors'
```

Audit of `python/sglang/srt/speculative/` on current `main` before this PR:

| worker | `pp_proxy_tensors` |
|---|---|
| `eagle_worker_v2.py` | yes |
| `dflash_worker_v2.py` | yes |
| `ngram_worker.py` | yes |
| `multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py` | yes — fixed inline in #29189 |
| `dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py` | yes — fixed after #39262 |
| `frozen_kv_mtp_worker_v2.py` | **no** |
| `uno_worker_v2.py` | **no** |

Root cause: `BaseSpecWorker` (`base_spec_worker.py`) is an ABC but never declares `forward_batch_generation`, so nothing holds the workers to the interface the scheduler calls through, and each one evolved its own signature.

## Modifications

**1. `frozen_kv_mtp_worker_v2.py`** — take `pp_proxy_tensors` and forward it on the target-prefill call.

**2. `uno_worker_v2.py`** — same, threaded through `_forward_prefill`.

Both follow the shape of the merged DSpark fix: the keyword is consumed only by `self.target_worker.forward_batch_generation` on the target prefill; the decode paths are untouched, exactly as in `dspark_worker_v2.py`.

**3. `base_spec_worker.py`** — declare `forward_batch_generation` as an `@abstractmethod` with the signature the scheduler uses, so the next divergence shows up at the class definition instead of at the first request.

All seven in-tree workers already define the method, so the abstract declaration changes nothing for them. `StandaloneWorkerV2` inherits `EAGLEWorkerV2`'s.

## Verification

Signature audit across every `forward_batch_generation` under `python/sglang/srt/speculative/` after the change:

```
OK   base_spec_worker.py                     BaseSpecWorker
OK   dflash_worker_v2.py                     DFlashWorkerV2
OK   dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py   DSparkWorkerV2
OK   eagle_worker_v2.py                      EAGLEWorkerV2
OK   frozen_kv_mtp_worker_v2.py              FrozenKVMTPWorkerV2
OK   multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2.py          MultiLayerEagleWorkerV2
OK   ngram_worker.py                         NGRAMWorker
OK   uno_worker_v2.py                        UnoWorkerV2
```

`ruff check --select=F401,F821` and `ruff format` are clean on the three changed files.

## Accuracy Tests

No math changes. The change is a keyword that was previously rejected and is now forwarded to the target worker, which is what the five other workers already do.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests — the abstract declaration is the durable guard proposed in #40155. If you would rather have a test that walks the workers and asserts the signature, say the word and I will add it under `test/registered/unit/`.
- [ ] Update documentation — not applicable.

title: fix(qwen3.5): apply the +1 aux-hidden-layer shift for DFLASH capture
body:
## Motivation

`Qwen3_5ForCausalLM.set_dflash_layers_to_capture` is defined twice in `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5_text.py`:

| line | added by | shift |
|---|---|---|
| 114 | #35758 `qwen 3.8 rebase` (2026-08-28) | `[layer_id + 1 for layer_id in layer_ids]` |
| 149 | #34771 `[Spec] Wire DFLASH aux-hidden capture into the Qwen3.5 text-only wrapper` (2026-08-14) | no shift |

Python keeps the last definition in the class body, so the one at line 149 is what runs and the one at line 114 is dead code. `ruff check --select=F811` flags it (that rule is not in this repo's pre-commit `--select` list).

**The live one is missing the `+1` shift.** The backbone sets the flag on the layer object:

```python
# qwen3_5.py
def set_dflash_layers_to_capture(self, layers_to_capture: list[int]):
    self.layers_to_capture = layers_to_capture
    for layer_id in self.layers_to_capture:
        setattr(self.layers[layer_id], "_is_layer_to_capture", True)
```

and the forward pass passes `captured_last_layer_outputs` to the flagged layer (`qwen3_5.py:1940`), so layer `i` captures the output of layer `i - 1`. Every other model wrapper in the tree shifts by one before calling the backbone:

- `llama.py:912` — `self.model.layers_to_capture = [val + 1 for val in layer_ids]`, with the comment *"we plus 1 here because in sglang, for the ith layer, it takes the output of the (i-1)th layer as aux hidden state"*
- `qwen3_moe.py:1177` — `self.model.set_dflash_layers_to_capture([val + 1 for val in layer_ids])`
- `gemma4_causal.py:1150` — `self.model.layers_to_capture = [val + 1 for val in layer_ids]`

`Qwen3MoeModel.set_dflash_layers_to_capture` and `Qwen3_5*.set_dflash_layers_to_capture` have identical bodies, so the wrappers should agree on the shift and today they do not.

Effect: Qwen3.5 + DFLASH captures the output of layer `val - 1` instead of layer `val`. It does not crash. The draft model simply consumes hidden states from the wrong layers, which shows up as a lower acceptance rate.

## Modifications

- Delete the shadowed definition at line 114.
- Add `[val + 1 for val in layers_to_capture]` to the live definition, with the same comment used in `llama.py`.

The deleted definition also carried input validation (unique / strictly increasing ids, range check, explicit `NotImplementedError` for PP > 1). None of that has ever executed. This PR keeps the live definition's `if not self.pp_group.is_last_rank: return`, which is what `llama.py` and `qwen3_moe.py` do. If maintainers want the stricter validation back, that is worth a separate change so this one stays a pure off-by-one fix.

## Accuracy Tests

No kernel math changes. The behavioral change is which decoder layers set `_is_layer_to_capture`, and the new value matches `llama.py` / `qwen3_moe.py` / `gemma4_causal.py`.

I do not have the hardware to run a Qwen3.5 + DFLASH acceptance-rate comparison. The check that would confirm it: run spec decode with the same `--speculative-*` config before and after and compare the reported accept length. Happy to add the run if a maintainer can point me at the CI job.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Indirect: this is expected to raise the DFLASH acceptance rate for Qwen3.5 back to where the other models sit. No hot-path code changes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (`ruff format`)
- [ ] Add unit tests — the capture ids are only observable through a model instance; open to suggestions on where a CPU-level test would fit.
- [ ] Update documentation — not applicable.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — see above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [AMD] Prefer QuickReduce before CustomAllReduce
body:
## Motivation

When QuickReduce and CustomAllReduce are both eligible, the current out-of-place all-reduce dispatch selects CustomAllReduce first. This prevents an explicitly configured QuickReduce codec from being used for overlapping message sizes.

This change gives eligible QuickReduce configurations priority while preserving the existing fallback chain. It also allows ROCm deployments that already enable AITER to use AITER's QuickAllReduce implementation without breaking launch scripts that still use the legacy SGLang environment names.

## Modifications

- Change plain out-of-place all-reduce dispatch from:

  ```text
  CustomAllReduce -> QuickReduce -> PyMSCCL++ -> torch symmetric memory -> PyNCCL
  ```

  to:

  ```text
  QuickReduce -> CustomAllReduce -> PyMSCCL++ -> torch symmetric memory -> PyNCCL
  ```

- Apply the same ordering in eager execution and the runtime `"auto"`resolver used by compiled and graph-replayed paths.
- Include QuickReduce eligibility in the eager symmetric-memory shortcut guard so that shortcut cannot bypass an eligible QuickReduce communicator.
- Add a QuickReduce factory that:
  - selects AITER QuickAllReduce when `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`;
  - falls back to SGLang's bundled implementation only when the AITER import is unavailable; and
  - leaves constructor failures visible to the existing communicator setup error handler.
- Translate legacy environment variables without overwriting explicitly set AITER values:

  | Legacy SGLang variable | AITER variable |
  | --- | --- |
  | `ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION` | `AITER_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION` |
  | `ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16` | `AITER_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16` |
  | `ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB` | `AITER_QUICK_REDUCE_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB` |

  The legacy `INT8` codec name maps to AITER's `FP8` name.
- Replace the old single-configuration collective benchmark flow with a one-command TP2/TP4/TP8 eager/graph sweep. The driver runs all backends, isolates each AITER graph shape in a fresh worker process, preserves unavailable rows, stores worker logs, and emits a Markdown report.
- Keep fused all-reduce + normalization dispatch unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

The compressed-codec checks used non-speculative servers with simulated acceptance disabled. GSM8K used all 1,319 questions, five-shot chat prompts, temperature 0, and no explicit `--max-tokens`. Qwen used `enable_thinking=false`; DeepSeek-V4 used reasoning effort `high`. HumanEval used 50 tasks.

| Model | TP | Evaluation | NONE score | INT4 score | Delta |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2 | 4 | GSM8K | 0.9712 | 0.9719 | +0.08 pp |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2 | 4 | HumanEval pass@1 | 0.896 | 0.876 | -2.00 pp |
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro | 8 | GSM8K | 0.9371 | 0.9128 | -2.43 pp |
| DeepSeek-V4-Pro | 8 | HumanEval pass@1 | 0.916 | 0.924 | +0.80 pp |

For each pair, launch the same model with
`AITER_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=NONE` and then `INT4`.

<details>
<summary>Evaluation commands</summary>

```bash
# Qwen GSM8K
PYTHONPATH=python OPENAI_API_KEY=EMPTY python -m sglang.test.run_eval \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8888 \
  --model amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4-AttnFP8-V2 \
  --eval-name gsm8k --api chat --num-examples 1319 \
  --num-threads 256 --num-shots 5 --temperature 0 --top-p 1 \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'

# DeepSeek-V4 GSM8K
PYTHONPATH=python OPENAI_API_KEY=EMPTY python -m sglang.test.run_eval \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8888 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --eval-name gsm8k --api chat --num-examples 1319 \
  --num-threads 256 --num-shots 5 --temperature 0 --top-p 1 \
  --reasoning-effort high

# HumanEval; add --reasoning-effort high for DeepSeek-V4
PYTHONPATH=python OPENAI_API_KEY=EMPTY python -m sglang.test.run_eval \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8888 --model "${MODEL}" \
  --eval-name humaneval --num-examples 50 --num-threads 50 \
  --temperature 0 --top-p 1
```

</details>

Unit coverage:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/distributed/test_parallel_state.py \
  -k "quick_allreduce or custom_allreduce_precedes"

```

The tests cover QuickReduce priority, CustomAllReduce fallback, the symmetric-memory guard, AITER selection and fallback, constructor-failure propagation, environment aliases, report generation, and one-command sweep planning.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

### Collective microbenchmark

Environment:

- AMD MI355X
- BF16 input
- TP2, TP4, and TP8
- eager and HIP graph replay
- powers-of-two message sizes from 1 KiB through 512 MiB
- 20 warmups and 101 timed calls per row
- correctness against RCCL before timing
- latency = maximum of each rank's mean GPU-event time

The six configurations produced 1,320 logical backend/size rows.

| TP | Mode | Fastest lossless backend(s) | First compressed QR win | Largest compressed QR speedup |
| ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 2 | eager | SGLang CAR v1 | 2 MiB | 3.771x (INT3) |
| 2 | graph | SGLang CAR v1 | 1 MiB | 3.680x (INT3) |
| 4 | eager | SGLang CAR v1 / AITER CAR / PyNCCL | 2 MiB | 2.761x (INT4) |
| 4 | graph | SGLang CAR v1 / AITER CAR / PyNCCL | 2 MiB | 2.777x (INT4) |
| 8 | eager | SGLang CAR v1 / AITER CAR / PyNCCL | 8 MiB | 1.724x (INT4) |
| 8 | graph | SGLang CAR v1 / AITER CAR / PyNCCL | 8 MiB | 1.820x (INT4) |

Full-precision QuickReduce did not beat the fastest available lossless backend in any retained BF16 row. Reduced-precision codecs remain explicit configuration choices; this PR does not enable them by default.

No retained row failed correctness. The report preserves these availability
gaps:

- RCCL is not graph-captured by this harness.
- torch symmetric memory was disabled on this ROCm/PyTorch runtime.
- SGLang CAR v2 failed
  `torch._C._distributed_c10d._SymmetricMemory.rendezvous` with `HIP error: invalid argument`.
- INT3 is intentionally unavailable at TP4 and TP8.
- AITER CAR and QuickReduce rows outside their supported message-size ranges remain unavailable.

<details>
<summary>One-command BF16 sweep</summary>

```bash
python benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/benchmark_rocm.py \
  --sweep-output-dir results/allreduce \
  --dtype bf16
```

The command writes CSVs to `<output>/csv/`, worker logs to `<output>/logs/`,
and the final tables to `<output>/allreduce_report.md`.

</details>

### End-to-end performance

The serving A/B used random 8,192-token inputs and 1,024-token outputs with
radix cache and speculative decoding disabled. Each concurrency used four
measured requests and two warmup requests per slot, an infinite request rate,
and seed 42.

Higher throughput and negative latency changes favor INT4.

| Model | TP | Concurrency | NONE output tok/s | INT4 output tok/s | Throughput change | NONE median E2E | INT4 median E2E | E2E change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3.5 | 4 | 1 | 124.82 | 127.28 | +1.97% | 8,078.78 ms | 8,036.14 ms | -0.53% |
| Qwen3.5 | 4 | 4 | 419.60 | 426.71 | +1.69% | 9,743.27 ms | 9,608.19 ms | -1.39% |
| Qwen3.5 | 4 | 16 | 1,150.61 | 1,207.97 | +4.99% | 14,223.02 ms | 13,544.46 ms | -4.77% |
| DeepSeek-V4 | 8 | 1 | 66.69 | 67.17 | +0.72% | 15,350.65 ms | 15,239.41 ms | -0.72% |
| DeepSeek-V4 | 8 | 4 | 220.82 | 222.82 | +0.91% | 18,401.41 ms | 18,160.75 ms | -1.31% |
| DeepSeek-V4 | 8 | 16 | 642.30 | 656.76 | +2.25% | 24,891.97 ms | 24,327.29 ms | -2.27% |

| Model | Concurrency | NONE median TTFT | INT4 median TTFT | TTFT change | NONE median TPOT | INT4 median TPOT | TPOT change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3.5 | 1 | 227.95 ms | 181.78 ms | -20.26% | 7.675 ms | 7.688 ms | +0.16% |
| Qwen3.5 | 4 | 750.35 ms | 556.88 ms | -25.78% | 8.781 ms | 8.787 ms | +0.06% |
| Qwen3.5 | 16 | 2,016.86 ms | 1,500.50 ms | -25.60% | 11.942 ms | 11.758 ms | -1.54% |
| DeepSeek-V4 | 1 | 353.90 ms | 321.86 ms | -9.05% | 14.659 ms | 14.582 ms | -0.53% |
| DeepSeek-V4 | 4 | 364.48 ms | 335.12 ms | -8.05% | 17.307 ms | 17.256 ms | -0.29% |
| DeepSeek-V4 | 16 | 1,366.48 ms | 1,280.81 ms | -6.27% | 23.171 ms | 22.703 ms | -2.02% |

INT4 improved output throughput and median E2E latency at all six tested
points. The largest throughput gains were 4.99% for Qwen3.5 and 2.25% for
DeepSeek-V4 at concurrency 16. Qwen TPOT at concurrency 1 and 4 was flat
within 0.16%, while TTFT improved by 20.26% and 25.78%.

<details>
<summary>Serving launch and benchmark commands</summary>

```bash
# Set MODEL_SCRIPT to the Qwen TP4 or DeepSeek-V4 TP8 launcher.
EVAL_ONLY=true ENABLE_SPECULATIVE=false DISABLE_RADIX_CACHE=true CONC=16 \
  AITER_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION="${REGIME}" \
  "${MODEL_SCRIPT}"

for concurrency in 1 4 16; do
  num_prompts=$((concurrency * 4))
  warmup_requests=$((concurrency * 2))
  output_file="results/e2e_${REGIME}_c${concurrency}.json"
  python -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
    --backend sglang \
    --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8888 \
    --model "${MODEL}" \
    --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 8192 \
    --random-output-len 1024 \
    --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
    --num-prompts "${num_prompts}" \
    --max-concurrency "${concurrency}" \
    --request-rate inf \
    --warmup-requests "${warmup_requests}" \
    --output-file "${output_file}" \
    --seed 42
done
```

Run the loop once with `REGIME=NONE` and once with `REGIME=INT4`.

</details>

title: [Diffusion] Support MiniMax-H3 PDD(Parallel Decoding Distillation) inference
body:
Co-authored-by: @forrestl111 
## Motivation

Support offline inference with the MiniMax-H3 FL2VA and Ref2VA PDD acceleration checkpoints from [alibaba-pai/MiniMax-H3-Acc-LoRAs](https://huggingface.co/alibaba-pai/MiniMax-H3-Acc-LoRAs). These checkpoints contain backbone LoRA deltas and interval-specific output heads that require separate handling.

## Modifications

- Add tools to merge backbone LoRA weights and fuse 32 interval-specific output heads into 8 heads.
- Keep PDD heads outside the transformer checkpoint directory and preserve checkpoint indexes.
- Load fused heads through `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_MINIMAX_H3_PDD_HEADS`, with TP-aware output sharding and a shared projection path.
- Validate inference schedules against the fusion configuration. Warmup uses a prefix of the same schedule.
- Add regression tests for TP projection, checkpoint conversion, and schedule validation.

The standard inference path remains unchanged when PDD is disabled. PDD requests use `num_inference_steps=9`, corresponding to 8 denoising forwards.

## Accuracy Tests

- All 3 regression tests passed on the remote test host, covering TP projection, checkpoint conversion, and schedule validation.
- Inference was validated on NVIDIA CUDA with **TP=2, SP/Ulysses=4** and **TP=1, SP/Ulysses=8**.
- With TP2/SP4, completed **18 generations covering 9 paired comparisons**: T2VA, FL2VA, and video-reference Ref2VA, each at 5/10/15 seconds with seed 0.
- SSIM compares each PDD output against a freshly generated lossless output with identical input and seed.
- Metric: frame-mean YUV420 SSIM with Y:U:V weights of 4:1:1. Resolution and frame count were checked before comparison.
- TP1/SP8 smoke tests passed for T2VA, FL2VA, and video-reference Ref2VA using 5-second samples.

| Task | Duration | SSIM (PDD vs lossless) |
|---|---:|---:|
| T2VA | 5s | 0.7102 |
| T2VA | 10s | 0.6614 |
| T2VA | 15s | 0.7614 |
| FL2VA | 5s | 0.6300 |
| FL2VA | 10s | 0.6543 |
| FL2VA | 15s | 0.5535 |
| Ref2VA (video) | 5s | 0.8130 |
| Ref2VA (video) | 10s | 0.9788 |
| Ref2VA (video) | 15s | 0.8666 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Configuration: **8× NVIDIA H200, TP=2, SP/Ulysses=4, dense FlashAttention, 768p**.

Both modes use identical inputs and seed 0. Lossless uses 49 denoising forwards; PDD uses 8. Each server receives a warmup request before measurement.

The table reports server-side generation time from **`Pixel data generated successfully in ... seconds`**, excluding model loading, warmup, client polling, and video download.

| Task | Duration | Lossless (s) | PDD (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| T2VA | 5s | 41.16 | 8.03 |
| T2VA | 10s | 116.00 | 21.44 |
| T2VA | 15s | 224.78 | 40.52 |
| FL2VA | 5s | 44.61 | 8.94 |
| FL2VA | 10s | 120.21 | 22.12 |
| FL2VA | 15s | 231.89 | 41.25 |
| Ref2VA (video) | 5s | 138.78 | 27.79 |
| Ref2VA (video) | 10s | 432.25 | 79.52 |
| Ref2VA (video) | 15s | 864.08 | 153.75 |

Aggregate speedup, calculated as total lossless time divided by total PDD time:

- **Server-side generation: 5.49×**
- **Denoising: 6.05×**

These results use one measured run per case and one seed.

## Usage

Merge the adapter into a native MiniMax-H3 transformer checkpoint, then fuse the PDD heads:

```bash
python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.build_minimax_h3_pdd_weights \
    <native-transformer-dir> <pdd-lora.safetensors> <output-dir>

python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.tools.fuse_minimax_h3_pdd_heads \
    <output-dir>
```

Enable the fused heads:

```bash
export SGLANG_DIFFUSION_MINIMAX_H3_PDD_HEADS=<output-dir>/pdd_fused_heads.safetensors
```

Pass `--transformer-weights-path <output-dir>/transformer` to the server and set `num_inference_steps=9` in requests. Keep `pdd_config.json` beside the fused heads; request flow shifts must match the fusion configuration.

title: Sensenova bf16 rope npu
body:
## Motivation

SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT applies RoPE to query and key tensors in every attention layer. Using an NPU fused operator reduces this work and improves end-to-end generation latency. RoPE table precomputation also needs to handle decoder layers wrapped by Cache-DiT; directly accessing `layers[0].self_attn` causes warmup to fail.

## Modifications

- Add a SenseNova RoPE path that calls `torch_npu.npu_rotary_mul` for query and key tensors using `rotary_mode="half"`.
- Enable it with `SGLANG_SENSENOVA_NPU_FUSED_ROPE=rotary_mul`. The default remains the original implementation, which is also used when the fused path’s conditions are not met.
- Resolve the attention module inside a Cache-DiT wrapper before precomputing shared RoPE tables, and add a unit test for this case.
- Merge the existing `sensenova-release` history into a branch based on the updated `upstream/main`. The resulting PR diff includes earlier SenseNova changes from that branch.

## Accuracy Tests

- Python syntax checks and `pre-commit` passed.
- A unit test was added for the Cache-DiT wrapper case. Local pytest stopped during test collection because `orjson` is missing from the environment.
- **Pending:** Compare generated outputs and numerical error between the original and fused RoPE paths on the target NPU.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

End-to-end measurements for SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT with Cache-DiT enabled:

| RoPE path | Test configuration 1 | Test configuration 4 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Original | 299.6 s | 299.7 s |
| `npu_rotary_mul` | 280.09 s | 279.93 s |
| Latency reduction | ~6.5% | ~6.6% |

Cache-DiT settings: `FN=4`, `BN=2`, `WARMUP=8`, `RDT=0.10`, and `MC=1`.

**Pending:** Add an NPU profiler trace to confirm fused operator calls and operator-level latency.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with `pre-commit`.
- [x] Add a unit test for the Cache-DiT wrapper case.
- [ ] Document the new environment variable.
- [ ] Provide NPU accuracy results and profiler output.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [Diffusion] Add CLIP / CLIP-IQA / ImageReward quality checks for imag…
body:
## Motivation

The diffusion server tests have no accuracy gate on image output other than an
inline CLIP guard in the XPU FLUX.2-dev case. That guard has two problems:

1. It approximates cosine similarity by dividing CLIP's `logits_per_image` by a
   fixed `100`. `logits_per_image` is `exp(logit_scale) * cosine`, so the divisor
   is an assumption about a *learned* parameter of the checkpoint rather than a
   constant of the metric. It happens to be close for the checkpoint in use, but
   nothing enforces that, and it changes silently under a different or fine-tuned
   CLIP.
2. More importantly, it catches every exception and returns `None`, which
   **silently disables the assertion** whenever setup or inference fails — a
   missing dependency, a failed download, an OOM during scoring. The only
   accuracy check in the case can stop checking anything without the test going
   red.

This PR replaces that guard with three named metrics computed from explicit
cosine similarity, makes an unavailable-but-enforced metric a failure, and ships
an offline sweep tool so a floor is measured before it is enforced.

## Modifications

- **`multimodal_gen/test/quality_metrics.py`** (new) — `compute_clip_score` /
  `compute_clip_iqa` / `compute_image_reward` (plus a batched
  `compute_image_rewards`), `QualityThresholds` with `load_quality_thresholds` /
  `check_quality`, and `paired_delta`.
  - `clip_score` normalises the projected image and text features and takes their
    cosine directly, then multiplies by `100` purely as the reporting convention
    used by `torchmetrics.CLIPScore` and the published FLUX/SD numbers. The
    checkpoint's `logit_scale` is never used, so no fixed value is assumed.
  - It is reimplemented on plain `transformers` rather than calling
    `torchmetrics.multimodal.CLIPScore`, which does
    `get_image_features(...).norm(...)` and raises `AttributeError` on the pinned
    `transformers==5.12.1` where that call returns an output object
    (Lightning-AI/torchmetrics#3244). Backbone is `openai/clip-vit-base-patch32`,
    torchmetrics' default; scores are comparable only within one backbone.
  - Only the metrics a case actually enforces are computed
    (`compute_quality_scores` returns `None` for the rest), and an enforced metric
    that produced no value is reported as a **failure**, never a pass.
- **`multimodal_gen/test/server/quality_thresholds.json`** (new) — per-case
  floors, opt-in through `DiffusionTestCase.run_quality_check` (default `False`).
  A case with the check enabled and no entry in the table fails immediately.
- **`multimodal_gen/test/server/test_server_common.py`** — `_score_quality` /
  `_validate_quality`, wired through the existing `run_case_check("quality", ...)`
  path so a violation reports like every other case check.
- **`multimodal_gen/test/server/testcase_configs.py`** —
  `run_quality_check: bool = False` on `DiffusionTestCase`.
- **`multimodal_gen/benchmarks/bench_image_quality.py`** (new) — scores a
  `--save-output-dir` from `bench_offline_throughput` against the request manifest
  that generated it. Writes `<prefix>_per_image.jsonl` and `<prefix>_summary.json`;
  `--baseline` adds a paired per-prompt delta against another arm, which is what
  makes these metrics usable at small n; `--case-id` checks a whole directory
  against a case's floors; `--limit` truncates after pairing.
- **`multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_quality_metrics.py`** (new) — see
  **Test coverage** below. No GPU and no network.
- **`test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_flux2_dev.py`** — deletes the file's private
  CLIP helper and sets `run_quality_check=True` on `flux2_dev_image_t2i`. **This
  is the only case in the tree that enables the check.**
- **`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`** — `SGLANG_TEST_IMAGE_REWARD_PYTHON`
  (`EnvStr(None)`), in the test section.
- **`python/pyproject.toml`** — a `diffusion-eval` optional extra
  (`piq>=0.8.0`, `torchmetrics>=1.9.0`).
- **`docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/quality_eval.mdx`** + `docs/docs.json` nav entry.

## Exactly what is enforced today

| case | `run_quality_check` | populated floors | enforced when the case runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flux2_dev_image_t2i` (`test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_flux2_dev.py`) | **`True`** | `min_clip_score: 20.0` | `clip_score` only |
| `flux_2_klein_image_t2i` | not set (default `False`) | `min_clip_score: 15.0`, `min_image_reward: -1.3` | nothing — the entry is data for `bench_image_quality --case-id` |
| every other case | default `False` | none | nothing |

`min_clip_iqa` is populated for **no** case. So in CI this PR enforces exactly one
threshold: `clip_score >= 20.0` on the FLUX.2-dev XPU case, which is the same gate
the deleted helper intended (it asserted raw cosine `>= 0.20`), carried onto the
`100 * cosine` scale so the case is not silently weakened.

The `flux_2_klein_image_t2i` row is deliberately not wired to a running case: it
exists so `bench_image_quality --case-id flux_2_klein_image_t2i` can check a whole
sweep against measured floors offline. If a maintainer wants it gated in CI, that
is a one-line `run_quality_check=True` plus the ImageReward provisioning below.

## Why `clip_iqa` is unenforced and `clip_score` is only a tripwire

Scoring real output against a black frame and uniform noise (the control images
were produced by a throwaway script, not shipped, then scored with
`bench_image_quality.py`):

| metric | worst healthy | best broken | separation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clip_score` | 24.70 | 25.28 (black frame) | **-0.58, overlaps** |
| `clip_iqa` | 0.430 | 0.773 (uniform noise) | **-0.34, overlaps** |
| `image_reward` | -0.587 | -2.041 (black frame) | **+1.45** |

A black frame out-scores the worst healthy image on CLIP, and uniform noise lands
inside the healthy bulk on CLIP-IQA. So neither can separate a broken image from a
good one at any floor: `min_clip_iqa` is therefore populated nowhere, and the
`min_clip_score` floors that do exist sit far below the healthy distribution and
are documented as **decode-failure tripwires** — they catch "the pipeline returned
something that is not an image of the prompt", not a quality regression.
`image_reward` is the only one of the three whose distributions do not overlap, so
it is the only one a single-image floor can be based on; that is why the one
measured `min_image_reward` exists, on the case that has a measured entry.

For anything finer than a tripwire, use `--baseline`: a paired per-prompt delta
between two arms resolves differences far below what any floor can, because the
per-prompt spread of all three metrics dominates the arm-to-arm difference.

## Dependencies and how the second interpreter is provisioned

| metric | needs | why |
|---|---|---|
| `clip_score` | nothing beyond sglang's pinned `transformers` | computed in-tree |
| `clip_iqa` | `pip install "sglang[diffusion-eval]"` (`torchmetrics>=1.9.0`, `piq>=0.8.0`) | `piq` holds the canonical CLIP-IQA weights, which torchmetrics refuses to load without it |
| `image_reward` | a **second interpreter** named by `SGLANG_TEST_IMAGE_REWARD_PYTHON` | ImageReward imports `ImageReward/ReFL.py`, which requires `transformers<5`, while sglang pins `transformers==5.12.1`. The two cannot share an environment |

```bash
python -m venv /opt/imagereward
/opt/imagereward/bin/pip install image-reward 'transformers==4.46.3' 'diffusers==0.31.0'
export SGLANG_TEST_IMAGE_REWARD_PYTHON=/opt/imagereward/bin/python
```

sglang never imports ImageReward. `quality_metrics.py` runs a small stdin/stdout
script under that interpreter, handing images over by path, one launch per sweep
(the checkpoint is ~1.7 GB, so per-image launches would dominate).

**CI needs no change for this PR.** The only case with the check enabled enforces
`clip_score`, which needs neither the extra nor the second interpreter. The
contract if that changes is deliberate and worth stating plainly: a case that
enforces `min_image_reward` **fails** when `SGLANG_TEST_IMAGE_REWARD_PYTHON` is
unset — it does not skip. So gating a CI case on `image_reward` requires the runner
image to provision that venv first, and reviewers should treat the env var as a
prerequisite of enabling such a floor, not as an optional enhancement. If a
skip-when-absent policy is preferred for CI, say so and I will add it as an
explicit mode rather than as silent behaviour.

## Scope of the single threshold table

The table is not split per device, and that is a claim about **these floors**, not
about score invariance. Output quality does vary with precision, attention and
kernel selection, scheduler, seed and dependency versions, not merely GPU family.
The floors here are set far enough below the healthy distribution that they survive
that variation — which is exactly what makes them tripwires rather than quality
gates — whereas `perf_baselines/` has to be per-device because latency has no such
margin. If some configuration genuinely scores near a floor, the right fix is a
case-specific entry (or `--baseline` comparison), not a per-device table.

## Test

```bash
# 1. unit tests -- no GPU, no network, no model downloads
pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_quality_metrics.py -v

# 2. the gated registered case -- COLLECTION ONLY here (see Limitations)
pytest test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_flux2_dev.py --collect-only -q

# 3. offline sweep, end to end: generate, then score
python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.benchmarks.bench_offline_throughput \
    --model-path black-forest-labs/FLUX.2-klein-9B \
    --request-manifest prompts.jsonl \
    --save-output-dir out_arm1/ \
    --height 1024 --width 1024 \
    --num-inference-steps 4 --guidance-scale 1.0 --seed 42 \
    --batch-size 1

python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.benchmarks.bench_image_quality \
    --images out_arm1/ \
    --request-manifest prompts.jsonl \
    --out-prefix arm1 \
    --metrics clip_score clip_iqa image_reward \
    --case-id flux_2_klein_image_t2i \
    --log-every 25

# 4. paired comparison of a second arm against the first, and a truncated pass
python -m sglang.multimodal_gen.benchmarks.bench_image_quality \
    --images out_arm2/ \
    --request-manifest prompts.jsonl \
    --out-prefix arm2 \
    --metrics clip_score clip_iqa image_reward \
    --baseline arm1_per_image.jsonl \
    --limit 100 --log-every 25
```

Generate on one device: `bench_offline_throughput` names outputs
`<index-within-shard>-<request_id>`, and `bench_image_quality` re-checks that index
and id against the manifest row, so a sharded run raises `PAIRING ERROR` on every
shard after the first. That check is deliberate — mislabelling prompts would
silently corrupt every score.

### Test coverage

Behaviours asserted by the unit tests, all without a GPU, network access or model
weights (`transformers`, `torchmetrics` and `subprocess` are faked):

- an enforced metric that produced no value fails, rather than passing — the
  regression this PR exists to prevent;
- an unenforced metric is neither computed nor required;
- threshold lookup merges `defaults`, and an unknown case id yields no floors;
- the shipped table loads and enforces at least one floor;
- CLIP-IQA's `data_range` is pinned to the scale of the tensor actually passed;
- `clip_score` reads projected features off the `transformers` 5 output object;
- ImageReward scores are parsed from the subprocess's last JSON line, tolerating
  loader noise on stdout;
- a sweep launches the ImageReward interpreter exactly once for a whole directory;
- ImageReward with no second interpreter configured raises, rather than skipping;
- `paired_delta` returns the mean per-image difference and its own standard error;
- pairing rejects images whose index or request id does not match the manifest;
- every case with `run_quality_check=True` has an entry in the thresholds table
  (a repo-consistency test, so the two cannot drift).

### Limitations

- **`test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_flux2_dev.py` has been collected, not executed
  end to end** (`1 test collected`) — the environment used had neither the
  FLUX.2-dev weights nor the disk for them, and the case is registered to a 4-GPU
  nightly XPU suite. The server-side wiring is therefore covered by the unit tests
  plus collection, and the metrics themselves by the offline sweep. A CI run of
  that case is the missing piece, and reviewers should treat it as unverified until
  it goes green.
- The floors are measured for FLUX.2-dev and FLUX.2-klein only. Other image cases
  can opt in as their entries are measured; the repo-consistency test makes
  enabling the flag without an entry a failure rather than a silent pass.

## Checklist

- [x] Formatted with the repo's pre-commit configuration (black, isort, ruff
      `F401,F821,UP037`).
- [x] Unit tests added, runnable without a GPU, network or model weights.
- [x] Documentation added (`docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/quality_eval.mdx`) and
      registered in `docs/docs.json`.
- [x] New env var follows `.claude/skills/env-var-conventions` — typed descriptor
      in `Envs`, read only through `envs.X.get()`, overridden in tests with
      `.override(...)`.
