title: flashinfer: pass logits_soft_cap (and ragged window_left) at plan time; gemma-2 / grok ran uncapped
body:
﻿## Motivation

Fixes #33915. Related: flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#1193.

The FlashInfer attention backend never applies `logit_cap`. Since flashinfer >= 0.2,
`use_logits_soft_cap` is compile-time state that `plan()`/`begin_forward()` bakes into
the selected kernel module; the deprecated per-call `forward()`/`forward_return_lse()`
still accepts a `logits_soft_cap` argument but the value only reaches a kernel that was
planned with capping enabled. sglang passed the cap exclusively at forward() time and
never at any of the plan call sites, so every model with a nonzero `logit_cap` ran
uncapped on the default backend:

- gemma-2 family: `logit_cap = config.attn_logit_softcapping` (50.0)
- grok: `logit_cap = max(getattr(config, "attn_logit_softcapping", 30.0), 0.0)`

(gemma-3 / gemma-4 / gemma-3n pass `logit_cap=0.0` and are unaffected.) The triton
backend applies the cap, so the two backends disagreed on the same checkpoint.

`window_left` was dropped by the same mechanism on the ragged prefill path only: the
ragged wrapper was planned without it, and the no-prefix forward() call did not even
pass it per call. The paged prefill path already treats `window_left` as plan-time
state ("selects the module with the per-element window mask compiled in") â€” this PR
extends that idiom to the cap and to the ragged wrapper.

Verified against the pinned flashinfer 0.6.15.post1 wheel: `plan()` selects the module
with `logits_soft_cap > 0` / `window_left >= 0` and `forward()` stores the per-call
values that `run()` passes to the kernel â€” so the plan-time argument enables the
feature and the existing per-layer forward() arguments keep choosing the values:

```
1 cap at plan():                vs capped 0.999999 | vs uncapped 0.593908
2 cap at legacy forward() only: vs capped 0.593905 | vs uncapped 1.000000   <- the bug
3 cap at plan and forward:      vs capped 0.999999 | vs uncapped 0.593908   <- this PR
4 plan(cap25) forward(cap50):   vs cap50 0.999999 | vs cap25 0.857086      <- run-time value wins
5 plan(w8) forward(w8):         vs win8 1.000000 | vs full 0.413510
6 plan(w8) forward(w-1):        vs win8 0.413511 | vs full 1.000000        <- -1 stays full attention
```

(cosine vs an fp32 reference, ragged wrapper, gemma-2-27b shapes, flashinfer
0.6.15.post1 / torch 2.13.0+cu130 / RTX 4090; row 6 is why the single ragged wrapper
shared by SWA and full-attention layers can be planned with the model's window.)

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/flashinfer_backend.py`:

- New `_model_logits_soft_cap(model)`: reads the cap the model's `RadixAttention`
  layers request, once, at backend construction (same pattern as
  `trtllm_mha_backend` scanning `model.modules()` for encoder-only layers). The cap
  is per layer while planning is per forward batch, so it returns the single shared
  value â€” every capped in-tree model uses one cap for all layers â€” and raises for a
  model mixing distinct caps (planning one module per wrapper cannot represent that;
  a cap-enabled kernel handed runtime cap 0.0 would corrupt uncapped layers).
- `FlashInferAttnBackend.__init__` stores it; both indices updaters pass
  `logits_soft_cap=` at every plan site: decode `begin_forward` (both the regular
  and `fast_decode_plan` branches), paged prefill `begin_forward`, ragged prefill
  `begin_forward`.
- The ragged prefill `begin_forward` additionally gets
  `window_left=<model sliding_window_size>`, mirroring the paged path's plan-time
  window handling; full-attention layers keep passing `window_left=-1` per call,
  which remains exact full attention (row 6 above).
- The no-prefix ragged `forward()` now passes `window_left=swa_window_left` like the
  merge-path calls already did (the computation is hoisted above the branch).
- `fast_prefill_plan` accepts `logits_soft_cap` and mirrors upstream `plan()`'s
  `self._logits_soft_cap` assignment, since the shared call site now passes it.

For models with `logit_cap == 0` everywhere, `logits_soft_cap=0.0` is normalized by
upstream plan() exactly like the previous implicit `None` â€” identical module
selection, no behavior change.

Tests (`test/registered/attention/unittests/dense/test_flashinfer.py`, kit support in
`python/sglang/test/kits/attention_unittest/attention_methods/dense_attention.py`):

- `DenseAttentionCase` gains `logit_cap` (default 0.0); the fp32 reference applies
  `cap * tanh(scores / cap)`; the projected module forwards it to `RadixAttention`.
- Five regression subtests: capped extend on the ragged no-prefix path, capped
  extend on the ragged+paged merge path, capped decode, and SWA extends whose
  chunk length exceeds the window on both ragged sub-paths. All five fail on the
  pre-fix backend (greatest abs diff 0.08-0.40 vs atol 0.03) and pass with the fix.

## Accuracy Tests

Environment: 1x RTX 4090 24GB (RunPod), CUDA 12.8 toolkit / driver 580.159.04, torch 2.13.0+cu130,
flashinfer_python 0.6.15.post1 (+ flashinfer-cubin / flashinfer-jit-cache
0.6.15.post1), Python 3.12, sglang `-e python` at c69d593.

Pre-fix (tests only applied, backend unchanged) â€” all five regression subtests fail:

```
FAIL: test_logit_cap_cases (case='logit_cap_extend_ragged_no_prefix')
Greatest absolute difference: 0.185546875 (up to 0.03 allowed)
FAIL: test_logit_cap_cases (case='logit_cap_extend_ragged_paged_merge')
Greatest absolute difference: 0.08770751953125 (up to 0.03 allowed)
FAIL: test_logit_cap_cases (case='logit_cap_decode')
Greatest absolute difference: 0.0810546875 (up to 0.03 allowed)
FAIL: test_swa_ragged_window_cases (case='swa_window_extend_ragged_no_prefix_beyond_window')
Greatest absolute difference: 0.403076171875 (up to 0.03 allowed)
FAIL: test_swa_ragged_window_cases (case='swa_window_extend_ragged_merge_beyond_window')
Greatest absolute difference: 0.25634765625 (up to 0.03 allowed)
Ran 2 tests ... FAILED (failures=5)
```

Post-fix â€” the new regression tests pass:

```
test_logit_cap_cases ... ok
test_swa_ragged_window_cases ... ok
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 2 tests in 7.223s

OK
```

Post-fix â€” the full dense attention unit suites pass (existing coverage: eager
extend/decode, layout robustness, cuda-graph decode, split-op bcg/pcg, eagle /
dflash / ngram / frozen-kv-mtp verify and draft runner modes):

```
test_flashinfer.py: Ran 10 tests in 38.668s  OK
test_triton.py:     Ran 10 tests in 36.198s  OK   (sanity for the shared test-kit change)
```

Model-level sanity, gemma-2-2b-it (`attn_logit_softcapping=50.0`), greedy 32-token
generations with `return_logprob` on 4 fixed prompts, flashinfer vs triton backend
(same checkpoint, same server args, CUDA graphs on):

```
=== pre-fix flashinfer vs triton ===
prompt='The capital of France is'         same_text=False  decode_logprob max|d|=1.0633
prompt='Water is composed of two eleme'   same_text=True   decode_logprob max|d|=0.0526
prompt='def fibonacci(n):\n    '          same_text=True   decode_logprob max|d|=0.0362
prompt='In a shocking finding, scienti'   same_text=True   decode_logprob max|d|=0.0560
=== post-fix flashinfer vs triton ===
prompt='The capital of France is'         same_text=True   decode_logprob max|d|=0.0616
prompt='Water is composed of two eleme'   same_text=True   decode_logprob max|d|=0.0382
prompt='def fibonacci(n):\n    '          same_text=True   decode_logprob max|d|=0.0371
prompt='In a shocking finding, scienti'   same_text=True   decode_logprob max|d|=0.0565
```

Pre-fix, the flashinfer backend diverged from triton on greedy decode for 1 of the
4 prompts; with the fix the two backends produce identical text on all four, with
remaining logprob deltas at the usual bf16 cross-backend noise level. (Checkpoint:
`unsloth/gemma-2-2b-it`, an ungated mirror of the gated google checkpoint.)

Note: per the issue's analysis, the 2b checkpoint's logits rarely reach the cap
(`query_pre_attn_scalar == head_dim == 256`), so this is an integration check
(plan-time cap active on a real capped model, CUDA-graph capture/replay,
`fast_decode_plan`) rather than a cap-magnitude measurement; 27b does not fit the
validation GPU. The wrapper-level and unit-test evidence above is what isolates the
cap behavior.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No new per-token work: the cap/window are plan-time arguments, and forward() already
passed them per call. For capped or SWA models the plan selects the soft-cap /
sliding-window kernel variant (as the triton backend and HF eager semantics require);
uncapped non-SWA models select the exact same module as before. Not benchmarked.

## Checklist

      isort 7.0.0, ruff F401/F821/UP037 all clean on the touched files).
- [x] Add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation as needed (none needed).
- [x] Provide accuracy results (above).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [XPU] Enable GGUF Q4_K inference for Qwen3.5-family and Gemma4
body:
## Motivation

This PR introduces the first GGUF inference path for Intel XPU in upstream SGLang, without depending on the llm-scaler ESIMD extension. The implementation converts GGUF Q4_K weights at load time into the W4A16 representation already supported by `sglang-kernel-xpu`. The quantized execution path is XPU-gated, while the supporting model and loader changes touch shared Python code and therefore need cross-backend CI review.

This PR remains a draft while required upstream CI and maintainer review are in progress.

## Modifications

- Add Intel XPU GGUF linear and embedding quantization methods.
- Repack GGUF Q4_K weights into the existing XPU W4A16 layout.
- Add a hybrid GGUF MoE path:
  - Q4_K gate/up uses the XPU W4A16 grouped GEMM.
  - Q5_K/Q6_K/Q8_0 down projections are dequantized once at load time and use the native BF16 grouped GEMM.
- Add GGUF tensor-name mappings for Qwen3.5-family and Gemma4 models.
- Add Qwen GDN GGUF layout conversion and fused-shard loading support.
- Add quantization-aware Gemma4 embedding and tied LM-head handling, with a non-GGUF regression test.
- Reuse the standard colocated GGUF sidecar discovery: `config.json`, tokenizer files, and a safetensors index or shards live beside the GGUF file. No XPU-specific environment variable is introduced.
- Add focused CPU tests, CI registrations, and user-facing XPU GGUF documentation.

No new ESIMD kernel is introduced. Native Q4_K and decode-specific kernel optimization will be handled separately in `sgl-kernel-xpu`.

## Accuracy Tests

Hardware validation scope: Intel XPU only. CUDA, ROCm, and other accelerator backends were not run locally because those devices are not available in the test environment. Cross-backend regression coverage therefore relies on upstream CI and maintainer validation.

Validated with tokenizer-enabled OpenAI chat requests on two Intel XPU cards with TP=2. Natural-language responses were semantically correct for all five checkpoints:

- Qwen3.6-27B Q4_K_M
- Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_M
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M
- Gemma4-31B-it Q4_K_M
- Gemma4-26B-A4B-it UD-Q4_K_M

After rebasing onto current `main`, Qwen3.8-27B was revalidated using only colocated sidecar files (no custom GGUF environment variables). The OpenAI chat endpoint returned a semantically correct Chinese answer.

Focused unit tests:

```text
25 passed
```

The non-Rust upstream pre-commit suite passes locally, including ruff, formatting, codespell, CI registry validation, and lint-checker tests. The complete GitHub lint job also passes, including Rust hooks and Mintlify documentation-link checks.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Single-request streaming decode, TP=2, temperature=0, 64 output tokens. Steady-state values use runs 2-3.

| Model | TTFT | E2E | Decode throughput |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.6-27B Q4_K_M | 0.207 s | 5.592 s | 11.70 tok/s |
| Qwen3.8-27B UD-Q4_K_M | 0.206 s | 5.493 s | 11.92 tok/s |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_M | 0.174 s | 4.804 s | 13.61 tok/s |
| Gemma4-31B-it Q4_K_M | 0.138 s | 4.199 s | 15.51 tok/s |
| Gemma4-26B-A4B-it UD-Q4_K_M | 0.113 s | 3.395 s | 19.20 tok/s |

Latest-upstream Qwen3.8-27B smoke test (TP=2): 124.28 s weight load, 21.41 GB/card, and 128 forced output tokens in 10.62 s (12.05 tok/s end-to-end, including prefill). The first request after startup incurred about 30 s of Triton GDN JIT compilation; precompilation and native kernel work remain follow-ups.

Qwen hybrid GDN models currently require `--disable-radix-cache` on the Intel XPU attention backend because XPU uses a paged KV cache while the upstream no-buffer Mamba radix-cache strategy requires page size 1. This is documented and intentionally not addressed by changing shared cache policy in this GGUF PR.

## Draft follow-ups

- Pass required upstream CI, especially shared-code CUDA/ROCm coverage.
- Address maintainer feedback and reduce shared-code surface where practical.
- Follow up with native Q4_K/decode kernel optimization and Triton precompilation work in `sgl-kernel-xpu`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with the upstream pre-commit configuration.
- [x] Add focused unit tests and CI registrations.
- [x] Add user-facing documentation and a supported-model matrix.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed results for all five target checkpoints.

title: fix(models): guard both format_ue8m0 reads in deepseek weight loader (fixes humming weight-load crash)
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #40393.

On v0.5.20, serving a DeepSeek-family / GLM MLA checkpoint with `--quantization humming` crashes on every TP rank at the end of weight loading:

```
AttributeError: 'BlockQuantScaleParameter' object has no attribute 'format_ue8m0'
```

#38446 hoisted the `format_ue8m0` attribute read out of a short-circuit expression in `DeepseekV2WeightLoaderMixin.post_load_weights`, so it is now evaluated unconditionally. The attribute is only stamped by quant methods that requant scales to UE8M0 (fp8/DeepGEMM, flashinfer_trtllm, mega_moe, NPU methods); quant methods like `humming` never stamp it, so the read genuinely fails there.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py` — guard **both** unguarded reads with `getattr(..., False)`:

1. `is_ue8m0_uint8 = weight_scale.format_ue8m0 and ...` (line 632)
2. the `should_deepgemm_weight_requant_ue8m0(...)` branch (line 656), which is still reachable after (1) is fixed: when DeepGEMM UE8M0 requant is enabled (H100/H20, 128×128 block size) the condition evaluates `weight_scale.format_ue8m0` and raises the same `AttributeError` — fixing site (1) alone only relocates the crash 24 lines down.

The `getattr(..., False)` pattern matches existing defensive usage in `layers/linear.py` and `models/qwen3_5.py`. Behavior for quant methods that DO stamp the attribute is unchanged — the default `False` only applies where the attribute never existed.

### Relation to #40397

PR #40397 fixes the first read (site 1). As described above, the second read (site 2) is evaluated when the `elif should_deepgemm_weight_requant_ue8m0(...)` branch is taken, which is the common case on H100/H20 — so that PR alone still crashes for `--quantization humming`. This PR covers both sites; the audit is straightforward to re-verify: these are the only two non-defensive `format_ue8m0` reads in the repo (all other sites are writes/`getattr`).

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — the change only affects quant methods that never had the attribute (where loading previously crashed); methods that stamp `format_ue8m0` take the same code path as before.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — weight-loading-time code only, no runtime path touched.

title: [HiCache] Add radixshmem storage backend
body:
RadixShmemStorage is a HiCacheStorage L3 backend over a node-local radix-server. sglang keeps its host staging pool; pages are copied to and from radixshmem's SlotStore, and keys are the chained page hashes salted per pool and per rank (TP rank only for rank-sharded pools). The backend hands the server its slot geometry on the first storage call, once every host pool is registered: block_size is the KV page size and the slot holds the largest pool page. ALL_PAGES pools are stored as radix paths (prefix query, run pull); TRAILING_PAGES pools as one-block paths per page; pools without bytes (DeepSeek-V4's logical KV anchor) are never stored.

Registered as builtin backend "radixshmem" on the zero-copy v1/v2 path. Unit tests run against an in-memory fake. Verified on DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 with --hicache-host-memory-mode buffer_only: a flushed 10k-token prompt is served from storage (cached_tokens_details.storage == 9984).

title: [Spec] Model-agnostic last-stage draft embedding under pipeline parallelism
body:
## Motivation

**Update after #30775 merged.** The decode-side PP x spec path now carries its own inline checkpoint read of the draft embedding in `eagle_worker_v2` (type scan for the draft's `VocabParallelEmbedding`, a candidate-name table, `DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights`), gated on `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC`. This PR replaces that inline code with a shared module so the env-gated decode path and the PD-prefill path (#39378's gate) use one loader, and extends it to `multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2` / `frozen_kv_mtp_worker_v2`.

Part of #39634 (P0). Under pipeline parallelism the EAGLE/MTP draft runs only on the last stage, while the target's input embedding lives only on the first stage (`embed_tokens` is a `PPMissingLayer` elsewhere). `EagleDraftWorker.init_lm_head` calls `target.get_embed_and_head()`, which raises `AttributeError` on the last stage for every model whose getter is `self.model.embed_tokens.weight, self.lm_head.weight` (DeepSeek, GLM, Llama, ...).

Today each model works around this in its own file: Qwen3.5 (#37471) keeps a draft-owned embedding and loads it in `qwen3_5_mtp.load_weights`; #39378 materializes a second `embed_tokens` on the target's last stage for DeepSeek/GLM. That per-model work is why the PP+spec gates in #39378 / #39602 / #38698 are architecture allowlists.

## Modifications

- **`speculative/pp_draft_embedding.py`** (new)
  - `resolve_target_embed_and_head`: PP-safe wrapper; a `PPMissingLayer` embedding yields `embed=None` and the head is read directly; any other `AttributeError` propagates.
  - `load_draft_embedding_from_checkpoint`: resolves the checkpoint through `DefaultModelLoader._prepare_weights` (so ModelScope, `--download-dir`, `load_format` and the `.bin` fallback match the target load; `dummy` skips), locates the input embedding via `model.safetensors.index.json` and reads only that shard (no index: keys are collected across all shards before choosing; `layers.<n>.` MTP embeddings are never picked), and loads it into the draft's own embedding through its `weight_loader`. The draft embedding is the draft's single `VocabParallelEmbedding` (not `ParallelLMHead`); a draft without one fails with an explicit error. Returns the parameter so the existing `set_embed_and_head(embed, head)` call is unchanged.
  - `resolve_draft_embed_and_head` takes no pipeline-rank arguments: a stage whose target embedding is a `PPMissingLayer` loads the draft's own embedding; `pp_size == 1` never returns `embed=None`.
- **`eagle_worker_v2`, `multi_layer_eagle_worker_v2`, `frozen_kv_mtp_worker_v2`**: all three `init_lm_head` paths go through `resolve_draft_embed_and_head` and no longer read the PP group. The `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC` early-return block and its helpers (`_find_draft_input_embedding`, `_load_checkpoint_tensor`, `_EMBED_TENSOR_NAMES`) are removed; their re-openable load-format guard and extra checkpoint spellings are folded into the module. No model file changes.
- **`arg_groups/validation_hook.py`**: the `_PP_EAGLE_SUPPORTED_ARCHITECTURES` allowlist and the `model_architecture` argument of `check_pipeline_parallel_compat` are removed. The list existed because only some model families could hand the draft an embedding on the last stage; with the checkpoint loader that is true for every model, and a draft without any embedding fails in the loader with an explicit error instead.
- **`test/registered/e2e/pp/test_pp_spec_embed_scan.py`**: imports retargeted to the module.

## Behavior changes

- The removed `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC` block carried `assert hot_token_id is None and not is_eagle3()`. EAGLE3 under PP is still rejected by `validation_hook.py`; `--speculative-token-map` now takes the generic `head.clone()[hot_token_id]` path instead of being rejected. `set_lm_head_from_target` now also runs on the env-gated path.
- PD-prefill PP + EAGLE/MTP is no longer limited to the DeepSeek / GLM-5.2 / Qwen3.5 architectures listed in #39378 (GLM-5.3-Flash, `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration`, was rejected by that list on main).

Relationship to #30775: that PR carries its own checkpoint embedding read in `init_lm_head`, active only under `SGLANG_ENABLE_PP_SPEC`; this PR replaces it. The type-based draft lookup and the extra tensor spellings here are taken from #30775.

Known follow-ups once this lands: drop the model-specific embedding handling in `qwen3_5_mtp.load_weights` (until then Qwen3.5 loads its draft embedding twice, correct but one redundant shard read) and the target-side `pp_stage_needs_embedding` in #39378.

## Accuracy / validation

- Unit tests (`test/registered/unit/spec/test_pp_draft_embedding.py`, CPU, 8 cases): PP-safe resolution incl. an unrelated `AttributeError` not being swallowed, index and no-index selection over a `layers.61.embed_tokens` decoy, `.bin`-only checkpoint, full-vocab tensor handed to `weight_loader`, `load_format` gating (`dummy` / streaming), loud failure for a draft without an embedding. The drafts use the real `VocabParallelEmbedding` under a published topology. `test_server_args.py::TestPipelineParallelCompat` updated for the removed allowlist.
- E2E, env-gated decode path: #30775's `test/registered/e2e/pp/test_pp_spec.py` (4-GPU H100) exercises this module.
- E2E, PD-prefill path (GB300, this branch merged with main `d229952`): GLM-5.3-Flash, PD 1P(TP2xPP2 + MTP) : 1D(TP4 + MTP) over Mooncake, GSM8K-200 via `sglang.test.run_eval`: **score 0.990, accept length 3.45** (TP4 + MTP reference 0.990 / 3.39). The last prefill stage logs `Loaded draft embedding model.embed_tokens.weight from checkpoint key model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight (154880, 4096)`, a key the previous inline loader did not know.

## Motivation

This PR adds C++ group-aware CPU shared-memory kernels for all-gather, all-to-all, and all-reduce, enabling communication within arbitrary process groups instead of assuming the communication group is the global world, which is required to support combined SP and TP on CPU.

## Modifications

1.  Add new CPU SHM kernels: shm_group_allgather, shm_group_allreduce, and shm_group_alltoall, with group-aware all-to-all added to support Ulysses SP communication on CPU.

title: [HiSparse] Prepare write slots once in attention metadata
body:
Prepare physical KV write locations when DSA attention metadata is initialized, then reuse them for fused MLA cache writes throughout the batch. HiSparse pools translate logical locations once for gfx95 decode; resident pools retain their locations. Modes without prepared decode metadata resolve locations at the writer. Hybrid and TBO backends delegate lookup to the backend that owns the active metadata.

The new coverage checks decode graph replay, eager execution, padding, resident pools, and fallback behavior. Focused CPU and MI355X GPU validation passed on that source commit.

## C1 steady-state decode

Measured on GLM-5.2 FP8 with BF16 KV, TP4 MI355X, a 32,768-token input and 256-token output, using 64 warmup tokens and the next 192 decode intervals. Measured source commit: `87c1754b5990`. Runtime: stock SGLang v0.5.20 on ROCm 7.2.4. Parent: `c0f7b4d`. Lower is faster.

| Prefetch | Parent median (ms/token) | This PR median (ms/token) | Latency reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Off | 20.111 | 19.918 | ~1% |
| On | 18.375 | 18.201 | ~1% |

One trial per source and prefetch mode was run on the same TP4 allocation. These results are descriptive, not independent restart replications.

title: [HiSparse] Batch gfx95 planner prefix scans
body:
Add an opt-in batched prefix scan for the qualified gfx95 linear miss planner. The planner gathers four independent lookup passes before one wave64 scan while preserving hit and eviction order. The real KV copy still follows planning before restored KV is read; unsupported configurations retain the existing path.

The gfx95 regression covers eager and graph execution, request-index and sequence-length dtypes, and empty, full, mixed, newest-token, and short-sequence cases. CPU protocol coverage checks the opt-in gate and copy ordering.

## C1 steady-state decode

Measured on GLM-5.2 FP8 with BF16 KV, TP4 MI355X, a 32,768-token input and 256-token output, using 64 warmup tokens and the next 192 decode intervals. Measured source commit: `32df4400f778`. Runtime: stock SGLang v0.5.20 on ROCm 7.2.4. Parent: `38876dd`. Lower is faster.

| Prefetch | Parent median (ms/token) | This PR median (ms/token) | Latency reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Off | 17.249 | 17.145 | +0.60% |
| On | 17.751 | 17.692 | +0.33% |

One trial per source and prefetch mode was run on the same TP4 allocation. These results are descriptive, not independent restart replications.

title: [HiSparse] Plan ROCm misses and reuse KV copy plans
body:
On qualified ROCm gfx95 AITER paths, record cache misses first and perform the real KV transfer with a copy-only kernel. Use sixteen copy blocks for that transfer. When shared-index prefetch is disabled, follower layers reuse the anchor miss plan and copy synchronously on the current stream. Prefetched copies retain their existing stream and event ordering; unsupported configurations keep the fused swap-in path.

The planned-copy path rejects the debug skip-I/O setting because it requires real KV transfer. Focused protocol tests cover capability gates, fallback behavior, plan/copy ordering, the copy grid, shared-index reuse, and the prefetch kill switch.

## C1 steady-state decode

Measured on GLM-5.2 FP8 with BF16 KV, TP4 MI355X, a 32,768-token input and 256-token output, using 64 warmup tokens and the next 192 decode intervals. Measured source commit: `38876dd01b81`. Runtime: stock SGLang v0.5.20 on ROCm 7.2.4. Parent: `87c1754`. Lower is faster.

|---|---:|---:|---:|

| On | 18.201 | 17.751 | +2.48% |

One trial per source and prefetch mode was run on the same TP4 allocation. These results are descriptive, not independent restart replications.

title: [sgl-router] Launch reorg routing with existing policy options
body:
## Motivation

The binary always launches legacy routing even though the reorg handler and policies exist. Add `--chat-routing reorg` and let the existing `--policy` and tuning flags select the reorg implementations automatically. No separate policy switch or configuration file.

## Modifications

- Keep legacy routing and its defaults unchanged. Reorg supports `power_of_two` (default), `cache_aware`, and `session_aware` through the existing options.
- Build default plain/PD buckets from live discovery, sharing engine load, local/remote cache state, and expiring session bindings. Decode uses power-of-two; `--filter overloaded --max-in-flight N` applies admission to both roles.
- Reject unsupported combinations. Legacy role-specific `--bucket-config` files cannot define complete reorg PD buckets; explicit bucket configuration remains a follow-up.

```bash
sgl-router --model-id qwen3 --worker-urls http://localhost:30001 \
  --chat-routing reorg --policy cache_aware
```

title: [Tool Call] Forward unknown tools to clients by default
body:
## Summary
- Flip the default of `SGLANG_FORWARD_UNKNOWN_TOOLS` from `false` to `true` so that tool calls with names not in the declared list are forwarded to the client (with `tool_index=-1`) instead of being silently dropped.
- This matches the behavior of hosted APIs and is essential for agent loops: the client validates tool names and returns an error to the model, which can then recover with the correct name.
- The previous drop behavior was invisible on the wire and indistinguishable from "the model decided to stop", causing agent runs to terminate early when the model made a minor naming mistake.

## Changes
- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: Changed default of `SGLANG_FORWARD_UNKNOWN_TOOLS` from `False` to `True`.
- `docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx`: Updated documentation to reflect the new default and explain the behavior.
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_unknown_tool_name.py`: Renamed test to clarify it tests the opt-out behavior; added new test verifying the new default (forward) behavior.
- `test/registered/unit/function_call/test_function_call_parser.py`: Updated test to explicitly set `SGLANG_FORWARD_UNKNOWN_TOOLS=False` to maintain the original test intent (testing the drop behavior).

## Test plan
- [x] `test_unknown_tool_name.py`: All 3 tests pass (dropped when disabled, forwarded when enabled, forwarded by default).
- [x] `test_function_call_parser.py::TestLfm2Detector::test_detect_and_parse_unknown_function`: Passes with explicit env override.
- [x] `test_k2_v3_detector.py::test_unknown_tool_respects_forwarding_policy`: Passes (already uses explicit overrides).
- [x] `test_spark25_detector.py::test_malformed_block_is_text_and_unknown_tool_honors_policy`: Passes (already uses explicit overrides).

## Backward compatibility
Deployments that want the old drop behavior can set `SGLANG_FORWARD_UNKNOWN_TOOLS=false`.

Fixes #40817

title: [diffusion] Support LLaDA-Image BF16 generation and editing
body:
## Motivation

Add native SGLang Diffusion serving for [InclusionAI/LLaDA-Image](https://huggingface.co/InclusionAI/LLaDA-Image) and [InclusionAI/LLaDA-Image-Turbo](https://huggingface.co/InclusionAI/LLaDA-Image-Turbo), including their FP8 variants. The integration supports text-to-image generation and single-image editing through the OpenAI-compatible Images API, with single-GPU and sequence-parallel deployment.

## Contributors

- InclusionAI, Ant Group: Kun Chen (@kunchengit), Chengzhang Wu (@Anmuliar), Chaoyang Wang (@wzy-ustc)
- SGLang community: Kaige Li (@stephenkgli), Yuhan Zhou (@Dayuxiaoshui), Yihao Wang (@AgainstEntropy), Mick Qian (@mickqian), Richard Wang (@rwang5203)

## Modifications

- **Pipeline.** Add the LLaDA-Image DiT, pipeline configuration, sampling parameters, scheduler integration, embedded LLaDA2 MoE text encoder, source-image conditioning, and model registry entries.
- **Serving.** Support `/v1/images/generations` and `/v1/images/edits`, with request validation for image dimensions, pixel area, text length, output count, and exactly one edit source.
- **Sequence parallelism.** Support SP=1 and SP=2 with global stochastic-noise slicing, full text-encoder replication per SP rank, and a dedicated CFG FlashInfer attention path with fail-closed conditioning-mask validation.
- **FP8.** Support dynamic FP8 DiT weights and experts-only FP8 LLaDA2 checkpoints, including ModelOpt conversion, RMSNorm dtype handling, structured checkpoint metadata, legacy metadata compatibility, and component-path overrides.
- **Safety and lifecycle.** Propagate checkpoint revisions and remote-code trust into the embedded worker, reject unsupported residency and weight-update modes explicitly, and preserve generic non-conditioning attention behavior.

## Reproduction

Start Turbo with SP=1:

```bash
sglang serve --model-path inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image-Turbo --revision 033d068d0702ed81c45ec1bfbe61e318d843d948 --trust-remote-code --port 30000
```

Start Turbo with SP=2:

```bash
sglang serve --model-path inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image-Turbo --revision 033d068d0702ed81c45ec1bfbe61e318d843d948 --trust-remote-code --num-gpus 2 --sp-degree 2 --ulysses-degree 2 --ring-degree 1 --port 30000
```

Generate an image:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/images/generations -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"A cinematic photograph of a red fox standing in fresh snow at golden hour, detailed fur, shallow depth of field","size":"1024x1024","n":1,"response_format":"b64_json","num_inference_steps":4,"guidance_scale":1.0,"seed":42}'
```

Edit an image:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/images/edits -F "image=@input.png" -F "prompt=Place the subject on a beach" -F "size=1024x1024" -F "n=1" -F "response_format=b64_json" -F "num_inference_steps=4" -F "guidance_scale=1.0" -F "seed=42"
```

The production FP8 path uses the same commands with `inclusionAI/LLaDA-Image-Turbo-FP8` pinned to revision `2b822499be3f33a6f83c988dafab7986ebd1f733`.

## Accuracy Tests

The benchmark generated and decoded all 6704 expected artifacts: 2212 GenEval images, 1280 LongText images, 1212 GEdit images, and 2000 CVTG images.

| Configuration | GenEval macro | LongText en | LongText zh | CVTG Word Accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Base 50-step BF16 | 0.8404 | 0.9120 | 0.9198 | 0.7792 |
| Turbo 4-step SP=1 | 0.8190 | 0.8959 | 0.9123 | 0.8267 |
| Turbo 4-step SP=2 | 0.8190 | 0.8959 | 0.9123 | 0.8267 |

| Turbo GEdit metric | SP=1 | SP=2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| en semantic / quality / overall | 7.9242 / 7.3682 / 7.5728 | 7.9175 / 7.3432 / 7.5451 |
| zh semantic / quality / overall | 7.7375 / 7.3867 / 7.4347 | 7.7327 / 7.4177 / 7.4534 |

GenEval, LongText, and CVTG reproduced the SP=1 scores exactly under SP=2. All six GEdit metrics remained within ±0.15 using the same evaluator.

Matched SP=1 and SP=2 T2I outputs were byte-identical. The matched edit output measured MAE 2.7935, PSNR 30.1759 dB, and RGB Pearson correlation 0.9919.

The production Turbo-FP8 checkpoint passed live SP=1 and SP=2 T2I, image editing, repeat determinism, and request-boundary validation at 1024x1024 with 4 steps and CFG 1.0.

The final post-rebase suite passed 59 tests and 4 subtests. The broader affected selection passed 341 tests and 102 subtests, including live CUDA RMSNorm coverage. The repository-configured Ruff, Ruff format, isort, and `git diff --check` checks also passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The following values are median client-wall latency over ten sequential requests after two warmups on NVIDIA L20X at 1024x1024.

| Task | 4-step SP=1 | 4-step SP=2 | 50-step SP=1 | 50-step SP=2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| T2I | 0.6216s | 0.4629s | 12.2036s | 7.6757s |
| Edit | 1.7717s | 1.2141s | 32.8138s | 19.9279s |

## Known Limitations

- The embedded text encoder requires reviewed remote code, so deployments must use `--trust-remote-code` and should pin the checkpoint revision.
- Sequence parallelism currently supports SP=1 or SP=2 with Ulysses only; SP=2 accepts one output per request.
- The embedded text encoder must remain resident and does not support generic memory sleep or hot weight updates.
- The full 6704-image quality suite was not rerun on the production FP8 checkpoint, so this PR does not claim FP8 quality-score parity.

title: [Fix][NPU] fix pin mem hang
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

In theory, the NPU platform supports `pin_memory=True` just like the CUDA platform. Combined with `non_blocking=True`, this allows host-to-device operations to be performed completely asynchronously. However, with the current implementation, enabling `pin_memory=True` causes non-DSA models in the DP-Attn scenario to hang.

Also see [issue 38971](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/38971).

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->


For this sample ci test case (NPUGraph, DP-ATTN, MLA arch):

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /path/to/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-W8A8 --trust-remote-code --tp 2 --dp 2 --enable-dp-attention --chunked-prefill-size 1024 --attention-backend ascend --device npu --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8880 --max-running-requests 32 --cuda-graph-bs-decode 2 8 16
```

Do gsm8k test:

```
python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 1600 --num-shots 2 --data-path /path/to/gsm8k.josnl --max-new-tokens 512 --parallel 4 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8880
```

If we change the return value of `NPUDeviceMixin.is_pin_memory_available` to `True`, the system will occasionally hang during normal inference. The dumped stacks typically show Prefill on one side and Decode on the other, with one side having just transitioned from the IDLE state.

I set `TASK_QUEUE_ENABLE=0` to rule out the impact of operator submission order. I also compared the `plog` logs from both cards and ruled out issues involving extra or missing communication operations. In addition, I injected hooks through the WatchDog framework to collect the inputs to the DP operators on both sides, as well as the inputs used for graph replay on both sides. All of these inputs appeared to be correct.

I then narrowed down the issue to `_local_decode_cuda_graph_vote`. When modified so that one side returns `False` and falls back to Eager mode as soon as it detects an IDLE state, the hang no longer occurs. However, with this change, a single cURL request will no longer follow the graph execution path, resulting in a significant performance degradation.

Further investigation narrowed it down to `AscendAttnBackend.forward_decode_graph`. After commenting out the CANN-style FIA operator executed by DSV2 and directly returning `query`, the hang also disappeared. The issue was narrowed down to the FIA operator.

Eventually, I identified the root cause as `NPUCudaGraphBackend.replay_with_input_update`. Adding a synchronization operation at this point resolves the hang. The final solution is to retrieve the Event from the graph operation and synchronize the Event from the previous iteration before executing the graph in the next iteration, ensuring safe graph execution.

title: [MM] Keep scheduler padding in packed token arrays
body:
## Motivation

Multimodal padding runs **inside the scheduler process** while handling generation and embedding requests. Tokenizer ingress already produces native `array("q")` token buffers, but this scheduler-side padding still advertises lists and round-trips the full prompt through Python integers. In particular, `torch.as_tensor(array)` walks the sequence instead of viewing its buffer, adding per-token CPU work to the scheduler's request-handling path.

```text
Scheduler process (offset-based padding):
Before: array -> as_tensor (sequence walk) -> tolist -> array
After:  array -> bulk copy + frombuffer -> array -> ownership copy
```

Keep the model-padding boundary packed by default, with cheap assertion guardrails at representation-sensitive boundaries.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Synthetic CPU microbenchmark of offset-based scheduler padding at **`70729c719c`** against baseline **`6e1338dd1eb1546518bdffe3b69d2ea0e011ef28`**. aarch64, Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, one CPU thread; median of 41 alternating trials after 5 warmups. Both sides include the scheduler's final ownership copy. Ten sparse MM spans, up to 32 tokens per span:

| Prompt tokens | Baseline (ms) | Optimized (ms) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4,096 | 0.6279 | 0.03021 | 20.8x |
| 16,384 | 2.3663 | 0.03552 | 66.6x |
| 131,072 | 18.8500 | 0.11690 | 161.3x |

These are offset-based padding CPU measurements, **not** end-to-end TTFT or serving-throughput improvements.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python benchmark/io/bench_mm_token_padding.py \
  --baseline-ref 6e1338dd1eb1546518bdffe3b69d2ea0e011ef28 \
  --tokens 128 4096 16384 131072 --items 0 1 10 \
  --threads 1 --trials 41 --warmups 5
```

The benchmark verifies token values, source immutability and a separate scheduler-owned result before timing. Add `--json` for machine-readable output. All inputs are generated; no request/trace data or benchmark-output files are added to the repository.

## Modifications

- Trust the existing packed input at the scheduler boundary. Assert eight-byte `array("q")` inputs in the shared padding helpers and each model callback's output once. No redundant wrapper input check or per-token coercion.
- Use `torch.frombuffer` on a bulk array copy for offset-based padding. Preserve modality grouping, inclusive offsets, int64 values, and the original unpadded input.
- Make token-pair padding construct arrays directly. Preserve marker scans, grouping and data offsets, including zero-length spans.
- Use `duplicate_pad_mm_input_ids` to validate model output and create a separate scheduler-owned copy, including when a model returns its input or retains the padded buffer in multimodal metadata.
- Update stale padding annotations/imports in 58 model files. All 68 model padding method bodies are unchanged.
- Let EVS consume either existing list metadata or packed model-padding metadata, while retaining its existing list-output contract.
- Add a synthetic benchmark that loads the exact baseline helper classes from a supplied local git ref.

Inputs were already arrays on normal scheduler paths; the input annotation changes reflect that existing contract. Padding outputs now remain packed too: out-of-tree `pad_input_ids` implementations must accept and return native `array("q")`. The assertions are internal guardrails and are disabled by `python -O`. The public request format and tokenizer/IPC wire format are unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Existing VLM E2E suites cover both padding strategies, multiple input formats and chunked prefill. Follow the PR's CI checks for GPU/E2E results.

Local pre-commit checks and all 12 offset-based benchmark cases pass: 128, 4,096, 16,384 and 131,072 tokens with 0, 1 and 10 MM items. A separate smoke run covers empty input and the text output format.

AST verification confirms all 68 model padding bodies are unchanged, all their input/output annotations are arrays, and both scheduler callbacks use the checked boundary.

## Checklist

- [x] Include reproducible synthetic speed comparisons.
- [x] Document the stricter model-hook contract.
- [x] Keep model forward algorithms and GPU kernels unchanged.
- [x] Final pre-commit checks.
- [ ] GPU/E2E CI.

title: [Fix] Preserve inline instructions for Responses and Kimi K3 Messages
body:
**Entrypoints PR stack** (merge bottom-up; each PR is based on `main` and includes the PRs below it)
1. #39711
2. #40077 ← this PR
3. #39716

Review only the last 3 commits; the earlier commits belong to the PRs below.

---

## Motivation

Responses always moves an inline `developer`/`system` input into the leading system message. Appending an instruction to a conversation therefore rewrites the start of the prompt and throws away the whole cached prefix, which is common for agentic clients.

- **Controlled test on a production Kimi K3 deployment:** a ~50K-token Responses conversation hit 50,176 cached tokens when repeated or extended with a user turn. Appending one developer instruction dropped the hit to **0**. Replaying the original right afterwards hit 50,176 again, so the prefix was still cached.
- **Production:** after deploying this change on a production Kimi K3 deployment, token-weighted prefix-cache hit rate for `/v1/responses` went from **25.5% to 90.7%**, and from 12.9% to 92.2% for prompts ≥128K tokens. Chat Completions stayed flat (91.8% → 93.0%). This compares two 30-minute windows on 2026-09-18. They weren't matched, and the deploy included other changes, so treat it as supporting evidence rather than an A/B test.

Anthropic Messages already keeps inline system messages when the chat template renders them (#28906), but it probes the tokenizer's Jinja template. Kimi K3 renders with a native encoder and has no Jinja template, so K3 Messages requests are still hoisted.

## Modifications

- `OpenAIServingChat.supports_inline_system` is resolved once at startup from the renderer that actually builds the prompt: the native encoder allowlist (`spec_supports_inline_system`, currently `kimi_k3`) when a native encoder is active, `False` for a conversation `--chat-template`, and otherwise the existing Jinja probe (`detect_inline_system_support`).
- Anthropic Messages and Responses both read that attribute. Responses skips the system-message merge when it is set.
- Behavior change: Responses now keeps inline instructions in place for any HF Jinja template that renders mid-conversation system messages, the same rule #28906 applied to Messages. Messages now merges under a conversation `--chat-template` or a native encoder outside the allowlist, since the probed Jinja template is not what renders those prompts.
- #39518 made the same fix for DeepSeek V4.1 Messages but targeted the `dsv4.1` branch and was closed unmerged when that branch was deleted. Adding `dsv41` to the allowlist is a one-line follow-up once its encoder is checked.

## Tests

- `test_serving_responses.py::test_inline_instruction_keeps_history_prefix` (4 cases): the K3 and inline-Jinja cases fail on main because the instruction is hoisted. The conversation-template and dropping-Jinja cases pin the merge fallback; the conversation-template case fails if the resolver ignores `--chat-template`.
- `anthropic/test_serving.py::test_inline_system_support_comes_from_the_prompt_renderer` fails on main, where Messages probes a missing Jinja template and hoists.
- `test_serving_responses.py`, `test_serving_responses_stream.py`, `test_serving_chat.py`, and `anthropic/test_serving.py` pass.

title: [DSA] Add opt-in SM90 LiteTopK fused indexer top-k prefill path
body:
## Motivation

This PR brings the **SM90 (Hopper) counterpart to #32094**, which added the LiteTopK fused indexer top-k prefill path for SM100. We observe a comparable speedup on H100 (1.21x–1.40x, table below).

I would also like to invite @yuan-luo to help this PR due to his help in my sm100 implementation.

The feature is **off by default**:

```bash
SGLANG_USE_SM90_LITETOPK=1
```

## Modifications

**New** — `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/sm90_litetopk/`
- `csrc/sm90_litetopk.cuh`, `csrc/pr_hot.cuh` — the SM90 HOT12288 scorer and online bucket gate.
- `csrc/litetopk_sm90.cu`, `csrc/online_aux.cu` — launchers and auxiliary kernels.
- `__init__.py` — the Python adapter: workspace/carry-state management and the fail-closed `try_run` entry point.

**Modified**
- `dsa_indexer.py` — an `sm90_eligible` gate plus `try_sm90_litetopk()` / `observe_sm90_litetopk()` in `_get_topk_ragged`. Both the full-logits and row-chunked branches call the same adapter, so the first dense sub-chunk bootstraps subsequent HOT sub-chunks.

No packaging changes are needed: `srt/**/*` in `[tool.setuptools.package-data]` already carries the `csrc/` sources into the wheel. The CUDA sources are JIT-compiled lazily on the first eligible invocation and the adapter falls back to the dense indexer on build failure.

### Configuration

| env var | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `SGLANG_USE_SM90_LITETOPK` | `0` | enable the path |
| `SM90_LITETOPK_CAPACITY` | `49152` | candidate capacity (must be >= 12288 and divisible by 256) |
| `SM90_LITETOPK_DEEP_GEMM_INCLUDE` | — | optional DeepGEMM/CUTLASS include path |
| `SM90_LITETOPK_BUILD_VERBOSE` | `0` | verbose JIT build output |

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on NVIDIA H100, PyTorch 2.8.0, CUDA 12.9:

- Real 128K capture, Q=64: **exact top-k, recall 1.0**, no invalid or duplicate indices.
- Odd Q=3 adapter path: exact top-k, recall 1.0.
- Q=17 with SGLang's native ragged selector: exact top-k, recall 1.0.
- Candidate-overflow case correctly returns to the dense path.
- Source K verified **byte-for-byte unchanged** after a rejected HOT attempt.
- Both CUDA extensions compile for `sm_90a`.

Recall is exact by construction: the bucket gate only ever tightens and stays above the bucket of the true k-th best score, so a stale threshold admits extra candidates but never drops one; the final select trims the superset exactly.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Indexer top-k latency, NVIDIA H100 (SM90), native SGLang dense path vs. this path:

| KV length | native SGLang | SM90 LiteTopK | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128K | 11.916 ms | 9.855 ms | **1.21x** |
| 256K | 24.637 ms | 19.639 ms | **1.25x** |
| 512K | 50.696 ms | 38.018 ms | **1.33x** |
| 768K | 77.370 ms | 55.445 ms | **1.40x** |
| 1M | 103.558 ms | 74.367 ms | **1.39x** |

The speedup grows with context length, as expected — the dense path's cost is dominated by materializing and scanning the full `[num_q, seq_len]` logits matrix, which this path skips after the bootstrap chunk.

title: [dLLM] Support DiffusionGemma serving
body:
## Motivation

SGLang rejects the DiffusionGemma architecture as unknown. This PR adds native BF16 text and image serving using the shared dLLM and FDFO paths from #27551 and #27877.

Fixes #29904.

## Changes

- Add the model, multimodal processor, weight loader, and Gemma4Renoise sampler, with TP1, TP2, and TP4 support.
- Encode causal context separately from each bidirectional 256-position denoising canvas, retaining request KV state across FDFO rounds and output blocks.
- Enable decode CUDA graphs with current self-conditioning embeddings and prefix-only attention metadata. Batch denoiser statistics and soft embedding work, shard the vocabulary embedding, and use the existing fused QKV normalization kernel.
- Rebase onto `db272201a2` and adapt to the current argument-resolution and request-lifecycle APIs. Keep default adaptive convergence unchanged; allow an explicit zero confidence threshold for fixed-work measurements.
- Use the checkpoint's tanh GELU in the expert layers. Fuse sampler division/argmax while retaining RNG draws, and tune H200 MoE kernels without changing precision or routing.
- Reject unsupported request fields and server settings before model execution.

## Validation

- 272 tests and 64 subtests passed, including CUDA sampling/RNG equivalence, expert activation, QKV normalization, graph metadata/replay, scheduling, request lifecycle, and server arguments.
- Full pre-commit passed on all 35 changed files.
- Real H200 serving passed at TP1, TP2, and TP4: arithmetic, normal text, image OCR, a 2,662-token prompt with multi-block generation, and unsupported-request HTTP 400 responses. TP1/TP4 used default adaptive convergence; TP2 used fixed-step generation and also completed the explicit synchronous serving benchmark.
- An additional native-MoE CPU dispatch test fails in this GPU environment and reproduces on unchanged source; details are recorded in `benchmark/dllm/PROFILE.md`.

## Performance

The measurements use the same checkpoint and two physical H200s, TP2, BF16 weights/KV cache, exact pretokenized prompts, resource limits, 256 canvas positions, and all 48 denoising steps. Each case has three warmups and 15 measured trials. Across the two scheduling modes, all 936 requests, including warmups, have matching corresponding prompt hashes and token counts. Both modes use compilation and CUDA graphs.

Median end-to-end batch latency:

| Prompt tokens | Concurrency | Optimized FDFO | Optimized sync |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128 | 1 | 0.722 s | 0.655 s |
| 128 | 4 | 1.390 s | 1.276 s |
| 128 | 8 | 2.334 s | 2.229 s |
| 2048 | 1 | 0.901 s | 0.833 s |
| 2048 | 4 | 1.704 s | 1.586 s |
| 2048 | 8 | 3.036 s | 3.150 s |

These fixed-work measurements disable EOS stopping and exclude profiled timings.

## Limits

- PP, CP, quantized loading, and untied embeddings are unsupported.
- Prefill CUDA graphs, chunked prefill, and radix caching remain disabled for this model; decode CUDA graphs are enabled.
- Functional smoke checks do not establish model accuracy, and this benchmark does not establish adaptive-generation performance or useful-text throughput.

title: [Responses] Close generation iterators when SSE consumers exit
body:
**Entrypoints PR stack** (merge bottom-up; each PR is based on `main` and includes the PRs below it)
1. #39711
2. #40167 ← this PR
3. #40077
4. #39716

Review only the last 3 commit(s); the earlier commits belong to the PRs below.

---

## Motivation

When a client stops reading a `/v1/responses` SSE stream, the formatter generator is closed, but nothing closes the engine generation under it. Once nothing iterates it, `TokenizerManager.generate_request` aborts its scheduler request only when its generator is closed, so the abort is left to whenever garbage collection finalizes the abandoned generators.

## Modifications

- `create_responses` wraps both streaming formatters (Harmony and non-Harmony) in one helper, `_close_generation_with_stream`, which closes the formatter and then the generation iterator when the consumer exits.
- `_generate_with_builtin_tools` closes each `generate_request` generator with `contextlib.aclosing`, so closing it reaches the engine request.
- Formatter output is unchanged. Chat Completions iterates `generate_request` inside its own formatter and is out of scope here.

## Tests

- `test_serving_responses.py::test_stream_close_closes_engine_generation[harmony=False/True]` reads a stream through `create_responses` to its first content delta, closes it, and checks the mocked `generate_request` generator was closed before `aclose()` returned. Both cases fail on main. They also fail with only one of the two changes above.
- `test_serving_responses.py`, `test_serving_responses_stream.py`, and `anthropic/test_serving.py` pass (142 tests, 15 subtests).

title: [Feature] Add constrained per-request DSpark draft LoRA support
body:
## Motivation

Related to #37772. Allow requests sharing one target model to select different LoRA-adapted DSpark drafts. Existing target-adapter selection remains separate from the new `draft_adapter` field.

This PR is ready for design and code review. The per-request GPU serving path has not been validated. Feedback is especially welcome on whether materialized merged variants and homogeneous scheduling are an acceptable initial scope, or whether upstream requires low-rank kernels with mixed-adapter batches.

## Modifications

- Add a validated local PEFT/safetensors merger for DSpark projection weights, including packed QKV and gate/up layouts. Reject unsupported adapter semantics and shared embedding/output-head updates.
- Support a single startup adapter with `--speculative-dspark-lora-path`, or multiple named adapters with `--speculative-dspark-lora-paths '{"adapter_a":"/adapters/a","adapter_b":"/adapters/b"}'`.
- Carry `draft_adapter` through native generation, OpenAI chat/completions, sync/async Engine calls, request normalization, and scheduler state. An omitted/null selector uses the base draft; unknown names are rejected before enqueueing.
- Group requests by draft adapter. Stop admission at the first different adapter so later matching arrivals cannot continually bypass it.
- Activate the selected weights before both prefill and decode, restore base weights for parameters an adapter does not modify, and invalidate both derived KV projection caches.
- Reject unsupported execution configurations and online weight replacement before either model is mutated.

The per-request mode is restricted to an unquantized Qwen3 DSpark draft on one CUDA GPU, eager execution, non-overlap scheduling, FCFS, and disabled prefix caching. Sessions, beam search, runtime adapter loading, and mixed-adapter GPU batches are unsupported.

The bank stores dense copies of modified packed weights, plus the corresponding base weights; it does not duplicate the entire draft. This trades extra GPU memory, synchronized weight copies, and reduced batching flexibility for reuse of existing kernels. It is not a low-rank-resident serving implementation.

## Accuracy Tests

**39 focused CPU tests pass**:

| Area | Tests |
| --- | ---: |
| Adapter loading, merge numerics, packed layouts, artifact rejection | 14 |
| Adapter-bank switching, restoration, cache invalidation | 6 |
| Request normalization, grouping, Engine/worker dispatch | 13 |
| Configuration and compatibility regressions | 6 |

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s test/manual/lora -p 'test_dspark*draft*.py' -v
```

A regression test verifies that upstream target-only pipeline stages keep their existing dispatch behavior without accessing draft-adapter state. Per-request adapter banks remain restricted to one pipeline stage.

Several integration-method tests extract actual source bodies with AST to avoid importing CUDA dependencies on the local CPU host. They do not validate full server startup, HTTP/IPC flow, the full scheduler, GPU kernels, or stream ordering.

An earlier **startup-only patch**, before the per-request extension, passed a limited H100 smoke test: Qwen3-14B target, `deepseek-ai/dspark_qwen3_14b_block7`, BF16, TP1, eager, concurrency one; eight prompts, two repeats, four arms (target-only/original draft/zero adapter/nonzero synthetic adapter), totaling 64 successful requests with matching greedy token IDs. Target parameter hashes stayed unchanged and adapted draft tensors matched an independent merge reference. **Those results do not validate the current per-request implementation or trained-adapter quality.**

Pending: current-branch GPU startup and end-to-end request tests, BF16 and FP16 cache paths, concurrent switching/cancellation/retraction, combined target/draft LoRA, and sampled-output correctness.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run for this implementation. No speedup, acceptance improvement, or memory-efficiency claim is made. Switching overhead, resident/peak memory, and throughput under alternating adapter traffic need measurement.

Changed Python compiles; focused Ruff lint/format checks and `git diff --check` pass. The full repository pre-commit suite and GPU CI have not been run.

title: [Metrics] Count terminal requests and tokens by outcome
body:
**Metrics PR stack** (merge bottom-up; each PR is based on `main` and includes the PRs below it)
1. #38600
2. #39706
3. #40275
4. #40255 ← this PR

Review only the last 3 commit(s); the earlier commits belong to the PRs below.

---

## Motivation

Under PD, aborted requests report prompt tokens with zero cached tokens. That drags down the aggregate cache-hit ratio without any cold prefill work having happened. The existing prompt and cache counters can't separate aborts from successful requests.

## Modifications

- New counters labeled by `outcome` (`success` = `stop` or `length`, or `abort`):
  - `sglang:finished_requests_by_outcome_total`
  - `sglang:finished_prompt_tokens_by_outcome_total`
  - `sglang:finished_cached_tokens_by_outcome_total`
- Dashboards can compute cache-hit ratio on `outcome="success"` and show aborts separately. The token counters report request usage, not executed prefill work.
- They are separate `_by_outcome` series rather than a new label on the existing counters, so existing dashboards and queries keep working.
- Scheduler-side aborts are counted in `_handle_abort_req`: waiting-queue disconnects, `SGLANG_REQ_WAITING_TIMEOUT`, priority preemption, chunked-prefill and retract aborts, and PD bootstrap/prealloc failures. These requests never reach `collect_metrics`.
  - They increment only the request counter, because the tokenizer has no reliable prompt length for them. The help text says so.
  - Each request is counted once, because whichever handler runs first removes its `rid_to_state` entry.

## Tests

- `test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py::TestFinishedOutcomeMetrics` (2 methods):
  - batch-output outcomes: stop and length count as success, abort as abort, an unfinished request isn't counted;
  - a scheduler-side abort through the real `_handle_abort_req` is counted once, with no token counts, even when a late echo arrives for the same rid. This fails if `_handle_abort_req` doesn't count the outcome, because scheduler-side aborts never reach `collect_metrics`.
- `test_stat_loggers_di.py::TestFinishedOutcomeCounters` (1 method): token counters skip requests without token counts.

CPU: 118 tests pass across the stack's five affected unit files.

title: fix(function_call): honor SGLANG_FORWARD_UNKNOWN_TOOLS in one-shot Qwen3Coder/Gemma4/KimiK2/KimiK3 detectors
body:
## Motivation

Fixes #39640.

`SGLANG_FORWARD_UNKNOWN_TOOLS` defaults to `False`, and `BaseFormatDetector.parse_base_json` implements that by dropping a call whose function name is not among the request's declared tools. Detectors that override `detect_and_parse` and parse the output themselves never reach that check, and four of them do not repeat it: `Qwen3CoderDetector` (`qwen3_coder`, `step3p5`), `Gemma4Detector`, `KimiK2Detector`, and `KimiK3Detector`. An undeclared function name comes back to the client as a tool call, and `FunctionCallParser.parse_non_stream` returns `calls` as-is, so nothing downstream restores the boundary. The other 26 registered parser names already honour the flag on this path.

## Modifications

- `qwen3_coder_detector.py`, `gemma4_detector.py`, `kimik2_detector.py`, `kimik3_detector.py`: in `detect_and_parse`, look the parsed name up in `_get_tool_indices(tools)` and apply the same warn-then-skip-unless-flag-set check the base class and the other overriding detectors (`pythonic`, `gpt_oss`, `lfm2`, ...) use. Kimi K3 moves from a list comprehension to a loop so a skipped call does not leave a gap in `tool_index`.
- `test_unknown_tool_name.py`: parametrised one-shot cases for the four detectors, dropped by default and forwarded with the flag on. Verified red before the fix on all four.
- `test_function_call_parser.py`: `TestGemma4Detector.test_detect_and_parse_unknown_tool_index` encoded the old pass-through; it now runs with the flag on, which is the case it was actually pinning (`tool_index == -1`).
- `test_kimik3_detector.py`: `test_attr_unescaping_and_raw_string_args` used an undeclared tool `a&b`; it now declares it, so the unescaped name has to match the declared tool.

Scope is the one-shot path only. The streaming paths of these detectors are the separate contract tracked in #23453 / #33902 / #35512.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A. Parser change only; no kernel, model forward, or sampling changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A. One dict lookup per parsed call.
